July 29, 1941

From the
Director of Police Services
to the French Consul-General,
Shanghai.

Sir,
The events that are at present taking
place in the Far East, the Franco-Japanese Agreements
relating to Indo-China and the measures taken by the
United States in regard to Japanese and Chinese
credits, had repercussions on the market on Saturday
and Monday morning. The speculators sent up prices
-- a rise which was entirely artificial - particularly
the price of rice. Saigon rice on Monday morning rose
from $118.50 to $125 per zar of 80 kilograms. On
July 25, the price fluctuated between $114 and $116
and rose to $118.50 on Saturday morning.

Under the circumstances, the price quoted by
retailers on the basis of replacement prices could
not help rising. It appeared to be necessary to act
immediately to prevent speculators from indulging
in shameless practices which, in March last, had sent
up the price of Saigon rice to $150 per zar.

In this connection, we have, in accord with
the Director-General of the Municipal Services,
published in the local Press a note, a translation of
which is attached.

The measure taken is intended to "block" the
retail price at the average prices quoted on the
morning of July 25, namely:-

目前远东地区发生的事态、有关印度支那的法日协定，以及美国针对日本和中国信贷所采取的措施，在周六和周一上午对市场产生了反响。投机者抬高了价格——这种上涨完全是人为的——尤其是大米价格。周一上午，西贡米每扎尔（zar，80公斤）的价格从118.50美元涨至125美元。7月25日，价格在114美元至116美元之间波动，并于周六上午涨至118.50美元。

在此情况下，零售商基于重置成本报出的价格不可避免地会上涨。看来有必要立即采取行动，以防止投机者从事无耻的行径，此类行径曾在去年三月将西贡米的价格推高至每扎尔150美元。

为此，我们与工务局总监协商，在当地报刊上刊登了一则通告，其译文附后。

所采取的措施旨在将零售价格“冻结”在7月25日上午的平均报价水平，即：-

TRADUCTION

(Note publiée dans la presse locale)

A la suite des évènements qui se déroulent
en Extrême-Orient et des arrangements intervenus entre
l'Indochine et le Japon, la Bourse du riz a enregistré
une augmentation des quotations largement supérieure
aux quotations moyennes de ces dernières semaines, il
s'agit là d'une hausse non justifiée contre laquelle
les autorités françaises ont décidé d'agir.

Les commerçants sont avisés que la vente au
détail du riz doit continuer à se faire sur la base des
cours du 5 juillet, et qu'aucune augmentation de prix
ne pourra être imposée aux acheteurs sans autorisation
préalable du comité de fixation des prix.

D'une façon générale, les autorités françaises
ont décidé de n'autoriser aucune augmentation de prix
sans que la justification de ces augmentations lui ait
été fournie au moyen de documents authentiques.

译文

（刊登于当地报刊的通告）

鉴于远东局势的发展以及印度支那与日本之间达成的安排，大米交易所记录的报价涨幅远远超过近几周的平均报价，此种上涨缺乏正当理由，法国当局已决定对此采取行动。

特此告知各商人，大米零售须继续以7月5日的行市为基础进行，未经价格核定委员会事先批准，不得向买家强行加价。

总体而言，法国当局已决定，在未通过正式文件向其证明涨价理由的情况下，不予批准任何价格上涨。

Translation of letter to Council from
Shanghai Pulse and Rice Dealers'
Association.
Dated 27th May, 1941.

Rice Commission on

Our members engaged in the business of supplying rice to
retail shops depend entirely on their income from commissions to
meet their expenses. Owing to the recent advance in the prices
of commodities, the expenses have increased considerably, and
now the income is rather insufficient.

The Executive and Supervisory Committees of this Association
have decided at a meeting that from 1st June next the commission
for the supply of rice to retail shops will be changed to $1 per
picul, plus the various usual charges.

Later, the Market Control Committee held a meeting and
resolved that the various charges be fixed at 60 cents per bag for
rooting; at 80 cents per bag for districts west of the Whangpoo
River and for Hongkew, and at 60 cents per bag transported to
Hongkew by boat.

Apart from notifying the Market and the Rice Shops'
Association, the Council is hereby requested to take note and to
place the matter on record.

(Chopped) Shanghai Pulse and Rice Dealers' Association.

(Note: Received for translation late a.m. 28th May, 1941.)

Alliance

Jt H H1

S.I., Sp. Br. Station. File No. Date April 24, 1941.

SUBJECT:
Secret "allowances" on rice transactions

The question of measures to counter the
charging of premiums over and above the fixed price
has already engaged the attention of this Branch
but it is very difficult to detect instances of it.
The rice dealers adopt a jargon known only to
themselves when putting through deals and no money
is actually paid over in the market. Further, the
bill of sale is made out in accordance with the
fixed price and the premium paid secretly.

Detectives are daily posted in the Rice Market
in efforts to combat this evil and recently four several persons
suspected of charging premiums have been brought
to this office but sufficient proof to take action
against them has in no case existed.

主题：
大米交易中的秘密“津贴”

关于采取措施打击在固定价格之上收取溢价的问题，本科早已关注，但很难发现此类实例。米商在进行交易时使用只有他们自己知道的行话，市场上实际上并不进行金钱交割。此外，销售单据是按照固定价格开具的，而溢价则是秘密支付的。

侦探们每天被部署在米市场，努力打击这种弊病，最近有几名涉嫌收取溢价的人被带到本办公室，但在任何情况下都不存在足以对他们采取行动的充分证据。

March 14, 1941.

While there is a record stock of rice in
Shanghai, the price continues in an upward trend
and there is little doubt that certain merchants
are hoarding and profiteering. Observations are
being kept on the market but it is extremely
difficult to detect profiteering owing to precautions
taken by the principals to such transactions. As to
hoarding, the Guild, if sincere, should be able to
supply information although there is always the danger
of change of ownership of an offender's stock, to
Japanese probably, once he realizes that investigation

x Copy to D.B. 39A/5124

The present situation concerning future supplies and sales of rice locally is considered decidedly unfavourable to both dealers and consumers who have openly expressed a nervousness as to the future.

Recently market prices of rice have soared to unprecedented heights as holders of rice are reported to be clinging tenaciously to their stocks. Reasons advanced for this situation may be said to be (a) owing to the tense political situation existing in the Far East which fact is effecting sources of supply to Shanghai and (b) increase in C. I. F. owing to limited space on the few ships now transporting cargo to Shanghai.

Regarding sales of foreign rice no sales have been made in the Rice Market, 515 Foochow Road, during the past few days, owing to the holders being unwilling to dispose of their stocks at prices fixed by the Rice Price Adjustment Committee, which were approved by the S.M.C. However, black market dealings are reported to have been secretly made between dealers both inside and outside the market, at prices ranging from $8 to $10 a sar above the fixed prices. Sir,

The Council's Supplies Sub-Committee, which advises the Council on food matters, has suggested to the Council that in order to prevent profiteering, speculation and hoarding of rice, certain measures of control should be introduced by Members of the Rice Market. The measures of control which the Council suggests should be given a trial are as follows:-

(1) That it be made obligatory for all wholesale dealers in rice to be members of the Market.

(2) That registration be made in the Market of all reputable rice brokers and provision be made by the said broker for a suitable guarantee to be furnished, such guarantee to be satisfactory to the Rice Guild.

(3) That it be obligatory for all merchants to write down all sales in their books as also on vouchers. When a transaction is concluded triplicate bills must be furnished, one to be given to the buyer, one to the market management and the third to be retained by the seller. Such bills should clearly state the price, quantity, quality, name and address of buyer and seller. Books, vouchers and the bills to be open for inspection by Officers of the Council whenever required.

(4) That communication in the market of all the local wholesale rice transactions be compulsory and the maintenance of the present minimum proportion of ten bags of rice at a time be enforced. That a deposit of $5 per bag be required on each transaction being completed and the delivery of delivery of coupons within 7 days of completion of transaction to be strictly enforced, failing which the deposit shall be forfeited.

负责就食品事务向工部局提供建议的工部局供应小组委员会已向工部局建议，为防止大米方面的牟取暴利、投机和囤积居奇，米市场成员应实施某些管制措施。工部局建议试行以下管制措施：

(1) 强制所有大米批发商成为市场会员。

(2) 在市场登记所有信誉良好的大米掮客，并由该掮客提供适当的担保，该担保须令米业公会满意。

(3) 强制所有商人在账簿及凭证上记录所有销售情况。交易达成时，必须提供一式三份的账单，一份给买方，一份给市场管理处，第三份由卖方留存。此类账单应清楚注明价格、数量、质量、买卖双方的姓名和地址。账簿、凭证和账单须在工部局官员要求时供其检查。

(4) 强制通报市场内所有本地大米批发交易，并强制执行目前每次至少十袋大米的最低比例规定。每笔交易完成后需缴纳每袋5美元的押金，并严格执行在交易完成后7天内交付提货单的规定，否则押金将被没收。

由公会指定一家认可银行收取每袋5美元的押金，并在工部局官员要求时出具此类押金的收据以供检查。

（批注：日期 1941年2月6日 m）

rice has been sold at an average price of $80.90 per bag of
224 lbs. On the 15th inst., 3,000 tons of No. 1 Saigon rice
was sold at an average price of $93.50 per bag of 224 lbs.
which means that the cost per zah would be $73.46. Adding
10% would mean that the rice should be resold at a price
not exceeding $81.00 per zah.

I do not know what your views are but I do think
the Rice Fixing Committee should be communicated with and
requested to reduce the present rates at which the rice is
being sold on the rice market.

With kindest regards,

Yours sincerely,

Leslie W. Hutten.

Translation of letter to Council from
the Rice Price Fixing Committee
Dated 9th January, 1941.
Address: No.15 Avenue Edward VII.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 14 JAN. 1941）

Rice Market; Brokers permitted to return

On the 8th instant we called a meeting to re-adjust the prices of foreign rice; the price list is enclosed herewith. We beg to state also that in compliance with the Council's decisions we resolved on 24th December last year to temporarily refuse admittance to rice brokers into the market for two weeks from 26th December. We have now received a letter from the Rice Brokers' Association (社誼聯客捐糧米) as follows:-

"As the time limit prescribed by your Committee has now expired, we beg to request you to permit us to re-enter the market to resume business and make our living. To prevent malpractices the regulations governing rice brokers have been revised. From now on all transactions will be made according to fixed prices. Should any seller charge a price exceeding the fixed limit, the broker concerned must strongly object, or be disqualified at once."

The matter was brought up for discussion, and it was decided that in view of the real hardships on the brokers they should be permitted temporarily to enter the market and resume their business as from the 9th instant. The effect of this step will be observed; should a broker in future commit any irregularity, he will be immediately stopped from carrying on his business and summarily expelled from the market. This resolution is on record.

Apart from notifying the public, the Council is hereby

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL TREASURER'S OFFICE）

Rice Prices
Soar Beyond
Official Limits

Quotations for rice on the local
rice market soared again yesterday
when all official limits fixed by the,
S.M.C. and the Price Fixing Com-
mittee of Shanghai Bean and Rice
Guild were shattered by dealers
here.
Top-grade Saigon rice sold for as
much as $92 per shéh although the
maximum price for this grain fixed
by the committee is only $87. A
corresponding increase was also
noted for other grades of Saigon
rice.
Buyers were reported to have
complained to police authorities
that even though the official limits
were observed at some local rice
houses, these establishments had
been selling second grade Saigon
Rice for first grade.
Meanwhile, Shanghai is all "set"
for the establishment of a public
granary which was approved at a
meeting of the Shanghai Municipal
Council. Members of the committee
in charge of organization include
Messrs. Yu Ya-ching, T. K. Ho and
Wang Yu-ching.
In the granary will be stored
200,000 bags of Saigon rice which
will be bought with funds supplied
by various business organisations
and individuals. Mr. Yu has pledg-
ed to supply 30,000 bags of the
grain for storage.

米价
飙升超出
官方限价

昨日本地米市的米价报价再次飙升，这里的经销商打破了工部局和上海豆米业公会价格核定委员会制定的所有官方限价。
尽管委员会规定的该品种最高价格仅为87元，但顶级西贡米的售价高达每石92元。其他等级的西贡米也出现了相应的涨幅。
据报道，买家向警方投诉称，尽管一些本地米行遵守了官方限价，但这些店铺一直将二等西贡米当作一等米出售。
与此同时，上海正“准备”建立公共粮仓，该计划已在上海公共租界工部局会议上获得批准。负责组织委员会的成员包括虞洽卿、何德奎和王玉庆先生。
粮仓将储存20万袋西贡米，资金由各类商业组织和个人提供。虞先生已承诺提供3万袋粮食用于储存。

Date August 29, 19 40.

Subject Rice Situation - increase in prices this morning.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

The prices of rice showed a further increase
this morning at the rice market, 315 Foochow Road,
despite the maximum prices fixed by the Rice Price
Adjustment Committee of the Bean and Rice Hong Owners'
Guild. The price of first quality Saigon rice
reached $61.00 per "zar", i.e. $1.50 in excess of the
stipulated price of $59.50 per "zar". The increase
is attributed to uneasiness due to the situation in
Indo-China.

In consequence of the increase in the
price of rice, the Market closed at 11 a.m., August 29,
instead of the scheduled time at 12 noon.

The Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Guild is
convening an urgent meeting for 3 p.m. to-day,
August 29, in its office, 15 Avenue Edward VII, in
order to discuss the situation.

Logan

Subject Increase in the price of rice.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Following the issue of a proclamation on
December 10, 1939, by the Shanghai Municipal Council
and the French Municipal Council prohibiting rice
hoarding, speculation and profiteering, and the
subsequent punishment of dealers guilty of selling rice
at a price in excess of the limit fixed by the Bean and
Rice Hong Owners' Guild, the price of the commodity
remained steady for some time.

On January 18, 1940, the price of Saigon rice
began an upward trend due to the unfavourable fluctuation
in exchange and the fact that prices in the producing
areas and also freight charges are quoted in U.S.
currency. On February 14 Volkart Brothers, 34 Avenue
Edward VII, and Kian Gwan Co., 110 Hamilton House, the
principal importers of foreign rice, quoted $57.50 and
$55.50 per bag for 1st and 2nd quality Saigon rice for
new orders, (i.e. $46.00 and $44.60 per "cwt"
respectively).

Taking advantage of the increased price set
for new orders, holders of Saigon rice already stored in
Shanghai raised the price of their stocks. When the
Rice Market, 515 Foochow Road, opened on February 13,
after having been closed for nine days for the Spring
Festival holidays, an increase of $6.00 was registered.

28th July 1939.

Sir Robert Calder-Marshall,
Chairman,
S.M.C. Sub Committee Food Supplies.
c/o Messrs. Calder-Marshall & Co.Ltd.
Glen Building.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir Robert,

I see from this morning's "The Credit Men's Economic
Bulletin", Vol. I, No. 144, page I, that the S.M.C. and the F.M.C. :-

"are determined to eradicate all speculative activities in
the local rice market, it was reported yesterday. In
pursuance of this policy they will shortly carry out a
thorough investigation of the rice stocks in the local
godowns and the names of their owners, and will request
the banks to strictly reduce their grant of mortgage loans
on rice.
"In connection with rumours that the authorities will extend
the restricted price of $20 per picul for white rice and
$16 per picul for provincial rice, these were reported to
have been denied."

and on page 10, of the same bulletin, under heading "Trading at standstill
they state that:-

"Sellers were all holding off from the market and only small
amounts of poor quality cereals were transacted at the price
of $20. It was reported that owing to the restrictions
enforced here, interior merchants were shipping their produce
to other markets, and as a result only a total of about
1,400 bags arrived during the day."

At one of our meetings I mentioned that one of the results of
price fixing would be "that rice shops would mix in more of the poorer
quality". This has occurred and at the present higher prices it is only
the lower grades which are available; for the higher grades the buyers
have to pay much higher prices.

尊敬的罗伯特爵士，

我从今早的《债权人经济公报》(The Credit Men's Economic Bulletin) 第一卷第144期第I页看到，工部局 (S.M.C.) 和公董局 (F.M.C.) ：

“据昨日报道，决心根除当地大米市场的所有投机活动。为执行这一政策，他们不久将对当地仓库中的大米库存及其所有者姓名进行彻底调查，并将要求银行严格减少以大米的抵押贷款发放。
“关于当局将把白米每担20元和省米每担16元的限价延期的传闻，据报道已被否认。”

在同一公报的第10页，“交易停滞”标题下，他们指出：

“卖家都持币观望，远离市场，只有少量劣质谷物以20元的价格成交。据报道，由于此处实施的管制，内地商人正将其产品运往其他市场，结果当天仅到货约1,400袋。”

在我们的一次会议上，我曾提到限价的后果之一是“米店会掺入更多劣质米”。这种情况已经发生，在目前较高的价格下，只有低等级大米有售；对于高等级大米，买家必须支付高得多的价格。

Date Nov. 20, 1937.
Subject Practice of rice shopkeepers in underweighing rice.
Made by C.D.I. Shih Tse-ling. Forwarded to /

Owing to the shortage of rice stocks and the
extremely pressing demand for this commodity, local rice
shops have resorted to limit the quantity of rice to be
sold to each person to that obtainable for $1.00. The
price mutually agreed upon between the rice shop owners
and the authorities is 9 cents per "sai-chin" (市斤),
or 1 1/9 lb. which is equivalent to $17.68 per bag of 220 lbs.
Only at this price a bag of rice yields very little profit
to the shop keeper, as the wholesale price for which he
purchases is $17.74 per bag. It has always been the
practice amongst shopkeepers, when a shortage existed, to
underweigh the quantity of rice sold to each buyer. This
malpractice is known to almost every Chinese. None,
however, has dared raising an objection for fear of
retaliation by the shopkeeper who would refuse further
supplies to anyone lodging such a complaint.

C.D.I.

Lih Pao publishes the following letter :- 19... ( ... )

Abuse by A Rice Shop

"Mr. Liao Liao ( 了 了 ),
    "Following the fall of Nentao, the Special Districts
in Shanghai became isolated. Owing to difficulties of
transportation, the residents, most of whom belong to
the poorer class of people, are faced with a shortage of
food supplies. Shanghai is not actually short of rice
for a great quantity has been purchased by the wealthy
for storage. Most of the rice shops have sold out their
stocks, but some are hoarding to make an extra profit.
    "I was delighted to read a report appearing in
local newspapers on November 13 to the effect that there
is no fear of a shortage of food supplies, as the S.M.C.
is distributing its stocks amongst the local rice shops
for retail to poor people at the price of $0.09 per
catty. This is indeed a very generous act on the part
of the S.M.C. and the Rice Shop Owners' Association.
However, unless the proprietors of rice shops give some
consideration to the hardships of the poor people and
continue to handle the small sales of one to two catties,
the poor people will be unable to obtain supplies.
    "It is a good measure to limit the sales
to $1 per person, but unfortunately it does not prevent
rich people from purchasing large quantities. Some doors
away from my home on ---- Road, there is a rice shop
whose back door lies in a narrow alleyway. The other
day the proprietor of this shop secured a number of bags
of rice from the S.M.C. and stated that it would be sold
to poor people only. Actually, he sold a large quantity
of the rice to certain wealthy families. To a certain
rent collecting agent and a rich family, he sold 11 bags
of rice. On the other hand, only three bags of rice
were sold to poor people over the counter during the
whole day.
    "In view of this, it is to be hoped that the
authorities will adopt appropriate measures to put a
stop to such evil practices.
                                "Bah Ting ( 白 丁 )."

米店之恶行

“了了先生：
    “南市沦陷后，上海特别区成为孤岛。由于交通困难，居民（大多属于贫苦阶层）面临粮食短缺的困境。上海实际上并不缺米，因为大量大米已被富人购入囤积。大多数米店已售罄库存，但有些米店为了获取额外利润而囤积居奇。
    “我很高兴读到11月13日当地报纸上的一篇报道，称不必担心粮食短缺，因为工部局正将其库存分配给当地米店，以每斤0.09元的价格向穷人零售。这确实是工部局和米业同业公会的一项非常慷慨的举措。然而，除非米店店主体谅穷人的疾苦，继续办理一两斤的小额销售，否则穷人将无法获得供应。
    “限制每人购买金额为1元是一项好措施，但不幸的是，这并不能阻止富人购买大量大米。在我家附近的----路，有一家米店，其后门位于一条狭窄的小巷中。前几天，该店店主从工部局获得数袋大米，并声称只卖给穷人。实际上，他将大量大米卖给了某些富裕家庭。他向某位收租代理人和一个富裕家庭出售了11袋大米。另一方面，整天柜台前仅向穷人售出了三袋大米。
    “鉴于此，希望当局采取适当措施，制止此类恶劣行径。
                                “白丁。”

pages.en:
FOOD PROFITEERING

THE determination and speed shown by the Shanghai
Municipal Council in effecting measures to curb board
ing and profiteering in rice throughout the International
Settlement last week cannot fail to win the widespread ap-
proval of everyone in the city, with the possible exception
of the rapacious merchants concerned. While all forms of
profiteering are to be condemned in times of war—and this
practice appears to have been prevalent in every civilized
country during such times since the history was first record-
ed—that of reaping undue profits on food supplies is es-
pecially repugnant to all persons of humanitarian inclination.
Especially is such action deserving of severe measures of
regulation in China, where the great mass of people spend
such a large portion of their small income on food. At the
present time, with many heads of families out of work and
existing entirely on slim savings accounts, any increase
in the price of rice causes real distress and in many instan-
ces starvation.

Under the program instituted by the Council yester-
day some 50 rice shops in the Settlement will sell the grain
at nine cents per catty from stock supplied them by the
S.M.C. Precaution against hoarding on the part of the
public is taken by limiting individual purchases to $1. This
action is said to have been necessitated by the closing of
a large number of rice shops, apparently with the idea of
hoarding their stocks until the price had risen sufficiently
to give them a handsome profit.

Shanghai rice stocks at the present time are said to
total some 20,000 bags of 200 pounds each. A large ship-
ment, ordered from abroad, is expected to reach the city
this week, comprising 25,000 bags. The following week
three shipments are scheduled to arrive, which will increase
total stocks by some 115,000 bags. Shanghai is also said to
have large supplies of wheat and flour, there being more
than 500,000 bags of flour and 800,000 bags of wheat in
godowns. With each bag of wheat equal to three bags of
flour when milled, the total flour supply is around 2,900,000
bags.

While there is little possibility that the city as a whole
will starve from lack of supplies, there is the very real
danger that prices will be boosted so much the large section
of the Chinese population thrown out of employment by
the fortunes of war in this area will be unable to buy even
the barest necessary food supplies. A grave problem would
also arise as regards the feeding of tens of thousands of
homeless in refugee camps. Limited funds at best are
available for the continuance of these projects. If the rela-
tively few dollars available for this worthy work are greatly
reduced in purchasing power because of increased food costs,
then either more money must be raised (which is certain
to become increasingly difficult) or a great many people will
starve who would not otherwise face so unhappy a prospect.

（印：P.B. 1937）
（批：Dec. 23. Rice / D.B. S"）
pages.zh:
粮食投机牟利

上海公共租界工部局上周在实施遏制整个国际租界内大米囤积和投机牟利的措施方面所表现出的决心和速度，无疑会赢得全市各界的广泛赞同，可能除了那些贪婪的相关商人之外。虽然任何形式的投机牟利在战时都应受到谴责——而且自从有历史记录以来，这种做法在所有文明国家似乎都很普遍——但在粮食供应上获取不当利润的行为尤其令所有具有人道主义倾向的人感到厌恶。在中国，广大民众将微薄的收入中的很大一部分用于购买食物，因此这种行为尤其值得采取严厉的监管措施。目前，许多户主失业，完全依靠微薄的储蓄生活，任何大米价格的上涨都会造成真正的痛苦，在许多情况下甚至导致饥饿。

根据工部局昨天启动的计划，租界内约50家米店将以每斤9分钱的价格出售由工部局提供给它们的库存大米。通过将个人购买限额限制在1美元，采取了预防公众囤积的措施。据说，由于大量米店关闭，这一行动成为必要，这些米店显然是想囤积库存，直到价格涨到足以让他们获得丰厚利润为止。

据称，目前上海的大米库存总量约为20,000袋，每袋200磅。一批从国外订购的大宗货物预计将于本周抵达本市，共计25,000袋。下周计划有三批货物抵达，将使总库存增加约115,000袋。据说上海还有大量小麦和面粉储备，仓库中有超过500,000袋面粉和800,000袋小麦。由于每袋小麦磨制后可相当于三袋面粉，面粉总供应量约为2,900,000袋。

虽然整个城市因缺乏供应而挨饿的可能性很小，但确实存在极大的危险，即价格被推高太多，以至于该地区因战争命运而失业的大批中国人口甚至无法购买最基本的必要粮食。此外，关于难民营中数万无家可归者的供养问题也将成为一个严重的问题。用于维持这些项目的资金本就有限。如果用于这项有益工作的相对少量的美元因食品成本增加而购买力大幅下降，那么要么必须筹集更多资金（这肯定会变得越来越困难），否则许多原本不会面临如此不幸前景的人将会挨饿。

（印：P.B. 1937）
（批：12月23日。大米 / D.B. S"）

November 12, 1937. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

CHAMBER INSTRUCTS RICE HONGS TO REGULATE RICE PRICES :
COUNCILS ORDERING LARGE QUANTITIES OF FOREIGN RICE

Acting on instructions, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce is co-operating with local rice hongs to regulate food supplies in Shanghai. In addition to issuing a notice stating that the price of rice must not exceed $14 per picul, the Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Association and the Rice Shop Keepers' Association are making arrangements for the unloading of rice from boats along the wharves at Nantao. Meanwhile, schemes are being devised to send men to the interior to purchase and transport rice to Shanghai.

On November 11, all rice shops in the International Settlement and the French Concession limited sales to a single customer to only one dollar's worth of rice. Some rice shops have posted up notices stating that business was suspended for the time being owing to lack of stocks. The Yui Chen Tai (裕成泰) Rice Shop, Fukien Road, and the Van Chong (萬昌) Rice Shop, Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession, continued to sell rice yesterday for the convenience of poor people and the shops were very much crowded. Detectives and policemen were on duty in front of the shops to maintain peace and order. The price of flour has increased to $4.20 per bag.

Information secured from rice hongs shows that although stocks of rice now in Shanghai are not large, there are ample supplies of wheat and flour. Furthermore, flour mills have re-opened. The Settlement authorities have ordered large quantities of foreign rice from abroad. For this reason, there should be no fear for a shortage of foodstuffs in this locality.

The price of rice in this city was very confused yesterday. For the maintenance of the livelihood of the poor, the authorities of the Foreign Settlements are doing their best to enable rice boats to come into safety zones and have designated a certain number of places where rice at a cheap price may be obtained in quantities not exceeding $1.00 worth per customer.

Since the withdrawal of the Chinese armies, rice coming from Wusih and other places can find no way to reach this city. Even rice boats coming from Sungkiang cannot reach this port. Upon receipt of a report that some 15,000 piculs of rice from Kiangying could not be sent to this city owing to the war, the Kiangying Fellow Countrymen's Association yesterday sent representatives to call on the International Relief Committee to request it to make arrangements for the dispatch of this rice to Shanghai. The Committee has requested Father Jacquinot to negotiate with the French Municipal Council for protection for the transportation of rice to Shanghai. It is learned that the authorities of the Foreign Settlements are paying close attention to this question and will devise measures for the transportation of rice to Shanghai.

Prices of all foodstuffs in this locality are on the increase. Yesterday a dollar could buy only one catty and 7 ounces of pork. The prices of vegetables were raised by 30 to 40%. Quantities of foodstuffs in the markets yesterday were smaller than usual. Such conditions are only temporary and it is believed that the situation will become normal toward the end of this month.

1937年11月12日。晨间翻译。

《大公报》及其他当地报纸：-

商会指示米号 regulate 米价：
工部局订购大量外米

奉命行事，上海总商会正与当地米号合作，调节上海的粮食供应。除了发布通知规定米价不得超过每石14元外，豆米业同业公会和米业同业公会正在安排在南市码头卸载船运大米。同时，正在制定方案，派人前往内地采购并将大米运往上海。

11月11日，国际租界和法租界的所有米店限制每位顾客只能购买价值1元的大米。一些米店张贴告示，称因缺乏库存，暂时停业。福建路的裕成泰米店和法租界蒙太尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）的萬昌米店昨日继续出售大米，以方便穷人，店内拥挤不堪。侦探和警察在店前执勤，以维持治安。面粉价格已涨至每袋4.20元。

从米号获得的信息显示，虽然目前上海的大米库存不多，但小麦和面粉供应充足。此外，面粉厂已重新开工。租界当局已从国外订购了大量外米。因此，本地不必担心粮食短缺。

昨日本市米价非常混乱。为了维持穷人的生计，外国租界当局正尽力使运米船只进入安全区，并指定了一些地点，供人以低价购买大米，每位顾客限购价值不超过1.00元。

自中国军队撤退以来，来自无锡等地的大米无法运抵本市。甚至来自松江的运米船也无法到达本港。接到报告称，因战争原因，约15,000石来自江阴的大米无法运往本市后，江阴同乡会昨日派代表拜访国际救济委员会，请求其安排将此批大米运往上海。委员会已请求饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）与法公董局谈判，为运米至上海提供保护。据悉，外国租界当局正密切关注此事，并将制定措施将大米运往上海。

本地所有食品价格均在上涨。昨日一元钱只能买到一斤七两猪肉。蔬菜价格上涨了30%至40%。昨日市场上的食品数量少于往常。这种情况只是暂时的，相信月底情况将恢复正常。

Central China Daily News publishes the following article:

ACTION DESIRED AGAINST RISING PRICES OF FOODSTUFFS

During the past two days, the prices of
all kinds of foodstuffs have been rising. Most of the
articles affected are daily necessities. In some cases,
the prices have been raised two or three times in a day.
Some rice shops informed their customers that they
had sold out all their stocks.
Thus people who used to eat rice are now
taking to congee, while those who used to take congee
are going hungry.
In case of shortage of supplies, shops should
not raise the prices but should sell only limited quantities
of foodstuffs to each person. Actually, there should
be no anxiety over food supplies.
It is to be noted that the increasing prices
of daily necessities may affect the peace and order of the
Foreign Settlements. The Chinese Ratepayers' Associations
should pay attention to the matter and should make
arrangements with the Settlement authorities to take action
against all traitorous merchants who speculate in food
supplies or who manipulate the market.
pages.zh:
《华中日报》刊登如下文章：

要求对食品价格上涨采取行动

过去两天，各种食品价格一直在上涨。受影响的大多是日常必需品。在某些情况下，价格在一天内上涨了两三倍。一些米店告知顾客，他们的库存已全部售罄。
因此，过去吃米饭的人现在改喝粥，而过去喝粥的人则在挨饿。
如果在供应短缺的情况下，商店不应提高价格，而应只向每个人限量出售食品。实际上，不必对粮食供应感到焦虑。
值得注意的是，日常必需品价格的上涨可能会影响外国租界的治安秩序。华人纳税会应注意此事，并与租界当局做出安排，对所有投机粮食或操纵市场的奸商采取行动。

REPORT
Date November 10, 37

Subject.. Dung Sheng Tai Rice Shop, 585 Fokien Road - dispute with customer
over price of rice.

Made by D. I. Pan Lien-pih    Forwarded by. [Signature]

With reference to the attached newspaper translation
relating to a dispute between the Dung Sheng Tai Rice Shop
(鄧永泰), 585 Fokien Road, and a customer over the price of
rice, enquiries made by the staff of Section 1, Special Branch
ascertained the following:-

On October 28, 1937, a male Chinese approached the Dung
Sheng Tai Rice Shop at 585 Fokien Road and purchased a picul
of rice which the shop charged him $14 for, this being 40 cents
above that fixed by the Bureau of Social Affairs and the
Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee. This price
was charged by the shop because the customer demanded that he
be supplied with the best quality "Kan Mee" and stated he did
not want "Kan Mee" which had been mixed with another inferior
rice. That same afternoon this person made a report to the
Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee, Room 606,
the
Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII, to effect that the shop
in question was selling rice at prices higher than those
permitted by the authorities and produced the bill he received
from the shop as evidence. The Committee then submitted a
petition to the Shanghai Martial Law Commander's Headquarters
in connection with the matter, who later served a summons on Mr.
Dung Yuan Ding (鄧元庭), the owner of the shop, instructing
him to attend the Martial Law Commander's Headquarters for
interrogation in the afternoon of November 5. Upon receipt
of the summons, Mr. Dung approached Messrs. Koo Shing Ih (顧馨一)
Chairman of Rice Hong Owners' Association , and Wong Shiao-lai
(王曉籟), Chairman of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, for
advice in the matter and through their good offices, the matter
was finally settled. The Chinese Chamber of Commerce

主题.. 福建路585号邓永泰米店 - 因米价与顾客发生纠纷

制作人 D. I. 潘连璧    转呈人 [签名]

关于附件中有关福建路585号邓永泰米店与顾客因米价发生纠纷的报纸译文，经特务科第一股职员调查，查明如下：-

1937年10月28日，一名中国男子来到福建路585号邓永泰米店，购买了一石大米，店家向他收取14元，这比社会局和上海市政粮食调整委员会规定的价格高出40美分。店家收取此价格是因为顾客要求供应最好的“粘米”（Kan Mee），并表示不想要掺有其他劣质米的“粘米”。当天下午，此人向位于爱多亚路1454号浦东会馆606室的上海市政粮食调整委员会举报，称该店以高于当局允许的价格出售大米，并出示了从店里收到的账单作为证据。委员会随后就此事项向上海戒严司令总部提交请愿书，后者后来向店主邓元庭先生发出传票，指示他于11月5日下午前往戒严司令总部接受讯问。收到传票后，邓先生就此事项咨询了米业同业公会主席顾馨一先生和华商总会主席王晓籟先生，并通过他们的斡旋，此事最终得以解决。华商总会

National Herald and other local newspapers:

RICE SUPPLIES FOR SHANGHAI.

After the outbreak of hostilities in this locality,
the Bureau of Social Affairs, in co-operation with the rice
merchants' guild and other public bodies, formed the
Shanghai People's Food Adjustment Committee with the object
of bringing about a reduction in the price of rice and
devising ways and means for the transportation of rice
to Shanghai.
It is now learned that the Committee will be
dissolved as from to-day because it will not be able to
obtain supplies of rice from inland should an unexpected
change in the local situation take place. Plans for the
procuring of rice supplies from the interior will henceforth
be in the hands of the rice dealers themselves.

A complaint has been made to the Shanghai People's
Food Adjustment Committee to the effect that the Dung Zung
Tai Rice Shop, No. 585 Fokien Road, sold rice on
October 28 at $14 a picul, in violation of the order
which stipulated that the price of best quality rice must
not be more than $13.60 per picul. A receipt issued by
the shop in question was enclosed.
It is reported that the Commander of the Shanghai
Martial Law Enforcement will summon the proprietor of the
shop for interrogation.

《国民日报》及其他本地报纸：

上海的大米供应。

本地战事爆发后，社会局与米业公会及其他公共团体合作，成立了上海市民食粮调节委员会，旨在降低米价并筹划将大米运往上海的方法。
现获悉，鉴于若本地局势发生意外变化，该委员会将无法从内地获得大米供应，故决定自今日起解散。今后，从内地采购大米供应的计划将由米商自行负责。

有人向上海市民食粮调节委员会投诉，称福建路585号东众泰米店（Dung Zung Tai Rice Shop）于10月28日以每石14元的价格出售大米，违反了规定上等米价格不得超过每石13.60元的命令。随信附上了该店开具的收据一张。
据悉，上海戒严司令官将传唤该店店主进行讯问。

TO FACILITATE REPLY PLEASE QUOTE
THIS NUMBER........F.30/12..........
AND DO NOT DEAL WITH MORE THAN
ONE MATTER IN THE SAME LETTER

Council Chamber.

ADMINISTRATION BUILDING.

Shanghai, September 15, 1937.

Major K. M. Bourne,
Acting Commissioner of Police.

re: Market Price of Rice.

Sir,

I find the daily Police Reports on the rice situation very useful and interesting, but as the rice trade uses the "zar" which is a measure, like our bushel for wheat, and furthermore, as each quality has a different weight for the "zar", the present Police Reports giving prices "per picul" give figures which are really very vague.

Saigon Rice. Since the beginning of the troubles the Police Reports repeatedly quote values of "Saigon Rice" stocks of which - until the S.M.C. imported a rice reserve from Saigon - do not exist in the Shanghai market, excepting very small odd lots left over from imports of about a year ago. Actually the native rice market does not quote on Saigon rice but on SEE MEE (私米).

I have gone into this matter with rice hongs and shops and find that their prices are for the following:-

KAN MEE (梗米)

This is the best quality Chinese Rice of a bold large round grain.
A "zar" (石) is equivalent to 170 shih chin ( ) = ½ kilo each = 85 kilos or 187.36 lbs. Price C$ ______ per zar.

SEE MEE (私米)

As indicated by the name "SEE" it is a long thin grain and there are three grades of it in the market.

| I | II | III |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| "zar" eq. 170 shih chin | 167 shih chin | 162 Shih chin |
| eq. 85 kg. | 83½ kg. | 81 kg. |
| eq. 187.36 lbs. | 184 lbs. | 178½ lbs. |
| C$______ | C$______ | C$______ |

All prices are per "zar" of Rice WITHOUT Bags - value of Bags now about C$0.50 each.

You will see from the above that the only correct basis to quote prices is per "zar" and the reader is supposed to know the equivalent weight in pounds per "zar" of each particular quality.

It will hardly be necessary for the writer of the Police Reports to convert the values to the parity of our own standard picul of 133⅓ English lbs.

本编号........F.30/12..........
且同一封信中请勿处理
超过一件事项

议事厅。

行政大楼。

上海，1937年9月15日。

K. M. 伯恩少校（Major K. M. Bourne），
代理警务处处长。

事由：大米市场价格。

先生：

我发现警方关于大米情况的每日报告非常有用且有趣，但由于米业使用“石”（zar）作为计量单位，就像我们测量小麦用的蒲式耳一样，而且不同品质的米每“石”的重量也不同，因此目前警方报告中给出的“每担”价格数据实际上非常模糊。

西贡米。自骚乱开始以来，警方报告反复引用“西贡米”库存的价值，但在工部局从西贡进口储备米之前，上海市场上并不存在这种米，除了一年前进口遗留下来的极少量零星批次。实际上，本地米市报价的不是西贡米，而是私米（SEE MEE）。

我已就此事向米行和米店进行了调查，发现他们的价格针对的是以下品种：

梗米（KAN MEE）

这是品质最好的中国米，颗粒粗大圆润。
一“石”（zar）等于170市斤（ ）= 每斤½公斤 = 85公斤或187.36磅。价格：法币______每石。

私米（SEE MEE）

正如其名“私”所示，这是一种细长的米粒，市场上有三个等级。

| I | II | III |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| “石”等于170市斤 | 167市斤 | 162市斤 |
| 等于85公斤 | 83½公斤 | 81公斤 |
| 等于187.36磅 | 184磅 | 178½磅 |
| 法币______ | 法币______ | 法币______ |

所有价格均为每“石”大米不含袋子的价格——目前每个袋子的价值约为法币0.50元。

从上述内容可以看出，报价的唯一正确基础是每“石”，读者应知道每种特定品质每“石”对应的磅数重量。

警方报告的撰写者几乎无需将这些数值换算成我们标准的133⅓英磅担的平价。

S.1., Special Branch STATION. File No.................... Date April 29, 1941.
SUBJECT: Rice and Flour Situation
The rice situation in Shanghai remains unfavourable, in spite of the large stock of rice on hand and fresh supplies continuing to arrive. The market prices of rice have soared continuously during the past fortnight, as holders of rice are reported to be clinging tenaciously to their stocks, whilst the retailers and consumers show a keen demand for the cereal. This situation is due to the tense political situation existing in the Far East and the increase in freight charges for transportation of rice to Shanghai (the freight charge from Rangoon to Shanghai is said to be 200 shillings per ton as against 120 shillings per ton about a month ago.)
（批：Copy to Mr Obradell + Dr Pelham）

rice leaving Shanghai for the interior, chiefly from

Foreign rice imported into Shanghai during the first quarter of the year, according to Police estimates, totalled 57,000 tons. During the same period last year the figure was 144,000 tons. The off-take might be said to have been fairly steady, but stocks still appear to be under the mark.

As requested, we will revert to this matter in our next issue. It is, however, felt that any good purpose will be served by emphasising the fact that stocks of rice, according to Police estimates, fell to as low as 57,000 tons in February. Apart from the fact that the position would appear to be grossly exaggerated, such meagre stocks suggest what might be termed "a panic shortage" and would lead dealers and private households to hoard on a larger scale than ever before.

Yours faithfully,
FINANCE AND COMMERCE, LTD.
Editor O.T. Breakspear

根据警方估算，今年第一季度进口到上海的外国大米总量为57,000吨。去年同期的数字为144,000吨。可以说提货量相当稳定，但库存似乎仍然低于标准水平。

按照要求，我们将在下一期报告中再就此事项进行回复。然而，我们认为，强调这样一个事实会有益处的：根据警方估算，大米库存在2月份降至低至57,000吨。除了这一情况似乎被严重夸大之外，如此微薄的库存表明了一种可称为“恐慌性短缺”的状况，并将导致经销商和私人家庭以前所未有的规模进行囤积。

August 30, 1939.

RICE SITUATION DURING THE PAST THREE MONTHS

The following is a summary of the rice situation
during the past three months.
(1) Stocks, supplies and consumption:
At the beginning of June, 1939, a stock of approximately
800,000 "zars" was on hand in Shanghai, distributed among
various bank godowns, rice hongs and shops in the International
Settlement and French Concession, while the incoming supplies
amounted to an average of 7,000 "zars" per day. Owing to the
restrictions imposed by the Japanese authorities on June 10
on export of rice from a number of rice producing areas in
Kiangsu (referred to in following paragraphs), the incoming
supply during the latter part of June was reduced to an
average of 4,200 "zars" per day. In consequence of the
small supplies, the stock on hand dropped to 625,000 "zars"
by the end of June (a reduction of 125,000 "zars"). The rate
of consumption was approximately 10,000 "zars" a day.
During July, supplies from the interior remained at
an average of 4,000 "zars" per day, but the rate of consumption
was increased to 14,000 "zars" per day. This increase was
brought about by the dealers in Hangchow and Shiashih, who
purchased more than 50,000 "zars" of rice in Shanghai and
transported same to the districts mentioned, during the
early part of July, as well as by the people in the suburbs
of Shanghai who bought stocks from the Settlement. As a
result, a further drop of 300,000 "zars" was registered in
local stocks and by the end of July, approximately 320,000
"zars" were on hand.
In August, the daily supply from the interior was
reduced to 3,000 "zars" a day, owing to the ban on export of
rice from Wuhu in July (referred to in following paragraphs).
However, towards the end of August the city authorities, in view
of the high prices prevailing in the local market, encouraged

过去三个月的米粮状况

以下是过去三个月米粮状况的摘要。
(1) 库存、供应和消费：
1939年6月初，上海手头约有800,000“石”的库存，分布在国际租界和法租界的各银行仓库、米行和店铺中，而 incoming supplies（入境供应）平均每天为7,000“石”。由于日本当局于6月10日对江苏（下文段落提及）多个产米区的大米出口实施限制，6月下旬的入境供应减少至平均每天4,200“石”。由于供应量少，到6月底手头库存降至625,000“石”（减少了125,000“石”）。消耗率约为每天10,000“石”。
7月份，来自内地的供应保持在平均每天4,000“石”，但消耗率增加到每天14,000“石”。这一增加是由杭州和嘉兴的商人造成的，他们在7月上旬在上海购买了超过50,000“石”的大米并运往上述地区，同时也因为上海市郊居民从租界购买库存。结果，本地库存进一步下降了300,000“石”，到7月底，手头约有320,000“石”。
8月份，由于7月份芜湖禁止大米出口（下文段落提及），来自内地的日供应量减少到每天3,000“石”。然而，到了8月底，鉴于当地市场价格高企，市政当局鼓励

by every means to transport rice to Shanghai, with the
result that recent arrivals show a slight increase when
compared with those of a short time ago. (The average
arrivals between August 25 and 29, 1939, amounted to 6,900
"zars" daily).

The stock of rice on August 29 was approximately
58,500 "zars", showing a reduction of 273,000 "zars" when
compared with that held at the end of July, 1939.

In addition to the regular weekly stock taking by
the Bean and Rice Dealers' Guild, 15 Avenue Edward VII,
the Shanghai Municipal Council on July 31 made an investiga-
tion into the stocks held in godowns in the Settlement and
French Concession. This investigation was carried out with
the assistance of the managements of the various godowns, who
were requested to report to the Council the quantity of rice
in their respective godowns on July 31. These reports show
a stock of 166,328 bags or approximately 232,000 "zars".

(2) Interference with supplies by Japanese:

At the beginning of June, 1939, daily arrivals of rice
in Shanghai from Quinsan, Soochow, Sungkiang and Wuhu areas
averaged approximately 7,000 "zars". About June 10, 1939,
the Japanese authorities prohibited the export of rice from
Soochow, Quinsan and Changchow areas, declaring that the
rice in those areas should be reserved for their local consump-
tion, with the result that supplies brought to Shanghai dropped
to an average of approximately 4,200 "zars" daily. Since
then, the principal sources of supply for Shanghai have been
Wuhu and Sungkiang areas.

On or about June 20, 1939, interference with the
arrival of supplies from Sungkiang commenced, when some
thirty rice boats carrying approximately 5,000 "zars" bound
for Shanghai were held up in the vicinity of Sungkiang. The
pages.zh:
- 2 -

通过各种手段将大米运往上海，结果是最近的到达量与不久前相比略有增加。（1939年8月25日至29日的平均到达量为每天6,900“石”）。

8月29日的大米库存约为58,500“石”，与1939年7月底持有的库存相比，减少了273,000“石”。

除了爱多亚路15号豆米业公会进行的常规每周库存盘点外，上海工部局于7月31日对租界和法租界仓库中的库存进行了调查。这项调查是在各仓库管理方的协助下进行的，他们被要求向工部局报告7月31日各自仓库中的大米数量。这些报告显示库存为166,328袋或约232,000“石”。

(2) 日本人对供应的干扰：

1939年6月初，来自昆山、苏州、松江和芜湖地区的大米日均到达上海量约为7,000“石”。1939年6月10日左右，日本当局禁止从苏州、昆山和常州地区出口大米，宣称这些地区的大米应保留供当地消费，导致运往上海的供应量降至平均每天约4,200“石”。此后，上海的主要供应来源是芜湖和松江地区。

1939年6月20日左右，来自松江的供应到达开始受到干扰，当时约三十艘载有约5,000“石”大米、驶往上海的米船在松江附近被扣留。这些

pages.en:
- 3 -

boats were however later released through private arrangements with the authorities concerned and arrived in Shanghai on July 3.

On July 3, the authorities in Wuhu discontinued the issue of transportation passes for the export of rice to Shanghai, but consignments continued to arrive here by means of passes already issued, and made valid until the end of July.

In spite of this restriction, occasional small consignments arrived here from Wuhu during August, dependent upon the persons handling the transportation. However, some 60,000 bags of rice (See Mee) purchased by local dealers, in Wuhu at the end of July, failed to reach here. As a result of this, the daily arrival of supplies to Shanghai was reduced to some 3,000 "zars".

The following are instances in which the transportation of rice to Shanghai has been interfered with by the Japanese authorities :-

On August 16, 700 bags of "See Mee" arrived at the Shanghai North Railway Station by rail from Wuhu via Nanking. The consignees, who went to the North Station to take delivery of the cargo, were warned by the Japanese authorities against transporting the rice into the Settlement south of the Creek. Consequently the rice was removed to the Hongkew area (definite address unknown).

On August 22, fifteen rice boats, arriving from the Tsingpu area via the Soochow Creek, were held up by the Japanese Naval Landing Party authorities at the Toyoda Cotton Mill, 200 Jessfield Road, O.O.L. 2,200 "zars" of rice on these boats were later released and brought into the Settlement on August 25, after the dealers agreed to sell the remaining 2,200 "zars" on the same boats to the populace in the Western District outside the perimeter at a price of
pages.zh:
- 3 -

船只后来通过与有关当局的私下安排获释，并于7月3日抵达上海。

7月3日，芜湖当局停止签发向上海出口大米的运输通行证，但凭借已签发且有效期至7月底的通行证，货物继续运抵此处。

尽管有此限制，8月份仍有零星的小批货物从芜湖运抵此处，这取决于负责运输的人员。然而，本地商人在7月底于芜湖购买的约60,000袋大米（See Mee，音译：细米）未能运抵此处。因此，运抵上海的日供应量减少到约3,000“石”。

以下是日本当局干扰大米运往上海的实例：

8月16日，700袋“See Mee”（音译：细米）经南京由铁路从芜湖抵达上海北站。前往北站提货的收货人被日本当局警告，不得将大米运入苏州河以南的租界。因此，大米被移至虹口地区（具体地址不详）。

8月22日，十五艘经苏州河从青浦地区抵达的米船，在极司菲尔路200号丰田棉纺厂被日本海军陆战队当局扣留。这些船上的2,200“石”大米后来获释，并在商人同意以每

pages.en:
- 4 -

$23.00 per "zar".

On the afternoon of August 25, seventeen boats,
carrying approximately 3,400 "zars" of rice, were held up
by the Japanese authorities at Yang Ka Doo, Pootung, while
proceeding to the Settlement. The Japanese authorities
demanded that the rice be sold to the populace at Yang Ka
Doo at a moderate price, while negotiations for the release
of the boats were in progress.

On the morning of August 26, 850 bags of rice arrived
at the Shanghai North Station by rail from Fengking and
Kashan, but were prevented by the Japanese military from
being transported into the Settlement. The rice was later
released and brought into the Settlement on August 28,
after the holders had sold 80 bags of rice at $20.00 per
"zar" to the Japanese.

(3) Council's action in connection with the rice situation.

Owing to the drop in supplies from the interior
following the ban on export of rice from Soochow and Quinsan
areas on about June 10, 1939, the price of rice in the local
market began to show an increase on June 12, 1939. The
increase continued and in view of this, a conference was
held on June 22 between the principal members of the Bean
and Rice Hong Owners' Guild, 15 Avenue Edward VII, and the
municipal authorities of the foreign settlements. As a
result of this meeting, a price limit of $21.00 per "zar"
for "Kan Mee" and $17.00 per "zar" for "See Mee" was
instituted with effect from June 23, 1939. The price limit
was reduced by $1 on July 17, when dealers endeavoured to
dispose of stocks owing to the hot and damp weather.

In order to ascertain whether or not the dealers
observed the price limit, a police officer has been posted at
the Rice Market, Tsing Lien Kah Teashop, 815 Foochow Road,
since June 23, 1939. The rice market which was established
pages.zh:
- 4 -

“石”23.00美元的价格将同船剩余的2,200“石”大米出售给外围西区民众后，于8月25日运入租界。

8月25日下午，十七艘载有约3,400“石”大米的船只在前往租界途中，在浦东杨家渡被日本当局扣留。在就释放船只进行谈判期间，日本当局要求以适中价格将大米卖给杨家渡的民众。

8月26日上午，850袋大米由铁路从奉庆（音译）和嘉善（音译：Kashan疑为Kashing即嘉兴之误，此处依原文音译或保留不确定地名，根据上下文Kashan极可能指嘉兴，但遵循规则4，若不确定则保留原文或音译，此处Kashan对应嘉兴可能性极大，但前文已有Shiashih/嘉兴? 不，前文是Hangchow and Shiashih，Shiashih通常指嘉兴。此处Kashan可能是OCR错误或另一地名。鉴于规则3，能确定的用通行中文，Kashan若指嘉兴则应用嘉兴，但拼写差异较大。暂按音译处理或标注不清。考虑到前文有Shiashih，此处Kashan可能是OCR识别错误，实为Kashing。但规则4要求照实译出或标原文不清。此处译为“奉庆和嘉善（音译）”较为稳妥，或者如果Kashan确认为嘉兴，则用嘉兴。历史地理上Fengking可能是奉贤？Kashan可能是嘉兴。此处保守翻译为音译并注明。）运抵上海北站，但被日军阻止运入租界。这批大米后来获释，并在持有人以每“石”20.00美元的价格向日本人出售了80袋大米后，于8月28日运入租界。

(3) 工部局针对米粮状况采取的行动。

由于1939年6月10日左右禁止从苏州和昆山地区出口大米，导致来自内地的供应下降，当地市场的大米价格于1939年6月12日开始上涨。价格上涨持续，鉴于此，6月22日，爱多亚路15号豆米业公会的主要成员与外国租界的市政当局举行了会议。会议结果是，自1939年6月23日起，对“Kan Mee”（音译：粳米）实行每“石”21.00美元的限价，对“See Mee”（音译：细米）实行每“石”17.00美元的限价。7月17日，由于商人试图因炎热潮湿的天气处理库存，限价下调了1美元。

为了查明商人是否遵守限价，自1939年6月23日以来，一名警官一直驻守在福州路815号清莲阁茶楼的米市场。该米市场建立于

pages.en:
- 5 -

in January, 1938, is actually only a meeting place for
dealers, instituted to facilitate transactions, but has no
control although having a board of management.
On or about July 20, the rate of foreign exchange
decreased considerably and prices of various commodities
increased. The dealers, taking advantage of this change,
coupled with the gradual diminution of local stocks and
reduced supplies from the interior, raised the prices of
rice to above the price limit. Owing to observation by
the police, the dealers resorted to doing business in a
secret manner without the knowledge of the police and even
conducted business at places outside the market.
On July 26, 1939, Wong Ngoeh Sung ( 王玉生 ),
employee of the Kiu Dah ( 久大 ) Rice Shop, 780 Rue
Ratard, was discovered doing business in this manner. The
matter was referred to the French Police and the management
of the shop punished accordingly.
On August 4, two rice brokers were accused by two
other brokers of transacting business at the Rice Market
at prices above the limit. Subsequent enquiries into the
case failed to reveal any evidence, but it was believed
that the allegation was made for personal spite, occasioned
by a private grudge. No punishment was meted out in this
case.
On August 17, affairs at the Rice Market were in a
state of confusion owing to the dealers demanding excessive
prices, disregarding the price limit and watch by the
police. The management decided to close for three days
between August 18 and 20. The market resumed operations
on August 21 without any improvement in the situation, the
price continuing to increase until August 23, when a maximum
price of $42.00 was registered. After that date, the price
gradually decreased owing to small demand and slightly
pages.zh:
- 5 -

1938年1月，[该市场]实际上只是为便利交易而设立的商人聚会场所，虽设有管理委员会，但并无管控权。
7月20日左右，外汇汇率大幅下跌，各类商品价格上涨。米商利用这一变化，加之本地库存逐渐减少及内地供应缩减，将米价抬高至限价以上。由于警方监视，米商转而采取秘密方式进行交易，避开警方耳目，甚至在市场以外的地点进行交易。
1939年7月26日，久大（Kiu Dah）米号（位于拉塔德路780号）雇员王玉生（Wong Ngoeh Sung）被发现以这种方式进行交易。此事已移交法租界巡捕房处理，该米号管理层受到相应处罚。
8月4日，两名米经纪被另外两名经纪指控在米市以超过限价的价格进行交易。随后对该案的调查未能发现任何证据，但据信该指控是出于私人恩怨引发的个人报复。此案未予处罚。
8月17日，由于米商索要高价，无视限价及警方监管，米市事务陷入混乱状态。管理方决定于8月18日至20日期间停业三天。8月21日市场恢复运营，但局势毫无改善，价格持续上涨，直至8月23日达到最高价42.00元。此后，由于需求微小且到货量略有

increased arrivals, and by August 30, a reduction of

(4) Importation of foreign rice:

Owing to the gradual reduction in the local stocks
and incoming supplies, various rice hongs in Shanghai placed
an order through Louis Dreyfus & Company, 181 Kiangse Road,
in May, 1939, for the importation of 20,000 bags of Saigon
Rice, but this order was later cancelled about June 10,
1939, in consequence of the fall in the rate of foreign
exchange. The proprietors of the rice hongs managed to
make a profit of $25,000 through the buying of foreign
exchange beforehand, this after defraying the necessary
expenses and commission due to the importing firm.

On June 28, 1939, another order for 6,000 bags of
Saigon Rice was placed by the Zung Feeng Rice Shop, 103
Sinsa Road, in conjunction with another rice shop. This
consignment arrived in Shanghai on July 21, 1939.

About the middle of August, 1939, when the rice
situation became serious, another order for 18,000 bags of
foreign rice from Saigon was placed through Mr. Yu Ya Ching
and is due to arrive here on September 8. 10,000 bags
of this consignment will be distributed to the Shanghai
pages.zh:

增加，价格逐渐回落，至8月30日，记录显示价格下降了6.00至8.00元。

过去三个月米价呈现上升趋势，价格对比如下：

(4) 外国大米进口：

由于本地库存和 incoming supplies（进货）逐渐减少，上海各家米行于1939年5月通过江西路181号的路易·德雷福斯公司（Louis Dreyfus & Company）下单，进口20,000袋西贡米，但该订单后因外汇汇率下跌，于1939年6月10日左右取消。米行老板通过预先购买外汇，在支付必要费用及应付给进口公司的佣金后，获利25,000元。

1939年6月28日，新沙路103号众丰（Zung Feeng）米号联合另一家米号再次订购6,000袋西贡米。该批货物于1939年7月21日抵达上海。

1939年8月中旬，当米荒形势变得严峻时，又通过虞洽卿（Yu Ya Ching）先生订购了18,000袋来自西贡的外国大米，预计将于9月8日抵达。该批货物中的10,000袋将分配给上海

pages.en:
- 7 -

Refugee Relief Association for the consumption of refugees
and the remaining 8,000 among Mr. William Gockson, General
Manager of the Wing On Cotton Mill, Mr. Wong Yu-ching,
Manager of Foh Sing Flour Mill, the Bean and Rice Dealers'
Guild and an unknown individual or concern. It is not yet
known as to how they will dispose of their portions of the
consignment.

Plans for further importation of foreign rice are
now being discussed by Messrs. Yu Ya Ching, Yulin Hsi and
several other prominent personalities in the rice trade.
Persons wishing to purchase foreign rice may register at
the office of the Shanghai Chartered Accountants' Associa-
tion, Room 405, Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII, but
their orders must be for 50 bags or more. When the demand
reaches a total of 10,000 bags, an order will be placed
with a foreign firm.

(5) Rice shops running out of stock and looting:

Owing to the inadequacy of stocks and excessive
prices demanded by wholesale dealers, local rice shops
have experienced difficulties lately in purchasing stocks.
Commencing from August 10, the shops limited their sales
to each customer at half a "zar" or even less, and a few
days later, a number of shops exhausted their stocks and
closed up.

On August 20, looting or attempted looting of rice
shops began. Since then, 18 cases have come to notice
in various parts of Shanghai. Of these cases, 8 occurred
in the International Settlement.

(6) Mayor Fu's action in connection with the rice situation.

On June 22, 1939, Fu Hsiao-an ( 傅筱庵 ), Mayor
of the Shanghai City Government, addressed a letter to the
Shanghai Municipal Council requesting the Council to
ascertain the quantities of rice stored in various godowns

难民救济协会，供难民消费，其余8,000袋则分配给永安棉纺厂总经理William Gockson（音译）先生、福新面粉厂经理王禹卿（Wong Yu-ching）先生、豆米业公会以及一个身份不明的个人或商行。目前尚不清楚他们将如何处置各自分得的那部分货物。

虞洽卿、奚玉林（Yulin Hsi，音译）及其他几位米业知名人士正在讨论进一步进口外国大米的计划。欲购买外国大米者可在爱多亚路1454号浦东同乡会405室上海会计师公会办公室登记，但订单数量必须在50袋或以上。当总需求量达到10,000袋时，将向一家外国公司下单。

(5) 米店缺货与抢米：

由于库存不足及批发商索要高价，本地米店最近在采购库存方面遇到困难。从8月10日开始，各店限制每位顾客购买半“石”或更少，几天后，多家米店库存耗尽并关门停业。

8月20日，开始发生针对米店的抢米或未遂抢米事件。自此以来，上海各地已发现18起此类案件。其中，8起发生在公共租界。

(6) 傅市长就米荒局势采取的行动。

1939年6月22日，上海特别市政府市长傅筱庵致函工部局，请求工部局查明租界内各仓库的大米储存量，并采取有效措施制止投机和囤积居奇，同时将米价限定为每“石”15元。信中还指出，市政府正采取措施促进大米从芜湖的运输，以缓解本地局势。

1939年6月30日，在极司菲尔路92号西区警察分局外张贴了一份市政府发布的公告，称已要求工部局和法公董局禁止以每“石”15.00元以上的价格出售大米。

1939年7月29日，在西区越界筑路区域发现了上海特别市政府社会局发布的另一份通知的副本。该通知重申了上述公告中傅市长的命令，将米价限制在15.00元。

1939年8月21日，傅市长再次致函工部局，声称米价上涨并非由于本地库存不足或进货稀缺，而是由不法商人和无情投机者的囤积居奇及操纵所致。在这封信中，傅市长强调，为了终结大米投机，应由新政权接管特区，这将使投机者受到法律制裁。

On June 30, 1939, a proclamation issued by the City

per "zar" was found posted outside the Western District

On July 29, 1939, copies of another notice issued
by the Bureau of Social Affairs of the Shanghai City
Government were found posted in the outside roads area
in the Western District. The notice reiterated the order
of Mayor Fu contained in the abovementioned proclamation,
limiting the price of rice at $15.00.

On August 21, 1939, Mayor Fu addressed another
letter to the Council alleging that the increase in the
prices of rice was not due to the inadequacy of local
stocks or the scarcity of incoming supplies, but was
brought about by the hoarding and manipulation of the
part of unscrupulous merchants and heartless speculators.
In this letter, Mayor Fu emphasized that, in order to put
an end to the speculation in rice, the special districts
should be taken over by the new regime, which would bring
the speculators to justice.

1939年8月10日。

罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士（Sir Robert Calder-Marshall），
工部局粮食供应小组委员会主席。
转交：R. Calder-Marshall & Co., Ltd. 公司
格兰大楼。
上海。

尊敬的罗伯特爵士：

关于我本月7日的去信，我在信中认为目前的大米库存足以维持50至60天，您将从本月8日的警务报告中注意到，根据他们掌握的信息，库存量远少于向我报告的数量，即总共约230,000石或袋，按每日最低消耗8,000袋计算，仅能维持约30天。如果我们考虑到在库存完全耗尽前的一两周，那么在严重危机必然爆发之前，最多只剩下两周时间。

我明确认为，包围上海并占领产米区的军事当局有一个明确的计划，旨在阻止物资进入这些地区，因此，继续与他们谈判以缓解局势是完全无用的。由于从西贡运来物资至少需要两周时间，我们没有时间继续这种自欺欺人的政策。作为工部局粮食供应小组委员会的成员，我深感有责任强调这一点。换句话说，如果要使本市免于食物骚乱和混乱——若无立即救济，这种局面必将在未来2或3周内开始——就必须立即采取直接和积极的行动。

面粉前景。- 根据8月4日的警务报告，当日上海机制面粉的库存约为1,100,000袋，小麦库存约为1,800,000担（@ 80公斤）。这批小麦磨成面粉后，将产出约2,000,000袋，因此我们可见的面粉总量约为3,800,000袋。

本地面粉价格目前约为每袋49磅规元6.80元，但小麦到达面粉厂的成本，加上汇率的进一步下跌，以及无法运入更多供应的事实，使得面粉厂有理由将价格提高至每袋规元8.00元，出于我的提案目的，我将采用此数字作为成本。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 11 AUG. 1939）
10th August 1939.

Sir Robert Calder-Marshall,
Chairman - S.M.C. Sub-Committee for Food Supplies.
c/o Messrs. R. Calder-Marshall & Co., Ltd.
Glen Building.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir Robert,

With reference to my letter of the 7th inst., wherein I thought that there is now sufficient stocks of rice for 50/60 days, you will note from the Police Report of the 8th inst. that, according to their information, the stocks are very much less than had been reported to me, viz. a total of about 230,000 sah or bags which, at a minimum of 8,000 bags per day, would last about 30 days. If we consider that a week or two before the stocks are completely exhausted there is, at the maximum, only about two weeks left before a serious crisis must begin.

I am definitely of the opinion that the Military Authorities surrounding Shanghai and in occupation of the rice producing areas have a definite plan to stop supplies coming into these areas and therefore it is quite useless to continue negotiating with them with a view to relieving the situation. As it requires a minimum of two weeks to get supplies up from Saigon there is no time left to continue in this policy of self-deception. As a member of the S.M.C. Sub-Committee for Food Supplies I feel very strongly that it is my duty to emphasise this point. In other words, direct and positive action must be taken at once if we are to save this city from food riots and chaos which must commence, if there is no immediate relief, within the next 2 or 3 weeks.

FLOUR AHEAD.- According to the Police reports of the 4th August the stock of Shanghai-milled flour on that date was about 1,100,000 bags, and the stock of wheat about 1,800,000 piculs (@ 80 kilos). This stock of wheat, when milled into flour, will produce about 2,000,000 bags, so that we have in sight about 3,800,000 bags of flour.

PRICE OF LOCAL FLOUR is now about G$6.80 per bag of 49 lbs., but the cost of the wheat to the mills, plus further drop in exchange, plus impossibility of bringing in further supplies, justifies the mills raising their prices to G$8.- per bag, and for the purpose of my proposal I will adopt this figure as the cost.

尊敬的罗伯特爵士：

关于我本月7日的去信，我在信中认为目前的稻米库存足以维持50至60天，但从本月8日的警务报告来看，据警方掌握的信息，库存量远少于向我汇报的数字，即总计约23万石（或袋），按每日最低消耗8,000袋计算，仅能维持约30天。如果我们考虑到在库存完全耗尽前的一两周，距离严重危机爆发最多只剩下两周时间。

我明确认为，包围上海并占领稻米产区的军事当局有着明确的计划，旨在阻止物资进入这些区域，因此继续与他们谈判以图缓解局势是毫无用处的。由于从西贡运来物资至少需要两周时间，我们已没有时间继续这种自欺欺人的政策了。作为工部局粮食供应小组委员会的一员，我深感有责任强调这一点。换言之，如果要使本市免于因粮食短缺而引发的骚乱和混乱——若无立即的救济措施，这种局面必将在未来两到三周内开始——就必须立即采取直接且积极的行动。

面粉前景。——根据8月4日的警务报告，当日上海本地加工面粉的库存约为110万袋，小麦库存约为180万担（每担80公斤）。这批小麦磨成面粉后，可产出约200万袋，因此我们可见的面粉总量约为380万袋。

本地面粉价格目前约为每袋（49磅）6.80元（大银元），但考虑到 mills（面粉厂）的小麦成本、汇率的进一步下跌以及无法运入更多补给的情况，面粉厂将价格提高至每袋8.00元（大银元）是合理的，出于我的提案目的，我将采用此数字作为成本。

pages.en:
Please note the following comparison between cost of rice and of
flour:-
RICE
C$23.- per zah 80 kilos or 176½ lbs. divided by 49 lbs. (the weight
per bag of flour) equals 3.6 times the weight of flour.
FLOUR
3 49 lbs. per bag @ C$6 X 3.6, to be equivalent weight of rice, equals
C$21.60, or about C$1.40 per bag (of rice) cheaper.

The making of the flour into bread will of course absorb this difference
so that allowing for rice at a dollar or so dearer than the present controlled
price and compared with flour at a slightly higher price than actual present
market price, the comparison is still in favour of flour.

For the average working-man in the streets, it would be possible to
mix in about 20% bran, making a very good wholesome bran-bread which would
be a great economy and at the same time an excellent food.

BAKERIES.- I have no figures as to the existing number of bakeries and
their capacities, but the Revenue Department, together with the Police, will
no doubt be able to give exact figures within the next few days. However,
for the purpose of my discussion we will assume that the existing bakeries
are able to bake enough for the requirements of 100,000 people, and as we
must foresee feeding 3 million inhabitants, 1 million of whom are able to
take care of themselves, the existing facilities for making bread must be
increased, let us say, 20 times.

This should not present any very great difficulties as with the large
number of Russian, Austrian and German refugees now in town, there must be
at least several hundred men who are experienced in this line of business.
In any event the experts available can train the new men very quickly.

BAKING OVENS.- No time must be lost by the two Councils to call together
the principal bakeries and get them to extend their plants as well as prepare
new ovens at convenient sites for efficient and quick distribution.

IMMEDIATE INTRODUCTION OF BREAD, ESPECIALLY BRAN-BREAD should be organ-
ized with the existing bakeries even on a small scale, and the rice shops be
induced (even compelled) to sell this bread. A programme of a fixed number
of loaves against each dollar of rice might easily be enforced as it would
work no hardship whatsoever on the people and at the same time make it
possible to extend the period before the present stock of rice is exhausted.

SHANGHAI MILLERS.- I am convinced that the two Groups of Mills, Foh Sing
and Foo Foong, can be relied on for full cooperation in this programme, even
to the extent of consigning the Flour to the two Councils for distribution
to the Bakeries, and any flour which is unused, when fears of any crisis
have passed and/or for other reasons, would be taken back by them at original
cost. It could be arranged that accounts be paid once a month as long as
these accounts are passed through the Council.

请注意以下大米与面粉成本的比较：-

大米
每担（zah）80公斤或176.5磅，计国币23元。除以49磅（每袋面粉的重量），等于面粉重量的3.6倍。

面粉
每袋49磅，单价国币6元 x 3.6（相当于同等重量的大米），等于国币21.60元，即每袋（大米）便宜约国币1.40元。

将面粉制成面包自然会吸收这一差价，因此，即使假设大米价格比目前的管制价格贵一元左右，并与比实际当前市场价格略高的面粉价格相比，比较结果仍然有利于面粉。

对于街头的普通工人来说，可以在面粉中混入约20%的麦麸，制成一种非常优质、健康的麦麸面包，这既大大节约成本，同时又是一种极好的食物。

面包房。- 我手头没有关于现有面包房数量及其产能的数据，但税务局会同警务处无疑能在未来几天内提供确切数字。然而，为了便于讨论，我们假设现有的面包房能够烘焙足够满足10万人需求的面包，鉴于我们必须预见要供养300万居民，其中100万人能够自给自足，现有的面包制作设施必须增加，比方说，增加20倍。

这应该不会带来任何非常大的困难，因为目前市内有大量的俄罗斯、奥地利和德国难民，其中至少有数百人拥有从事此行业的经验。无论如何，现有的专家可以非常快速地培训新人。

烤炉。- 两个公董局必须抓紧时间召集主要面包房，让他们扩大厂房，并在便于高效快速分销的地点准备新烤炉。

应立即着手组织现有面包房（即使是小规模地）引入面包，特别是麦麸面包，并诱导（甚至强制）米店销售这种面包。可以轻易实施一项计划，规定每购买一元钱的大米必须搭配固定数量的面包，因为这不会对民众造成任何困难，同时又能延长现有大米库存耗尽前的时间。

上海磨坊主。- 我深信，福新（Foh Sing）和阜丰（Foo Foong）这两大磨坊集团可以在此计划中给予充分合作，甚至可以将面粉委托给两个公董局分配给各面包房，而当任何危机恐慌过去和/或因其他原因导致面粉未使用时，他们将以原价收回。可以安排只要这些账目通过公董局结算，就每月支付一次款项。

LOUIS DREYFUS & CO.
P O BOX 667
SHANGHAI
- 3 -

Another very good effect of such a programme is that the parties
working against Shanghai would realise that we are not as vulnerable as
they believe, and if they are convinced of this point it is possible
that they may not continue their pressure or at least increase it.

I apologise for the length of this report, but if there are some
points which are not clear to you, or to those who read us in copy, I
shall be glad to answer any questions.

Yours very truly,
Arthur Eveleigh

路易·德雷福斯公司（LOUIS DREYFUS & CO.）
邮政信箱 667号
上海
- 3 -

此类计划的另一个非常好的效果是，那些与上海作对的一方会意识到我们并不像他们认为的那样脆弱，如果他们确信这一点，他们可能会停止施压，或者至少不再加剧压力。

我为本报告篇幅过长致歉，但如果有任何要点对您或收到副本的读者不清楚，我将乐意回答任何问题。

您忠实的，
阿瑟·伊夫利（Arthur Eveleigh）

Date August 7, 1939.

Subject Letter from L. Dreyfus & Company to the Chairman of the
S.M.C. Food Supplies Sub-Committee.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With reference to the attached copy of a
letter from Louis Dreyfus & Company to Sir Robert
Calder-Marshall, Chairman of the S.M.C. Food Supplies
Sub-Committee, in which it is mentioned that because
of the restrictions on the price of rice enforced
here, merchants in the interior were shipping their
produce to other markets resulting in only 1,400
bags arriving here daily; enquiries by this office
have failed to confirm this report although the
arrivals during the last week were actually smaller,
i.e. approximately 2,700 "zars" or 2,000 bags a day.
The drop in the arrivals is more or less seasonal
and is partly due to the decreased stocks in the
interior. The ban on export by the authorities in
certain rice producing districts is also a contributory
factor and recent supplies have principally come
from Sungkiang and the Wuhu areas.

It is said that the buying price in the
Sungkiang areas ranges from $15 to $16 per "zar"
and after adding transportation charges and other
expenses of about $3 per "zar", costs about $18 to
$19 which is $1 or $2 below the price limit. Wuhu
rice is bought at $12.50 to $13.50 per "zar" plus
transportation charges, etc. and costs $15.60 being
the maximum price and the price limit for this rice
is $16.00.

In view of the foregoing, the present price

关于附上的路易·德雷福斯公司致工部局食品供应小组委员会主席罗伯特·考尔德-马歇尔爵士（Sir Robert Calder-Marshall）信函副本，信中提及由于此处实施大米限价，内地商人将其产品运往其他市场，导致每日抵沪大米仅1,400袋；经本处调查，未能证实该报告，尽管上周的实际到货量确实较少，即每天约2,700“担”（zars）或2,000袋。到货量的下降大致具有季节性，部分原因是内地库存减少。某些产米区当局禁止出口也是一个促成因素，最近的供应主要来自松江和芜湖地区。

National Herald and other local newspapers:

FOOD SUPPLIES FOR SHANGHAI

Owing to the sudden change in the local war situation, it has become difficult to transport food into the Foreign Settlements, consequently the prices of food-stuffs in the Settlements have greatly increased. Some rice shops suspended business yesterday morning because they had sold all their stocks. It is said that the Settlement authorities have devised sound measures for the maintenance of food supplies.

Pork is now being sold at $1 for one catty and seven ounces. The price of vegetables has risen by 20% only because fairly abundant supplies are still coming in from Pootung. The prices of firewood, charcoal, coal and other fuel are also on the increase.

The following joint notice was issued by the Shanghai Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Association and the Rice Shop Owners' Association:-

"At this time of emergency, the maintenance of the people's food supplies is most important. All rice hongs and shops should sell their rice within the price limit of $14 per picul fixed by the former People's Food Adjustment Committee. Offenders against this order will be reported to the authorities for severe action."

It is said that investigations are being made by the authorities into certain cases wherein some rice shops are reported to have sold rice at more than $15 per picul.

A reporter of this paper was informed by Mr. Koo, a leading rice merchant, yesterday afternoon that there need be no anxiety over food supplies. Mr. Koo stated that there were 700,000 piculs of rice in stock in Shanghai and more supplies were coming. The reporter also interviewed many inland rice merchants and learned that 300,000 piculs of rice will be transported to Shanghai shortly.

The authorities of the International Settlement and the French Concession are also paying close attention to the question of rice supplies and are planning to purchase rice from Hongkong, Saigon and Siam.
pages.zh:
《国民日报》及其他本地报纸：

上海的粮食供应

由于本地战局突变，向外国租界运输粮食变得困难，因此租界内的食品价格大幅上涨。一些米店因售罄库存，于昨日上午停止营业。据悉，租界当局已制定健全的措施以维持粮食供应。

猪肉目前的售价为每斤七两1元。蔬菜价格仅上涨了20%，因为浦东仍有相当充足的供应运入。木柴、木炭、煤炭及其他燃料的价格也在上涨。

上海豆米行号同业公会和米业同业公会联合发布了以下通告：-

“在此紧急时刻，维持民众粮食供应最为重要。所有米行和米店应按前人民食粮调节委员会规定的每石14元的限价出售大米。违反此令者将报请当局严厉查处。”

据悉，当局正在调查某些案件，据报道有些米店以每石超过15元的价格出售大米。

本报记者从主要米商顾先生处获悉，昨日下午他表示无需对粮食供应感到焦虑。顾先生称，上海现有大米库存70万石，且更多供应正在途中。记者还采访了许多内地米商，得知将有30万石大米在短期内运抵上海。

国际租界和法租界当局也密切关注大米供应问题，并计划从香港、西贡和暹罗购买大米。

EXTRACT FROM INTELLIGENCE REPORT

November 11, 1937.

4,800 "zars" of rice ("Kan Mee") were unloaded
from the 40 boats berthed at Nantao on November 10 and
transported to shops in the Settlement and French
Concession.

On the early morning of November 10, approximately
150 boats carrying about 25,000 "zars" of "Kan Mee,"
arrived at Nantao from the vicinity of Sungkiang. These
boats have not yet been unloaded pending negotiations
with the Chinese military authorities in Nantao who
insist that the rice be stored in Nantao for the
consumption of the people in that district. To avoid
interference by the Chinese military, the rice dealers
are reported to have also negotiated with the French
Authorities for the unloading of the boats under the
protection of the French soldiers guarding the water
mains at Nantao. The French authorities agreed to the
proposal on condition that the rice be transported only
to the French Concession for sale.

The majority of rice shops in the Settlement were
closed this morning, November 11, but continued to sell
small quantities through shop windows.

Copy sent to Mr. T. W. Gubb
Deputy C. O. S. M. E.

1937年11月11日。

11月10日，停泊在南市的40艘船只卸下了4,800“担”大米（“粳米” Kan Mee），并运往租界和法租界的店铺。

11月10日凌晨，约150艘载有约25,000“担”“粳米”的船只从松江附近抵达南市。这些船只尚未卸货，正等待与南市的中国军事当局进行谈判，后者坚持要求将大米储存在南市以供该地区民众消费。为避免中国军队的干扰，据报道米商也与法国当局进行了谈判，请求在守卫南市直流水管的法国士兵保护下卸货。法国当局同意了该提议，条件是大米只能运往法租界销售。

租界内的大多数米店在今日（11月11日）上午关闭，但继续通过店铺窗口少量出售。

Rice

At 6.30 p.m. October 14, three representatives of the
Changshu Rice Dealers' Guild entertained 22 local Chinese
journalists to a tea party on the 6th floor, Pootung Guild,
1454 Avenue Edward VII, when the journalists were informed
of the unsuccessful attempts of the Rice Dealers' Guild to
obtain the release of 12 rice boats loaded with 2,500 "zars"
of "Ken Mee" which had been detained by the Changshu
Authorities since September 10. The journalists were further
informed that should the Changshu Authorities persist in their
present attitude, the Rice Dealers' Guild would have no
other recourse than to resort to the expedient of suspending
business as a counter-measure. The hosts then expressed the
hope that local Chinese newspaper circles would assist by
publishing unbiased views of the controversy in the local
press. The function terminated at 7.20 p.m.

5,000 "zars" of rice were transported to shops in the
Settlement and French Concession on October 14 from the
following places :-

1,000 "zars" of "Ken Mee" from rice boats berthed at
jetties in the Louza district. Twenty boats, 12 of
which arrived on October 14, are now in that district
awaiting unloading.

4,000 "zars" of "Ken Mee" from rice boats berthed at Nantao
and Sicawei. Fifty three boats, 30 of which arrived
on October 14, are now berthed at these centres

Section 1, Sp. Br.
August 16, 1937.

Rice Situation

The rice hongs in Shanghai remain closed to-day, August 16.
About 80% of the local rice shops suspended business this morning;
the remaining shops are doing business through small window holes
from the stock in hand. The prices quoted vary greatly: prices for
Chinese rice ranging from $14 to $17 and that of Saigon Rice ranging
from $12 to $14 per picul. Before August 13, 1937, the stock of rice
was in the region of 150,000 piculs, distributed between rice shops
and hongs in Shanghai. Since the outbreak of hostilities, no fresh
stocks have been brought to Shanghai and the people of the wealthy
and middle classes, fearing a possible shortage, purchased large
quantities. As a result, the stock in Shanghai has been greatly
depleted and now the rice shops refuse to sell the small stocks
they have.

Although there is a stock of some 150,000 piculs stored in local
godowns, most of the godowns are situated in the Eastern District
and Pootung. Only 30,000 piculs are accessible, this being stored
in the godowns of the China Merchants S. N. Co. and China Navigation
Company on the French Bund.

In order to alleviate the situation, local rice merchants have
formed an organization entitled the Shanghai Municipality Provisions
Maintenance Association. This Association has applied to the S.M.C.
and C.M.F. authorities for passes for the transportation of rice from
Chinese controlled territory to the French Concession and the Settle-
ment. The association has also made arrangements with the S.M.C.
for the use of wharfs on the south side of the Soochow Creek for
unloading the rice.

According to the leading rice merchants, about 20,000 to 30,000
piculs will arrive in Shanghai from the interior in a day or two.
The Bureau of Social Affairs has issued an order prohibiting the
traders from increasing the price of rice in excess of $15.00 per
picul.

Certified true copy.

A. G. Richards.

1937年8月16日。

大米情况

上海的米行今日（8月16日）仍然关闭。约80%的本地米店今晨停止营业；其余店铺利用手头库存通过小窗口进行交易。报价差异很大：中国大米价格在每石14至17元之间，西贡大米价格在每石12至14元之间。1937年8月13日之前，大米库存约为150,000石，分布在上海的米店和米行中。自敌对行动爆发以来，没有新的大米库存运抵上海，富裕和中产阶级民众因担心可能短缺而大量购买。结果，上海库存大幅减少，现在米店拒绝出售其仅有的少量库存。

虽然本地仓库中存有约150,000石大米，但大多数仓库位于东区和浦东。只有30,000石可供调用，这些大米储存在法外滩的招商局轮船公司和太古轮船公司的仓库中。

为缓解局势，本地米商组建了一个名为“上海市政给养维持协会”的组织。该协会已向工部局和法公董局当局申请通行证，以便将大米从中国控制区运往法租界和租界。该协会还与工部局达成协议，使用苏州河南侧的码头卸载大米。

据主要米商称，约20,000至30,000石大米将在一两天内从内地运抵上海。社会局已发布命令，禁止商人将大米价格提高至每石15.00元以上。

认证真实副本。

A. G. Richards.

weather in May and June and the poor irrigation

The Chinese rice dealers do not appear

of rice from the producing areas, after the

It is, however, probable that a portion of the

Subject Situation in Rice Producing Areas in Kiangsu and
Chekiang.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Present Situation

The following is a general survey of the
present situation in the rice producing areas in
Kiangsu and Chekiang, from where Shanghai receives
a portion of its rice supplies.

(a) Changshu, Changchow and Wusieh

Changshu, Changchow and Wusieh are the
producing centres for best quality Kan Mee rice.
It is reported that, in addition to the quantities
of rice in the hands of farmers, some 900,000 piculs
of grain are stored in various rice mills in these
places, which is capable of producing approximately
450,000 "zars" of rice.

Export of rice from these areas is strictly
controlled by the Japanese authorities. The Mitsui
Bussan Kaisha, Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha and Central
China Co. (Japanese) are the principal firms
permitted by the Japanese authorities to purchase
and transport rice therefrom.

Supplies of rice during the past two
months, however, were brought here by rail by a
number of Chinese dealers, by virtue of Japanese
transportation permits which they purchased from
dealers in Changchow and Wusieh at from $2,200 to
$2,400 per permit. Each permit authorizes the
transport of 125 bags. The dealers in Changchow
and Wusieh originally obtained the permits from the
Japanese authorities at negligible charges when they

Local rice dealers express pessimistic

in planting the rice shoots, because of the dry
weather which has caused the fields to become dry

The local rice dealers are of the opinion

few days, the rice crops this year will be seriously
affected.

Stock in Shanghai and Consumption

At present there is a stock of approximately
636,000 "zars" of rice distributed among rice shops
and godowns in the Settlement (including wharf
godowns in Hongkew) and French Concession. In
addition, some 100,000 "zars" are stored in foreign
owned wharf godowns in Pootung, thus making the
total stocks available in Shanghai some 736,000
"zars".

Besides, local rice dealers have placed
orders for the importation of some 140,000 bags of
foreign rice (approximately 175,000 "zars") which
is due to arrive at the end of June and beginning
of July, 1940.

The actual rate of consumption in
Shanghai is in the region of 10,000 "zars" a day,
but the present rate of sale by the rice shops is
approximately 6,000 "zars" a day. This discrepancy

Subject Rice Situation - Harvest of 1939.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Enquiries among local principal rice dealers show that a good harvest is anticipated during the current season. The following is a summary of the information obtained.

Kiangsu

The average yield in province of Kiangsu before the hostilities is estimated at some 40,000,000 "zars" per annum. However, in consequence of the occupation of the area by the Japanese and operation of Chinese mobile units, many districts in the vicinity of highways and railways have not been cultivated, thus this year's yield has been reduced by about 20% to approximately 32,000,000 "zars".

Of this amount, some 10,000,000 "zars" are produced in Kiangpeh and is mostly of "See Mee" quality. As a rule, Shanghai did not benefit very much by the rice from Kiangpeh, the crop being consumed in that locality and any surplus being mostly disposed of at places in the interior. Between August and October, approximately 150,000 "zars" arrived in Shanghai from Kiangpeh, but supplies ceased on November 1, as crops are being reserved for local consumption. In certain areas further interior, exportation is prohibited by the Chinese authorities (National Government) who are still functioning. No further quantities are available for export.

The remaining 22,000,000 "zars" are produced in the southern part of Kiangsu, the principal source of rice supplies for Shanghai. If transportation is

April 1, 1941.

RICE SITUATION

(A) Shanghai Rice Price Adjustment Committee
- dissolved.

Thirteen members of the Rice Price
Adjustment Committee held a meeting in the office
of the Bean & Rice Hong Owners' Guild, 15 Avenue
Edward VII, between 4 p.m. and 5.30 p.m. March 31.
Mr. Voo Chien Keng presided and made a report to
the effect that a letter had been received from
the Rice Shop Owners' Association requesting the
Committee to devise suitable measures for the
relief of rice shops, which have experienced
difficulties in conducting business in consequence
of the price of rice prevailing in the "black
market" having been far in excess of the prices
fixed by the Committee. Discussions then took
place and it was decided that the Committee be
formally dissolved forthwith and that the fixed
prices be cancelled. It was also decided that
a letter be addressed to the Shanghai Municipal
Council explaining the reasons for the dissolution
and requesting the authorities to devise effective
measures immediately to stabilize the rice situation.

(B) Rice Shop Owners' Association - meeting

Some 60 members of the Shanghai Rice Shop
Owners' Association held a meeting in the office
of the Association, Lane 153, 52 Shanhaikwan Road,
between 5 p.m. and 6.30 p.m. March 31, 1941. Mr.
Chang Hyien Sion ( 張念萱 ), the Chairman, presided.

1941年4月1日。

大米情况

(A) 上海米价调整委员会
- 解散。

3月31日下午4时至5时30分，米价调整委员会的十三名成员在爱多亚路15号豆米业公会办事处举行会议。吴建卿先生主持了会议，并报告称收到米店业主协会来信，请求委员会制定适当措施以救济米店，由于“黑市”米价远高于委员会规定的价格，米店在经营上遇到困难。随后进行了讨论，决定立即正式解散该委员会，并取消规定价格。还决定致信上海公共租界工部局，解释解散原因，并请求当局立即制定有效措施以稳定大米局势。

(B) 米店业主协会 - 会议

1941年3月31日下午5时至6时30分，上海米店业主协会约60名成员在山海关路52弄153号协会办事处举行会议。主席张念萱先生主持会议。

(2) That the legal advisor of the Association be
requested to assist in the appeal to be filed

Sir,

Report on 11th Meeting of Shanghai
Rice Price Fixing Committee

Present at the meeting were 17 members of the
Committee and representatives from S.M.C., F.M.C. and
Chinese Chamber of Commerce. Mr. N.S. Chang(      ) was
elected Chairman.

The Chairman announced the receipt of a reply
from F.M.C. which generally agreed on the principle laid
down by the Committee during the previous meeting and
asked the members to discuss on the possibilities of
price fixing.

The undersigned requested the Chairman to
clarify further on the question of reasonable profit.
The Chairman replied that although at the last meeting
it was first proposed to fix the reasonable profit at not
more than 5%, this was later altered, after a brief con-
sultation among the members themselves, to from 5% to 10%
with the latter fixed as a maximum. This was necessary,
he said, in order to encourage future orders and to
protect the rice dealers from undue losses which would
result from fluctuations in exchange rates and market
prices. Thus for instance, for the time being, most
dealers were not only making no profit but were actually
losing money to the extent of about 10% of the original
cost prices, on account of financial difficulties and the
improved rates of exchange. He also asserted that this
reasonable profit was a net profit for the dealers and
therefore did not include weight losses, insurance etc.
which alone would amount to over 5%, as the following would
show.

本人请主席就合理利润问题作进一步澄清。主席回答说，虽然在上次会议上最初提议将合理利润定为不超过5%，但在委员们内部短暂协商后，后来改为5%至10%，并将后者定为上限。他说，这是必要的，以便鼓励未来的订单，并保护米商免受因汇率和市场价格波动而造成的不当损失。例如，目前大多数米商不仅没有盈利，实际上还亏损了约占原始成本价10%的金额，这是由于财务困难和汇率改善所致。他还断言，这一合理利润是指米商的净利润，因此不包括重量损耗、保险费等，仅这些费用就超过5%，如下表所示。

with Mr. T.K. Ho, Deputy Secretary regarding the margin

The undersigned, however, pointed out that he
could see no reason why a maximum net profit of 5% would
not be sufficient under the circumstances and added that the
question was still under the careful consideration of the
Council and that an early reply would be expected.
With regard to fixing of prices, the members agreed
that it was inadvisable to do so at the present moment since
the fixed prices would inevitably be higher than the market
