At the suggestion of a member, the Chairman
requested that the Council would use its influence in sup-
pressing the unreasonable attacks made over certain of the
local radio stations on the people engaged in the rice trade
as this would greatly discourage those who were doing their
best to avert a grave situation.

我现在可以回复您关于本地米价的几封来信。奉命告知您，理事会供应小组委员会认为，进口（洋）米的本地价格不应超过基于实际交易的重置价格加上合理利润。委员会认为，如有必要，在与米业公会协商后，由贵委员会确定何为合理利润。委员会还认为，当进口（洋）米价格确定后，贵委员会也应将“粳米”（即一等国产米）的价格确定在一个合理的水平。

Dr. P. Pedersen,

Sir,

REPORT ON EMERGENCY MEETING OF THE
SHANGHAI RICE PRICE FIXING COMMITTEE.

The above meeting was held on 1st October 1940 at
15 Avenue Edward VII at 4.00 p.m. 12 members were present
while S.M.C. representative and the undersigned also attended.
Mr. Tsu Tse Hsiang ( ) was Chairman.
The Chairman announced that the meeting was called
at the special request of Mr.T.K. Ho, Deputy Secretary, S.M.C.
for the purpose of re-fixing the prices of rice in such a
way as to be in accordance with the cost of replacement and
so as to ensure a continuous source of supply.
He remarked that in view of the high cost of
replacement at present, to re-fix the prices would virtually
mean the increase of over $10.00 to the previously fixed
prices as the following would indicate:-

| | Total Replacement Cost Including Insurance, Godown,etc. | Previously Fixed Prices |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1st Quality Saigon Rice | $74.00 per sah | $61.00 per sah |
| 2nd Quality Saigon Rice | $68.00 per sah | $56.00 per zph |

The above total cost was said not including any
profit for the importing merchants and in the opinion of
those present, it should be $2.00 per sah at a minimum,
thereby making the total to be $70.00 at least. If no profit
was allowed, nobody would naturally ever attempt to place
any orders.
During the discussion that followed, members were
divided over their opinion but generally they showed reluctance
at re-fixing the prices because of the too wide margin
existing between the old and the proposed prices and fear.

上海米价评定委员会紧急会议报告。

上述会议于1940年10月1日下午4时在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）15号举行。12名委员出席，工部局代表及签署人亦列席。朱子衡（Tsu Tse Hsiang）先生任主席。

主席宣布，此次会议是应工部局副秘书何德奎（T.K. Ho）先生的特别要求而召开，目的是根据重置成本重新核定米价，以确保供应来源的连续性。

他指出，鉴于目前重置成本高昂，重新核价实际上意味着在先前核定的价格基础上上涨超过10美元，具体如下所示：-

| | 总重置成本（含保险、仓库费等） | 先前核定价格 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 一等西贡米 | 每担74.00美元 | 每担61.00美元 |
| 二等西贡米 | 每担68.00美元 | 每担56.00美元 |

据称，上述总成本未包含进口商的任何利润。与会者认为，利润至少应为每担2.00美元，从而使总额至少达到70.00美元。如果不允许利润，自然无人会尝试下单。

在随后的讨论中，委员们意见分歧，但普遍对重新核价表现出犹豫，原因是旧价与建议价格之间的差距过大，且担心

pages.en:
- 2 -

for public criticism. Despite the undersigned's assurance
that the Authorities promised to accord them full support in
this connection, they preferred to have official written
assurances rather than anything verbal as they said that even
their previous petition to the S.M.C. had not yet been
officially replied.
Regarding the fixing of prices for Domestic rice
(Kar Mee) as suggested by Mr. T.K. Ho, the members pointed
out that the arrival of this rice in the Settlement on
bicycles was most uncertain and since it was sold almost
directly to shops and not through the Rice Market and since
the prices also varied almost daily, depending chiefly on
the extent of restrictions applied by the Japanese
Authorities and various unexpected expenses en route, it
would be difficult to do so.
The following resolutions were finally reached:-
(1) That all data regarding replacement cost and
the new tentative prices the Committee proposed to fix be
forwarded to S.M.C. through the good offices of Mr. T.K. Ho
and that unless official written approval and advice be
received, no other action to be taken and further sessions
be suspended.
(2) That letters be despatched to public bodies
advising them to continue joint-purchasing.
The meeting ended at 5.00 p.m.

Junior Inspector.

受到公众批评。尽管签署人保证当局承诺在此事上给予他们全力支持，但他们更希望得到官方的书面保证，而非口头承诺，因为他们表示，即使他们此前向工部局提交的请愿书也尚未得到官方回复。

关于何德奎先生建议的对国产米（Kar Mee）进行定价一事，委员们指出，这种大米通过自行车运入租界的情况极不确定，且其销售几乎是直接面向店铺，而非通过米市场进行；此外，价格几乎每日变动，主要取决于日本当局实施的限制程度以及途中各种意外费用，因此难以对此进行定价。

最终达成以下决议：-
(1) 有关重置成本及委员会拟议的新暂定价格的所有数据，应通过何德奎先生的斡旋转呈工部局；除非收到官方书面批准和建议，否则不采取其他行动，并暂停后续会议。
(2) 致函各公共团体，建议其继续联合采购。

会议于下午5时结束。

上海米价评定委员会第八次会议报告。

上述会议于1940年9月13日下午4时30分在上海粮食交易所大楼举行，出席者包括委员会12名委员，以及工部局、法公董局和总商会的代表。朱子衡（朱子衡）先生任主席。

主席特别提请讨论了委员会因近期米价局势失控的发展而陷入的极度困难境地。他还提及了联合采购计划所涉及的困难，并引用了几家本地进口商行的回函作为参考。

从这些回函来看，重置成本甚至高于黑市报价，具体数字如下：-

（印：INDEACO BY (S.R) REGISTRY DATE 20/ 9）

| | 重置成本 | | 本地价格（黑市） |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| | (100公斤) | (80公斤) | (80公斤) |
| 一等 | $57.00 | $55.60 | $66.00 |
| 二等 " | $50.00 | $54.60 | $63.00 |

作为最后手段，主席提出以下建议：-

(1) 通过工部局的努力，接触工部局董事俞雅清（Yu Ya Ching）先生。据悉他存有超过10万袋西贡米，原拟用于宁波的救济工作，但因运输限制而滞留

pages.en:
- 2 -

up in Shanghai owing to transportation restrictions, in order
to try to secure his assistance so that this stock could be
released for the local market. Such a measure, if successful,
is bound to bring forth a marked improvement.

(2) That the Mixed Cereals Association be asked to start
its own joint purchasing scheme.

Both the above were disapproved by members present
with reasons given below:-

(1) Little or no support could be expected from Mr. Yu
Ya Ching since his stock of rice is also meant to relieve rice
shortage in Ningpo.

(2) Too much capital would be involved in the case of
ordering large stocks of rice and the losses incurred would be
enormous in view of the discrepancies between local prices and
replacement cost.

The general opinion prevailed that to make any changes
in the stipulated prices fixed on 3rd inst. was out of the
question but in the meantime, no value could be attached to
the work of this Committee if the fixed prices were not adhered
to as at present.

Finally, 2 resolutions were passed by the meeting.

(1) That the difficulties now confronting this Committee
be reported to the Authorities of both areas for their advice.

(2) That future meetings of the Rice Price Fixing Committee
be temporarily suspended pending the receipt of advice and
directions from both Authorities.

The meeting concluded at 5.30 p.m.

Junior Inspector.

September 12, 40.

The Chairman,
The Shanghai Rice Price Fixing Committee,
15 Avenue Edward VII,
Shanghai.

Sir,

I have to acknowledge receipt of and to thank you
for your letters of August 31 and September 7 relative to
rice prices.

In reply I have to inform you that the subject is
receiving attention and a stricter control of the Rice Market
is contemplated.

As you know the Council views the establishment and
continued existence of a stock of rice with considerable
satisfaction. The Council believes that the building up of
stocks is to the interest of rice merchants themselves and
is a part of their operations. The Council regrets that it
cannot itself at the present time embark on any plan of rice
purchase.

Private enterprises are however encouraged to
import stocks of rice and I can assure you that parties
prepared to undertake the importation of supplies will
receive all possible advice and encouragement from the
Council in their efforts.

The Council has learned with much satisfaction of
the steps taken by you and hopes that with your assistance an
improvement in the situation may soon be possible.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

T. W. Cobb
Deputy Secretary.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMANDER 13 SEP 1940）
T.

Translation of letter to Council
from the Shanghai Rice Price Fixing
Committee.

Dated 7th September, 1940.

Address: 15 Avenue Edward VII.

Rice: Collective Purchase of suggested.

On the 6th instant we held our 6th ordinary
meeting; we are grateful that an officer of the Council
was present. With regard to the price of imported rice
it was decided to maintain the price fixed on the 3rd
instant in accordance with the advice of the Settlement
Authorities. We have notified that rice market to observe
this decision, and have requested the Settlement and
Concession Authorities as well as the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce to give assistance to this matter so that the
price of rice may not be clandestinely enhanced. The
public is asked to report to us the name of any person
who infringes this arrangement so that he may be handed
over to the Authorities for punishment. Please note the
above decision. We shall be very grateful if the Council
would give us adequate assistance so that the fixed price
may be followed and clandestine raising of price stopped.

On 31st August we wrote to the Council concerning
the joint purchase of rice by various organizations. The
Council is asked in conjunction with the French Municipal
Council and the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, to summon the
representatives of various trades, and urge them to promise
to purchase a certain number of bags of rice each. By so
doing the stock will be replenished and the food problem
will be solved.

Reply solicited.
Shanghai Rice Price Fixing Committee.
(Note: Received for translation late p.m. 9th Sept., 1940).

Rice Transactions: Control of.

The following suggestions are submitted by Rice
dealers to Mr. Ho, Chinese Deputy Secretary of the
Municipal Council, with a view to preventing illegal
transactions and adopting measures for improving the
administration of the rice market.

(1) Hereafter all transactions between hongs and
shops should be confirmed by the Settlement and Concession
authorities in conjunction with the representative of the
Shanghai City Chamber of Commerce, otherwise the transaction
will be considered as illegal.

(2) The Council should take advantage of this
opportunity to order the rice market to re-organize, and
it should adopt an "official hong" system for the purpose
of stabilizing the market, and curbing illegal transactions.

(3) As inter-hong transactions should be absolutely
prohibited, the Settlement Authorities are requested to take
effective steps to rigorously suppress such transactions,
which are sometimes referred to as "passing the ball".

(4) The Council should detail officers to inspect
the transactions account books of the various rice hongs
and dealers daily.

(5) Detectives who are not known to rice dealers
should be sent by turns to the rice market to investigate
the rice situation and illegal transactions daily.

(6) The existence of refreshment stalls in the rice
market is a great inconvenience to the public; such stalls
should be removed.

Translation of letter to Council
from the Rice Price Fixing Committee.
Dated 31st August, 1940.
Address: No.15 Avenue Edward VII.

Rice Prices.

The price of foreign rice has recently advanced
so high that the difference as compared with the local
market prices has become greater than ever. Although the
earlier Chinese crop has already arrived, transportation
is frequently interfered with. Under existing conditions
it is unlikely that stocks will increase; for this reason
the prices have risen and we can no longer maintain the
price limit announced on 16th July. Some time ago this
Committee called a meeting with the consent of the
Settlement authorities to discuss actual conditions and
to fix maximum prices for the various kinds of foreign
rice. Apart from announcing the prices in the Market we
beg to enclose herewith a list for the Council's information.

In the above connexion we wish to state that to
stabilize prices the present plan is only a palliative
measure; the main thing is to increase the stocks. As
the best way to attain this object would be for various
dealers to make large purchases, we venture to request the
Council to urge all merchants to start a "mass rice purchase
movement" so that stocks may be increased and prices
stabilized. Please grant this request.

Encl: 1 price list.

(Chopped) Shanghai Rice Price Fixing
Committee.

Central China Daily News 8-

▲ Price Readjustment Committee Being Formed

Owing to the disruption of communications,
the supply of daily necessities during the past six months
has been affected. In addition, as a result of the
fall in the value of Chinese dollar and the rise in the
price of gold, the people of various places throughout
the country, especially those of Shanghai, have been
facing much hardship by the increase in the price of
all commodities. The prices of daily necessities, such

as rice, flour, vegetables, oil, salt, firewood and
charcoal, have increased by 500% to 600% when compared
with that they were six months ago. Common people and
coolies are finding it difficult to maintain their living;
some have been forced to run risks while many have
committed suicide.

In view of the continuous increase in the
prices of commodities, important local bodies recently
suggested the formation of a committee to adjust the
prices of all commodities. If such a body is to be
formed, it must have wide powers for it has not only
to place restrictions upon the prices of commodities,
but it should also be empowered to adopt strict measures
to enforce its orders. All cases of violation of the
restrictions placed upon the price of rice and of manipulation
or hoarding of commodities should be severely punished
by the body with a fine and the confiscation of all his
commodities. The proceeds received from the sale of the
confiscated goods and the fine should be handed over to
the Committee for expenses. Thus the activities of
traitorous merchants in manipulating the price of goods
will be stopped and prices can be adjusted.

The Foreign Settlements should be requested
to devise ways and means to regulate supplies. When
the supply meets the demand, no more shortage will be
felt and the prices of commodities will decline.

For this reason, the Preparatory Committee
of the Price Readjustment Committee will invite the
Chinese Ratepayers' Associations, the Chinese Chamber
of Commerce, the trade guilds and other influential
bodies to take part in the formation.

Shun Pao, Eastern Times 8-
pages.zh:
《华中日报》 8月-

▲ 正在组建价格调整委员会

由于交通中断，过去六个月的生活必需品供应受到影响。此外，由于法币贬值和金价上涨，全国各地人民，尤其是上海市民，因所有商品价格上涨而面临巨大困难。大米、面粉、蔬菜、油、盐、柴炭等生活必需品的价格，与六个月前相比上涨了500%至600%。平民和苦力难以维持生计；有些人被迫冒险，许多人自杀。

鉴于商品价格持续上涨，当地重要团体最近建议成立一个委员会来调整所有商品的价格。如果要成立这样一个机构，它必须拥有广泛的权力，因为它不仅要限制商品价格，还应被授权采取严格措施强制执行其命令。所有违反大米价格限制以及操纵或囤积商品的案件，应由该机构处以罚款并没收其所有商品。没收物品出售所得款项及罚款应交给委员会作为经费。从而制止奸商操纵物价的行为，使价格得到调整。

应要求外国租界设法规范供应。当供应满足需求时，短缺感将不再存在，商品价格将会下降。

为此，价格调整委员会筹备委员会将邀请华人纳税会、中华总商会、同业公会及其他有影响力的团体参与组建。

《申报》，《时事新报》 8月-

委员们同意主席的意见，即密切监视价格形势，并且委员会应在一周内再次开会，以决定是否应进一步降价。
(b) 大米库存。警方报告称，据估计上海今日的大米总库存约为647,000石，而6月23日报告的数字为675,000石。在6月23日至26日期间，来自内地的稻米供应平均每日抵达约3,600石，其中大部分是来自芜湖的籼米。鉴于这一数量不足以满足社区需求（即每日约10,000石），主席询问新粮何时上市。Eveleigh 先生回答说，新粮将在九月份上市，并指出目前内地供应充足；只是不允许自由运抵此处。
Ho 先生表示，据米商称，停运并非系统性的——他们仍然有可能将大米从芜湖至上海铁路沿线的小站运出。然而，目前从芜湖运出的大米并未受到干扰。
Eveleigh 先生告知委员们，一些有远见的商人已以每袋1½石21½美元的价格订购了500吨西贡米。

pages.en:
-3-
Discussion ensues as to the ways and means of increasing
the importation of this vital commodity into Shanghai from the
interior. Mr. Eveleigh refers to the arrangement whereby a Chinese
company situated in the Land Bank Building is buying wheat from the
interior for consumption in Shanghai in co-operation with certain
Japanese interests, and suggests that something along these lines
might be tried in regard to the supply of rice. Dr. Pedersen states
that he has come into contact with one of the men appointed by the
Asia Development Board to control the movement of rice between Wuhu
and Shanghai, and that this person would be willing to buy rice for
Shanghai. Mr. Eveleigh expresses the view that the Chinese rice
merchants themselves would be reluctant to negotiate directly with
the Japanese without the intervention of a neutral third party. Upon
the suggestion of the Treasurer it is decided that Mr. Eveleigh, Dr.
Pedersen and Mr. Ho approach the representatives of the Rice Guilds to
ascertain whether the rice merchants would be willing to buy rice from
the Asia Development Board either direct or through a neutral third
party, and if so, to make the necessary arrangements accordingly.
Mr. Ho states that he will arrange for this conference to meet at the
Secretariat to-morrow at 3.45 p.m. and will submit a report on the
outcome.

The meeting terminates at 2.50 p.m.
pages.zh:
-3-
随后讨论了增加从内地向上海进口这一重要物资的方法和手段。Eveleigh 先生提到，位于土地银行大楼的一家中国公司与某些日本利益方合作，从内地购买小麦供上海消费，他建议在稻米供应方面可以尝试类似的做法。Pedersen 博士表示，他接触到了亚洲开发董事会指派的一名负责控制芜湖与上海之间大米流动的人员，此人愿意为上海购买大米。Eveleigh 先生认为，在没有中立第三方介入的情况下，中国米商本身不愿直接与日本人谈判。根据司库的建议，决定由 Eveleigh 先生、Pedersen 博士和 Ho 先生接洽米业公会代表，以确定米商是否愿意直接或间接通过中立第三方向亚洲开发董事会购买大米，如果是，则相应做出必要安排。
Ho 先生表示，他将安排此次会议于明天下午3点45分在秘书处举行，并将提交关于结果的报告。

会议于下午2点50分结束。

pages.en:
POLICE FORCE
23 MAY 1939

Transmission of letter to Council from
Shanghai Rice Circulation Price Fixing
Committee.

Rice Situation.

With a view to stabilizing the prices of rice, this
Committee on the 12th instant wrote to the Council to request
it to take two steps, viz: (1) to appoint representatives
to serve on the Committee, and (2) to order supplies from
abroad or, alternatively, to make arrangements for facilitating
transportation from inland places.

On the 19th we were much disappointed to receive the
Council's reply refusing to comply with our request. During
the ten days since our previous letter was written, the rice
market has experienced violent vicissitudes. At first, supplies
of the best quality became unavailable, then prices of inferior
qualities rose to the price limit, later surreptitious transactions
took place in violation of restrictions, and finally, such
transactions became open secrets. Hence the continued rapid
advance in the prices of rice.

In the past few days the price for keng rice of the best
quality has risen to over $17 per picul, which is more than $2
in excess of the limit. The price of Hsi rice is approximately
$15, which is about $1 in excess.

We have seriously warned all the dealers to strictly
observe the limits and have encouraged them to report to us
cases of irregular transactions so that penalties may be inflicted;
but the warning has been ignored. We are now at the end of our
wits.

From the 12th to the 19th instant, only 28 holders of rice
stocks have registered. The quantity they hold is only 65,503 bags,
pages.zh:
警务处
1939年5月23日

转呈上海米粮流通平价委员会致工部局的信函。

米粮情况。

为了稳定米价，本委员会于本月12日致函工部局，请求其采取两项措施，即：(1) 指派代表加入本委员会，以及 (2) 从国外订购供应品，或者 alternatively，安排便利从内地运输。

19日，我们非常失望地收到工部局拒绝 comply 我们请求的回复。在我们上一封信发出后的十天里，米市经历了剧烈的动荡。起初，最上等品质的供应变得 unavailable，接着劣质米的价格涨至限价，随后违反限制的私下交易发生，最后，此类交易成为公开的秘密。因此，米价持续快速上涨。

在过去几天里，最上等品质的粳米价格已涨至每担17美元以上，超出限价2美元多。籼米的价格约为15美元，超出约1美元。

我们已严肃警告所有经销商严格遵守限价，并鼓励他们向我们报告违规交易案例，以便实施处罚；但警告被无视。我们现在已束手无策。

从本月12日至19日，仅有28名大米库存持有者进行了登记。他们持有的数量仅为65,503包，

pages.en:
- 3 -
which represent only a little over ten per cent of the total
local stocks. It is therefore evident that the majority of
our rice has not the least chance of being sold at a profit,
and in undertaking this task we have but little hope of success;
but this object has been attained to a great extent by the
efforts of our members, who have endeavoured to prevent the
rise in our previous prices; and it is not possible to do more.

The present condition of affairs in this Committee makes
it impossible for us to continue our work with any hope of
success. We have done all that was possible within the
scope of our functions and powers. Owing to the lack of
funds and authority, we have not been able to achieve most of our aims. The community
must now depend entirely on the Council, which controls the
settlement, to take the present situation in hand and to devise
adequate measures to cope with it. The Council will either order
the purchase of foreign rice or import it from inland districts as a preventive measure; or, it will take
other suitable steps to prevent a shortage and to stabilize the
market. This is what we earnestly hope it will do.

As our limited abilities have prevented us from
accomplishing most of our undertakings, there is no reason for
our Committee to continue to exist. At a meeting held on the
20th instant we decided to dissolve the Committee.

The functions of the Committee will hereafter be
performed by various Rice Dealers' Organizations. The Committee
is dissolved owing to adverse circumstances; we hope the Council
will excuse us. We also beg to point out that although the prices
of "keng" rice and "Hsi" rice have both recently exceeded the limit,
the price of the latter is more stable. Formerly the difference
in prices between these two categories was about one dollar; now
pages.zh:
- 3 -
这仅占本地总库存的百分之十稍多。因此显而易见，我们的大多数大米根本没有机会以盈利方式售出，而在承担这项任务时，我们对成功几乎没有希望；但这一目标在很大程度上已通过我们成员的努力得以实现，他们致力于防止我们之前的价格上涨；且已无法做得更多。

本委员会目前的状况使我们无法带着任何成功的希望继续我们的工作。我们在职能和权力范围内已做了所有可能做的事。由于缺乏资金和权威，我们未能实现我们的大多数目标。社区现在必须完全依赖控制租界的工部局来处理当前局势，并制定适当的措施来应对。工部局要么作为预防措施下令购买外国大米或从内陆地区进口；要么，它将采取其他适当步骤以防止短缺并稳定市场。这是我们恳切希望它做的。

由于我们有限的能力阻碍了我们完成大多数承诺，本委员会没有理由继续存在。在本月20日举行的会议上，我们决定解散本委员会。

本委员会的职能今后将由各个米商组织履行。本委员会因不利情况而解散；我们希望工部局能谅解我们。我们也谨指出，虽然近期“粳”米和“籼”米的价格均超过了限价，但后者的价格更为稳定。以前这两类米之间的价差约为一美元；现在

pages.en:
- 7 -

the difference has rather been the following, due to the
following reasons: 1. Cost:- The cost of rice in all, is "Pat" rice;
"Ken" rice does not exceed 200, Yens ; 2. Distribution:-
who is the "Pat" rice dealer; and it is same for "Ken"
rice. The price of rice in Shanghai is fixed, at sale at
of rice from 6.1h to 8.4d if still available. In our
opinion the price of rice will be raised by;
the price of "Pat" rice will be raised by, the
livelihood of the poor class will not be affected.

The prices of the rice have not reached the
cost of foreign rice. Shortage of local rice will occur
if the Council will immediately order importations of foreign
rice. We hope that our humble view will meet the Council's
favourable consideration.

(Comal)

Shanghai Rice Organizations
Rice Fixing Committee.

(Note: Received for translation on 23rd May, 1939.)

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL MAY 23 1939 TRANSLATION OFFICE）

价差反而如下，原因如下：1. 成本：- 所有米的成本均为“Pat”米；
“Ken”米不超过200日元；2. 分销：-
谁是“Pat”米经销商；“Ken”米也是如此。上海的米价固定，在仍有存货的情况下，从6.1h到8.4d出售。在我们

“Pat”米的价格将被提高，
贫困阶层的生活不会受到影响。

米价尚未达到外国米的成本。
如果工部局立即下令进口外国米，本地米将出现短缺。我们希望我们的浅见能得到工部局的有利考虑。

(Comal)

Translation of a letter dated September 25, 1941
addressed by the Shanghai Rice Market Control Committee
to the Assistant Commissioner (Special Branch), S.M.P.

Assistant Commissioner,
Special Branch, S.M.P.

With a view to putting a stop to cases of
fighting at the Rice Market, it has been resolved at
the 90th meeting of this Committee that henceforth
acts of violence at the Market during business hours
will be strictly prohibited and that any breach of
this decision will render both parties involved
liable to be suspended from doing business in the
Market for a period of five days.

Apart from posting a notice to the above
effect at the Market, this Committee sends this
letter for your information so that you will place
the matter on record.

(Signed & chopped) Voo Chien Keng
Chairman of the Shanghai Rice
Market Control Committee,
House 52, Lane 153, Shanhaikwan
Road.

Translation of an urgent notice issued by Rice
Market Control Committee on June 15, 1941

The following letter has been received from
the Rice Transportation Handcart Coolies' Union :-

"An amicable solution of the recent
strike of rice transportation handcart
coolies has been reached through the impartial
mediation of your Committee. Although no
written agreement was signed at that time,
in principle there has been some binding
effect, such as the promise to allot 40%
of rice transportation work to be under-
taken by handcarts and 60% by motor trucks.
"However, handcarts have been denied
the work of transporting rice on No. 2
Pontoon opposite Canton Road, and all
efforts by overseers have proved futile.
Lest this should give rise to further
disputes, for which the persons handling
rice deliveries are responsible, this
Union sends this letter with the request
that the employees of various rice hongs
handling the rice deliveries be notified
to abide by the principle so as to avoid
disputes."

In view of the foregoing and in furtherance
of a notice issued on May 14, it has been resolved
at the 87th meeting of the Market that a further
notice be issued to all rice hongs to instruct
their employees handling rice deliveries to allot
rice transportation work to be done by handcarts
in consideration of the livelihood of the coolies
and in order to avoid disputes.
pages.zh:
米市场管理委员会于1941年6月15日发布的紧急通知译文

收到米运输手车苦力工会的如下来信：-

“通过贵委员会的公正调解，近期米运输手车苦力的罢工已达成友好解决。虽然当时未签署书面协议，但在原则上已产生一定的约束力，例如承诺将40%的大米运输工作分配给手车，60%分配给卡车。
“然而，在广东路对面的2号浮桥处，手车被拒绝从事大米运输工作，监工们的一切努力均证明无效。为避免由此引发进一步纠纷，且负责大米交付的人员对此负有责任，本工会特致此信，请求通知各米行负责大米交付的员工遵守上述原则，以避免纠纷。”

鉴于上述情况，并为贯彻5月14日发布的通知，市场在第87次会议上决定，再次向所有米行发布通知，指示其负责大米交付的员工，考虑到苦力的生计并为避免纠纷，将大米运输工作分配给手车完成。

515 Soochow Road, between 11.40 a.m. and 12 noon
May 5. Mr. Voo Chien Keng, Chairman of the Market,
presided and made a report to the following effect -
"the Rice Market has now more or less turned into an
exchange and the price has fluctuated greatly,
undoubtedly due to manipulation." Discussions then
took place and it was decided that the temporary
arrangements, enforced on May 2, separating purchasers
and sellers into two groups and conducting business
transactions between them under the supervision of
the "Inspection Board" formed by the Market authorities,
be abolished. It was proposed that new rules be
enforced that the Market open between 10 a.m. and
11 a.m. only and that rice brokers doing business
in the Market be held responsible for registering
with the Market Control Committee regarding sales
transacted. For failing to register, the brokers
concerned will have their admission badges withdrawn
and be deprived of the right of doing business in
the Market. It was eventually decided that the above
measure be put into force from May 6, 1941 as a trial.

On the morning of May 5, a rice broker named
Pao Wei Foo (包偉福) was found to have been conducting
private transactions in violation of the regulations
of the Market Control Committee. He was arrested
by the Market Inspection Board.

Translation of a Notice of Rice
Market dated May 2, 1941

It is hereby notified that in view of the
ignorance by a number of the merchants of the regulations
pertaining to the sales and purchases in this market,
which were formulated during a joint meeting of seven
local rice business organizations some time ago, and
in order to rectify this irregularity, the following
decisions were reached during a meeting of members of
the Rice Market Control Committee, held on May 1 and
all concerned are expected to observe same :

1) That only cash sales be allowed in this market.
2) That any transactions to be done in this market be
made according to the following procedure :

a) Only authorized brokers and agents are
allowed in the market and they
should never conduct any business
of their own.

b) Purchases by rice shops should be made
direct with the rice hong8 concerned.

c) Only transactions done in accordance
with this procedure, accompanied by a
bill to that effect will be regarded as
in order. Any irregularity or
disregard of the above decisions
will result in expulsion from the
market of those concerned.

特此通知，鉴于许多商人无视不久前由七个本地米业组织联席会议制定的有关本市场买卖的规定，为纠正这种不规范行为，米市场管理委员会成员在5月1日的会议上达成了以下决定，望各方遵守：

1) 本市场仅允许现金交易。
2) 在本市场进行的任何交易应按以下程序进行：

a) 仅授权经纪人和代理人进入市场，他们
绝不得从事任何自己的业务。

b) 米店的采购应直接与相关的
米行进行。

c) 只有按照此程序进行的交易，并附有
相应账单，才被视为合规。任何违规或
无视上述决定的行为，将导致
相关人员被逐出市场。

SUBJECT: Rice Shop Owners' Association - meeting

Some 200 rice shop owners held a meeting
in the Rice Shop Owners' Association, Lane 126, 53
Shanhaikwan Road, between 3 p.m. and 5.30 p.m. on
April 27. Mr. Huang Jui Yuan (黄汝园), committee
member of the Association, presided and made a
report to the effect that although rice shops had
been refraining from purchasing supplies of rice in
the Rice Market, the black market prices showed no
signs of a downward tendency, and that the reason for
the non-decrease was quite clear. Discussions then
took place, and it was decided that rice shop owners
continue to refrain from purchasing supplies of rice
in the Rice Market at the black market price, pending
instructions from the Municipal Authorities. It was
also decided that efforts be made to bring to light
black market transactions so as to eliminate same.

However, the above resolution was not enforced
this morning, April 28, in consequence of the removal
of the fixed prices by the Rice Market Control
Committee in compliance with the instructions from
the S.M.C. (a translation of the notice regarding
the removal of the fixed prices is attached hereto).
The rice brokers and rice shop owners, who suspended
purchasing rice supplies in the Rice Market on April
23 and 24 as a protest against the holders demanding
surcharges in addition to the fixed price, resumed
normal trading to-day, April 28, 1941.

主题：米店业主协会 - 会议

4月27日下午3时至5时30分，约200名米店业主在山海关路53号126弄的米店业主协会举行会议。协会委员黄汝园先生（Huang Jui Yuan）主持会议，并报告称，尽管米店一直 refrain from（克制/避免）在米市场采购大米供应，但黑市价格并未显示出下降趋势，且不降的原因十分清楚。随后进行了讨论，决定米店业主继续避免以黑市价格在米市场采购大米供应，等待市政当局的指示。还决定努力揭露黑市交易，以便消除之。

然而，由于米市场管理委员会遵照工部局（S.M.C.）的指示取消了固定价格（附取消固定价格通知的译文），上述决议未在今日（4月28日）上午执行。此前于4月23日和24日为抗议持货人在固定价格之外要求附加费而暂停在米市场采购大米供应的米经纪和米店业主，于今日（1941年4月28日）恢复了正常交易。

SUBJECT: Situation at the Rice Market this morning, April 23

The trade situation in the Rice Market, 515 Foochow Road, on the morning of April 23, 1941, was almost at a standstill. Only a small quantity of rice was offered for sale and changed hands, owing to the dealers assuming a wait and see attitude, pending further developments.

A notice was posted in the Market by the Market Control Committee, notifying dealers to refrain from conducting black market dealings at prices above the fixed price. A translation of the notice is attached hereto.

The rice brokers were verbally notified by Tsai Vee Ziang (蔡维翔), Chairman of the Rice Brokers' Lien Nyi Society, to suspend their activities in the Market for a period of three days, commencing from to-day, April 23.

The Shanghai Rice Shop Owners' Association is calling a meeting at 3 p.m. to-day, April 23, in its office at Lane 153, 52 Shanhaikwan Road, for the purpose of discussing the situation and action to be taken by rice shops at the present time.

Translation of notice No.189 issued by the Rice
Market Control Committee dated 23/4/41
------

It is hereby notified that this Rice Market was
established with a view to regulating the supply and
stabilizing the price of the staple food. It has
been in existence for more than three years. During
the course of its existence, unfavourable changes have
taken place and consequently at the present, the market
has lost its primary object.

The supply of foreign rice is at present continuing,
in spite of insufficient shipping space and the heavy
increase in freight charges. The present stock in
Shanghai is not less than one million bags. The
Settlement authorities, in favour of the rice dealers,
removed the restrictions on the price of rice, but
before 10 days had elapsed, the price of rice had again
soared. With a view to maintaining the peace and good
order of the Settlement, the authorities again restricted
the prices and notices to this effect were published by
the Market Control Committee. Immediately afterwards,
the price again became unsteady. This is a bad state of
affairs. Dealers are hereby earnestly advised to transact
business through the proper channels and refrain from
engaging in black market dealings above the fixed price.
Those who disobey instructions will deserve punishment.
All concerned are notified to observe the instructions and
preserve the good reputation of this Market.
pages.zh:
米市场管理委员会于1941年4月23日发布的第189号告示译文
------

特此通告，本米市场之设立，旨在调节主食供应并稳定其价格。该市场已存在三年有余。在其存续期间，局势发生不利变化，致使目前市场已丧失其首要目标。

尽管航运舱位不足且运费大幅上涨，洋米供应目前仍在继续。上海目前的库存不少于一百万包。租界当局为照顾米商利益，取消了对米价的限制，但不到十天，米价再次飙升。为维护租界的和平与良好秩序，当局再次限制价格，并由市场管理委员会发布了相关告示。随后，价格再次变得不稳定。此种状况甚为恶劣。特此恳切劝告各米商通过正当渠道进行交易， refrain from engaging in black market dealings above the fixed price（ refrain from engaging in... 此处原文意为“避免从事高于固定价格的黑市交易”，结合上下文译为：不得以高于规定价格从事黑市交易）。违者将受惩处。望各方遵守指令，维护本市场的良好声誉。

The situation at the Rice Market in the
Tsing Lien Koh Teashop, 515 Foochow Road, deteriorated
on February 24. Only "Kan Mee" and "Nui Mee" rice
which is not affected by the price limits, was on
sale in the Market. A small amount of inferior
quality foreign rice was offered for sale at the
prices fixed by the Rice Price Adjustment Committee.
There are several qualities in one grade of rice.
Only a limited amount of the poor quality is for
sale, the good quality is being held by the dealers
who are unwilling to dispose of at the fixed prices
because they anticipate a rise in the price in
view of the present tense situation in the Far East.
It is reported that sales of rice were
transacted on February 24, at prices of $1 to $2 in
excess of the fixed prices in such a manner as to
avoid detection by the Authorities. During these
transactions at the Market there are usually about
1,000 dealers present and they talk in terms known
only to themselves. It is possible for dealers
outside the Rice Market to make transactions without
the knowledge of the market officials.
In consequence of the report that black
market quotations have taken place, Mr. Tsai Vee
Xiang (蔡維翔), Chairman of the Rice Brokers'

February 23, 1941. Morning Translation

Bing Pao, Central China Daily News, Kuo Min Daily News and New
China Daily News :-

PRICE OF RICE EXCEEDS LIMIT : ILLEGAL TRANSACTIONS CONDUCTED
BY BROKERS SHOULD BE QUICKLY SUPPRESSED

During the past few days, much instability
has prevailed in the rice mart due to the manipulation by
rice speculators who are withholding their rice stocks from
disposal. During the transactions conducted at the rice
mart yesterday, only inferior quality goods and broken rice
were offered because both the superior and middle qualities
of rice were scarce due to manipulation by certain persons.
However, private dealings outside the rice mart have been
conducted on a wide scale and the selling price has exceeded
the limit fixed by $2 or $3.
Of late the rice brokers have again resumed
their former activities and have been conducting illegal
transactions outside the rice mart. The Rice Brokers Lien-
Nyi Society has however remained indifferent to such
activities. It is therefore hoped that the authorities
of the two Foreign Settlements will instruct the society
to take immediate steps against these brokers and prosecute
them for activities endangering the food supplies of the
people, so as to serve as deterrent to others.
According to a well-known merchant of a
certain trade, the following measures should be adopted
immediately if it is desired to bring about a stabilization
of the price of rice :-
(1) An extensive investigation into the
amount of rice now hoarded should be conducted and the
owners should be forced to offer it for sale with a certain
percentage of profit within a time specified, or else the
rice should be confiscated.
(2) Persons not connected with the rice trade
should be denied entry into the rice mart while rice brokers
should be prohibited to practice at the rice mart.
(3) The fixed price of rice should be strictly
adhered to and all illegal transactions should be stopped.
At the same time enquiries should be immediately made with
a view to ascertaining whether or not the profit derived from
the sale of rice at the fixed price exceeds the legal profit
of 5% or 10%. If so, a lower price should be fixed.
(4) Immediate efforts should be made to
regulate the sources of supply of both foreign and domestic
rice and special ships should be chartered for the
transportation of rice at moderate freight charges.
(5) Efforts should be made to adjust the
organization of the various food provision bodies and to
advise the people to take an enthusiastic part in making
joint purchases of rice. They should be prevailed upon not
to rely upon the rice shops for supplies of their daily
necessaries.
(6) The 9th cheap sale of broken rice should
be continued so as to enable the poor people to obtain rice
at low price.

《平报》、《华中日报》、《国民日报》及《新中国日报》：-

米价超限：经纪人非法交易应迅速取缔

过去几天，由于米商投机者囤积居奇，米市波动剧烈。在昨日米市进行的交易中，仅出售劣质货物和碎米，因为优质和中质大米因某些人的操纵而稀缺。然而，米市外的私下交易大规模进行，售价超出限定价格2或3美元。
近来，米行经纪人又恢复了以往的活动，在米市外进行非法交易。然而，米业公会对这些活动一直漠不关心。因此，希望两租界当局指示该公会对这些经纪人立即采取行动，并以危害民众粮食供应的活动为由起诉他们，以儆效尤。
据某行业的一位知名商人称，若欲实现米价稳定，应立即采取以下措施：-
(1) 应对目前囤积的大米数量进行广泛调查，并强制业主在指定时间内以一定的利润比例出售，否则没收大米。
(2) 禁止与米业无关的人员进入米市，同时禁止米行经纪人在米市执业。
(3) 应严格遵守大米固定价格，制止一切非法交易。同时，应立即进行调查，以确定以固定价格出售大米所获利润是否超过5%或10%的法定利润。如果是，则应设定更低的价格。
(4) 应立即努力规范洋米和国米的供应来源，并租用专用船只以适中的运费运输大米。
(5) 应努力调整各粮食供应机构的组织，并建议民众热情参与联合购米。应劝导民众不要依赖米店供应日常必需品。
(6) 应继续第九次廉价出售碎米，以便穷人能以低价获得大米。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 助理专员 / 特务科 / 1941年2月23日）

February 23, 1941. Morning Translation

Central China Daily News, Kuo Min Daily News and New China
Daily News :-

Shanghai Food Provision Regulation Committee To Buy 800,000
Bags Of Rice For Supply To Local Residents

Due to the activities of manipulation by
traitorous merchants, the price of rice has gone up
continuously with the result that the poor people and the
salaried class have found it extremely difficult to maintain
their livelihood. With a view to bringing about a regulation
of food supplies and appeasing the minds of the public,
thereby bringing about a gradual drop in the price of rice,
Mayor Chen Kung-po of the Shanghai City Government has formed
the Shanghai Food Provision Regulation Committee with the
collaboration of various local bodies and banking circles.
A sum of $19,000,000 has already been promised by the various
circles. Recently a meeting was held by the Committee at
which measures relating to the purchase of rice were discussed.
It is learned that the Committee has decided
to purchase at first 800,000 bags of rice. This rice will
be transported to Shanghai by the end of this month or the
middle of March, when it will be sold at cost price because
the aim of the Committee is to regulate food supplies and
increase rice stocks in Shanghai.

Chinese-American Daily News (brief comment) :-

SETTLEMENT AUTHORITIES SHOULD SUPPRESS THE TRAITOROUS
MERCHANTS SO AS TO PRESERVE THEIR PRESTIGE

We petitioned to the authorities several
days ago that as the value of the legal tender is going
up, the prices of commodities should be kept down so that
the burden of the poor class people may be alleviated.
Unexpectedly, apart from failing to drop,
the prices of daily necessaries have been on the increase.
The price of rice exceeded the limit yesterday, while the
prices of bean curd and other foodstuffs will be increased
as from February 26. In the eyes of the traitorous
merchants law does not exist. It is not known whether
the Settlement authorities will exercise their power to
give practical suppression of the traitorous merchants.
The residents have heard enough of the high
tunes of the Settlement authorities to keep down the prices
of commodities; now they want to see how the Settlement
authorities will fulfill their promise so as to preserve
their prestige.

《华中日报》、《国民日报》及《新中国日报》：-

上海市粮食管制委员会将购买80万包大米供应本地居民

由于奸商操纵活动，米价持续上涨，导致贫民和薪金阶层难以维持生计。为了调节粮食供应并安抚民心，从而使米价逐渐下降，上海市政府市长陈公博与各地方团体及银行界合作，成立了上海市粮食管制委员会。各界已承诺提供1,900万美元资金。最近，委员会举行会议，讨论了有关购买大米的措施。
据悉，委员会决定首先购买80万包大米。这批大米将于本月底或3月中旬运抵上海，届时将以成本价出售，因为委员会的目标是调节粮食供应并增加上海的稻米库存。

《中美日报》（短评）：-

租界当局应取缔奸商以维护其威信

数日前我们曾向当局请愿，鉴于法币价值上升，应保持商品价格低位，以减轻贫苦阶层的负担。
出乎意料的是，日用必需品的价格非但没有下降，反而一直在上涨。昨日米价超出限额，而豆腐及其他食品的价格将从2月26日起上涨。在奸商眼中，法律并不存在。不知租界当局是否会行使权力，切实取缔奸商。
居民们已听够了租界当局关于压低商品物价的高调；现在他们想看看租界当局如何履行承诺，以维护其威信。

Between 4 p.m. and 5.45 p.m. October 2,
1939, thirty five representatives of the seven
different rice dealers' organizations in Shanghai
held a meeting in the office of the Bean and Rice
Hong Owners' Guild, 15 Avenue Edward VII, with Ying
Ts Kong (邢志剛), committee member of the guild,
presiding. A set of provisional regulations
governing business transactions between rice dealers
at the Rice Market were discussed and passed.
Among these regulations are the following
articles :-
1. Only business transactions are to be conducted
at the Rice Market, but no speculations are to
be allowed.
2. Rice merchants or brokers should sell rice only
to the hongs at the Rice Market.
3. Rice shops should purchase rice from the hongs
at the Rice Market.
4. Offenders of any of these regulations will be
refused transactions at the Rice Market or be
given due punishment.

Yu Jen-ying (俞人英 ), editor of the paper, was called
to Headquarters on September 7 when he was asked as to
the source of the information. He stated that it was
reproduced from a report appearing in the "Chinese-
American Daily News" (中美日報) of August 26, 1939.
The "Chinese-American Daily News" of that
date was examined and it was found to contain a report
which says:- "Yesterday a box for complaints was
installed at the rice mart in the hope of receiving
complaints against rice hoarding. Any reports so
submitted will be submitted to the authorities for
necessary action."
As the text of the article in the "Hsin Hwa
Pao" is at great variance with that appearing in the
"Chinese-American Daily News", it is obvious that the
editor of the mosquito paper, while reproducing the
report, had not faithfully followed the original text.
The editor who called at Headquarters on
September 8 was warned that whether or not he had copied
the news item from another paper he would be held equally
responsible for publishing any inaccurate or objectionable
matter contained therein.

由 D.S.I. Golder 撰写并转发。

就附上的1939年8月29日小报《新华报》（Hsin Hwa Pao）刊登的关于米市状况报道的译文而言，该报编辑俞人英（Yu Jen-ying）于9月7日被传唤至总部，询问信息来源。他称这是转载自1939年8月26日《中美日报》（Chinese-American Daily News）的一篇报道。
经查阅当日的《中美日报》，发现其中含有一篇报道，内容如下：“昨日米市安装了一个投诉箱，希望能收到针对囤积居奇行为的投诉。任何此类提交的报告将呈交当局采取必要行动。”
由于《新华报》文章的文本与《中美日报》刊登的内容大相径庭，显然该小报编辑在转载报道时并未忠实遵循原文。
9月8日到访总部的编辑受到警告，无论他是否从其他报纸抄录新闻，他都将对发布其中任何不准确或令人反感的内容承担同等责任。

August 29, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Hsin Hwa (新華 ), a mosquito paper, publishes the following
articles

AUTHORITIES INSTALL BOX FOR COMPLAINTS AGAINST
UNSCRUPULOUS RICE MERCHANTS

The authorities have enforced a re-registration
of the shops in the Rice Market and have thoroughly
investigated the source of supplies owned by rice merchants
as well as the hongs or shops undertaking the sale of rice
supplies. At the same time, they have installed a box
for complaints and in case the public had reliable
information on the hoarding of rice supplies by unscrupulous
merchants, they could write a complaint containing detailed
particulars and send it to this box so that the authorities
might impose punishment upon these unscrupulous merchants
when the complaints had been found true.

Translation of letter received at the Rice Market
on August 5, 1939

To the authorities,

Of late, newspapers report that secret
transactions in rice have recently taken place in the
Rice Market at higher prices and on a large scale.
This is due to the sudden decrease in the stocks stored
in godowns. The present stock in godowns is only
sufficient for one month's consumption locally. As the
population in Shanghai is huge, how can the situation
be relieved? The source of supply for Shanghai is
in Japanese occupied areas and therefore beyond the
power of the Settlement authorities. As these areas
are controlled by the "dwarf slaves", documents or
permits issued by the Settlement authorities authorizing
the transportation of rice are of little use and would
point to a blockade but this I think is well known to
you.

Now the situation is serious. It is apparent
that the Council cannot help in the matter. Saigon Rice
when imported to Shanghai will cost too much. The Council
is unable to maintain a level in prices and hardships will
be experienced by both the Chinese and foreign community.

Hoping that steps will be taken by the Council
to relieve the situation and awaiting the effect of your
administrative power.

Chang Tseng (签名), an

1939年8月5日米市收到信件的译文

致当局：

近来，报纸报道米市近期发生了大规模、高价的秘密大米交易。这是由于仓库储存量突然减少所致。目前仓库的库存仅够本地一个月的消费。鉴于上海人口众多，如何缓解这一局势？上海的供应来源位于日军占领区，因此超出了租界当局的管辖能力。由于这些地区由“倭奴”控制，租界当局签发的授权运输大米的文件或许可证几乎无用，且会指向封锁行动，但这点我想你们早已知晓。

目前局势严峻。显然，工部局在此事上无能为力。西贡大米进口到上海的成本过高。工部局无法维持价格水平，华洋社群都将遭受困难。

希望工部局采取措施缓解局势，并期待贵方行政权力发挥作用。

张增（签名），一

on August 3 and obtained a sample of rice from the

主题：关于以高于限价进行大米交易的查询。

由 Crawford 警督制作并转呈

1939年8月4日上午10时45分，两名大米经纪人在福州路米市被指控以每“石”23.00美元的价格进行大米交易，比上海公共租界工部局设定的限价高出3美元。

这两人分别是符夢熊 (Voo Mong Yoong)，九江路大陆商场福都街11号大中商品服务社经理，以及朱濟平 (Tsu Chi Ping)，海宁路宝珠里27号。两人于中午12时被带至总局接受讯问。经对案件仔细调查，发现另外两名在米市经营的经纪人張君孝 (Chang Chung-fah) 和姚洪濤 (Yao Hung-dao) 向管理层举报，称他们听到上述两人以每“石”23.00美元的价格交易大米，随后管理层通知了警方。现查明，大中商品服务社根据合同向商务印书馆的员工供应大米，为履行该合同，在需要300“石”而仅有200“石”库存的情况下，经理符夢熊 (Voo Mong-yoong) 前往米市，意图购买合同所需的必要数量。此时，符某不知情的情况下，举报人张某于8月3日前往大陆商场的大中商品服务社办公地点，并从该公司员工处获取了一份大米样品带走。（张某显然知晓与商务印书馆的合同及库存短缺情况）。随后在8月4日上午，他带着样品来到米市，看到符某正与经纪人朱濟平交谈，便指控其以每“石”23美元的价格出售大米，并立即出示样品包向管理层举报。深入调查该指控后发现，举报人張君孝不久前曾试图因市场价差向商务印书馆出售大米，但未成功，该交易最终由商品服务社的符某完成，因此该指控似乎是出于此怨隙。所有相关人员的陈述相互矛盾极大，而经理的陈述在大多数方面被证实更为真实，据此看来，整个案件似乎是一起个人报复事件。

在此次调查中发现，米市的运作存在诸多不足之处。第二名被告朱濟平目前失业，但此前受雇于新闸路亚兴米行担任经纪人，该行已停业两个月，在此期间他获发了米市通行证，但该通行证从未被收回。据信，此人一直在市场外私下与小客户进行小规模生意，每天虽出席米市，但从未进行任何交易。

Information has been received to the
effect that transactions in rice have been conducted
in Room 202, Grand Hotel, 120 Yu Ya Ching Road,
and enquiries made by this office have discovered
that Room 202 Grand Hotel was rented in July, last
year, by one Chang Hai-keng (張海根), native of
Sungkiang and another Chang Ah-doo (張阿大) alias
Doo Ah Koo (大阿哥), native of Shanghai, both of
whom are owners of boats engaged in the transportation
of rice to Shanghai from that area on behalf of the
rice merchants.

According to one of the waiters in the
Grand Hotel, Room 202 has been frequented by rice
merchants as well as managers and proprietors of
rice shops and transactions in rice have been
conducted there. During the past two or three
weeks, more rice shop people have been visiting this
place mostly in the forenoon and around mid-day.
Rice merchants on whose behalf the rice was transported
often stay in this room and play "mah-jong" on a
fairly large scale every day.

A visit was paid to the room in question
on August 2 and it was discovered that there was a
sample packet of white Chinese rice on the table,
which according to Chang Hai-keng (張海根), the
occupier, was a sample taken from the Rice Market.
At the time of the visit, four persons appearing to
be managers of rice shops or hongs were playing

据大饭店的一名服务员称，米商以及米店经理和店主经常光顾202室，并在那里进行大米交易。在过去两三周内，更多米店人员访问此地，大多在上午和中午左右。代表其运输大米的米商经常住在这个房间，并且每天进行规模相当大的“麻将”游戏。

Subject Observation duty at Rice Market, Foochow Road.

Made by D.P.S. Killingbeck    Forwarded by C. Crawford

On July 17, 18 and 19, 1939, between 9.30 a.m.
and 11.30 a.m., D.I. Pan Lien-pih and D.P.S. Killingbeck
attended the Rice Exchange Market, held on the third
floor of a teashop at 519 Foochow Road. Also present
for periods during the three days were C.I. Pao, Insp.
Boorman and S.I. Shao from Louza Station.

Business was carried on as usual, and no
untoward incident occurred at any time. The total amount
of rice sold during the session was 49,700 "zars", of
this amount, 16,100 "zars" were sold on July 17, 15,400
"zars" on July 18 and 18,200 "zars" on July 19.

The controlled price limit of $20.00 per "zar"
for white Chinese rice (Kan Mee), and $16.00 per "zar"
for another kind of Chinese rice known as "See Mee"
was adhered to, and rice was sold at the following
prices :-

Translation of letter to Chinese Deputy 27
Secretary from Shanghai Bean and Rice
Dealers' Association.
Dated 19th January, 1938.

Rice Dealers: Stabilization of prices

After the "United Rice Market" formed by rice
dealers in Nantao and Chapei suspended operations in
October last year, there have been very few transactions
in rice; meanwhile the dealers' employes have gradually
dispersed. Though large quantities of Chinese rice have
now arrived in Shanghai; it is regrettable that there is
no market for it. The dealers now propose to use every
morning from the 15th instant and the 2nd floor , Ch'ing
Li Koh, Foochow Road, as a gathering place where they
may make transactions and devise measures for the
stabilization of price. Besides, they may take the
opportunity to foster friendly relations and to provide
their former employes with employment. Will you therefore
kindly instruct the various Police Stations to accord them
protection.

(Chopped) Fu Zi-keng
Director of Shanghai Rice Dealers' Market

(Note: Received for translation p.m., 21st Jan. 1938.)

米商：稳定价格

自去年十月南市和闸北米商组成的“联合米市”停止运作以来，大米交易寥寥无几；与此同时，米商的雇员已逐渐离散。尽管目前大量国产大米已运抵上海，但遗憾的是有货无市。米商现提议自本月15日起，每天上午利用福州路庆利阁二楼作为聚集场所，进行交易并制定稳定价格的措施。此外，他们可借此机会增进友好关系，并为以前的雇员提供就业机会。因此，恳请指示各警察分局给予他们保护。

（盖章）傅子庚
上海米业市场董事

Made by. C.D.I...Kuh Pao Hwa............Forwarded by....D.S.I...Wilcox

The following notice was published by Tsu Ts
Shiang (朱子香) in the advertisement columns of
the "Sin Wan Pao" dated September 11, 1941 :-

"In March this year I was attacked by my
old disease and on this account I resigned
from my posts (committee member) in the Bean
& Rice Hong Owners' Guild and the Shanghai
Cereal Dealers' Guild. Since then I have not
taken part in any organization.

"Of late, however, my condition has become
so much worse that I have been compelled to
enter hospital to receive treatment. I have
to express my sincere gratitude for the visits
paid by my relatives and friends, but owing to
strict restrictions placed by the hospital
regulations, I am unable to receive them. I
publish this notice requesting my relatives
and friends not to call on me."

Notice by Chang Nyien Sien

The following notice was published by Chang Nyien
Sien (張念萱) in the advertisement column of the
"Shun Pao", dated July 16, 1941 :-

"Last Summer, I was afflicted with a disease
resembling apoplexy. After several months' treatment,
my condition gradually improved. Since this Summer,
I have again felt tired and weak in mind and body.
According to my medical doctor's diagnosis, it is the
symptom of my old disease and a long rest is necessary.
In compliance with the doctor's instructions, I have
wound up all my business and resigned from the post of
Chairman of the Shanghai Municipality Rice Shop Owners'
Guild. Hereafter, I shall devote my whole attention to
the recuperation of my health. I therefore publish
this notice for the information of my relatives and
friends."
pages.zh:
张念萱的告示

张念萱在1941年7月16日的《申报》广告栏中发布了以下告示：

“去年夏天，我患上了类似中风的疾病。经过几个月的治疗，病情逐渐好转。今年夏天以来，我又感到身心疲惫虚弱。据医生诊断，这是旧病复发的症状，需要长期休息。遵照医嘱，我已结束所有业务，并辞去了上海市米店业主公会主席的职务。今后，我将全心致力于休养康复。特此登报声明，以供亲友知悉。”

pages.en:
Notice by Ghui Tseng Hwa

The following notice was inserted by Ghui Tseng
Hwa ( 瞿振華 ) in the advertisement columns of the
"Sin Yan Pao"and "Cheng Yien Pao", dated July 17, 1941 :-
"Yesterday I received a letter from a certain
body.
Regarding the matter, I have no interest
in it nor have I any knowledge about it. I have taken
no part in outside affairs for a long time and I have
published notices to this effect in the newspapers on
several occasions.
I hereby publish this notice again for the
information of the public."
pages.zh:
瞿振华的告示

瞿振华在1941年7月17日的《新燕报》和《诚言报》广告栏中刊登了以下告示：
“昨日我收到某团体的来信。
关于此事，我既无兴趣，也不知情。我已久不参与外界事务，并曾多次在报纸上刊登此类声明。
现再次登报声明，以告公众。”

pages.en:
Notice by Ching Peng Zung

The following notice was inserted by Ching Peng
Zung ( 金本仁 ) in the advertisement columns of the
"Sin Wan Pao", dated July 17, 1941 :-

"As a merchant, it has been my aim to devote
my whole attention to my own business. I have never
taken part in any outside affairs. Lest the people in
outside circles should not know the truth, thus giving
rise to misunderstandings, I hereby publish this notice
for public information."
pages.zh:
金本仁的告示

金本仁在1941年7月17日的《新闻报》广告栏中刊登了以下告示：

“身为商人，我一向致力于专心经营自己的业务。我从未参与任何外界事务。唯恐外界人士不明真相，从而产生误解，特此登报声明，以告公众。”

S.I., Special Branch........Sxxxxx File No.................... Date....May 21, 1941.........

SUBJECT: Joint Meeting of Rice Dealers' Organizations

Seven committee members of the Bean and Rice
Hong Owners' Guild, Cereal Dealers' Guild and the Rice
Market Control Committee held a joint meeting in the
office of the first mentioned body, 15 Avenue Edward
VII, between 4.30 p.m. and 5.40 p.m. May 20, with Mr.
Kiang Hung Ping (江鴻斌) presiding. The following
resolutions were discussed and passed :-

1. That in reply to a query from the French Police
regarding reasonable profit on rice imported to
Shanghai, a letter be addressed to the French Police
informing them that the dealers would be satisfied
if they could earn a net profit of 5% after defraying
expenses incurred and making good the loss of weight.

2. That in connection with the recent increase in
storage charges by the godowns, including Roosevelt
Terminal, Butterfield & Swire, etc., letters be
jointly addressed by rice dealers' organizations
and other bodies to the godown owners, protesting
against the increase.

3. That the Rice Brokers' Lien Nyi Society, 16 Rue de
la Porte du Nord, be instructed that with a view
to preventing rice transactions from being carried
out in the Provisions Market, 15 Avenue Edward VII,
in the afternoons, no brokers be allowed to enter
that Market, and that pickets be detailed by the
Society for the purpose of keeping a sharp watch.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE）

March 15, 1941.

Shanghai Bean & Rice Hong Owners'
Guild and Cereal Dealers' Guild-
joint meeting.

Fifteen committee members of the Shanghai
Bean & Rice Hong Owners' Guild and the Shanghai
Cereal Dealers' Guild held a joint meeting in their
offices, 15 Avenue Edward VII, between 4.30 p.m.
and 5.30 p.m. February 14. Mr. Ying Ts Kong
(邢志剛) presided and stated that letters had
been received from Mr. Chen Ts Yi (陳子彝),
Chairman of the Bean & Rice Hong Owners' Guild,
and Mr. Tsu Ts Shiang (朱子香), Chairman of the
Cereal Dealers' Guild, to the effect that owing to
adverse public criticism they had decided to resign
from the posts of Chairmen of their respective
guilds. The committee decided to return the letters
to the senders together with a conciliatory letter
requesting that the Chairmen re-consider their
intentions to resign and resume the office which they
now hold.

Mr. Voo Chien Keng (符前耕), Chairman
of the Rice Market, informed the meeting that he
and two other representatives of the Rice Price
Adjustment Committee had called on Mr. T.K. Ho,
Deputy Secretary of the S.M.C. on March 13 and
requested that the price limits fixed by the Price
Adjustment Committee be removed in order to eradicate
black market dealings. Mr. Ho, in reply, stated
that a formal letter regarding the proposed
cancellation of the fixed prices should be addressed
to the Council by the Rice Price Adjustment Committee.

1941年3月15日。

上海豆米业公所和粮食业同业公会-
联席会议。

2月14日下午4时30分至5时30分，上海豆米业公所和上海粮食业同业公会的十五名委员在爱多亚路15号的办公室举行联席会议。邢志剛 (Ying Ts Kong) 先生主持，并声明收到豆米业公所主席陳子彝 (Chen Ts Yi) 先生和粮食业同业公会主席朱子香 (Tsu Ts Shiang) 先生的来信，称由于公众舆论批评不利，他们决定辞去各自公会的主席职务。委员会决定将信件连同和解信一并退回给发件人，请求主席们重新考虑辞职意向，并恢复其现任职务。

米市主席符前耕 (Voo Chien Keng) 先生向会议通报，他和米价调整委员会的另外两名代表于3月13日拜访了工部局副秘书长 T.K. Ho 先生，并要求取消价格调整委员会规定的限价，以根除黑市交易。Ho 先生回复称，关于拟议取消固定价格的正式信函应由米价调整委员会致送工部局董事会。

S.I, Special Branch
REPORT
Date Feb. 26, 1941.

Subject Rice Situation - Representation of rice dealers to
Council.

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum

At 10 a.m. February 25, Mr. Chen Ts Yi
(陳子彝) of the Bean & Rice Hong Owners' Guild,
Mr. Tsu Ts Chiang (朱子青) of the Shanghai Cereal
Dealers' Guild and Mr. Voo Chien Keng (符前耕),
Chairman of the Rice Market, called on Mr. T.K. Ho,
Deputy Secretary of the S.M.C. in the Administration
Building and submitted to him the following requests:
(A) That the Council appoint representatives to
co-operate with members of the rice trade
organizations for the purpose of investigating
rice stocks stored in various godowns in
Shanghai.
(B) That the Hongkong authorities be requested to
permit the exportation of rice to Shanghai.

In connection with "A", the representatives
of the Guilds proposed to conduct an investigation
into the stocks of rice stored in the various
godowns in Shanghai, subsequent to which holders
of stocks were to be instructed to sell in the
market. In addition, the guilds proposed to have
published a notification to the effect that rice
involved in sales transacted prior to February 24
must be taken delivery of by February 27, and that
failing to do so, the bargain money paid ($5 per bag)
would be confiscated and the rice re-sold to other
persons. A notice to the above effect to be posted
in the Rice Market, 515 Foochow Road, on the morning
of February 26.

REPORT
Date Feb. 12, 19 41.
Subject Press report regarding private transactions at
the Provisions Market at 15 Avenue Edward VII.
Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Tabrum

Reference the attached translation of a
newspaper report appearing in the Chinese press
on February 8, 1941 regarding secret rice
transactions in progress during afternoons at
the Market at 15 Avenue Edward VII: Enquiries
show that it is the Provisions Market operated
jointly by the Cereal Dealers' Guild and the
Bean & Rice Hong Owners' Guild for wholesale
business in rice, bean, oil, wheat, flour and
other cereals and that the Market is opened both
in the forenoon and the afternoon for the
convenience of the dealers. Two rooms have been
set aside exclusively for rice transactions in
the afternoons (not "secret rooms" as mentioned
in the attached translation). However, during
the latter part of 1940, rice dealings at the
Provisions Market were on such a large scale that,
to prevent speculation, the Cereal Dealers' Guild
and the Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Guild decided
at a joint meeting on December 4, 1940, that all
rice transactions be conducted at the Rice Market
at 515 Foochow Road, which is open in the forenoon
in order to facilitate control, and that transactions
at the Provisions Market at 15 Avenue Edward VII
in the afternoon be strictly prohibited. This
decision was accordingly enforced and the two rooms
locked up.

主题 关于爱多亚路15号食品市场私下交易的新闻报道。
由首席侦探督察 Tabrum 制作并转发

参照所附译文，该译文出自1941年2月8日中文报刊上的一篇新闻报道，内容涉及爱多亚路15号市场下午正在进行的秘密大米交易：经查询，该市场是由粮食业同业公会和豆米业公所联合经营的食品市场，从事大米、豆类、油、小麦、面粉和其他谷物的批发业务，为方便商人，市场上午和下午均开放。另有两间房间专门用于下午的大米交易（并非如所附译文中所述的“密室”）。然而，在1940年下半年，食品市场的大米交易规模过大，为防止投机，粮食业同业公会和豆米业公所在1940年12月4日的联席会议上决定，所有大米交易均在福州路515号的米市进行，该市场上午开放以便于管制，并严格禁止下午在爱多亚路15号的食品市场进行交易。该决定随即得到执行，这两间房间也被锁闭。

S. 1. Special Branch.
February 10, 1941.

Shanghai Provisions Adjustment Committee
proposed formation reported in the newspaper.
--------------------------------------------------

With reference to the attached newspaper
translation on the proposed formation of a
"Provisions Adjustment Bureau", enquiries have
been made and the following ascertained.

In view of the abnormal increase in the price
of rice during the winter season, which is greatly
affecting the livelihood of the Chinese community,
Mayor Chen Kung Po of the Shanghai City Government
proposed to form a "Shanghai Provisions Adjustment
Committee ( 粮食調正局 )" with a
capital of $20,000,000 as a sinking fund for the
purpose of relieving the rice situation by
regulating the supply and price of rice in this
City. Regarding the project, Mayor Chen has
approached Messrs Nying Teh Kwong ( 岑德廣 )
and Zau Shih Chun ( 式軍 ), the former is
Chairman of the National Relief Committee of the
Nanking Government, and the latter is Chief of the
Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei Consolidated Tax Bureau
and concurrently Commissioner of the Revenue Bureau
attached to the Ministry of Finance, and they are
said to have promised to render their cooperation
and assistance, which, it is reported, would be
of value in facilitating the scheme. Mr. Nying,
by virtue of his position, can assist in obtaining
the requisite capital while Mr. Zau who is closely
related with the Japanese Special Service
Department and the Asia Development Board, may
be able to persuade the Japanese Authorities
concerned from being opposed to the project.

S. 1. 特科。
1941年2月10日。

报纸报道拟成立上海副食品调整委员会。
--------------------------------------------------

参照附件中关于拟成立“副食品调整局”的报纸译文，经查询，查明情况如下。

鉴于冬季大米价格异常上涨，严重影响了华人社群的生计，上海市政府市长陈公博提议成立“上海副食品调整委员会（粮食調正局）”，设立2000万美元作为平准基金，旨在通过调节本市大米的供应和价格来缓解大米局势。关于该项目，陈市长已接洽岑德广先生和鄒式軍先生，前者是南京政府全国救济委员会主席，后者是江苏浙江安徽统税局局长，兼任财政部所属税务局局长。据悉，他们已承诺提供合作与协助，据报道，这将有助于推动该计划。岑先生凭借其职位，可协助获得所需资金；而鄒先生与日本特务机关及兴亚院关系密切，或许能够说服相关日本当局不反对该项目。

pages.en:
- 2 -

Necessary arrangements are being made by Messrs
Nying and Zau with the Japanese authorities
and if permission is obtained from the Japanese
authorities to purchase the rice required for this
purpose from the rice-producing districts, the
said committee propose operating in March, 1941.
It is also reported that the Committee,
when established, will limit its relief work to the
occupied areas within the Shanghai Special Municipality
only.
It will be remembers that during 1939
Mr. Loo Ying (盧英), Commissioner of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, suggested the
purchase of rice from Wuhu for the purpose of
retailing same to his subordinates at a cheap
price, but his suggestions were rejected by the
Japanese and in view of this, it is generally
believed that the present proposal by Mayor Chen
to form a Provisions Adjustment Committee may not,
it is thought, materialize.

Certified true copy
CSC.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

岑先生和鄒先生正在与日本当局进行必要的安排，如果从日本当局获得许可，从产米区购买所需的大米，则该委员会拟于1941年3月开始运作。
另据报道，该委员会成立后，将其救济工作仅限于上海特别市内的占领区。
人们会记得，1939年间，上海市政府警察局局长卢英先生曾建议从芜湖购买大米，以便以低价零售给其下属，但该建议被日本人拒绝。有鉴于此，人们普遍认为，陈市长目前关于成立副食品调整委员会的提议可能无法实现。

核证无误副本
CSC.

National Herald :-
REPORT OF PROPOSAL OF A CERTAIN PARTY TO FORM A "PROVISIONS
ADJUSTMENT BUREAU"

According to information secured from
foreign circles, progressing at the same time as the plan
of the two Foreign Settlements to establish granaries for
the storage of provisions is the plan of officials of the
Shanghai City Government to form a "Provisions Adjustment
Bureau." It is learned that the officials are attempting to
raise a reserve fund of $20,000,000 for the purchase of rice
in the rice producing areas. The promoters of this plan
believe that if the Bureau can obtain sufficient Chinese rice
from the areas under their control, the price of rice will
drop.

People in commercial circles doubt whether
the Japanese will agree to the proposal of these officials.
It is learned that the Dah Chong Co. (大昌公司) which was
promoted in July last year by Chinese for the purpose of
transporting rice to Shanghai from rice producing areas, was
forced to close up owing to disagreement with the Japanese.
The officials of the City Government stated that the "Provisions
Adjustment Bureau" will sell out at its original price the
rice which it purchases from the rice producing areas. It
could not be ascertained yesterday whether the rice will be
entrusted to the two Foreign Settlements for sale.

《国民新闻报》：
某方提议成立“副食品调整局”的报道

据从外籍人士圈子获得的消息，与两个外国租界建立粮食仓库以储存副食品的计划同时进行的，还有上海市政府官员成立“副食品调整局”的计划。获悉这些官员正试图筹集2000万美元的准备金，用于在产米区购买大米。该计划的发起者认为，如果该局能从其控制区获得足够的中国大米，大米价格将会下降。

商界人士怀疑日本人是否会同意这些官员的提议。获悉去年7月由中国人发起成立的大昌公司（大昌公司），旨在从产米区向上海运输大米，但因与日本人意见不合而被迫关闭。市政府官员表示，“副食品调整局”将以原价出售其从产米区购买的大米。昨日尚无法查明大米是否将委托给两个外国租界进行销售。

Subject Sale of rice by Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association.
Made by and Forwarded by D. J. Crawford.

Reference the attached letter from the Price
Investigation Office to the A.C. (Social Branch)
regarding the sale of rice to Ningpo people by the
Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association, enquiries
show that the Association, for the benefit of Ningpo
residents in Shanghai, sold to them some 2,000 bags
of foreign rice in the months of October and November,
1940, at $78.75 per bag. This rice belonged to the
Ningpo Shaoshing Relief Association and was stored in
the Bank of China godown, 1040 North Soochow Road,
at the beginning of September, 1940. This rice was
bought by the Association for the relief of poor
people at Ningpo and Shaoshing but in consequence of
a blockade of the Chekiang coast by the Japanese,
was shipped to Shanghai. Through loss of weight
during transportation, many of the bags only weighed
about 200 lbs instead of the stipulated weight of
220 lbs, but the weight was brought up to 210 lbs.
(10 lbs less than stipulated) by the Association before
delivery was taken by the buyer.

At the same time, the Association also
conducted a registration of people desirous of buying
rice in a group purchase plan. The registration was
discontinued on December 4, 1940, when some 4,000
bags were registered for order and a deposit of $75.00
per bag was collected. It was the original intention
of the Association to order the rice from abroad

关于物价调查办公室致助理警司（特别课）的附信，提及宁波同乡会向宁波籍人士出售大米一事，经查询显示，该会为照顾在沪宁波居民，于1940年10月和11月期间，以每袋78.75美元的价格向他们出售了约2,000袋洋米。这批大米属于宁波绍兴救济协会，于1940年9月初存放在北苏州路1040号中国银行仓库。该会购买此米原旨在救济宁波和绍兴的贫民，但因日军封锁浙江海岸，故运至上海。由于运输途中重量损耗，许多米袋重量仅约为200磅，而非规定的220磅，但在买方提货前，该会将重量补足至210磅（比规定少10磅）。

同时，该会还针对希望参与集体购米计划的人员进行了登记。登记工作于1940年12月4日停止，当时已登记订购约4,000袋，并收取每袋75.00美元的定金。该会原计划通过一家进口商行从国外订购大米

Chief Health Inspector's Office,
January 21st, 1941.

The Commissioner of Public Health.

The Ningpo Dong Sgang Wen's Cheap rice.

This Guild under the patronage of Mr. Yu Ya Ching circulated
the information that cheap rice was available if any Ningpo
people would care to deposit $75.00 with them. They were told
the rice had not arrived and would be distributed at a cheap
rate so that if a balance remained this would be returned.

Our Office coolie with others deposited $75.00 on December
the 4th and was asked to call and take the rice as it had
arrived.

On going to take delivery he was told that the price now
was $99.30 for 2nd quality Saigon rice and that this money
must be handed in because the deposit could not be returned.

On going to the godown he was informed by the caretaker
that this rice was not fresh but had been in stock 5 months
already stored on the 2nd, floor. The weighed rice handed to
him amounted to only 210 lbs adv: only and it cost $3.00 for
transportation.

Other buyers were of the same opinion as our boy, i.e that
they have been meanly overcharged.

Sgn. J. E. Penman
Chief Health Inspector.

首席卫生视察员办公室，
1941年1月21日。

致公共卫生处处长。

关于宁波同乡会文氏廉价大米。

该会馆在虞洽卿先生的支持下散布消息，称若有宁波人愿意向其存入75.00美元，即可提供廉价大米。他们被告知大米尚未运到，将以低价分发，因此若有余额将予以退还。

我们办公室的一名苦力与其他人在12月4日存入了75.00美元，并被告知在大米运到后前来提货。

当他前去提货时，被告之现在二等西贡米的价格为99.30美元，且必须缴纳这笔钱，因为定金不予退还。

当他前往仓库时，看守人告知他这批大米不新鲜，已库存5个月，一直存放在二楼。交给他的过秤大米仅为210磅广告重量，且运费高达3.00美元。

其他买家的看法与我们的伙计相同，即他们认为被恶意多收了费用。

签名 J. E. Penman
首席卫生视察员。

January 3, 1941. Afternoon Translation.

Central China Daily News, Bing Pao and Kuo Min Daily News :-

THE SHANGHAI PROVISION CO-OPERATION ASSOCIATION

The Shanghai Provision Co-Operation Association was formally inaugurated on December 22, 1940. At 4 p.m. yesterday, a meeting was held by the Supervisory and Executive Committees of the Association at the Dent Moore Hotel, No. 35 Ningpo Road.

Yesterday a responsible member of the Association stated that the aim of the Association is to enable the middle and low class people to obtain rice at cheap prices.

The following are the regulations of the Association governing purchases of foreign rice:-
(1) The Association accepts orders for the purchase of provisions. If one to five bags of foreign rice are ordered, a sum of $20 for each bag of rice will be collected in advance. If six to twenty bags of foreign rice are ordered, a sum of $30 for each bag will be collected in advance. If more than 20 bags of foreign rice are ordered, a sum of $45 for each bag will be collected in advance.
(2) According to the regulations of the Association, regular members can order a bag of foreign rice for every $100 paid, while common members are permitted to order one bag. All members are exempt from paying the order money.
(3) If the Association is unable to buy foreign rice, order money received by the Association in advance will be returned accordingly. However, there will be no interest charged for the order money.
(4) If the amount of orders reaches a certain point, the Association will, according to the market rice, order foreign rice, which will be published in newspapers on the following day and the purchasers will be notified separately. The purchasers have the right to examine the original contracts and must observe the conditions in the contracts.
(5) The Association will insure the foreign rice on board ships and in godowns for the period between the dates of order and distribution. The Association will not compensate losses for any untoward incidents.
(6) Freight, premium expenses used in Customs and on wharves, godown charges, interests, shortage of quantity of rice, etc. required in the ordering of provisions will be proportionately covered by the purchasers.
(7) At the time when the ordered goods are about to arrive, the Association will notify the purchasers to pay the remainder. After receiving the notice of the Association, the purchasers have to pay the remainder to the designated office at a specified date.
(8) If the purchasers do not pay the remainder at the specified time, they have to cover the expenses arising in connection with this. If the purchasers do not give reasons as to the delay in paying godown charges, interests, premiums, etc., the Association will dispose of the goods. If there is any loss, the purchasers will have to bear it.

P.T.O.

《华中日报》、《平报》及《国民日报》：

上海粮食协进会

上海粮食协进会于1940年12月22日正式成立。昨日下午4时，该会监理委员会及执行委员会在宁波路35号登特摩尔饭店（Dent Moore Hotel）举行会议。

昨日，该会一位负责人称，该会的宗旨是使中下层民众能够以低廉价格购得大米。

以下是该会关于购买洋米的规定：
(1) 本会接受订购粮食之委托。若订购洋米一至五包，每包须预先缴纳20元。若订购洋米六至二十包，每包须预先缴纳30元。若订购洋米超过二十包，每包须预先缴纳45元。
(2) 根据本会规定，正式会员每缴付100元可订购一包洋米，而普通会员仅准许订购一包。所有会员均免缴订购手续费。
(3) 若本会无法购得洋米，所预收的订购款将如数退还。但订购款不计利息。
(4) 若订单数量达到一定数额，本会将视市面米价情况订购洋米，并于次日在报纸上刊登公告，同时分别通知购买者。购买者有权查阅原始合同，并必须遵守合同条款。
(5) 自订购之日起至分发之日止，本会将投保洋米在船舱及仓库期间的保险。对于任何意外事故造成的损失，本会不予赔偿。
(6) 订购粮食所需的运费、海关及码头保险费、仓租、利息、大米短少量等费用，将由购买者按比例分担。
(7) 当所订货物即将抵达时，本会将通知购买者支付余款。购买者在收到本会通知后，须于指定日期向指定办事处支付余款。
(8) 若购买者未在规定时间内支付余款，须承担由此产生的相关费用。若购买者未能就延迟支付仓租、利息、保险费等给出理由，本会将处置该批货物。如有任何损失，须由购买者承担。

January 3, 1941. Afternoon Translation.

With regard to the question of foodstuffs in Shanghai, the price of various grades of rice has been going up continuously and has reached a critical stage, because of hoarding of ready stock by the speculative rice worms. There has been great confusion in the transactions between rice shops, hongs and dealers in the mart, so that all kinds of illegal dealings have been effected. Unless such malpractice be suppressed, legal transactions in the rice mart will become affected, while the regulation of food supplies and the restriction upon the price of rice will be rendered difficult. For this reason, the authorities of the two Foreign Settlements have ordered the Rice Price Adjustment Committee to fix a new price limit and to prohibit rice brokers from practising in the rice mart for two weeks. After the enforcement of this measure, the transactions in the mart have appeared to be on the increase and samples of high grade of rice have been produced. Although there are still direct transactions between rice hongs and dealers, yet these have been reduced. The rice mart will be reopened to-day. It is expected that the price of rice may drop.

Since the authorities of the two Settlements have strictly curbed the illegal transactions and the Rice Price Adjustment Committee has fixed and published the new price limit, the price of rice has been gradually stabilized. Of late, with the efforts of authorities concerned, the arrival of Saigon rice will not cease. The rice ordered for this month will arrive soon. The speculative rice merchants dare not hold ready stocks on account of the strict orders of the authorities and the arrival of rice, and attempt to sell their stocks at a reduced price. The price of rice seems to be on the decline.

It is learned that the rice brokers are trying to enter the rice mart. It is hoped that the authorities will take notice of this and will not let them manipulate the price, so as to affect the food supplies and peace and order.

Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald, Cheng Yien Pao :-

With a view to introducing readjustment in the rice mart, the authorities of the two Foreign Settlements, together with the various rice trading bodies, have prohibited rice brokers from practising in the rice mart for a period of two weeks. As a result of this prohibition, the price of rice has been stabilized. However, following the adoption of this prohibition, the Rice Brokers' Lien-Nyi Society has approached various parties concerned for an earlier lifting of this prohibition, but its request has been turned down by the authorities, who have, at the same time, stipulated that rice brokers, when practising in the rice mart after the expiration of the period of the prohibition on January 10, should abide by the following rules:-
(1) No transactions beyond the price limit fixed by the Rice Price Adjustment Committee should be undertaken.
(2) No purchase of rice for non-rice merchants or speculators should be made.
Whoever violates these rules shall be subjected to the cancellation of the entry pass.
There are at present more than 500 rice brokers in Shanghai. Prior to the hostilities, the commission for every bag of rice transacted was $0.01; this has now been increased to $0.05 or $0.10. In addition to this increase, certain rice brokers have even been engaged in speculation in the rice mart. It was for this reason that the prohibition was instituted.
pages.zh:
1941年1月3日。下午译件。

关于上海的粮食问题，由于投机米商囤积现货，各级大米价格持续上涨，已达危急阶段。米店、商行与市场经销商之间的交易混乱不堪，致使各种非法交易得以进行。若不遏制此类弊病，米市的合法交易将受到影响，粮食供应的调控及米价的限制也将变得困难。为此，两租界当局命令米价调整委员会制定新的限价，并禁止米经纪人在米市执业两周。实施此项措施后，市场交易似乎有所增加，并出现了高等级大米的样品。虽然米行与经销商之间仍有直接交易，但已减少。米市将于今日重新开放。预计米价可能会下跌。

自从两租界当局严厉取缔非法交易，且米价调整委员会制定并公布新限价以来，米价已逐渐稳定。近来，在有关当局的努力下，西贡米的运抵并未中断。本月订购的大米即将运抵。由于当局严令以及大米陆续运到，投机米商不敢囤积现货，并试图降价抛售库存。米价似乎呈下降趋势。

据悉，米经纪人正试图进入米市。希望当局对此予以关注，不让他们操纵价格，从而影响粮食供应及治安秩序。

《中美日报》、《国民新闻报》、《诚言报》：

为了整顿米市，两租界当局联合各米业团体，禁止米经纪人在米市执业两周。由于这一禁令，米价得以稳定。然而，禁令实施后，米业同业公会已向有关各方交涉，要求提前解除禁令，但遭到当局拒绝。当局同时规定，米经纪人在1月10日禁令期满后至米市执业时，应遵守以下规则：
(1) 不得进行超出米价调整委员会所定限价的交易。
(2) 不得为非米商或投机者代购大米。
凡违反上述规则者，将被吊销入场证。

目前上海有米经纪人500多名。战前，每交易一包大米的佣金为0.01元；现已增至0.05元或0.10元。除了佣金的增加外，某些米经纪人甚至参与米市投机。这正是实施禁令的原因。

关于上海粮食问题，由于投机米商囤积现货，各级大米价格持续上涨，已达危急阶段。米店、商行与市场经销商之间的交易混乱不堪，导致各种非法交易盛行。若不遏制此类弊病，米市的合法交易将受到影响，粮食供应的调控及米价限制也将变得困难。为此，两租界当局命令米价调整委员会制定新的限价，并禁止米经纪人在米市执业两周。实施此项措施后，市场交易似乎有所增加，并出现了高等级大米的样品。虽然米行与经销商之间仍有直接交易，但已减少。米市将于今日重新开放。预计米价可能会下跌。

自两租界当局严厉取缔非法交易，且米价调整委员会制定并公布新限价以来，米价已逐渐稳定。近来，在有关当局的努力下，西贡米的到货并未中断。本月订购的大米即将运抵。由于当局严令以及大米到货，投机米商不敢持有现货，并试图降价抛售库存。米价似乎呈下降趋势。

据悉，米经纪人正试图进入米市。希望当局对此予以关注，不让他们操纵价格，以免影响粮食供应及治安秩序。

《中美日报》、《国民新闻报》、《诚言报》：

为了对米市进行调整，两租界当局会同各米业团体，禁止米经纪人在米市执业两周。由于这一禁令，米价得以稳定。然而，禁令实施后，米经纪人联义社向有关各方游说，要求提前解除禁令，但遭到当局拒绝。当局同时规定，米经纪人在1月10日禁令期满后至米市执业时，须遵守以下规则：
(1) 不得进行超出米价调整委员会所定限价的交易。
(2) 不得为非米商或投机者代购大米。
凡违反上述规则者，将被吊销入场证。

目前上海有米经纪人300多名。战前，每运输一袋大米的佣金为0.01元；现已增至0.05元或0.10元。除佣金增加外，某些米经纪人甚至参与米市投机。正是出于此原因，才实施了该项禁令。

pages.en:
$20,000,000 Mark Reached
In Rice Granary Funds

Merchants Here Give Full Co-operation To Rice
Granary Committee, Sign Up 200,000 Bags Of
Staple Product; Trade Is Restricted •

Approximately $20,000,000 were subscribed in Shanghai by various factories and commercial enterprises toward the establishment of a public rice granary here to hold 200,000 bags of rice it was reported yesterday. As an aftermath of the meeting of leading rice merchants with members of the S.M.C. and the F.M.C. on Christmas Eve when plans were discussed to put into operation a series of drastic measures to curb profiteering on the rice market, no rice salesmen were seen in the market yesterday as severe penalties were announced to be imposed on all those entering the market without authorization.

Rice Granary Plan
Meanwhile a committee to co-ordinate work in connection with the establishment of a rice granary was formed under the chairmanship of Mr. Yu Ya-ching consisting of nine persons which include representatives of the two foreign councils and members of the local guild.

Aimed to stabilize all prices of the staple product the committee announced yesterday that contributions were flowing in steadily so that yesterday some 200,000 bags of rice were already subscribed.

Restrictions Imposed
Yesterday marked the first day that unprecedented restrictions were imposed on all rice merchants so that all sellers of Siamese rice were forced to register their transactions with the market authorities in order to enable the Rice Price-Fixing Committee to keep a check on all sales being made at higher prices than those prescribed on December 9.

Despite all restrictions merchants were reluctant to sell any of their stocks of first grade native rice which remained unquoted yesterday with the second-grade native staple product selling at $98 to $103 per zah on the "black bourse." Similarly the first-grade Saigon variety transactions were few in the course of yesterday's sessions with most of the business confined to outside deals on the "black bourse."

Big Arrival Expected
The prices of rice here, however, are expected by most merchants to drop considerably in the near future as reports circulated here yesterday claimed that some 80,000 bags of first-grade Saigon rice are slated to arrive here during the first week of January. This batch purchased a few months ago at the price of $80 per bag is expected to bring down the prevailing price of $121.25 per bag of this variety quoted here to somewhere around $97 per bag or $77.60 per picul, well below the maximum price set by authorities.
