米仓基金达到
2000万元

本地商人全力配合米仓
委员会，认购20万袋主
食；贸易受到限制 •

据昨日报道，上海各家工厂和商业企业为在此建立公共米仓以储存20万袋大米，共认捐约2000万元。这是平安夜主要米商与工部局（S.M.C.）及公董局（F.M.C.）成员开会讨论实施一系列严厉措施以遏制米市牟取暴利的计划后的结果。由于宣布将对所有未经授权进入市场者施以严厉惩罚，昨日市场上未见任何米贩身影。

米仓计划
与此同时，成立了一个协调建立米仓相关工作的委员会，由虞洽卿先生担任主席，成员共九人，包括两外国租界当局的代表和本地同业公会成员。

该委员会旨在稳定主食的所有价格，昨日宣布捐款源源不断，因此昨日已认捐约20万袋大米。

实施限制
昨日标志着对全体米商实施前所未有的限制的第一天，所有暹罗米卖家被迫向市场当局登记其交易，以便米价核定委员会核查所有以高于12月9日规定价格进行的销售。

尽管有种种限制，商人们仍不愿出售任何一级国产米库存，昨日该品种未报价，而二级国产主食在“黑市”上的售价为每石98至103元。同样，昨日交易期间一级西贡米的交易寥寥无几，大部分业务局限于“黑市”上的场外交易。

预计大量到货
然而，大多数商人预计近期本地米价将大幅下跌，因为昨日流传的消息称，约8万袋一级西贡米定于1月第一周运抵上海。这批大米是几个月前以每袋80元的价格购买的，预计将使本地该品种大米每袋121.25元的现行价格降至每袋约97元或每担77.60元，远低于当局设定的最高限价。

pages.en:
Public Rice Granary
Approved At Meeting

Business Leaders Form Committee Of Nine
To Take Charge Of Operations; 200,000
Bags Of Rice To Be Raised Publicly

A public granary for the storage of 200,000 bags of rice in Shanghai was approved at a meeting of local business leaders held yesterday at the invitation of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

A committee of nine persons, including Messrs. Yu Ya-ching, T. K. Ho, Wang Yu-ching and others, was formed to take full charge of the operation of the public granary.

The 200,000 bags of rice will be subscribed by public bodies, guilds and stores, it was decided at yesterday's meeting. Mr. Yu Ya-ching will contribute 30,000 bags of rice, the Rice Guild 60,000 bags, the Bankers' Association 50,000 bags, the Cotton Mill Owners' Association 20,000 bags, the Flour Mill Owners' Association 10,000 bags and the Coal Merchants' Guild 5000 bags.

Other Contributions
Other contributions to the granary will include the New Pharmaceutical Factory Owners' Association 2500 bags, Sugar Merchants' Guild 1500 bags, Hardware Merchants' Guild 1500 bags, Woollen Piecegoods Merchants' Guild 1000 bags, Contractors' Guild 500 bags, and the Lumber Merchants' Guild 1000 bags.

The remaining 13,500 bags will be subscribed by tobacco factories and the local department stores.

Some important decisions were also made at yesterday's meeting of the committee for fixing rice prices in Shanghai.

It was decided that as from December 26, rice salesmen will not be allowed to enter the rice market for two weeks. Another decision was made to the effect that, with the exception of members of the Rice and Cereal Merchants' Guild, those persons wanting to sell Siamese rice in the market must first register with the controlling office of the market, so as to check any unofficial transactions of rice at prices higher than the fixed maximum level.

The third resolution taken was that prices fixed by the committee on December 9 will be strictly enforced from now on.

Prices Soar
First grade Saigon rice yesterday was selling at $110 while the best grade of native rice sold at $112 per 100 kilo. Over 30,000 bags of rice were expected to arrive in Shanghai today, it is reported.

The 85,000 bags of Saigon rice ordered by local merchants some time ago are due to arrive in Shanghai in the early part of January, as the French authorities have lifted the export ban. This first grade of cheap rice, bought in Saigon at $79-$80 per bag, should bring about a considerable drop in local rice prices, according to well-informed business circles.

Inferior Quality
Meanwhile, Chinese inhabitants in the two foreign controlled areas still found it difficult to obtain the basic grain at the maximum price set up by the S.M.C. A Chinese reporter of the Evening Post, who bought yesterday one sah of No. 1 Saigon Rice at $87, which is the maximum price allowed by the Committee, found that it was mixed with rice of inferior quality.

In the black market, all kinds of rice were still quoted at about $5 above the maximum per sah. Native rice, which was being used only by rich Chinese families, was quoted at $97 per sah, with no noted increase as the stocks were continuing to be smuggled into the two foreign controlled areas in considerable quantity.

公共米仓
在会议上获批准

商界领袖组成九人委
员会负责运营；公开
募集20万袋大米

昨日，应上海公共租界工部局邀请，本地商界领袖举行会议，批准在上海建立储存20万袋大米的公共米仓。

成立了一个由九人组成的委员会，全面负责公共米仓的运营，成员包括虞洽卿、何德奎（T. K. Ho）、王禹卿等先生。

昨日会议决定，这20万袋大米将由公共团体、同业公会和商店认捐。虞洽卿先生将认捐3万袋，米业同业公会6万袋，银行公会5万袋，棉纺厂业主协会2万袋，面粉厂业主协会1万袋，煤业同业公会5000袋。

其他捐款
对米仓的其他捐款还包括：新药厂业主协会2500袋，糖业同业公会1500袋，五金业同业公会1500袋，呢绒匹头业同业公会1000袋，营造业同业公会500袋，以及木材业同业公会1000袋。

剩余的13,500袋将由烟草厂和本地百货公司认捐。

昨日上海米价核定委员会会议也作出了一些重要决定。

决定自12月26日起，米贩两周内不得进入米市。另一项决定规定，除米粮业同业公会成员外，凡欲在市场出售暹罗米者，必须首先向市场管理机构登记，以核查任何以高于固定最高限价进行的非官方大米交易。

通过的第三项决议是，从现在起严格执行委员会于12月9日核定的价格。

价格飙升
昨日一级西贡米售价为110元，而最佳等级的国产米每百公斤售价为112元。据报道，预计今日将有超过3万袋大米运抵上海。

本地商人此前订购的85,000袋西贡米定于1月初运抵上海，因为法国当局已解除出口禁令。据消息灵通的商界人士称，这种在西贡以每袋79-80美元购买的一级廉价大米，应会导致本地米价大幅下跌。

质量低劣
与此同时，两外国管制区的中国居民仍难以按工部局设定的最高限价获得基本粮食。《晚报》的一名中国记者昨日以87元购买了一石一号西贡米，这是委员会允许的最高限价，但他发现其中混杂了劣质米。

在黑市上，各类大米的报价仍比最高限价每石高出约5元。仅富裕中国家庭使用的国产米报价为每石97元，由于库存继续大量走私进入两外国管制区，价格未见明显上涨。

Date December 19, 40.
REPORT
Subject Bean & Rice Hong Owners' Guild & the Cereal Dealers' Guild -
joint meeting.
Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

18 Committee members of the Bean & Rice Hong
Owners' Guild, held a joint meeting in their offices,
15 Avenue Edward VII between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. on
December 18, with Mr. Chen Ts Yi ( 陈子彝 ) presiding.
The present rice situation was discussed and the
following resolutions were passed :
1. That the following 5 persons be elected as members
of a committee to take charge of the proposed
reserve stock of rice.
1) Messrs Chen Ts Yi ( 陈子彝 ),
2) Yang Woo Tsing ( 杨阿清 ), 3) Chu Tee
Shiung ( 朱子香 ), 4) Chen Sz Teh ( 陈立德 ).
5) Ho Chu Sung ( 何振生 ).
2. That the Bean & Rice Hong Owners Guild and the
Cereal Dealers' Guild purchase 50,000 bags of rice
respectively towards the proposed reserve stock.
3. That a sum of $50,000 contribution towards the
winter relief and cheap sale of rice be solicited
from the public by members and that the contribu-
tions be divided into the following 5 grades :
a) $1000 b) $500 c) $300 d) $200 e) $100 .

C. Crawford
D. I.
A.C. (Special Branch)

Translation of notice issued by Bean & Rice Hong
Owners' Guild and Cereal Dealers' Guild dated
December 16, 1940

It is to be noted that the maximum prices
for the various grades of foreign rice have been
fixed and announced by the Rice Price Adjustment
Committee and the Board of Management of the Rice
Market. The price of rice has again shown an
upward tendency during the past few days, and with
a view to suppressing black market quotations above
the limit, an urgent meeting was held on December 1'
1940, by the Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Guild and
the Cereal Dealers' Guild, at which it was decided
that the management of the Rice Market be instructed
to closely watch the business transactions conducted
by brokers. Should a broker be found to have been
concerned in sales at prices above the limit and
the Rice Brokers' Association fail to report the
offence, the whole body of brokers will be prevented
from entering and doing business in the Market.

If a member of either the Bean and Rice
Hong Owners' Guild or the Cereal Dealers' Guild is
found to have committed the same offence, he shall
be referred to and dealt with by the authorities.
He shall further be expelled from the Rice Market and
dismissed from the membership of the Guild.

The above will be strictly enforced in
order to stabilize the price of rice and to suppress
black market quotations. All dealers are hereby
notified to pay attention.

需注意，各类洋米的最高限价已由米价调整委员会及米市场管理董事会确定并公布。过去几天米价再次呈现上涨趋势，为了抑制超过限价的黑色市场报价，豆米行号业公会与粮食同业公会于1940年12月1[原文如此]日召开紧急会议，决定指示米市场管理处密切监视经纪人进行的商业交易。若发现经纪人参与以超过限价的价格进行的销售，而米业经纪人协会未报告该违规行为，则全体经纪人将被禁止进入市场并在市场内做生意。

若发现豆米行号业公会或粮食同业公会的会员犯有同样的违规行为，将移交当局处理。此外，该会员将被逐出米市场，并被开除出公会会籍。

为稳定米价并抑制黑市报价，将严格执行上述规定。特此通知所有商贩注意。

Translation of notice issued by Rice Brokers'
Association dated December 17, 1940
--------

The price of rice has been on the upward
trend recently. With a view to assisting in
stabilizing the prices, the committee members of
this Association called an urgent meeting yesterday
afternoon (December 16) and decided that members
of the Association must wear "temporary" badges.
Brokers must refuse to accept any quantities of
rice consigned to them for sale by the owners, if
the price is above the limit. Failure to observe
will lead to their being punished and their passes
for admission to the Rice Market withdrawn.
Members are hereby notified to pay special attention
to this matter.

近期米价呈上涨趋势。为了协助稳定物价，本协会委员于昨日下午（12月16日）召开紧急会议，决定协会会员必须佩戴“临时”徽章。如果价格超过限价，经纪人必须拒绝接受货主委托出售的任何数量的大米。若不遵守，将受到处罚，并收回其进入米市场的通行证。特此通知会员特别注意此事。

Extract from Daily Rice Situation Report
of December 12, 1940.

Fourteen committee members of the Bean and Rice Hong
Owners' Guild and the Cereal Dealers' Guild held a joint
meeting in their offices, 15 Avenue Edward VII, between 4 p.m.
and 5 p.m. December 11. Mr. Chen Ts Yi (陳子彝), Chairman
of the first named body, presided. Measures were discussed to
stabilize the rice situation as it prevails locally and the
following resolutions were passed :-

1. In connection with the resolution passed at a meeting held
on December 9 in the S.M.C. Administration Building regarding
the payment of bargain money and the period of taking delivery,
it was decided that bargain money of $5.00 per bag be paid
on the day when transactions are settled and that the delivery
be made in accordance with the rules passed on May 8, 1940,
i.e. 50% of the price for rice sold without a delivery order and
80% for rice sold with a delivery order to be paid on the 5th
day and that the delivery of the rice must be taken within 10
days when the full price must be paid. Should the buyer
fail to take delivery within 10 days, the seller will be
permitted to sell the rice involved on the 11th day at the
prevailing market price, and any profit thus obtained will be
handed over to the buyer, and any loss sustained made good from
the money already paid by the buyer. The Board of Management
of the Rice Market will be instructed to strictly enforce this
rule on December 12 and the offending dealers will be referred
to the authorities to be dealt with.

2. That the dealers be notified to register with the Guilds
not later than December 14, 1940, the quantities of No. 1 Saigon
rice on order through import firms as well as the quantities
on forward sales.

3. A reply has been received from the Rice Brokers' Association
requesting that the passes for admission to the Provisions Market
at 15 Avenue Edward VII, issued to the brokers be not cancelled
and stating that the brokers will be instructed to cease all

Date Dec 5, 1940.

Subject Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Guild and Cereal Dealers'
Guild - joint meeting.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Fifteen committee members of the Bean and
Rice Hong Owners' Guild and the Cereal Dealers'
Guild held a joint meeting in their offices, 15
Avenue Edward VII, between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. on
December 4, with Mr. Chen Ts Yi (陳子藝) presiding.
The present rice situation was discussed and the
following resolutions were passed :-

1. That in connection with the proposal submitted
by Mr. Yu Ya Ching to the Shanghai Municipal
Council regarding the storage of 200,000 bags
of rice as a reserve stock, the rice trade agree
to purchase 60,000 bags towards that amount.
It is, however, suggested that the 60,000 bags to
be purchased for that purpose be allowed to
circulate in the market instead of being put
aside, as the dealers have not sufficient cash
on hand but the amount will be supplemented from
time to time in order to keep it at the stipulated
level.

2. That three representatives be detailed to report
the above decision to the Municipal Authorities
at 2.30 p.m. December 6.

3. That all rice transactions be carried out at
the Rice Market at 515 Foochow Road in the
forenoon, and that transactions at the Provisions
Market at 15 Avenue Edward VII in the afternoon
be strictly prohibited. That no rice brokers
be allowed to operate at the Provisions Market

Rice: Excessive advance in prices.

In the last few days the price of rice has
advanced steadily, and there is no way to check the
increase. Although the Price Fixing Committee has raised
the maximum price allowed, as in accordance with the
Council's instructions, the price of rice continues its
upward trend. Market quotations to-day (the 5th) are
particularly high, first grade Saigon being quoted at
$67 or $68, which by far exceeds the limit of $61.50
fixed by the Committee. Even inferior qualities can hardly
be obtained for the maximum price.

Our members are retailers who supply the grain
direct to the public. They have now to purchase inferior
stocks at the maximum price, and, even though the stocks
are sold at a loss, the public will be liable to misunder-
stand the situation and blame the shops. At the present time
when the prices of all commodities are rising rapidly, the
poor are suffering acutely. If the price of rice is
allowed to rise without restriction, one cannot imagine
what may happen to the livelihood of the people. Our
members are labouring under extreme difficulties. If this
state of affairs continues without any steps being taken
to afford relief, the mass of the poor will be unable to
find food. The weaker will die of starvation and the
stronger will be driven to desperation. Peace and good
order will be affected.

本会会员为直接向公众供应粮食的零售商。他们现在不得不以最高限价购买劣质库存，即使亏本出售，公众也可能会误解情况并责怪店铺。在当前所有商品价格迅速上涨之际，穷人深受其苦。如果任由米价无限制上涨，不堪设想民众的生计将会如何。本会会员正面临极大的困难。如果这种状况持续下去而不采取任何救济措施，广大贫民将无法获得食物。弱者将饿死，强者将被逼入绝境。治安与秩序将受到影响。

Rice prices.

The market prices of rice is advancing continually.
Quotations for illegal transactions are so high that utter
confusion prevails in the market.

On the 5th instant we submitted a report to the Council
with a request for remedial measures. At a meeting held on
the 6th, the Rice Price Fixing Committee decided to maintain
the fixed price by notifying the market to strictly observe
restrictions. Unexpectedly, on the 7th (Saturday), the
price for illegal transactions advanced by $2. Our members are
unable to purchase any rice in the market at the price fixed
by the Price Fixing Committee. Unofficial quotations continue
to exceed the price limit.

Should no steps be taken to remedy the situation, our
member shops will be unable to bear the losses resulting from
the necessity of purchasing at a high price and selling at a
low price. There is no alternative but to sell out all the
present stocks and then suspend business to avoid further
loss. However, as rice is a vital necessity, suspension of
the rice business will immediately cause a panic, which will
in turn seriously affect peace and good order. Perceiving
that the situation is fraught with grave danger, we beg to
make direct representations to the Council.

In view of the gravity of the food problem, please
issue a stern warning to the rice market to take effective
steps to re-adjust matters and suppress all attempts to raise
the price by unofficial quotations. All transactions must be
made at the prices fixed by the Price Fixing Committee, and the
principle of "dealers selling to buyers and buyers selling to
shops" must be strictly enforced.

米价。

米的市场价格持续上涨。非法交易的报价如此之高，以致市场陷入极度混乱。

本月5日，我们向工部局提交了一份报告，请求采取补救措施。在6日举行的会议上，米价平抑委员会决定通过通知市场严格遵守限制来维持固定价格。出乎意料的是，7日（星期六），非法交易的价格上涨了2美元。本会会员无法以米价平抑委员会规定的价格在市场上买到任何大米。非官方报价继续超过价格上限。

如果不采取措施纠正这种情况，本会会员店铺将无法承受因高价买入、低价卖出而造成的损失。别无选择，只能售罄现有库存然后停业，以避免进一步损失。然而，由于大米是生活必需品，米业停业将立即引起恐慌，进而严重影响治安与秩序。鉴于局势充满严重危险，我们谨直接向工部局提出交涉。

鉴于粮食问题的严重性，请向米市场发出严厉警告，采取有效措施调整事态，压制所有通过非官方报价抬高价格的企图。所有交易必须按照米价平抑委员会规定的价格进行，并严格执行“商贩卖给买家，买家卖给店铺”的原则。

The sale of rice by one hong to another, sometimes
referred to as "passing the ball", should be rigorously prohibited
so that hoarding and speculation may be prevented, the advance

The food problem is of vital importance to the entire
public. As further exploitation of the rice market will cause
serious harm to the community, the Council is hereby requested
to establish an "official hong" to control the rice business
so that food supplies for the public may be regulated.
Please carry out the measures suggested.

(Chopped) Shanghai Rice Shops' Association.

Subject. Proposed formation of a "Rice Co-operative Society".

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

(Vide Special
Branch reports
dated 31/3/40
& 2/4/40).

In connection with the proposal of Mr. Kwei
Yien Fang ( 芳 ) regarding the formation
of a rice co-operative society, which was referred
to the Shanghai Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Guild
for discussion by the Shanghai Municipal Council,
a copy of the proposal has been obtained and is
attached together with translation.

The Bean and Rice Hong Owners' Guild has now
obtained the views of the various rice dealers'
organizations in Shanghai in connection with the
proposal and a reply has been prepared for
submission to the Shanghai Municipal Council. This
reply points out that the formation of such a
co-operative society is inadvisable and explains the
reason for this stand :-

a) According to the proposal submitted, the
Society should raise a capital of $20,000,000
from amongst the dealers connected with
the rice trade in Shanghai. Dealers in
Shanghai including the rice shops, hongs
and merchants engaged in importing rice
state they are not in a position to raise
such a large sum and in addition this sum
is considered insufficient to ensure a
stock of three months being kept on hand.
Such a stock would be in the region of
1,000,000 "zars" and require $50,000,000.

Copy out.

关于桂延芳（Kwei Yien Fang）先生提出的组建米业合作社的建议，上海公共租界工部局已将其转交上海豆米业公会讨论，现已取得该建议书副本，附后并附译文。

豆米业公会目前已就该项建议征询了上海各米商组织的意见，并拟定了一份回复提交上海公共租界工部局。该回复指出，组建此类合作社并不适宜，并阐述了持此立场的理由：-

a) 根据所提交的建议，合作社应向上海米业相关的经销商筹集资本2,000万元。上海的经销商，包括米店、米行以及从事大米进口的商人，均表示无力筹集如此巨款；此外，这笔款项被认为不足以确保维持三个月的库存。这样的库存量约为100万“包”（zars），需要资金5,000万元。

L. I.

April 5, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Pac :-

FORMATION OF RICE TRANSPORTATION AND SALE CO-OPERATIVE
SOCIETY SUGGESTED

(Concluded from yesterday's translation)

(7) The society will fix the prices of native rice and foreign rice for sale in the two Foreign Settlements according to the grades (it may be either done every day or once in three days) and publish these prices in newspapers. The prices will include suitable profits. For instance, the profit for the best quality rice is $4 per "zar," the profit for the second grade rice will be $2, while the profit for the third grade rice will be $1 or even $0.50. The consumers of the best quality rice are rich people and will not mind if more profits are taken from them, but the profits to be taken from the ordinary quality rice should be made as low as possible, for most of the consumers are poor people.

(8) Rice shops that join the society as shareholders will be given rice according to their business and capital and should sell the rice to the people according to the prices fixed by the society. The shops must not raise the price secretly or sell rice of insufficient weight, etc. Frauds discovered will lead to a severe fine. The Settlement authorities will be petitioned to withdraw the business licences of rice shops for repeated offences.

(9) Rice shops that join the society as shareholders should not conduct private transactions. When a shop is found to have done so, its shares in the society will be confiscated and in addition, the Settlement authorities will be requested to deal with it severely.

(10) Rice shops that join the society as shareholders will secure suitable profits by undertaking the sale of rice. As rice hongs will not be able to do any business because the right of transportation and sale is held by the society, the society will take out 10% from the total profits of the business and rice hongs that join the society as shareholders may enjoy this.

(11) Within a week after the establishment of the society, all rice stocks in the Foreign Settlements should be reported to the society and the latter will buy them according to the prices fixed. Hoarding of rice is not allowed except for rice stored for personal use; if hoarding is discovered the society will request the Settlement authorities to take action.

(12) In case of necessity, the society may establish offices for the purchase of rice in rice producing areas.

(13) The society will have a certain number of executive and supervisory committeemen.

(14) The society will petition the authorities of the Foreign Settlements to approve its establishment and submit details to the Courts for record purposes before commencing operations.

(14) Rules governing the distribution of profits and the internal organization and functions of the society will be made separately.
pages.zh:
1940年4月5日。下午译文。

《大美晚报》：-

提议组建米粮运销合作社

（接昨日译文）

(7) 合作社将根据等级确定在两处外国租界出售的国产米和洋米的价格（可以每日或每三日确定一次），并在报纸上公布这些价格。价格中将包含适当的利润。例如，最优质大米的利润为每“包”4元，二等米的利润为2元，而三等米的利润则为1元甚至0.50元。最优质大米的消费者是富人，即使从中获取较多利润他们也不会介意，但从普通质量大米中获取的利润应尽可能低，因为大多数消费者是穷人。

(8) 作为股东加入合作社的米店，将根据其业务规模和资本获得配给的大米，并应按照合作社确定的价格向民众出售。米店不得暗中抬价或出售分量不足的大米等。一旦发现欺诈行为，将处以重罚。对于屡犯者，将请求租界当局吊销米店的营业执照。

(9) 作为股东加入合作社的米店不得进行私下交易。一旦发现某米店有此行为，其在合作社的股份将被没收，此外，还将请求租界当局对其从严处理。

(10) 作为股东加入合作社的米店将通过承担大米销售工作获得适当利润。由于运输和销售权由合作社掌握，米行将无法开展任何业务，合作社将从业务总利润中提取10%，作为股东加入合作社的米行可享受这部分利润。

(11) 合作社成立后一周内，所有外国租界内的大米库存应向合作社申报，后者将按既定价格收购。除个人自用储存的大米外，不允许囤积大米；如发现囤积行为，合作社将请求租界当局采取行动。

(12) 如有必要，合作社可在产米区设立采购办事处。

(13) 合作社将设有一定数量的执行委员和监察委员。

(14) 合作社将请求外国租界当局批准其成立，并在开始运营前向法院提交详细资料以备备案。

(14) 关于利润分配以及合作社内部组织和职能的规则将另行制定。

April 4, 1940.
Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Pao :-

Formation of Rice Transportation and Sale Co-operative
Society Suggested

In view of the gravity of the rice situation,
Kwei Yien-fang ( 桂正芳 ), a leading local rice merchant,
is suggesting the formation of a co-operative society by
rice merchants to undertake the joint transportation and
sale of rice. It is to be hoped that the authorities of
the Foreign Settlements, rice merchants and social leaders
will give their support to the scheme.
The plan suggested by Kwei Yien-fang is as
follows :-
(1) With a view to protecting the welfare of the general
public as well as levelling the price of rice, it is
suggested that a co-operative society for the joint
transportation and sale of rice be formed. Rice
merchants in the Foreign Settlements will form a body
which will be known as the "Shanghai Special District
Rice Joint Transportation and Sale Co-operative Society".
(2) Under the supervision and direction of the authorities
of the Foreign Settlements, the new society will deal
specially with the work of transportation and sale of
native rice and foreign rice in the Special Districts.
(3) The society will be a limited liability concern with
a capital of $20,000,000 divided into 20,000 shares
of $1,000 each.
(4) The Committeemen of the society will be responsible
for its affairs. Money to be invested with the society
by rice merchants will be given interest of 8% per
annum.
(5) All rice hongs and rice shops in the Foreign Settlements
should join the society as shareholders. As for those
rice hongs and shops which do not wish to join the
society may request the Settlement authorities to order
them to join by a certain time. The business licences
of the hongs and shops will be withdrawn should they
fail to join within this period and rice merchants will
sever all connection with them.
(6) Native rice transported to Shanghai, whether ordered by
rice dealers or rice hongs, should all be handed to the
society for purchase. As to foreign rice, with the
exception of that ordered for their use by factories,
schools, stores and other bodies, the society will buy
all the rice ordered by these rice hongs and rice shops.
The society will request the Settlement authorities
to deal strictly with those who oppose this. In
future, all orders for foreign rice will be made direct
by the society only.

(To be continued.)

1940年4月4日。
上午译文。

《大美晚报》：-

提议组建米粮运销合作社

鉴于米情严峻，当地著名米商桂正芳（Kwei Yien-fang）建议由米商组建一个合作社，共同承担大米的运输和销售工作。希望外国租界当局、米商和社会领袖能支持该计划。
桂正芳提出的计划如下：-
(1) 为了保护公众福利并平抑米价，建议组建一个共同运输和销售大米的合作社。外国租界的米商将组成一个团体，名为“上海特别区米粮联合运销合作社”。
(2) 在外国租界当局的监督和指导下，新合作社将专门负责特别区内国产米和洋米的运输和销售工作。
(3) 合作社为有限责任公司，资本为2,000万元，分为2万股，每股1,000元。
(4) 合作社事务由委员负责。米商投入合作社的资金将获得每年8%的利息。
(5) 外国租界的所有米行和米店都应作为股东加入合作社。至于那些不愿加入合作社的米行和米店，可请求租界当局命令其在限期内加入。如果在此期限内未能加入，将吊销其营业执照，且米商将与它们断绝一切往来。
(6) 运抵上海的国产米，无论是米商还是米行订购的，均应交给合作社购买。至于洋米，除工厂、学校、商店及其他机构自用的订购部分外，合作社将购买这些米行和米店订购的所有大米。合作社将请求租界当局严厉处置反对者。今后，所有洋米订单将仅由合作社直接下达。

（待续。）

April 2, 1940.
Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Ta Mei Pao, National Herald, Chinese-
American Daily News :-

RICE DEALERS TO DISCUSS FORMATION OF FOODSTUFFS PRODUCTION
AND CONSUMPTION CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETY

Consequent upon the receipt of a notification
from the S.M.C. for the formation of a Foodstuffs Production
and Consumption Co-operative Society, the Shanghai Bean and
Rice Dealers' Guild held a joint meeting of various rice
dealers' bodies at 3 p.m. yesterday in its office, at 15
Avenue Edward VII. About 20 persons representing the Rice
Shop Owners' Guild, etc. were present. Mr. Ying Ts-kong
(荆志剛) presided.
A certain representative, in informing the
meeting of the informal conference called on Wednesday last
by Mr. T.K. Ho of the S.M.C., stated : "After considering
the suggestion forwarded by Mr. Kwei Yien-fang (貴延芳)
for the formation of a Foodstuffs Production and Consumption
Co-operative Society, Mr. Ho, who always shows deep concern
over the question of the staple food of the people, is of
the opinion that it is necessary to hold discussions for
the carrying out of the scheme in order to solve the food
problem."
The consensus of views expressed by other
representatives was that such a co-operative scheme was
reasonable, but in view of the large number of rice bodies
in Shanghai, the opinion of those rice bodies which were
not represented at this meeting should be sought before
going into the matter further.
The meeting then adopted the following
resolution :-
That the same representatives approach the
S.M.C. for copies of the original suggestion for distribution
among the various rice bodies which are to meet to discuss
the matter and which are to submit their views in writing to
the Bean and Rice Dealers' Guild not later than one week
hence so that a reply can be given to the S.M.C. on the opinion
of the rice bodies.

《申报》、《新闻报》、《大美晚报》、《国民日报》、《中美日报》：-

米商将讨论组建食品产销合作社

继收到上海公共租界工部局关于组建食品产销合作社的通知后，上海豆米业公会于昨日下午3时在其位于爱多亚路15号的办事处召开了各米商团体的联席会议。约有20名代表出席，其中包括米店业主公会等代表。荆志剛（Ying Ts-kong）先生主持会议。
一位代表在向会议通报上周三上海公共租界工部局何德奎（T.K. Ho）先生召开的非正式会议情况时表示：“在考虑了桂延芳（Kwei Yien-fang）先生提出的组建食品产销合作社的建议后，一直深切关注民众主食问题的何先生认为，有必要举行讨论以实施该方案，从而解决粮食问题。”
其他代表表达的普遍观点是，此类合作社方案是合理的，但鉴于上海米业团体数量众多，在进一步深入探讨此事之前，应征询未出席本次会议的那些米业团体的意见。
会议随后通过了以下决议：-
由同一批代表向上海公共租界工部局索取原始建议书的副本，分发给各米业团体，以便它们开会讨论此事，并在一周内以书面形式向豆米业公会提交意见，从而就各米业团体的意见向上海公共租界工部局作出回复。

Made/by. and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

At 2.30 p.m. March 27, 1940, Mr. T.K. Ho,
Deputy Secretary of the Shanghai Municipal Council,
called a meeting of the following representatives
of rice dealers organizations in the Administration
Building :-

Kwei Yien Fang (費延芳),
committee member of the Shanghai
Stable Food Regulation Committee.

Chang Hien Sien (張念萱),

Shop Owners' Guild.

Voo Chien Feng (符前耕),

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. I. REGISTRY No S. B. D.）
Date: December 8, 1939.

Subject. Bean and Rice Merchants' Association - properly known as Bean and
Rice Hong Owners' Guild"

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

The Bean and Rice Merchants' Association
(豆米行業同業公會) was formed about twenty years ago
by the owners of hongs dealing in beans and rice. The
object of the association is the promotion of friendship
and business among the dealers in the trades mentioned.

The association was formerly situated in Foh
Yeu Road, City, but was removed to 15 Avenue Edward VII,
on the outbreak of local hostilities in August 1937.
The association at present controls the rice market, 515
Foochow Road, for the purpose of facilitating and
centralizing transactions in rice, it also conducts
inspections of stocks held in godowns in Shanghai every
week.

The affairs of the association are managed
in a competent manner by a standing committee who are
all managers of bean and rice hongs.

There is no record nor is there anything known
of such associations as the Rice Merchants Association
or Sundry Foodstuffs Association.

C. Crawford
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

日期：1939年12月8日。

主题：豆米商协会——正式名称为“豆米业同业公会”

由警探长克劳福德撰写并转呈。

豆米商协会（豆米行業同業公會）约于二十年前由经营豆米的行号业主成立。该协会的宗旨是促进上述行业商人之间的友谊和业务往来。

该协会原址位于华界福州路，但在1937年8月本地战事爆发后迁至爱德华七世大道15号。目前，该协会管理位于福州路515号的米市场，旨在便利和集中大米交易；此外，该协会每周对上海仓库中的库存进行检查。

协会事务由一个常务委员会干练地管理，委员均为豆米行号的经理。

目前没有记录，也未闻知有诸如“米商协会”或“杂粮食品协会”之类的组织存在。

C. Crawford
警探长

August 24, 1939.
Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News, Central China Daily News,
Eastern Times, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao-

MEASURES TO MAINTAIN FOOD SUPPLIES DISCUSSED BY
VARIOUS BODIES

The problem of food supplies for the
inhabitants of Shanghai is becoming more and more serious.
The Ratepayers Association of the International Settlement
and the Chamber of Commerce have sent letters to the
S.M.C. requesting it to regulate rice importation.
Various public bodies have ordered 18,000 bags of foreign
rice from Saigon which is due to arrive at this port on
September 2:

Responsible members of certain public bodies
at 2 p.m. yesterday held a meeting and discussed measures
to maintain the food supplies for Shanghai.

The decision was reached that large quantities
of foreign rice should first be purchased to relieve the
situation in Shanghai. Companies, factories, and shops
that desire to order foreign rice are requested to register
with that body. Detailed measures will be issued later.
As for the money required for the purchase of this rice,
Mr. Yu Ya Ching is making arrangements with banks which
have agreed to lend the money. Mr. Yu also suggests
that a People's Food Supply Maintenance Association should
be organised to sell rice at reasonable prices.

As negotiations between the S.M.C. and the
Japanese about the regulation of rice importation and the
purchase of foreign rice by various bodies are in progress,
the bean and rice market was somewhat quiet yesterday.
It is learned that rice dealers have requested the Rice
Market Control Committee to check the rise in the price
of rice so as not to affect the people's livelihood.

According to news from navigation circles,
plenty of Sungkiang rice is coming to Shanghai. Yesterday
12 rice boats carrying more than 2,000 piculs of rice
arrived from Sungkiang, whilst to-day more than 30 rice
boats towed by launches of the Yeu Lee Navigation Company
(合利航運公司) are due in Shanghai with more than 5,000
piculs of rice.

Five days ago, the price of rice in
Oo Koo Tsun (五庫鎮) near Sungkiang rose to over $20
per picul. The people gathered together and removed all
the rice from the rice shops and rice hongs and made a
fair distribution among the inhabitants. They then set
fire to the rice shops and rice hongs which were all burnt
down.

晨间译稿

《中美日报》、《华中日报》、
《时报》、《新闻报》、《申报》——

各团体讨论维持粮食供应之措施

上海居民之粮食供应问题日益严峻。
公共租界纳税人协会及总商会已致函工部局，要求其管制大米进口。
各公共团体已从西贡订购一万八千包洋米，预计将于九月二日抵达本埠：

昨日午后二时，若干公共团体之负责人举行会议，讨论维持上海粮食供应之措施。

会议决定，首先应大量购入洋米，以缓解上海之局势。凡欲订购洋米之公司、工厂及商号，须向该团体登记。详细办法将随后公布。至于购米所需资金，虞洽卿先生正与银行接洽，各银行已同意贷款。虞先生并建议组织“民众食粮维持会”，以合理价格出售大米。

由于工部局与日方就管制大米进口及各团体购买洋米事宜正在进行谈判，昨日豆米市场略显平静。据悉，米商已请求米业同业公会抑制米价上涨，以免影响民生。

据航运界消息，大量松江大米正运抵上海。昨日有十二艘米船载米二千余石自松江抵达；今日由合利航運公司拖轮拖带之三十余艘米船亦将抵沪，载米五千余石。

五日前，松江附近五庫鎮之米价涨至每石二十元以上。民众聚集，将米店及米行之米全部搬出，在居民中公平分配。随后纵火焚烧米店及米行，致使全部焚毁。

Subject... Rice Situation - Letter from Employers' Federation
of Shanghai.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With reference to the letter (attached)
from the Employers' Federation of Shanghai addressed
to the Commissioner of Police requesting information
(a) whether the rice situation is causing concern
at the moment, and (b) whether the situation, if
serious, is likely to continue: a general survey
shows that the situation, though causing some concern,
is not regarded as serious except from the point of
view of heavy increases in the price of the different
qualities of rice. An explanation follows of the
situation.

Towards the end of April, 1939, an upward
trend was apparent in the price of rice, which con-
tinued to soar until it soon exceeded the limit of
$15.00 per "zar" for Best Quality Chinese Rice, a
limit imposed by the Price of Rice Adjustment
Committee. (This committee dissolved on May 20 when
it realized its impotency). On May 24, the price
of Best Quality Chinese rice was $17.70 per "zar",
the increase being partly due to an increase in the
buying price of rice in the producing areas and
partly due to manipulation and speculation by certain
dealers taking advantage of the oscillating attitude
of the authorities in control at present in the rice
producing areas.

The stock of rice on hand in Shanghai at
present is estimated to be approximately 790,000
"zars". This stock is considered sufficient for

主题……米粮状况——来自上海雇主联合会的信函

由督察长克劳福德（Crawford）撰写并呈报

兹就上海雇主联合会致警务处处长的信函（附后）所询事项作出回复，该信函要求提供以下信息：(a) 目前米粮状况是否引起担忧；以及 (b) 如果局势严重，是否可能持续：经总体评估显示，尽管该状况引起了一些担忧，但除不同等级大米价格大幅上涨这一角度外，并不被视为严重。下文将对当前状况作出解释。

1939年4月底，大米价格呈现明显的上升趋势，并持续飙升，不久便超过了“上白粳米”每“石”15.00元的限价，该限价系由米价调整委员会设定。（该委员会于5月20日意识到其无力管控局面后解散）。5月24日，“上白粳米”的价格为每“石”17.70元，价格上涨部分是由于产米区的收购价提高，部分是由于某些商人利用目前产米区当局的摇摆态度进行操纵和投机所致。

目前上海的大米库存估计约为790,000“石”。此库存量被认为足以满足

November 8, 1937.          Afternoon Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE SHANGHAI PEOPLE'S FOOD ADJUSTMENT COMMITTEE

The voluntary dissolution of the Shanghai
People's Food Adjustment Committee yesterday has given
rise to misunderstanding among the people.
A reporter of the Sin Sin News Agency secured
the following information from the Committee yesterday:-
"The Committee was established three months
ago by the Bureau of Social Affairs with the co-operation
of the Cereal Dealers' Association and other interested
parties. Recently, owing to the fact that the centre
of hostilities has been shifted to the Western District,
the Committee found it impossible to arrange for the
transportation of rice to Shanghai. Fortunately, there
are at present more than 600,000 piculs of rice in stock
in Shanghai and this is sufficient for local requirements.
Hereafter, the Bureau of Social Affairs will undertake the
control of rice and fix the price with the assistance of
the Cereal Dealers' Association, the Rice Shop Owners'
Association and other interested parties. Strict measures
will be adopted to deal with traitorous merchants who
sell rice above the fixed price of $14 per picul. It is
also learnt that the Food Control Committee of the S.M.C.
has already made certain arrangements to facilitate the
transportation of rice to Shanghai."

上海市民食粮调整委员会

上海市民食粮调整委员会于昨日自愿解散，在民众中引起误解。《辛辛新闻社》记者昨日从该委员会获悉如下情况：“本委员会系三个月前由社会局会同米业同业公会及其他有关方面共同成立。近来，由于战事中心转移至西区，本委员会发现无法安排大米运抵上海。幸而目前上海存有大米六十余万担，足以满足本地需求。此后，社会局将在米业同业公会、米店业主公会及其他有关方面的协助下，承担大米管制及定价工作。对于以高于每担14元限定价格出售大米的奸商，将采取严厉措施予以惩处。另悉，工部局粮食管制委员会已作出某些安排，以便利大米运抵上海。”

September 27, 1937.

RICE BAZAAR ESTABLISHED BY RICE HONG OWNERS ON AMOY ROAD

Twenty six rice hongs which are situated in Chapel have
established a temporary rice bazaar in the Doong Loh Teashop,
629 Amoy Road, to facilitate the transacting of the sale of
rice arriving on boats in the Soochow Creek. This bazaar
is being established with the permission of the Shanghai
Municipality Food Adjustment Committee in order to relieve
the committee from its straightened financial condition at present.

It appears that following the formation of the Food Adjustment
Committee, all transactions with rice dealers importing rice from
the interior and the distribution of stocks among local rice shops
were under its control. At the beginning, this committee obtained
a loan of $50,000 from the National Commercial Bank and $30,000 in
contributions from local rice hong owners; this money to be used to
pay rice dealers.

It is learned that the Food Adjustment Committee, instead
of using the money to pay the rice dealers, purchased a large
quantity of "See Mee" which was stored in godowns in Shanghai.
"See MEE" and "Kan MEE" to the total value of $140,000 has, it is
estimated, passed through the committee and distributed to rice shops.

Now that there is a lack of demand for "See Mee", local rice
shops have not been able to sell all their stocks and are unable to
raise money enough to settle with the Food Adjustment Committee.

Owing to this state of affairs, a meeting was convened on
September 26, 1937, in the office of the committee, Peetung Guild,
1454 Avenue Edward VII, when some 200 representatives of rice shops
attended. Mr. Koo Shing-ih (顧馨一), Standing Committee Member of
this Committee, suggested that while the $800 deposit paid by each
rice shop could not be allotted for any other purpose, a further sum
should be paid as deposit by each shop and the sum thus raised be

米行业主在厦门路设立米市

位于闸北（Chapei）的二十六家米行已在厦门路629号同乐茶楼（Doong Loh Teashop）设立临时米市，以便利苏州河上抵沪米船的稻米交易。该米市的设立已获上海市粮食调节委员会许可，旨在缓解该委员会目前拮据的财政状况。

据悉，粮食调节委员会成立后，所有与从内地进口稻米的米商进行的交易，以及向本地米店分配库存的工作，均受其控制。起初，该委员会从国家商业银行获得贷款50,000美元，并从本地米行业主处获得捐款30,000美元；这笔钱用于支付米商货款。

据了解，粮食调节委员会并未用这笔钱支付米商，而是购买了大量储存在上海仓库中的“See Mee”（音译）。“See MEE”和“Kan MEE”（音译）总价值达140,000美元，估计已通过该委员会并分发至各米店。

由于目前对“See Mee”缺乏需求，本地米店未能售出全部库存，也无法筹集足够资金与粮食调节委员会结算。

鉴于此种情况，1937年9月26日在该委员会办公室——爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）1454号浦东公所（Peetung Guild）召开了一次会议，约有200名米店代表出席。该委员会常务委员顾馨一先生建议，虽然每家米店支付的800美元保证金不得挪作他用，但每家米店应再缴纳一笔保证金，所筹款项用于

used to pay the outstanding account to the rice dealers. This
was opposed by a majority and the meeting terminated without
reaching any decision.

On September 24, the committee decided to allot $50,000
from the deposit money already paid by the rice shops which
totals $118,000 and to borrow $50,000 from Mr. Koo Shing-ih.

With this loan, and the $80,000 already mentioned, the
committee has succeeded in settling with the local rice dealers,
but in accomplishing this has left the committee without liquid funds.

As a result the 37 rice boats which arrived in Shanghai on and
after September 20, were unable to dispose of their cargoes until
September 26, when the rice hongs, realizing the straitened
financial circumstances of the Food Adjustment Committee, offered
to deal with the rice dealers and rice boat owners direct and dis-
tribute the stock as they saw fit according to customary procedure,
which was agreed to on the following grounds, that a commission of
10 cents be collected on each "sar" for the committee as compensation.

In consequence of this, a bazaar was established in the Doong
Leh (同樂) Teashop, 639 Amoy Road, on September 25 and the unloading
commenced on September 26.

On each "sar" of rice transacted at this bazaar, a total commis-
sion of 32 cents - 10 cents for Food Adjustment Committee, 15 cents
for Rice Hong Owners' Association and 7 cents unloading fee, is
collected from rice dealers. 15 cents on each "sar" is collected
from rice shops as transportation fee.

It is learned that Mr. Koo Shing-ih of the Food Adjustment
Committee is out of favour with the rice hong owners who accuse
him of selling his own rice out of stocks hoarded by him and his
relatives, instead of making purchase and arrangements with the rice
dealers from the interior for a regular supply.

支付欠付米商的账款。此提议遭到多数反对，会议未达成任何决议即告结束。

9月24日，委员会决定从米店已缴纳的总计118,000美元保证金中拨出50,000美元，并向顾馨一先生借款50,000美元。

凭借这笔借款及前述的80,000美元，委员会已成功与本地米商结清账款，但此举导致委员会流动资金耗尽。

因此，9月20日及之后抵达上海的37艘米船，直到9月26日才得以处理其货物。当日，米行业主意识到粮食调节委员会财政困难，提出直接与米商及米船主交易，并按惯例自行酌情分配库存。该提议基于以下条件获得同意：每包“sar”（音译，指袋/包）抽取10美分佣金作为给委员会的补偿。

因此，9月25日在厦门路639号同乐（Doong Leh）茶楼设立了米市，并于9月26日开始卸货。

在此米市交易的每包“sar”大米，向米商收取总计32美分的佣金——其中10美分归粮食调节委员会，15美分归米行业主协会，7美分为卸货费。此外，向米店每包“sar”收取15美分作为运输费。

据悉，粮食调节委员会的顾馨一先生已失宠于米行业主，他们指责他出售自己及其亲属囤积的库存大米，而非与内地米商进行采购和安排以确保持续供应。

核证无误副本。

200 representatives of rice shops attended. Mr. Koo Shing-
ih (顾馨一), Standing Committee Member of this Committee,
suggested that while the $500 deposit paid by each rice shop
should not be allotted for any other purpose, a further sum
should be paid as a deposit by each shop and the sum thus
raised be used to pay the outstanding account to the rice dealers.
This was opposed by a majority and the meeting terminated
without reaching any decision.

On September 24, the committee decided to allot $60,000
from the deposit money already paid by the rice shops which
totals $118,000 and to borrow $30,000 from Mr. Koo Shing-ih.

With this loan, and the $80,000 already mentioned, the
committee has succeeded in settling with the local rice
dealers, but in accomplishing this has left the committee
without liquid funds.

As a result, the 37 rice boats which arrived in Shanghai
on and after September 20, were unable to dispose of their
cargoes until September 26, when the rice hongs, realizing
the straightened financial circumstances of the Food Adjust-
ment Committee, offered to deal with the rice dealers and
rice boat owners direct and distribute the stock as they saw
fit according to customary procedure, which was agreed to on
the following grounds, that a commission of 10 cents be
collected on each "zar" for the committee as compensation.

In consequence of this, a bazaar was established in the
Joong Loh (同樂) Teashop, 629 Amoy Road, on September 25
and the unloading commenced on September 26.

On each "zar" of rice transacted at this bazaar, a total
commission of 32 cents - 10 cents for Food Adjustment

200名米店代表出席。该委员会常务委员顾馨一先生建议，虽然每家米店支付的500美元保证金不得挪作他用，但每家米店应再缴纳一笔保证金，所筹款项用于支付欠付米商的账款。此提议遭到多数反对，会议未达成任何决议即告结束。

9月24日，委员会决定从米店已缴纳的总计118,000美元保证金中拨出60,000美元，并向顾馨一先生借款30,000美元。

凭借这笔借款及前述的80,000美元，委员会已成功与本地米商结清账款，但此举导致委员会流动资金耗尽。

因此，9月20日及之后抵达上海的37艘米船，直到9月26日才得以处理其货物。当日，米行业主意识到粮食调节委员会财政困难，提出直接与米商及米船主交易，并按惯例自行酌情分配库存。该提议基于以下条件获得同意：每包“zar”（音译，指袋/包）抽取10美分佣金作为给委员会的补偿。

因此，9月25日在厦门路629号同乐（Joong Loh）茶楼设立了米市，并于9月26日开始卸货。

Translation of letter to Council
from the Shanghai Foodstuff Control
Committee (會員委節調食民市海上)
Dated 31st August, 1937.

Foodstuff Control Committee.

Since the commencement of hostilities a large number of
refugees, young and old, have fled hurriedly from various
localities into the Settlement. The stock of rice became
inadequate and looting resulted; the public was greatly disturbed.
To cope with the situation the Shanghai Foodstuff Control Committee
was jointly organized by the Military and Police Authorities in
Nanking and Shanghai, the Shanghai City Bureau of Social Affairs,
the Foodstuff Transportation Office, the Shanghai Chinese Chamber
of Commerce, the Civic Association, and the various Associations
Bankers, Native Banks and Rice Dealers; the Committee was formally
inaugurated on 16th August in the premises of the Chamber of
Commerce and a seal was prepared for use. For the sake of
convenience the Committee established its office and began to
function on 18th August on the 5th floor of the Peotung Bank
Building, Avenue Edward VII; the seal was put to use on that date.
During the last ten days no looting of rice has occurred. Will
the Council kindly note the above report.

(Signed and chopped)
Shanghai Foodstuff Control Committee
Wong Hsiao-lai
Chairman.

（印：2 SEP. 1937 CRIME BRANCH）

食料管理委员会。

自战事爆发以来，大量老少难民从各地匆忙逃入租界。大米库存不足，导致发生抢掠；公众深感不安。为应对局势，上海市食料管理委员会由南京和上海军政当局、上海市社会局、食料运输处、上海总商会、市民协会以及银行公会、钱业公会和米业公会等联合组织成立；委员会于8月16日在总商会会址正式成立，并刻制印章一枚以备使用。为方便起见，委员会于8月18日在爱多亚路浦东银行大楼五层设立办事处并开始运作；印章于当日启用。过去十天未发生大米抢掠事件。恳请工部局留意上述报告。

Subject Meeting of local rice merchants - rice shops selected
as depots for the sale of rice while hostilities last.
Made by [手写符号] and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

Under the auspices of the Shanghai Municipality
Provision Maintenance Association, recently formed by local
bodies in conjunction with the Bureau of Social Affairs,
a meeting was convened comprising 60 representatives from
the rice trade, in the Footung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII,
between 10 a.m. and 12 noon, August 18. After discussion,
the following resolutions were passed :-
1. That forty-four rice shops in the Settlement and French
Concession be selected as depots for the sale of rice
while hostilities last. (A list containing the
particulars of these shops is attached.)
2. That these shops open for business on August 19.
3. That the retail prices of best quality Chinese rice
must not exceed $15, and that of best quality Saigon
rice should not exceed $11 per picul.
4. That each customer be allowed to purchase half a picul
at a time.
5. That a letter be addressed to the S.M.C. and the C.M.F.
requesting them to provide police protection for the
above shops and also while the rice is being unloaded
at the jetties and its transportation.

C. Crawford

Translation of Letter from the Shanghai Rice Market
Control Committee, Lane 153, 52 Shanhaikwan Road

May 26, 1941.

A.C. (Special Branch),
S.M.P.

Sir,

This is to inform you that recently Messrs. Lee Kuo
Tsu (李國柱), Tsang Mou Zai (張茂才) and Liu
Yu Foo (劉于富) have organized a Foo Yih Co. (浦益)
whose duties will be to prevent pilfering of rice whilst
being transported along the jetties on the south bank of
the Soochow Creek, extending from Honan Road Bridge to
Garden Bridge, and on jetties on the Bund from Garden
Bridge to No. 2 Pontoon, opposite Canton Road. The
company will employ a number of inspectors to look after
rice transportation along the said jetties. They will
wear an identification armlet to be issued by the
Company (two specimens are attached).

The promoters of the company state that the company
will operate on similar lines to those of the Dah Lai
(大来) Transportation Company, which operates on the
north bank of the Soochow Creek, and the Yuin Kee (雲記)
Wharf Transportation Service Society, which operates on
jetties in Pootung and Hongkew. These two concerns have
been in existence for some time and their services in
preventing rice pilfering are satisfactory. The
formation of the new company has been approved by this
Control Committee during its 86th meeting. This
committee, therefore, applies on its behalf, for police
registration.

Hoping that you will approve the application and
instruct the police stations concerned to render due
assistance and protection to the staff of this concern.

Chopped: Rice Market Control Committee.

兹通知贵处，近期李國柱、張茂才及劉于富三位先生组建了一家名为“浦益”的公司，其职责是防止大米在苏州河南岸从河南路桥至外白渡桥沿线的码头，以及在外滩从外白渡桥至广东路对面的2号浮码头沿线的运输过程中被盗。该公司将雇用若干稽查员负责上述码头的大米运输监管工作。他们将佩戴由公司颁发的识别袖标（附有两个样本）。

该公司发起人称，该公司的运营模式将与在苏州河北岸运营的大来运输公司，以及在浦东和虹口码头运营的雲記码头运输服务社类似。这两家机构已存在一段时间，其在防止大米盗窃方面的服务令人满意。该新公司的成立已在本委员会第86次会议上获得批准。因此，本委员会代表该公司申请警方注册。

望贵处批准此申请，并指示有关警察局对该机构员工提供必要的协助和保护。

May 26, 1941.

A.C. (Special Branch),
S.M.P.

Sir,

This is to inform you that recently Messrs. Lee Kuo
Tsu (李國柱), Tsang Mou Zai (張茂才) and Liu
Yu Foo (劉于富) have organized a Poo Yih Co. (浦益公司 浦益服務社)
whose duties will be to prevent pilfering of rice whilst
being transported along the jetties on the south bank of
the Soochow Creek, extending from Honan Road Bridge to
Garden Bridge, and on jetties on the Bund from Garden
Bridge to No. 2 Pontoon, opposite Canton Road. The
company will employ a number of inspectors to look after
rice transportation along the said jetties. They will
wear an identification armlet to be issued by the
Company (two specimens are attached).

The promoters of the company state that the company
will operate on similar lines to those of the Dah Lai
(大來) Transportation Company, which operates on the
north bank of the Soochow Creek, and the Yuin Kee (雲記)
Wharf Transportation Service Society, which operates on
jetties in Pootung and Hongkew. These two concerns have
been in existence for some time and their services in
preventing rice pilfering are satisfactory. The
formation of the new company has been approved by this
Control Committee during its 86th meeting. This
committee, therefore, applies on its behalf, for police
registration.

Hoping that you will approve the application and
instruct the police stations concerned to render due
assistance and protection to the staff of this concern.

Chopped: Rice Market Control Committee.

Translation of letter received from the Shanghai
Rice Market Committee, 52 Neu Yih Lee, Shanhaikwan Road.
----------
October 28, 1940.
To the Shanghai Municipal Police.
According to one Kao Yung Chien representing
the Yung Kee Wharf Transportation Service Company,
cases of theft frequently occurred when rice was
being transported in the vicinity of godowns along
bank of the Whangpoo River. Larceny has also taken place
on the Whangpoo River. Rice merchants have therefore
suffered great losses in their business. Kao Yung Chien
has in cooperation with people engaged in the wharf
transportation business formed the Yung Kee Transportation
Service Company which will detail men to the various
wharves along the Whangpoo River with a view to protecting
the movement of rice to and from wharf godowns. The
Company will be responsible for any loss of cargo
whilst being transported by the merchants. The Rice
Market Committee at their 72nd meeting decided to grant
the monopoly to the Yung Kee Company in connection with
the transportation of rice. An identification badge
to be used by men sent out by the Company is forwarded
herewith for your information. You are requested to
issue instructions to those concerned to protect the
Company's representatives.
Shanghai Rice Market Committee.
G D. J. Kul.
£ 30/10

godowns are situated in this vicinity and quantities
of rice are removed to and from the godowns every
day. Groups of poor people gather at those places
and collect the rice falling from the bags while
being transported, but on a number of occasions

the street awaiting transportation. The Company

rice removed into the godowns and 2 cents for rice
from the godowns, and they will be responsible for
any losses sustained by stealing.

Removal of rice from the Settlement.

Sir,

At 12.35p.m. 26-9-40, C.P.C. 217 stopped m/truck
S.M.C.Lic. No. 73000, loaded with 40 bags of rice on N.
Honan Road near Broadway. It was ascertained from the
chauffeur that the rice was being transported to Markham
Road Railway Station to be entrained for Penpu. As they
were not in possession of an S.M.C. Permit authorizing
the removal, the C.P.C. brought them to this station.

At 6.50p.m. 26-9-40, the attached letter was brought
to the station by Mr. T. Iizuka, explaining that the rice
was to be transported to Penpu from the Mitsui Bussan
Kaisha, Ltd., D.I. Eddy communicated with Mr. Yorke
who did not think rice should be permitted to be removed
without a permit but owing to the late hour suggested
that Mr. Beasley, S.M.C. be informed. Mr. Beasley was
communicated with and stated that as cargo of rice could
not be stored under cover at this station and as rain was
imminent cargo be released but that letter be sent to M.
B.K. informing them that in future no such action would
be taken and that despite weather, rice would be detained
until permit was obtained.

Cargo was released at 7.15p.m. 26-9-40.

D.D.O."C" Div.

先生，

1940年9月26日下午12时35分，中央巡捕房警员217号在北河南路靠近百老汇路（Broadway）处拦停了一辆车牌号为 S.M.C.Lic. No. 73000 的卡车，车上装载40袋大米。经向司机查证，得知该批大米正运往马克姆路（Markham Road）火车站，拟装车运往彭浦（Penpu）。由于他们未持有工部局授权移运的许可证，中央巡捕房警员将他们带至本分局。

1940年9月26日下午6时50分，T. Iizuka 先生将附信送至分局，解释称该批大米将从三井物产株式会社运往彭浦。督察 Eddy 与 Yorke 先生联系，Yorke 先生认为不应允许无许可证移运大米，但因时间已晚，建议通知工部局的 Beasley 先生。随后与 Beasley 先生取得联系，他表示，由于本站无法在室内储存大米货物，且大雨将至，故准予放行货物，但应致函三井物产株式会社，告知今后不再采取此类行动，且无论天气如何，大米都将被扣留直至取得许可证。

货物于1940年9月26日下午7时15分放行。

Date May 24, 1940.

REPORT

Subject. Rice leaving for Ningpo detained by Japanese
Authorities.

Made by nd Forwarded by J.M. Ford

On May 21, 1940, 1,544 bags of foreign
rice, part of a consignment which was being
despatched to Ningpo from Shanghai by the s.s.
"Zuan Tai" and s.s. "Hai Joh" for cheap sale
purposes in Ningpo, were detained by the Japanese
Naval Authorities from the Floating Restaurant on
the grounds that no permission had been secured
from the Japanese authorities for export.

A consignment of 740 bags of foreign
rice was purchased by the compradores of the s.s.
"Zuan Tai" of the Hwa Lung Steamship Co., 93
Hongkong Road, from the Sing Foong (新丰) Cereal
Hong, Lane 12, 1 Rue Laguerre, on behalf of the
Ningpo Cheap Rice Sales Committee, Ningpo. The
rice was sent by lighter from the Chi Chong wharf,
Pootung, at about noon on May 21 for loading aboard
the s.s. "Zuan Tai" lying at the Nanking Road
Jetties. The transportation was carried out by
the Yue Zung Kung Shipping Hong, Lane 12, 8 rue
Laguerre, on behalf of the compradores of the steamer.
At about 2 p.m. when 591 bags had been put aboard
the s.s. "Zuan Tai", the Japanese Naval Authorities
from the Floating Restaurant Pontoon arrived on
the scene and seized the remaining 149 bags which
were still on the lighter and removed them to the
Floating Restaurant. The s.s. "Zuan Tai" sailed
from Shanghai at 3 p.m. May 21 without the 149 bags.

（左侧手写批注：）
May 24
Mr. Barclay
R.S.Y.
24/5/40

制作人 nd 转呈人 J.M. Ford

1940年5月21日，1,544袋洋米（这是由“钻泰”轮（s.s. "Zuan Tai"）和“海若”轮（s.s. "Hai Joh"）从上海发往宁波用于低价销售的一批货物的一部分），被来自水上餐厅的日本海军当局扣留，理由是未获得日本当局的出口许可。

华龙轮船公司（Hwa Lung Steamship Co.，香港路93号）“钻泰”轮的买办，代表宁波宁波低价售米委员会，从拉格莱路1号12弄的新丰（Sing Foong）粮行购买了740袋洋米。5月21日中午左右，这批大米由驳船从浦东积存码头运出，准备装上停靠在南京路码头的“钻泰”轮。运输工作由拉格莱路8号12弄的岳荣公（Yue Zung Kung）轮船行代表该轮买办办理。下午2点左右，当591袋大米装上“钻泰”轮时，来自水上餐厅浮码头的日本海军当局赶到现场，扣押了仍留在驳船上的剩余149袋大米，并将其移至水上餐厅。“钻泰”轮于5月21日下午3点离开上海，未携带这149袋大米。

（左侧手写批注：）
5月24日
Barclay先生

REPORT
Date May 10 1940.
Subject Rice to be sent away from Shanghai.
Made by Forwarded by Bradford

Mr. Loong Pi Yun (龍筱雲) reported to
the Municipal Police that rice is being transported
to Ningpo by Shanghai merchants in large quantities
out of Shanghai stocks. He is a native of Ningpo,
but is not connected with the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's
Association. He is a member of such charitable
organizations as the Shanghai Refugee Relief
Association, the World Red Swastika Society and
the Shang Shan Child Welfare Association, and
fears that the amount of rice being transported to
Ningpo will in the near future, when the practice
becomes general, reduce the local stocks.

Inquiries on the information submitted show
that 745 bags of foreign rice will leave Shanghai
for Ningpo by the s.s. "Santarim" at 4 p.m. May 10.
This quantity is covered by a transit permit issued
by the Customs Authorities and is part of a consign-
ment of 24,000 bags of foreign rice which arrived
in Shanghai by the s.s. "Dahpu" on May 9 and at
present are stored in the Chi Chong Wharf, Lootung.
(This quantity is not included in the daily return of
stocks.)

The 24,000 bags of rice mentioned above
were imported by the Kian Gwan Co. on behalf of a
number of Chinese rice and cereal hongs and are
expected to be trans-shipped to the following
places with the permission of the Customs authorities:

Section I, Special Branch. Station,
REPORT
Date January 16, 1940.
File No. .........

Subject Rice shipments - report concerning export from Shanghai.

Made by D. S. Henchman Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to the report alleging that
certain Shanghai firms are exporting rice from this
city, representatives of both Messers. Butterfield
& Swire and Jardine Matheson have been interviewed.
In the case of the first named company, it
is stated that rice is not being exported from
Shanghai but that certain Chinese rice hongs have,
when the price of rice in Tientsin and Chefoo has
exceeded the price in Shanghai, requested the company
not to unload shipments here but to forward to the
Northern ports referred to above; this, on occasion,
has led to cargoes being unloaded on the French Bund
and then reloaded into North-bound ships. The
French Police, Messers. Butterfield & Swire state,
have been informed regarding these transfers of
shipments.
Messers. Jardine Matheson's representative
stated that his company is not engaged in the export
of rice from Shanghai but explained that on a recent
occasion a shipment of rice from Saigon destined for
Tientsin, was transhiped in Shanghai, and that this
transfer formed the subject of enquiries by the
French Police.

D. S. Henchman
D. S.
A. C. ( Special Branch ).

West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date July 26th, 1939
Subject Attempted Removal of Rice from International Settlement without
S.M.C. Rice Permit.
Made by D.S. BEVAN Forwarded by Inspector,
Officer i/c.

Sir,
At 1 p.m. 26-7-39 C.P.C. 2648 telephoned to the station
and reported that there were about 100 sacks of rice about
to be loaded on a boat at North Soochow Road near North
Szechuen Road.
The undersigned and C.P.S. 80 immediately visited the
scene and ascertained that the Yih Tsung (益永) Rice Shop,
No. 146 Park Road were bringing 100 sacks of rice from the
Ding Shing (鼎興) Godown, Santai Road preparatory to
shipping 50 sacks to the Woo Tah (五泰) rice shop, Li Yi
Rice, Pootung, and 50 to the Wong Teung Yi (黃增記), Rice
Shop, Yangtzepoo, Pootung.
When questioned re their S.M.C. rice permit they produced
a custom's loading order issued by the Rice Surveyor's Office
dated 26-7-39.
Thereupon they were advised to obtain S.M.C. permit to
facilitate the removal of the rice from the International
Settlement. This they promised to do immediately.
In the meantime a C.P.C. has been posted to prevent the
shipping of the rice pending production of a permit.
C.D.I. Ross informed.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J.N. Bevan.
Det. Sergt.

Det. Det. 1/c.
D.D.O.'C' Div.
Copy for D.C. (Special Branch).

敬启者：

前敝行向位于河南路466弄8号的协大米行购买了99包大米，
该批大米存放于山西路桥北侧三泰路的鼎和栈房。
5月25日，敝行提取了该批大米，原计划将其运往浦东周浦的天生米行，
但被西虹口捕房拦下，理由是依据租界规定，此类运输未经许可。

因此，敝行将该批大米出售给位于法租界蒲石路128号的鼎泰米店。
由于鼎泰米店无仓储空间，该批大米现存于北苏州路1040号的中国银行栈房，
一旦有买家，将部分或全部提货。为避免西虹口捕房因误解而再次阻止大米移库，
特请贵处将上述情况通知该捕房，并请其允许装运该批大米。

To Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police.

Dear Sirs,

Sometime ago we purchased 99 bags of rice from the
Yah Dah (協大 ) Rice Hong, No. 8, Lane 466 Honan Road,
which was stored in the Ting Woo Godown(鼎和 ), San Tai
Road(三泰 ), north of the Shanse Road Bridge. On
May 25 we took delivery of the rice and intended to
ship it to the Tien Sung Rice Hong(天生 ), Chowpu,
Pootung, but was stopped by West Hongkew Police Station
as transportation was not permitted according to Settlement
regulations.

In consequence, we sold the rice to the Ting Tai
(鼎泰 )Rice Shop, No. 128 Rue Bourgeat, French Concession.
As the Ting Tai Rice Shop has no space for storage, the
rice is kept in the Bank of China Godown, 1040 North
Soochow Road, and will be taken delivery of, partly
or wholly, as soon as there are purchasers. For the
sake of any misunderstanding on the part of West Hongkew
Station who might again prevent the removal of the rice,
we request that you notify this station of the above
and ask them to allow the rice to be shipped.

(Chopped) Kung Dah Oil and Bean
and Cereal Hong.

Subject West Hongkew Report re Removal of Rice without Permit.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With reference to the attached report dated
May 25, 1939 from West Hongkew Station regarding the
removal of rice without an S.M.C. Permit, enquiries
by this office ascertain that the twenty-six bags
were removed from the Ting Woo Godown, Lane 57, 2-4
Santai Road, on March 25, being part of a consignment
of 125 bags stored in that godown, which is owned by
the Kung Dah Cereal Hong (公大雜糧号), 85-87 Rue Marco
Polo, the manager being one Mr. Chiang Vong-sung
(姜望生). This consignment of 125 bags was recently
sold to the Tien Sung (天生) and Tien Tai (天泰)
Rice Shops at Chowpu, Pootung and the twenty-six bags,
mentioned above, were being sent to this destination.
The remaining ninety-nine bags are now still in the
godown.

This Kung Dah Cereal Hong was endeavouring
to smuggle the rice out in the hope that the police on
duty would not cause trouble. The excuse given for
not having a permit being that it takes a long time
to obtain such permits.

REPORT
Date March 7, 1939.

Subject Rice situation - Export of rice from Shanghai.

Made by/ and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Information has been received that some five
rice houses, formerly situated in Nantao and now
established in the French Concession and the Settlement,
have been engaged during the past ten days in purchasing
quantities of rice in Shanghai (south of Creek) on
behalf of North China dealers for export to northern
ports. It is estimated that up to the present,
they have purchased a total of some 50,000 bags (= 70,000
"zars"), 10,000 bags of which have already been
exported using the wharves in the Eastern District
and transporting by Japanese vessels (Vide Special
Branch Report dated March 2, 1939). The remaining
amount is expected to be removed north of Creek in
small quantities by trucks and will be exported during
the week. This form of exportation, it is believed,
does not follow the procedure of going through the
customs.

In consequence of this heavy buying, the
price of rice in the local market has shown an
increase almost daily; the present price of best
quality Chinese rice having reached the maximum of
$14.00 per "zar", as was fixed by the former Shanghai
City Government.

Should this underhand method of export be
allowed to continue, the situation will undoubtedly
be affected in Shanghai; although the present stock
on hand is considered excessive, still a continual

据获情报，约五家原先位于南市、现设于法租界和公共租界的

它们共购买了约50,000包（= 70,000“担”），其中10,000包
已利用东区码头并通过日本船只出口（参见1939年3月2日的
政治部报告）。剩余数量预计将通过卡车分批运至苏州河以北，
并将在本周内出口。据信，这种出口形式并未遵循
经过海关的程序。

由于这种大量收购，本地市场的大米价格
几乎每日上涨；目前优质中国大米的价格已达到
每“担”14.00元的最高限价，这是由前上海市政府规定的。

如果允许这种暗中出口的方式继续下去，上海的局势无疑会受到影响；虽然目前的库存被认为过多，但仍持续

the price of rice in the local market was discussed
and the following resolutions passed :-

should not exceed $14.00 per "zar", and that the
dealers and rice market officials be advised to
take note of this decision.
2. That the French and Municipal Authorities be
requested by letter to devise ways and means to

3. That rice dealers be instructed to pay forthwith
the income tax due for the past year, and that the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce be requested to inform
the Association as to which organ the income tax
should be paid.

Fourteen committee members of the Shanghai Bean
and Rice Hong Owners' Association, 11 Avenue Edward VII,
held a meeting in the Shanghai Merchants' Club, 3rd floor,
460 Hankow Road, between 3.30 p.m. and 5.30 p.m. November
16, when Mr. Kiang Hung-ning (江鴻斌) and Mr. Chen Ts-yi
(陳子彝) made a report on their visits to the Chinese
Maritime Customs and the Shanghai Municipal Council regarding
the exportation of rice from Shanghai. According to the
report of those two members, Mr. T.K. Ho, Deputy Secretary
of the Council, intimated that the Council would only permit
the export of 80,000 bags (later increased to 100,000 bags)
in one month to avoid an excessive increase in the prices
and also to avoid a possible shortage. Certificates would
be issued by the Council to cover the exportation, but no
export would be allowed on the price of rice reaching the
maximum price of $14.00 per "zar". Detailed reports with
regard to the arrival and the sales of rice should be
submitted twice monthly for the information of the Council.
It was finally decided to comply with the decision
of the Municipal Council but further representations be
made to the Council on November 17.

MUNICIPAL GAZETTE
193
Of the Council for the Foreign Settlement of Shanghai
Vol. XXXI SHANGHAI, FRIDAY, JULY 15, 1938. 1727

NOTIFICATION No. 4976.
MOVEMENT OF RICE.
UNTIL further notice no export of Chinese rice from the International Settlement of Shanghai will be permitted.
Applications for permits for the movement of rice from the Settlement to surrounding areas should be made to Room No. 150, First Floor, Administration Building, 209 Kiangse Road.
By order,
T. W. GUBB,
Acting Secretary.
Council Chamber,
Shanghai, July 7, 1938.

NOTIFICATION No. 4978.
"HUI HUA" CHEQUES AND ORDERS.
NOTICE is hereby given that Rates, Taxes, Dues and Fees are payable to the Council in local currency by cheque or cash. With effect from Monday, July 11, 1938, however, the Council will in its discretion accept "Hui Hua" cheques or orders, provided that payment in such form is accompanied by the relative amount of cash necessary to meet discount charges on conversion of "Hui Hua" into local currency on the date payment is made.
By order,
T. W. GUBB,
Acting Secretary.
Council Chamber,
Shanghai, July 9, 1938.

NOTIFICATION No. 4977.
EDUCATIONAL GRANTS-IN-AID.
1. Foreign Schools.
FORMS of application and copies of the conditions governing the issue of grants-in-aid to foreign schools within the International Settlement or paying rates to the Shanghai Municipal Council may be obtained from the Acting Superintendent of Education, Administration Building.
Applications for grants-in-aid for the year 1939 must be submitted not later than September 15, 1938.

2. Chinese Schools.
Forms of application and copies of the conditions governing the issue of grants-in-aid to Chinese schools within the International Settlement may be obtained from the Acting Superintendent of Education, Administration Building. To qualify for a grant a school must have been in existence at least one full year within the Settlement.
Applications for grants-in-aid for the year 1939 must be submitted not later than September 15, 1938.
By order,
T. W. GUBB,
Acting Secretary.
Council Chamber,
Shanghai, July 14, 1938.

EVICTION OF REFUGEES.
A joint petition by the several parent refugee organizations has been submitted to the Council supplicating for a postponement of Police action in assisting landlords in the eviction of refugees.
The petition represents that owing to delays in obtaining suitable camp sites, difficulties of procuring the necessary building materials and the protraction of negotiations aiming to secure the consent of all the authorities concerned, the refugee organizations have not yet found it possible to have ready alternative camps to accommodate the many thousand refugees whose eviction is sought by landlords. The difficulties represented by the refugee organizations have been investigated and found to be valid.
The petition of the parent refugee organizations is supported by the Shanghai International Red Cross, which has stated that the compulsory eviction of several thousand refugees at the present time, when no alternative accommodation exists, would result in the peace of the city being jeopardized by consequent begging and stealing and forcible entry on the part of refugees. Health conditions would also be endangered by increasing the possibilities of infection through distribution of the refugees throughout the city.
It was the Council's hope that by a postponement in lending the assistance of its Police to landlords in effecting evictions, sufficient time would be allowed the refugee organizations to provide alternative accommodation. These hopes, the Council regrets, have not materialized. The Council is compelled, therefore, in the interests of public peace, order and good health, further to withhold Police action invoked by landlords to evict refugees. It is appreciated, however, that a legal obligation rests upon the Council to carry out evictions in individual cases where landlords have secured a Court Order lawfully authorizing an eviction.
The Council is lending its assistance to the refugee organizations in their endeavours to expedite the provision of new camp accommodation for refugees.

NOTIFICATION No. 4974.
COLLECTION OF MUNICIPAL RATE.
NOTICE is hereby given that Municipal Rate in respect of Chinese and Foreign houses for the quarter ending September 30, 1938, is due on July 1, 1938. Ratepayers are reminded that rates on foreign style buildings will not be called for by collectors but must be remitted to the Revenue Office, 209 Kiangse Road, by the concerned upon receipt of demand note.
By order,
T. W. GUBB,
Acting Secretary.
Council Chamber,
Shanghai, June 30, 1938.

REQUEST FOR USE OF SCHOOL PREMISES.
The Municipal Council on July 6 endorsed a recommendation submitted by the Education Board that a request from the Association for the Education of Street Children for the free use of the Council's school premises during the summer months, for the purpose of establishing classes for poor children, be not complied with. Rejection of the request was based on the grounds, among others, of the danger of later infection of the regular pupils resulting from verminous infestation of the premises.

PRIMARY SCHOOL ACCOMMODATION.
The Municipal Council on July 6 endorsed a recommendation submitted by the Education Board that a sub-committee, consisting of Mrs. Lancelot Giles and Messrs. Chen Che-chen and Yulin Hsi, be formed to consider and formulate suggestions on possible arrangements to secure additional suitable temporary premises to accommodate as many pupils as possible in the Council's Primary Schools for Chinese children. The Board was informed that the present enrolment in these schools was 74 per cent. as compared with the figures in June, 1937, and that over 1,500 applications for admission to four of the six primary schools had already been received as against 365 vacancies.

SCHOOLS CLOSING EXERCISES.
At a meeting of the Education Board on June 30, gratification was expressed by members at the keenness displayed by pupils at various Council Schools at the recent prize distributions and closing exercises. Members reported that they were very favourably impressed with the high standard attained by the pupils.

NOTIFICATION No. 4979.
ARMED WATCHMEN.
NOTICE is hereby given that, with effect from July 15, 1938, the charges for the hire of weapons issued for the arming of private watchmen under police supervision will be as follows:—
1st Quarter, payable in advance $20.00
For each succeeding period of three months $12.00
These charges will cover the cost of ammunition required for training as well as the maintenance of the weapon in an effective condition.
Forms of application for the hire of arms under these conditions are obtainable at the Police Station of the districts in which the watchmen will be employed.
By order,
T. W. GUBB,
Acting Secretary.
Council Chamber,
Shanghai, July 14, 1938.

上海公共租界工部局
第三十一卷 上海，1938年7月15日，星期五。第1727号

第4976号通告。
大米运输。
在另行通知之前，禁止从上海公共租界出口中国大米。
凡申请将大米从租界运往周边地区的许可证者，应向江西路209号行政大楼一楼150室提出申请。
奉命，
T. W. GUBB，
代理秘书。
工部局会议室，
上海，1938年7月7日。

第4978号通告。
“汇划”支票及汇票。
特此通知，捐税、税款、规费及费用应以本地货币通过支票或现金向工部局缴纳。然而，自1938年7月11日星期一起，工部局将酌情接受“汇划”支票或汇票，但以此种形式付款时，须附带足额的现金，以支付在付款当日将“汇划”款项兑换为本地货币所产生的贴现费用。
奉命，
T. W. GUBB，
代理秘书。
工部局会议室，
上海，1938年7月9日。

第4977号通告。
教育补助金。
1. 外国学校。
有关向公共租界内或向上海工部局纳税的外国学校发放补助金的申请表及条件副本，可向行政大楼的代理教育督学索取。
1939年度的补助金申请必须于1938年9月15日之前提交。

2. 中国学校。
有关向公共租界内的中国学校发放补助金的申请表及条件副本，可向行政大楼的代理教育督学索取。学校须在租界内至少存在满一年，方有资格获得补助金。
1939年度的补助金申请必须于1938年9月15日之前提交。
奉命，
T. W. GUBB，
代理秘书。
工部局会议室，
上海，1938年7月14日。

驱逐难民。
各主要难民组织联合向工部局提交请愿书，恳请推迟警务处协助房东驱逐难民的行动。
请愿书称，由于难以获得合适的营地选址、采购必要的建筑材料存在困难，以及旨在争取所有相关当局同意的谈判拖延，难民组织尚未能准备好替代营地，以容纳成千上万被房东要求驱逐的难民。经调查，难民组织所陈述的困难属实。
上海国际红十字会支持各主要难民组织的请愿，并表示在目前没有其他住所的情况下，强制驱逐数千名难民，将导致难民因乞讨、偷窃和强行闯入而危及城市治安。此外，难民散布于全市各处也会增加感染传播的可能性，从而危及卫生状况。
工部局曾希望，通过推迟动用警务力量协助房东执行驱逐，能为难民组织提供足够的时间来提供替代住所。工部局遗憾地表示，这些期望并未实现。因此，为了公众和平、秩序及良好卫生的利益，工部局被迫继续搁置房东所要求的驱逐难民的警务行动。然而，工部局认识到，在房东已依法获得法院签发的驱逐令的个别案件中，工部局负有履行驱逐的法律义务。
工部局正在协助难民组织，努力加快为难民提供新营地住所的工作。

第4974号通告。
征收市政捐。
特此通知，截至1938年9月30日的季度中，华式房屋与西式房屋的市政捐应于1938年7月1日到期缴纳。提醒纳税人，西式建筑的捐税不会由收捐员上门收取，纳税人在收到缴款通知单后，必须自行将捐款汇至江西路209号财务处。
奉命，
T. W. GUBB，
代理秘书。
工部局会议室，
上海，1938年6月30日。

关于使用校舍的请求。
工部局于7月6日核准了教育委员会提出的一项建议，即不予批准流浪儿童教育协会提出的在夏季月份免费使用工部局校舍以设立贫困儿童班级的请求。拒绝该请求的理由包括（但不限于）校舍若滋生虫害，可能导致日后正规学生受到感染的危险。

小学校舍容纳问题。
工部局于7月6日核准了教育委员会提出的一项建议，即成立一个由Lancelot Giles夫人、陈哲臣先生（Chen Che-chen，音译）和奚玉林先生（Yulin Hsi，音译）组成的小组委员会，审议并制定建议，就可能的安排提出方案，以获取额外的合适临时校舍，尽可能多地容纳工部局华人小学的学生。据悉，目前这些学校的入学人数为1937年6月数据的74%，且在六个小学中的四个学校已收到超过1,500份入学申请，而空缺名额仅为365个。

学校结业典礼。
在6月30日举行的教育委员会会议上，委员们对近期各工部局学校在颁奖及结业典礼上学生们表现出的热情表示满意。委员们报告称，学生们所达到的高标准给他们留下了非常好的印象。

第4979号通告。
武装看守。
特此通知，自1938年7月15日起，在警方监督下为私人看守配备武器所收取的租赁费用规定如下：—
第一季度，预付 20.00元
此后每三个月 12.00元
上述费用涵盖训练所需弹药的费用以及保持武器有效状态所需的维护费用。
在此条件下申请租赁武器的表格，可在看守受雇所在区域的警察署领取。
奉命，
T. W. GUBB，
代理秘书。
工部局会议室，
上海，1938年7月14日。

194 THE MUNICIPAL GAZETTE, FRIDAY, JULY 15, 1938.

COMMITTEE MEETING.
Staff Committee, July 8.—Present: Messrs. G. E. Mitchell (Chairman), W. J. Keswick, E. Y. B. Kiang, F. N. Matthews, O. Okamoto, L. T. Yuan and Yu Ya Ching. Absent: Messrs. W. Gockson, R. G. MacDonald and W. H. Plant.

LIBRARY COMMITTEE.
Mr. Wei-tsung Chien has accepted the invitation of the Municipal Council to take the place on the Library Committee rendered vacant by the departure from Shanghai of Dr. Y. H. Ou.

POLICE AWARDS FOR GALLANTRY.
Issue of awards to police officers engaged in a shooting affray with armed robbers on March 24 last has been approved by the Municipal Council, on recommendations submitted by the Permanent Awards Board.
The shooting affray took place at 1240 Avenue Edward VII. Six foreign and nine Chinese members of the Force from Chengtu Road Station were engaged. Two of the foreigners and two Chinese policemen entered the house and tackled three robbers. Shots were exchanged and two of the robbers collapsed while the third was also taken prisoner. The Permanent Awards Board found that the conduct of Insp. S. V. Gash, Sgt. D. Johnstone, C.D.S. 192 and C.D.C. 254 (who formed the party to go inside the house) was very courageous and recommended that they receive the Police Distinguished Conduct Medal, Class I.
Insp. B. B. Everest, Det.-Sgt. J. W. M. Dickson and D/Sub-Insp. Tsai Liu, who remained on guard at the front gate of the house, also engaged in an exchange of shots with one of the robbers and chased him along Avenue Edward VII where he was eventually brought to the ground by Insp. Everest jumping on to his back. No fewer than seventeen shots were fired by this robber at the police, the majority being at very close range.
The Board unanimously recommended Insp. Everest and Det.-Sgt. Dickson for the Police Distinguished Conduct Medal, Class II.
The recommendations of the Permanent Awards Board, endorsed by the Commissioner of Police, have been approved by the Watch Committee of the Council.

MUNICIPAL STAFF.
Order Book Extracts, July 2-9.
Fire Brigade.—The resignation of Workshops Officer W. C. Watson is accepted with effect from July 31, 1938.
Police Force.—The resignation of Sergeant E. C. Vestrup is accepted with effect from February 25, 1939.
Long leave is granted to the following from the dates specified:—

INDUSTRIAL ACCIDENTS DURING JUNE.
During the month of June there were reported to the Industrial Section a total of 149 industrial accidents of which seven were fatal. The causes of 138 were known with sufficient accuracy and 36 cases have been the subject of detailed investigation and instruction in prevention. 11 accidents involved women workers. Classified by causes 34 accidents were associated with machinery operated by power, of which two were fatal. There were two non-fatal accidents from electrical causes, 22 persons were struck by falling bodies and 26 falls resulted in three fatalities.
By industries, 23 persons in the machinery and metal products trades were injured; 18 accidents occurred in the course of building construction of which one was fatal; 10 persons were injured in the chemical industry; 22, three being fatal, in the textile trades; 13 in the food and tobacco industry; and 27 persons were injured, two fatally, in the transportation of goods.
Although the increase over the earlier part of the year reflects a revival of industrial activity the figures are greatly below the total of 224 accidents reported in June, 1937.

警务人员英勇奖章。
工部局董事会已批准向去年3月24日参与持械抢劫枪战案的警务人员颁发奖章，此项决定系根据常设奖励委员会提交的建议作出。
该枪战案发生在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）124号。成都路捕房共有六名外籍巡捕和九名华籍巡捕参与行动。其中两名外籍巡捕和两名华籍巡捕进入屋内，与三名劫匪搏斗。双方交火后，两名劫匪倒地，第三名劫匪也被抓获。常设奖励委员会认定，S. V. Gash 督察、D. Johnstone 警佐、华籍巡捕第192号及华籍巡捕第254号（组成进入屋内的行动小组）表现极为勇敢，建议授予他们一等警务优异行为勋章。
B. B. Everest 督察、J. W. M. Dickson 侦缉警佐和蔡刘（Tsai Liu，音译）副督察留守在房屋前门警戒，也与其中一名劫匪交火，并沿爱多亚路追捕该犯，最终由 Everest 督察跳上其背部将其制服。该劫匪向警方开枪不少于十七发，多数是在极近距离射击。
委员会一致推荐 Everest 督察和 Dickson 侦缉警佐获颁二等警务优异行为勋章。

MUNICIPAL ADVOCATE'S
REPORT FOR JUNE.

The Acting Municipal Advocate
states in his report that 8,072 cases
were prosecuted in the Shanghai
First Special Area District Court and
the Kiangsu High Court, Second
Branch, during June, as compared
with 8,403 cases in May. Out of the
total number of cases prosecuted,
6,762 were Administrative Cases, and
1,310 were Criminal Cases. Out of
the total number of Administrative
Cases brought to trial, 4,989 persons
failed to appear and their bail was
confiscated, and 37 were withdrawn
as compared with 4,749 cases in
which bail was confiscated and 11
cases withdrawn in May. 1,736 Ad-
ministrative Cases were prosecuted
to completion, out of which number
1,732 persons were convicted and four
were acquitted. 80 Criminal cases
were withdrawn, and 1,230 were
prosecuted to completion, out of
which number 1,125 persons were
convicted and 105 acquitted. The
total number of Administrative and
Criminal Cases prosecuted to com-
pletion was 2,966 as compared with
3,603 cases in May. 2,732 persons
were convicted, and 234 persons
acquitted, as compared with 3,468
persons convicted and 135 persons
acquitted in May.

In addition, there were 108 private
criminal prosecutions, as compared
with 84 in May.

Percentage of Convictions. — 83.3
per cent. of the persons charged in
Criminal Cases, and 99.7 per cent.
of the persons charged in Administra-
tive Cases were convicted, making
a total percentage of convictions for
the month 91.5 per cent. as compared
with 94.1 per cent. for the month of
May.

Appeals (a) By the Council.—Two
appeals were made during the month
of June, one to the Supreme Court,
and one to the High Court. Three
appeals were concluded during the
month of June. The total number
of appeals by the Council pending
on June 30 was as follows:— In the
Supreme Court, 1; in the High
Court, 5.

(b) By the Defendants.—109 ap-
peals were perfected during the
month, 14 to the Supreme Court, and
95 to the High Court. 115 appeals
by the defendants were concluded
and dealt with as follows:—

Accused found Not Guilty 4
Appeals dismissed 89
Appeals withdrawn 4
Cases sent back for retrial 5
Case not entertained 1
Sentence increased 1
Sentences reduced 11

There were 254 appeals filed by the
defendants pending on June 30 as
follows:— In the Supreme Court,
94; in the High Court 160.

Extradition. — No applications for
handing over were made by the
Extra-Settlement authorities during
the month.

Cases Pending.—On June 30, there
were pending in the High Court and
District Court 57 cases, which,
together with 260 cases on appeal,
make a total of 317 cases. In addition
to the above, there were seven cases
in which the accused were held on
writs of detention.

夏季饮料——

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
C.S.6, Special Branch...Sxxxx,
REPORT    Date ......July 13, 1938.
Subject................Rice Movements - July 13. 1938.
Made by.................and ................Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

At 1.40 p.m. July 13, a message from Yulin Road
Station reports that about 50 bags of Chinese rice were
transported from a godown of the National Industrial Bank,
in Thibet Road to the Dah Shing Rice Shop situated at the
corner of Tinghai and Pingliang Road.
Subsequent enquiries revealed that the rice is
destined for consumption by Chinese workers employed in
Japanese mills in the Yulin Road District.

At 3.35 p.m. July 13, a message from Louza Station
reports that a truckload of rice was detained at the Station.
The rice was to be transported to an address in the French
Concession.
Owner of rice advised to apply for a permit from
Mr. Harrup of the Finance Department, S.M.C. Permit is being
applied for.

（印：1/2 13 7 A）

主题................大米流动情况 - 1938年7月13日。
制作人.................和 ................由帕普（Papp）巡官转发。

7月13日下午1时40分，榆林路捕房发来消息报告称，约50包中国大米从西藏路国家工业银行（National Industrial Bank）的一座仓库运至定海路与平凉路转角的大兴米店。
随后的调查显示，这批大米 destined for 供职于榆林路地区日本纱厂的中国工人消费。

7月13日下午3时35分，老闸捕房发来消息报告称，一辆卡车装载的大米在该捕房被扣留。该批大米拟运往法租界某地址。
已告知大米所有者向工部局财务处的哈鲁普（Harrup）先生申请许可证。目前正在申请中。

（印：1/2 13 7 A）
