Copy of Police Order No. D.8713 dated July 12,1938.
----------

It is notified for information that in accordance with
Municipal Notification No. 4976 dated July 7, 1938, no Chinese
rice will be exported from the International Settlement without
a permit issued and signed by the Deputy Commissioner (Special
Branch). All duties must be warned of the above and rice that
is found being transported from the Settlement without the
necessary permit will be taken to the nearest police station
and the Special Branch informed immediately.

Close watch will be kept on the movements of rice from
the Settlement South of the Creek to the Settlement North of
the Creek and details of such movements must be reported to
the Special Branch. (C.R. F.2900/146)

FINANCE DEPARTMENT
May 20, 19 38

The Commissioner of Police.

Export of Chinese Rice from Shanghai.

With reference to the Police Report dated May 18, 1938,
in which mention is made of the export of 50,000 bags of
Chinese rice from Shanghai by the s.s."Chengtu" and the s.s.
"Fooshing" which left for Swatow, Hongkong and Kwangtung on
May 17, I send you herewith a copy of a memorandum giving
the results of certain enquiries which have been instituted
in the matter.

In view of the circumstances disclosed I should be
obliged if you would make arrangements to keep me informed
as to the movement of rice from the Settlement, whether for
export or otherwise. I think you will appreciate the point
that I do not contemplate being burdened with large stocks
of rice for the protection of the Community if certain
interests, with the cognisance of the French Police, continue
to evacuate local supplies from the Settlement.

（批：hig 21/）

警务处长。

从中国上海出口大米。

关于1938年5月18日的警务报告，其中提到“成都”号（Chengtu）轮船和“福星”号（Fooshing）轮船于5月17日离港前往汕头、香港和广东，从上海出口了50,000包中国大米一事，现随函附上一份备忘录副本，列出了对此事进行某些调查的结果。

鉴于所披露的情况，如蒙安排随时向我通报从公共租界运出大米的情况（无论是用于出口还是其他用途），我将不胜感激。我想您会理解这一点：如果某些利益方在法国警察的知情下继续从公共租界撤走本地供应，我不希望背负为保护社区而储备大量大米库存的重担。

（批：hig 21/）
J. T. 福特（Ford）
财政司兼主计长。

pages.en:
May 20, 1938.

Export of Chinese Rice from Shanghai.

The Police Report of May 18, 1938, mentioned the
fact that 50,000 bags of Chinese rice were exported from
Shanghai by the s.s."Chengtu" and s.s."Fooshing", which
left for Swatow, Hongkong, and Kwantung on May 17.
The Special Branch state that this information was
received from the Rice Guild and they have no details.
Interviews with the respective shipping companies
(Butterfield & Swire and Jardine, Matheson & Co.,) reveal
that during the past ten days considerable export of
Ordinary quality (that is, the lowest grade) Chinese rice
has taken place and further shipments have been arranged.
Jardine's shipping comprador offered the explanation that
the quantity of Chinese rice in Shanghai being now greatly
in excess of immediate requirements the surplus must be
disposed of as this quality cannot be stored with safety
through the Summer, the rice being without husk and full
of moisture.
Both shipping companies are operating on the French
Bund and they stated that permits were obtained by the
shippers without difficulty from the French Police.
An interview with Monsieur Moret (Successor to
Monsieur Sarly) of the Political Department of the French
Police revealed that the rice in question emanated from
the International Settlement and passed through the French
Concession under the usual transit permit which was
issued freely in the ordinary course of business and that
no irregularities were observed.
pages.zh:
1938年5月20日。

从中国上海出口大米。

1938年5月18日的警务报告提到，“成都”号轮船和“福星”号轮船于5月17日离港前往汕头、香港和广东，从上海出口了50,000包中国大米的事实。
特务科称，此信息来自米业公会，他们没有任何细节。
对各轮船公司（宝丰洋行（Butterfield & Swire）和怡和洋行（Jardine, Matheson & Co.））的访谈显示，在过去十天里，普通品质（即最低等级）的中国大米已有大量出口，并已安排了进一步的装运。
怡和洋行的航运买办解释说，由于目前上海的中国大米数量大大超过即时需求，必须处理掉 surplus，因为这种品质的大米无法安全度过夏季储存期，该大米无壳且水分充足。
两家轮船公司均在法外滩运营，他们表示，发货人很容易就从法国警察那里获得了许可证。
对法国警察政治部的莫雷特先生（Monsieur Moret，萨利先生（Monsieur Sarly）的继任者）的访谈显示，涉案大米源自公共租界，并在通常的过境许可证下通过法租界，该许可证在正常业务过程中自由签发，未观察到任何违规行为。

TRANSLATION OF FRENCH POLICE REPORT NO. 2173/S DATED 19.1.38.

SUBJECT: Untaxed Rice - Fraud on the part of the Charity
Organisations' Federation and the Yon Dah Rice
Hong.

The rice forming the subject of this report was
part of a consignment of 20520 bags imported by Messrs.
Raphael & Company arriving in Shanghai on January 10
in the s.s. Changon. This rice bought by Mr. KOO
SHING YI (顧馨一) (Yon Dah Rice Hong) was allowed to
enter duty-free with the assistance of a huchao issued
by the Inspector-General of Customs to the Charity
Organisations' Federation (上海各界慈善救災聯合會, No. 35
Yunnan Road. Of this consignment, 10,000 bags were
stored in a warehouse on Majestic Road (belonging to the
Chung-Kuo Cotton Enterprises Company (中國棉業公司堆));
the remaining 10520 bags were placed in the godowns of
William Hunt & Company (ex-China Merchants).

Considering that the rice warehoused entered duty
free, that this concession was only allowed in order to
permit the Charity Organisations' Federation to pay
less for the rice it distributes, that there is no doubt
that the entire thing is a fraud to which we cannot be
an accessory, the permits requested by Mr. KOO SHING YI
have been refused.

Further it seems to be in the interest of all all
to bring the above mentioned facts to the notice of the
Inspector-General of Customs, the Settlement Police and
the S.M.C. Food Sub-Committee.

1938年1月19日第2173/S号法国警察报告译文。

主题：未税大米——慈善团体联合会及允大米号之欺诈行为。

本报告所述之大米，系拉斐尔公司（Messrs. Raphael & Company）进口的一批货物中的一部分，共计20,520包，于1月10日由“长昂”号轮船（s.s. Changon）运抵上海。这批由顾馨一先生（允大米号）购买的大米，凭借海关总税务司签发给慈善团体联合会（上海各界慈善救災聯合會，云南路35号）的护照（huchao），获准免税入境。在这批货物中，10,000包存于麦琪路（Majestic Road）的一座仓库内（属中国棉业公司堆栈）；其余10,520包则存入威廉亨特公司（William Hunt & Company，原招商局）的货栈。

鉴于入库的大米系免税进入，且此项优惠仅旨在让慈善团体联合会以较低价格分发其大米，毫无疑问，整件事是一起欺诈行为，我方不能成为其帮凶，因此已拒绝顾馨一先生申请的许可证。

此外，似乎符合各方利益的做法是将上述事实提请注意海关总税务司、租界警务处及工部局粮食小组委员会。

Gentlemen,
Collections bringing in very little

we have the honour to bring to your notice that

Company, Roosevelt Terminal. 3,000 bags are to
be delivered as per the attached list. We have
the honour, therefore, to request that you issue

Yours etc.,

1937年8月28日，上海谷物业主公会、上海米业业主公会以及已解散的上海市粮食调节委员会，与以前从事从南市外滩及闸北苏州河码头运输大米的各运输公司合作，成立了一家联合大米运输公司，名为“义昌运输公司”，办公地点位于汕头路78号。汤立生被任命为新公司的经理。该公司拥有六十辆摩托卡车车队。

1937年12月，原先位于南市的米行老板对义昌运输公司感到不满，因为该公司将每包大米的运费从十二分提高到了十五分。由于这次涨价，业主们于1938年1月1日在蒙蒂尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）恒茂里65号成立了同发运输公司，由吴义山先生担任经理。

1938年1月7日上午10时10分，因同发公司运输一批西贡大米，义昌运输公司的人员与同发运输公司的苦力在外滩发生争执，但未酿成事故。1月8日上午，义昌运输公司聚集了约60名无业游民，前往外滩与同发公司的苦力制造麻烦。

Date November 9, 37
Subject Transportation of Changshu Rice to Shanghai.
Made by D. I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by
In connection with Special Branch report of October 2,
1937, dealing with the detention by the Changshu Hsien Government
of 2,500 "zars" of rice ordered by the Shanghai Municipality
Food Adjustment Committee for the local market, it is now learned
that the rice has been sold by auction by the Changshu authorities.
This procedure being adopted with the excuse that the people of
Changshu insisted upon the confiscation of the rice. All
efforts made by the Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment
Committee to effect the release of the rice have met with failure.
The Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee, Room
606, Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII, ceased functioning
on November 6, because of lack of support from local rice dealers
and rice hong owners associations and also because of difficulties
encountered in conducting negotiations with the different civil
and military authorities in matters relating to the transportation
of rice to Shanghai.
Pan Lien-pih

Subject Cereal & Rice Dealers' Association - application for protection
against loafers during unloading of rice.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang Forwarded by [Signature]

Mr. Fu Tseng Loh (符錚祿), a representative of the
Cereal & Rice Dealers' Association, called at Police Head-
quarters to-day, October 30, and explained that owing to the
erection of barbed wire barricades on the south bank of the
Soochow Creek to the west of Thibet Road Bridge, the unlading
of rice from rice boats onto Jetties 69, 70, 72/74 and 76 had
been interrupted with the result that some 80 rice boats
fully loaded with rice had been obliged to discontinue unload-
ing and had berthed in midstream. Owing to the sudden change
in the situation around the locality of the Thibet Road Bridge,
local rice dealers and rice boatmen, who are very anxious to
unload the cargo, apply to the Police for use of the public
jetties, located to the immediate west of the north end of the
Chekiang Road Bridge. Should this permission be granted,
Mr. Fu requested that Police be detailed to afford protection
against loafers during the unloading.

TRANSIT DUES ON RICE REMOVED A.M. 20-10-37

The following notice issued by the Shanghai
People's Food Adjustment Committee appears in to-day's
issue of the "Lih Pao," the "Shun Pao" and other local
newspapers :-
    "According to an order from the Ministry of
Finance, food provisions constitute an item of native
products that are required to pay transit dues. It will
be recalled that some time ago a telegram was sent to the
Ministry of Finance by this Committee requesting the
abolition of these dues on rice so that the food supplies
of the people might be maintained.
    "Now according to a notification No. 1619 issued
by the Customs House appearing in the local press to-day
(date not given), all cereals, including rice, wheat, etc.,
are exempt from payment of transit dues as from October 18
in accordance with instructions from the Ministry of Finance.
From the date of the promulgation of this notice, the price
of all kinds of rice on sale by rice shops should be reduced
by $0.40. The highest price for the best quality rice
should not exceed $14 per picul. A proportionate reduction
should be made in the price of rice of inferior quality.
    "This notice is hereby published for the general
information of the public."

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

    Following the abolition of the transit dues on
food provisions, the price of rice has dropped. Best
quality rice is now being sold at $14 per picul.
    A further reduction in the price of rice will
be likely in view of the arrival in Shanghai of large
quantities of the new crops

REPORT
Date.. October 19, 1937.
Subject Detention of rice by Martial Law Commander's Headquarters.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

The levy by the Shanghai-Woosung Martial Law
Commander's Office of a special "Huchao" fee for the transpor-
tation of rice into Shanghai was never made in ordinary times.
It is doubtful whether General Yang Hu, the Martial Law
Commander, has obtained permission from the Nanking Government
to make this levy. He is collecting the money on the pretext
that he has to afford protection to rice boats which necessitated
some expenses by his office. His boldness is due to the fact
that he has the support of General Chu Shao Liang, Commander-in-
Chief of the Chinese forces at the Shanghai front who is
apparently on very good terms with General Yang Hu.

According to information from the Tangpu, Mr.
Pan Kung Chan, Commissioner of the Social Bureau, who is
connected with the Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment
Committee, has telegraphed to Nanking reporting the interference
by General Yang Hu with rice transportation and it is expected
that a reply will be received soon.

Mr. Chen Yung, Secretary to Mr. T.V.Soong, has
been informed confidentially of the action of General Yang Hu.

For p.r.
（印：S.B. 19 OCT. 1937）
Tan Shao Liang
Superintendent.

On September 10, the Hsien Government of Changshu detained
15 boats loaded with 2,000 "zars" of rice bound on behalf
of the Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee, Room
No. 600, Yootung Building, 184 Avenue Edward VII, on the grounds
that the rice was bought on behalf of the "enemy." The
Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee, of which Mr.
Wong Shiao-lai is the chairman, therefore submitted a petition
to the Kiangsu Provincial Food and Fuel Adjustment Bureau at
Chinkiang, informing them that the rice was purchased by the
Food Adjustment Committee and requesting that the Hsien
Government of Changshu be instructed to release the boats.
In compliance with the request, the Kiangsu Provincial Food
and Fuel Adjustment Bureau ordered the Hsien Government to
release the shipment, but instead of releasing the rice boats,
the Hsien Government sold 1,500 "zars" of the rice by auction,
declaring that Mr. Wong Shiao-lai, chairman of the Shanghai
Municipality Food Adjustment Committee, was a traitor, and
that the rice was purchased by him on behalf of the "enemy."
The Hsien Government also declared that the detention of the
rice boats was carried out at the request of the people. The
Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee then requested
the Shanghai City Government Bureau of Social Affairs, the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the Shanghai Citizens'
Association to certify the shipment of rice, and on September
19, submitted a petition through the secretary of the Changshu
Rice Trade Association, Mr. Lu Loo Jin (盧慕琴), to the
Changshu Hsien Government, explaining the actual situation.
No reply was received to this petition, and Mr. Wong Shiao-lai
on September 28 despatched a telegram to the Kiangsu Provincial

As a rule, when the Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee desires to purchase rice from the interior, a report should be made to the Food Adjustment Committee of the district where the rice is to be purchased. When the permission of that district food adjustment committee has been obtained, a certificate to move traffic pass are then issued respectively by the Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee and the Nanking-Shanghai Martial Law Enforcement Commander's Headquarters to the boatmen concerned for transporting the rice to Shanghai.
In connection with the above shipment of 2,000 "piculs" of rice, as there was no food adjustment committee in existence in Changshu, the Shanghai Municipality Food Adjustment Committee did not make the usual report, nor did it inform the Changshu Hsien Government of the purchase of the rice. The Hsien Government considered this a slight and detained the rice boats as a reprisal.

FOOD PANIC IN SHANGHAI APPEARS IMMINENT

The hostilities in Shanghai have caused
the transportation of food stuffs from up country to come
almost to a standstill, and despite the Government's efforts

attempting to transport 12 boat loads of rice from Zangzau
to Shanghai was prohibited to remove same by the Zangzau

With reference to the contents of the attached letter
dated August 20, 1937 addressed to the Commissioner of
Police, I have to report that Miss L.M. Hinder, controller
of Food Stocks, has been interviewed; she states that
the Food Committee was fully aware of the request of Messrs.
Bunge & Co. Ltd., and that since this concern had been
able to prove to the Food Committee that the 1,800 tons
of rice had been contracted for prior to the outbreak of
hostilities here, a pass has been issued for the stock
to be removed through the Settlement and French Concession
to Chinese Territory, where (according to Miss Hinder), it
will be taken over by the Chinese Military authorities.
The pass was issued solely on the grounds of the stock
having been contracted for some time ago and in an effort
to avoid alienating the good feelings of the Chinese
Municipality authorities now shown to the Shanghai Municipal
Council.
In the event of any other cases of this nature coming to
Miss Hinder's notice, she will advise the Commissioner of
Police prior to issuing the required pass.

January 9th, 1941.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO :-

OFFICIAL PRICE OF RICE TO BE FIXED IN HONGKEW
DISTRICT

Thanks to the good offices of the
Japanese military authorities in importing rice to mitigate
the rice shortage among the local Japanese community,
a semi-official price of rice is about to be fixed in
Hongkew District. This will be the whole-sale price
plus a commission for retail merchants who undertake the
sale of the rice supplied by the Japanese military
authorities. This price will be about 5% lower
than the prevailing retail price.
It is estimated that some 20,000 bags
of rice have now been stocked by rice-dealers in Hongkew
District.

虹口地区将确定大米官方价格

得益于日本军方在进口大米以缓解当地日本社区大米短缺方面的斡旋，虹口地区即将确定半官方大米价格。该价格将是批发价加上承担销售日本军方供应大米的零售商的佣金。该价格将比现行零售价低约5%。
据估计，目前虹口地区的米商已储备了约20,000袋大米。

Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached translation of
an article appearing in the December 27th issue of
the "Tairiku Shimpo" regarding the proposed distribu-
tion of rice among local Japanese residents by the
Japanese Residents' Corporation, enquiries made at
the Japanese Residents' Corporation show that during
December, last year, the organization forwarded a
petition to the Japanese Military authorities for the
alloting of some 12,000 Zar of Sungkiang rice per
month for the consumption of local Japanese residents
in order to guarantee the staple diet of the Japanese
residents.

The Japanese Military authorities complied with
the request and arranged for the necessary amount of
Sungkiang rice. This rice is to be distributed
through the agents of the Japanese Army such as
the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, the Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha
and the Daimaru Yoko.

A meeting was held at the Daimaru Yoko, North
Szechuen Road, on December 31st, 1940, attended by
representatives of the above-mentioned agents of the
Japanese Army, officials of the Japanese Residents'
Corporation and the local Japanese rice retailers,
when the method of sidtribution was discussed.

It was decided that the rice be allotted to the
wholesale agents in question and through then to the
Japanese rice dealers. Consumers (Japanese families
only) will be allowed to purchase the necessary amount
of rice at the price of Yen 34.50 per 100 Lbs..
No tickets system will be employed for the time being.

报告
事由：当地日本居民的大米分配情况。
制作人：D. S. Kamashita 转呈人：D. I. Crawford。

关于附件中译自12月27日《大陆新报》刊登的关于日本居留民团拟向当地日本居民分配大米文章的内容，经向日本居留民团查询得知，去年12月期间，该组织向日本军方提交了一份请愿书，要求每月拨给约12,000石松江大米供当地日本居民消费，以保障日本居民的主食供应。

日本军方同意了该请求，并安排了所需数量的松江大米。这批大米将通过日本陆军的代理人进行分配，如三井物产株式会社、三菱商事株式会社和大丸洋行。

1940年12月31日，在北四川路的大丸洋行举行了一次会议，上述日本陆军代理人代表、日本居留民团官员以及当地日本大米零售商出席了会议，讨论了分配方法。

会议决定，将大米分配给有关的批发代理人，再通过他们分配给日本米商。消费者（仅限日本家庭）将被允许以每100磅34.50日元的价格购买所需数量的大米。暂时不采用票证制度。

As a result of an appeal made by
the Japanese Residents' Corporation to the Japanese
military authorities referring to the rice famine which
the 80,000 Japanese residents are now suffering, the military
authorities officially permitted on December 26 the monthly

As to the method of delivering this
amount of rice, perhaps the Japanese Residents' Corporation
will issue tickets for rice to the Japanese, who will be
able to get certain amounts of rice at cost price in exchange
for tickets at shops of Japanese grain merchants in the
Hongkew District.

日本机构“ne Ta Chong Company”（音译）最近在常州、宜兴、苏州和嘉兴地区收购大米。第一批一万多袋大米已运抵此处，下一批不久也将到达。昨天，约5000袋“粳米”和“糯米”从虹口运入租界。南浔“粳米”的价格为每石38.50至40元。常州上等“粳米”以每石43至43.50元的价格秘密出售，苏州和昆山的“粳米”价格为每石42至42.50元。

April 2, 1940.
Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Ta Mei Pao, National Herald, Chinese-
American Daily News :-

Company to be Formed to Regulate Provisions

It is strongly rumoured by rice dealers recently
that publicity for co-operation in the producing and
purchasing of provisions is merely an attempt of a certain
party to organize a provisions transportation company.
Yet according to news secured by this newspaper, this affair
is under the joint preparation of certain provisions
merchants, and it is planned to establish a "Dah Chong Company"
(大昌公司) with a capital of ten million dollars. The
purpose of this company will be to facilitate the transport
of rice and other provisions from the various districts.
The progress of this matter is being kept in secrecy, and
whether or not there are ulterior motives remains to be
seen.

《新闻报》、《申报》、《大美报》、《国民日报》、《中美日报》：

拟组建公司调节粮食供应

米商近期盛传，关于在粮食生产和采购方面进行合作的宣传，仅仅是某一方试图组织一家粮食运输公司的企图。然而据本报获悉的消息，此事正由某些粮商联合筹备，计划成立一家资本为一千万元的“大昌公司”。该公司的目的是便利从各地区运输大米和其他粮食。此事的进展一直保密，是否存在其他动机尚待观察。

With reference to the attached extract from the Shanghai Times dated February 18 regarding rice being sold at cheap rates in the Hongkew district, enquiries show that a Japanese firm named Hwa An Company (華安公司) situated at 806 Szechuen Road, is selling "Kan Mee" rice of 2nd quality between 9.30 a.m. and 12 noon and 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. daily. Purchasers must be in possession of tickets which are distributed to people in the alleyways in that vicinity and each ticket entitles the holder to buy two "suns" (0.02 "zar") at ¥0.50 or $0.75 equivalent to ¥25.00 or $37.50 per "zar".

Another rice shop named Daikan Rice Shop (大漢米店) situated at 170 Quinsan Road also conducted the cheap sale of rice of both Kan Mee (2nd quality) and See Mee rice. This sale commenced on February 16 at the rate of $3.60 for .125 "zar" for each purchaser, equivalent to $28.80 per "zar", but was discontinued on February 20 on instructions from the Japanese Consulate-General. The reason for this order is believed to be due to a complaint by the proprietors of Japanese shops situated in the vicinity who had their premises damaged by the large crowd which gathered at the rice shop.

The Fuchi Yang Hong, North Szechuen Road, which is mentioned in the attached extract as also selling cheap rice, is probably the Foh Kee (福記洋行)

SHANGHAI TIMES

Cheaper
Rice In
Hongkew

$17 Per Zah Less Than
On South Side Of
The Creek

Money-wise Chinese rather than hungry mobs swooped down on Hongkew rice shops yesterday to take advantage of the price of rice in the Japanese-occupied area, the "Tairiku Shimpo" reported yesterday afternoon.
Rice in Hongkew was $17 a zah cheaper than south of Soochow creek, the "Tairiku" pointed out.
Quick to learn of the lifting of traffic regulations applied to Chinese entering the areas guarded by the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party and the difference in the price of rice on the two sides of the creek, Chinese refugees have flocked to Hongkew rice shops and caused traffic jams at several points because the lines in front of the shops extended far out into the street, the paper said.
Rice on the south side of Soochow Creek was reported yesterday at $54 a zah, while the official rice price in the Hongkew area, as set by the Japanese military authorities, was $37 a zah, the "Tairiku" said.

Rice Hong Besieged
The employees of the Fuchi Yang Hong, a rice shop on North Szechuen Road, yesterday morning opened the shop to find a long waiting line of Chinese refugees with baskets and bags in their hands, the paper said.
By 9 o'clock in the morning, the paper continued, the street in the neighbourhood of the shop was crowded with several thousand Chinese. A policeman was called to the scene to control traffic. At one time traffic was at a standstill, the "Tairiku" said.
With a limited supply of rice on hand, the Fuchi Yang Hong was forced to sell only one sheng or 60 sen worth of rice a person. About 1,000 kilograms of rice was sold within a short time, the "Tairiku" stated.

《大陆新报》昨日下午报道，昨天涌入虹口米店的并非饥饿的暴民，而是精明的中国人，他们利用日军占领区的大米价格优势获利。
《大陆新报》指出，虹口的大米价格比苏州河以南每石便宜17美元。
该报称，中国难民迅速得知进入由日本特别海军陆战队守卫地区的交通管制已解除，以及河两岸大米价格的差异，纷纷涌向虹口的米店，导致多处交通堵塞，因为店前的队伍一直延伸到街道上。
《大陆新报》称，据报道，昨天苏州河以南的大米价格为每石54美元，而虹口地区由日本军方设定的官方大米价格为每石37美元。

米店被围
该报称，昨天早上，北四川路一家名为“Fuchi Yang Hong”的米店员工开门时，发现一群手持篮子和袋子的中国难民排着长队等候。
该报继续称，到上午9点，米店附近的街道上挤满了数千名中国人。一名警察被叫到现场维持交通秩序。《大陆新报》称，交通一度陷入停滞。
由于手头大米供应有限，“Fuchi Yang Hong”被迫每人只出售一升或价值60仙的大米。《大陆新报》称，短时间内售出了约1000公斤大米。

January 18th, 1940.

Date

Dear Mr. Phillips,

The Louis Dreyfus & Co. has recently approached the Japanese Authorities with a request that permission be granted to bring into the International Settlement south of Soochow Creek, some 130,000 bags of Saigon rice which have been shipped here on several occasions and stored in the area north of the Creek since the arrival of the first consignment on December 5th, 1939.

The Japanese Authorities are prepared, of course, to issue the required permission, provided that the above-said amount of rice will not be used for profiteering purpose so that it will contribute to alleviate the general acute situation arising out of the rice shortage in Shanghai. I believe that you will agree with our view in this matter in the light of the measures recently taken by your authorities as regards rice marketing.

I am writing this letter by way of drawing your attention to the above-mentioned stock of rice which is to be supplied to the local market in rather a large amount, with the hope that you may be able to see that the rice will be properly disposed of.

Yours sincerely,
(Sgd.) Y. Miura.

Shanghai, 24th October 1939.

R. W. Yorke Esq.,
Deputy Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

We recently received by the French Mail steamer "ATHOS II"
a shipment of Rice and there were six bags of sweepings left over at
the Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf Co's (Broadway) Wharf. Yesterday we sent
our office coolie, Tse Tsang Seng (朱章生 ) at about 9.40 A.M., to
take the ferry from the Bund to that Wharf. The ferry is regularly run
by the Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf between the Bund and that Wharf and is
called the "CLUTHAX"(克泰 ). Although it is now more than 24 hours
since he left the office he has not returned with our chit-book. In
the meantime we have received a reply from the Wharf in question, so
he of course has been at the Wharf. He has no Pass for going overland
to Hongkew, but we have always understood that for a British Wharf it is
possible for Chinese to proceed by ferries or boats on the river. We
cannot imagine what has happened to him and fear that he has been arrested
or detained at the Wharf by some "self-appointed"or other authorities.

As this particular incident is connected with our rice business
and you have been specially delegated by the S.M.C. for such work, we
appeal to you to investigate the matter at once. The coolie in question
is an old servant of our firm, is a very quiet and loyal worker, and we
are sure he has not done anything illegal or contrary to Police regulations.
He went on this work on our instructions and we are morally responsible
to see that no harm has come to him. Please do your utmost for his and
our behalf, and thanking you in advance, we beg to remain,

Yours faithfully,
P.P. LOUIS DREYFUS & Cie

尊敬的先生：

我们最近通过法国邮船“ATHOS II”号收到一批大米，在上海与虹口码头公司（百老汇路）的码头上剩下了六袋扫仓米。昨天上午约9点40分，我们派办事处的苦力朱章生（Tse Tsang Seng）从外滩乘渡轮前往该码头。该渡轮由上海与虹口码头公司运营，定期往返于外滩与该码头之间，名为“CLUTHAX”（克泰）。虽然他从办事处离开已超过24小时，但他尚未带回我们的签条簿。与此同时，我们收到了有关码头的回复，因此他当然曾到达码头。他没有陆路前往虹口的通行证，但我们一直认为，对于英商码头而言，中国人可以通过渡轮或河上船只通行。我们无法想象他发生了什么事，担心他已被某些“自封”当局或其他当局在码头逮捕或拘留。

由于这一特定事件与我们的大米业务有关，且您受工部局特别委派负责此类工作，我们恳请您立即调查此事。该苦力是我们商行的老仆人，是一位非常安静且忠诚的工人，我们确信他没有做任何违法或违反警察规章的事情。他是奉我们的指示去执行这项工作的，我们在道义上有责任确保他未受伤害。请为您和我们尽力而为，预先致谢，谨此致意，

您忠实的，

Subject (in full) Interference with the transportation of rice into
the Settlement at Garden Bridge.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

F
Mr. Webb.

On the morning of October 2, 1939, the
Japanese sentry on duty at the Garden Bridge prohibited
consignments of rice from being transported into the
Settlement by motor trucks via the Garden Bridge.
As a result some 3,000 bags of rice which arrived at
the Shanghai North Railway Station by rail on the
afternoon of October 1 failed to enter the Settlement.
Negotiations are said to be in progress between the
dealers concerned and the Japanese authorities.

C. Crawford
D. I.

REPORT
Date Sept. 22, 1939.

Subject. Japanese Monopoly of Rice Supply in Nantao.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by R. W. Mac [signature]

The rice supply in Nantao has been monopolized by the Japanese since September 8, 1939. This monopoly is managed by members of the Nantao Section of the Japanese Special Service Department and the Japanese Military Police with the assistance of Chinese staff of the Nantao Administrative Office.

Rice shops in Nantao, some 60 in number, which used to obtain their supplies from Siking, Teepao, Sungkiang, Pootung and the foreign settlements, are now selling rice supplied by the Japanese, who have a godown on Lungmen Terrace, opposite the Nantao Administrative Office, 50 Ih Soh Ka, Nantao. Rice shops obtain their stocks from the Japanese at a cost of approximately $20.00 per "zar" and sell same at $26 and $27 per "zar", or ¥21 and ¥22 in Japanese military notes. (Prior to September 14, the buying price was only $17 and the selling price $21.) At each of the shops is exhibited a poster inscribed "Place for exchanging military notes for rice."

The rice being supplied by the Japanese is "See Mee" which is brought from Wuhu by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.

No information can be obtained regarding the Nan Shing Company (南興公司) which is said to be controlling the rice supply in Nantao as mentioned in the attached newspaper translations dated September 18 and 21, 1939.

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

主题：日军对南市大米供应的垄断。

制作人 潘连璧 侦探长 转呈人 R. W. Mac [签名]

自 1939 年 9 月 8 日以来，南市的大米供应已被日本人垄断。这一垄断由日本特务机关南市分部成员和日本宪兵队管理，并得到南市行政公署中方职员的协助。

南市约有 60 家米店，过去从西京、提篮桥（音译，Teepao）、松江、浦东和公共租界等地进货，现在则销售由日本人提供的大米。日本人在南市一索卡 50 号、南市行政公署对面的龙门台（Lungmen Terrace）设有一个仓库。米店以每“石”约 20.00 元的成本从日本人处进货，并以每“石”26 元和 27 元的价格出售，或按日本军票计价 21 元和 22 日元。（在 9 月 14 日之前，进价仅为 17 元，售价为 21 元。）每家店铺都张贴着一张海报，上书“军票换米处”。

日本人供应的大米是“西米”（See Mee），由三井物产株式会社从芜湖运来。

关于南兴公司（南興公司），据称其控制着南市的大米供应，如附带的 1939 年 9 月 18 日和 21 日的报纸译文所述，但无法获得有关该公司的任何信息。

Date September 20, 1939.

Subject. Japanese and Rice Supplies for Shanghai.

Made by/ and Forwarded by D. S. I. Macadie

With reference to the attached extract from
the French Police Intelligence Report dated September
16 stating that the Japanese authorities are placing
difficulties upon the transportation of "See Kee"
from Kompo to Shanghai, enquiries show that this
refers to the detention of nine rice boats by the
Japanese authorities at the Floating Restaurant on
September 13, the boats being later removed to
Hongkew. Following the detention, the Kompo rice
dealers in Shanghai sent on September 14 telegram and
express letters to the dealers in Kompo advising them
to temporarily cease purchasing and sending rice to
Shanghai. Although the rice detained has now been
released through private arrangements, the dealers have
not yet decided to resume the transportation in the
near future. No confirmation can be obtained

September 16, 1939.

Shanghai Tramway Company's Workers Given Rice Allowance.

The management of the Shanghai Tramway Company,
No.185 Soochow Road, announced yesterday that commencing
with the month of September conductors and drivers (in all
1,600 men) will be given a rice allowance of $4.50 each per
mensem.

The 400 mechanics of the workshops in Baikal Road
and Hart Road are already in receipt of this allowance.

Japanese and Rice Supplies for Shanghai.

According to information secured from rice merchants,
the Japanese authorities are placing difficulties upon the
transportation of "See Mee" from Kiangpeh to Shanghai.
They are insisting that the Japanese firm of Mitsui undertake
the transportation of rice to Shanghai. Kiangpeh rice
dealers yesterday sent telegrams to the rice producing centres
requesting them to cease sending rice to Shanghai.

The 1,309 bags of rice seized by the Japanese from
No.4 Pontoon on The Bund have been bought by the Japanese
at a price which has not been made known.

（批：28 / 19/9 / Pnd / 19/9）

A cheap rice selling centre has been established

Subject Confiscation of two Cargo Boats by the Japanese Military

Made by P.S. D.D. Danemanis Forwarded by (Police)

Sir,
The undersigned begs to report that at
appr. 1 p.m. on 13/9/39 two cargo boats (S.M.C. Nos.
583 and 17113) were tied up to No. 4 Municipal
Pontoon and were unloading rice. The rice was owned
by the Honan Company, 33 Szechuen Road (Tel:-13651)
and had come from Kowan on the Yangtsze by the
s/s Tung Fang (Japanese steamer). After having
unloaded 52 bags of rice a Japanese Military Police launch
with 5 or 6 Japanese Military Policemen in uniform
tied up at the pontoon and ordered the loadah to stop
unloading. The undersigned was then informed of the
happening by a Chinese Coolie. Proceeding to No. 4
Pontoon, I came just in time to see that the launch
had taken the two cargo boats in tow and was steaming
off towards the Floating Restaurant. There were
3 or 4 boatsmen on the cargo boats. The undersigned
ascertained that the confiscated amount of rice is
334 bags. The undersigned immediately informed
Central Station by telephone.

I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
T. Danemanis.
P.S. 47.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / DEPUTY COMMISSIONER / SPECIAL BRANCH）

Yulin Road Station,
REPORT Date Sept. 8th., 39
19
Subject Japanese Firm Stores 10,000 sacks of rice, in
Yulin Road District.

Made by. D.S.I.Rosa Forwarded by

Sir:
while conducting investigation into a case of
theft in a godown at 222, Chemulpo Road, owned by
Messrs Fukki Yoko(福记)Co.,467, Kiangse Road,(Vide
F.I.R. 654/39Y.Rd.Stn.) it was learned that the
firm had a large stock of rice.
Enquiries ascertained that the firm has secured a
large consignment of rice from wuhu, which is being
discharged from steamers at the Jukong wharf. From that
point the rice is conveyed by motor-trucks hired from
the Tashiro Yoko(田代)Transportation Co.,52,Kasning
road, to the godown at 222, Chemulpo Road.
During the past three days some 10,000 odd sacks
of rice has reached the godown, and are now stored
within. It is expected that this total will reach
30,000 sacks at an early date.
As far as can be learned the rice will be sold
only in the Area North of the Creek, and will in all
probability be supplied to the depots established by
the Special Service Section of the Japanese Military,
for sale of rice to the general public(As mentioned in
Misc. 203/39 Y.Road Stn.)

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
D.S.I.

主题：日本公司在榆林路地区储存10,000袋大米。

制作人：副督察 Rosa 转呈人

先生：
在对江西路467号福记公司（Fukki Yoko(福记)Co.）拥有的芝罘路222号仓库盗窃案进行调查时（参见初报 654/39 榆林路警署），获悉该公司拥有大量大米库存。
经查询查明，该公司已从芜湖获得大批大米，该批大米正在菊公码头（Jukong wharf，音译）从轮船上卸货。随后，大米由从田代洋行（Tashiro Yoko(田代)Transportation Co.，地址：卡宁路52号）租用的卡车运至芝罘路222号的仓库。
在过去三天里，约有10,000多袋大米运抵仓库，目前储存在内。预计总数不久将达到30,000袋。
据所知，这些大米将仅在苏州河北岸地区销售，并且极有可能供应给日军特务机关设立的、面向公众销售大米的销售点（如杂项档案 203/39 榆林路警署中所述）。

S.1, Special Branch,
September 6, 1939.

Sale of rice by Japanese in area north of
Soochow Creek.
------------------------------------

The Special Service Section of the Japanese Military has
established a depot for the sale of rice at 373/5 Pingliang
Road, enquiries by this branch show that the depot occupies
three addresses, Nos. 373, 375 and 377 Pingliang Road. The
sale is sponsored by the Foh Kee (福记) Company (Fukuki Yoko),
a Japanese firm located at 467 Kiangse Road, and the rice being
sold was recently brought from Wuhu by rail.

During the course of enquiries, it has been ascertained
that depots for the sale of rice have also been established at
the following places by the Foh Kee Company since September 4:-
Shanghai Cereal Company (上海糧穀公司),
44 Woosung Road.
Mizushita Shop (水下商店),
43 Hanbury Road.
Eiyoya Rice Shop (营养屋白水店),
205 Nansing Road.
Shanghai Cooperative Society (上海購買組合),
1139 North Szechuen Road.
Hongkew Branch of Foh Kee Company,
593 North Szechuen Road.

At each place, a white cloth banner inscribed "Depot for
exchange of military notes for rice" is exhibited. The price
quoted varies according to market fluctuation, and the price
for yesterday, September 5, was Yen 18.40 per "dan" or Yen 23.60
per bag (= 1.25 "dan"), with a purchase of one bag to each customer
only. The first batch of rice brought to Shanghai from Wuhu, it
is said, amounted to 20,600 bags and the major portion has already
been sold.

Enquiries at this company for the purpose of buying rice to
bring south of the Creek met with a strong refusal.

Certified true copy.
J. F. Lovell

Made by. D.P.S. Mizoguchi.......Forwarded by. C. Gainsford S O

With reference to the attached extract
from the "Fairiku Shinpo" dated August 25, 1939, reporting
on the price of rice, enquiries elicit that in view of
the recent rise in the price of rice, the Japanese Residents'
Corporation authorities held a meeting in the Japanese
Residents' Corporation, Nansau Road, at 3 p.m. August 24,
to discuss and draw up measures regarding the problem of
the rise in the price of rice.

Among those present were officials of the
Residents' Corporation, members of the Japanese Chamber of
Commerce and Industry, and local Japanese rice merchants.

Mr. Matsuura, chief of the Social Affairs
Department of the Japanese Residents' Corporation, when
interviewed, stated that views and opinions had been
exchanged, but that no resolution had been arrived at with
regard to the problem.        It is reported that a
guild to deal with grain is to be established in the near
future with assistance of the Japanese official authorities
who will endeavour to adjust and regulate the price of
rice.        Enquiries show that the information on
the isolation of the Foreign Settlements is incorrect.

参照附件中1939年8月25日《每日新闻》关于米价的摘录，经查询得知，鉴于近期米价上涨，日本居留民团当局于8月24日下午3时在南佐路的日本居留民团召开会议，讨论并制定应对米价上涨问题的措施。

出席会议的有居留民团官员、日本工商会成员以及当地日本米商。

在接受询问时，日本居留民团社会部部长松浦先生表示，双方交换了看法和意见，但就该问题尚未达成决议。据报道，在日本官方当局的协助下，不久将成立一个处理粮食的同业公会，致力于调整和管制米价。查询显示，关于隔离外国租界的信息不实。

pages.en:
（批：Osaka
Shimpo
28.8.30）

ISOLATED FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS URGED TO REGULATE
PRICE OF RICE

The so-called "Hongkew side" is in a great
panic owing to the upward surge of rice prices caused by
a corner in the grain market by profiteering rice merchants.
In order to cope with the situation, Mr.
Amano, director of the Japanese Residents' Corporation,
Mr. Nakagawa, secretary of the Chamber of Commerce, and
local Japanese rice dealers, etc. met in the council hall
of the Residents' Corporation at 6 p.m. August 24 and
exchanged views regarding the improvement of the situation.
They reached the conclusion that the only
practical way would be to isolate the Foreign Settlements
with the aid of the Japanese Army and Navy.
pages.zh:
（批：大阪
每日新闻
1930.8.28）

敦促隔离外国租界以管制米价

所谓的“虹口方面”因投机米商囤积居奇导致米价飙升而陷入极大恐慌。
为应对这一局势，日本居留民团团长天野先生、工商会秘书中川先生以及当地日本米商等人，于8月24日下午6时在居留民团议事厅会面，就改善局势交换了意见。
他们得出的结论是，唯一切实可行的办法是在日本陆海军的协助下隔离外国租界。

On August 26, copies of a notice issued

REPORT
Date August 21, 1939.
Subject Japanese interference with rice supplies for Shanghai
Made by/ and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The Japanese authorities have been interfering
with the rice supplies for Shanghai, especially those
destined for the International Settlement and the
French Concession, and information from a fairly
reliable source is to the effect that it is their
intention to create a panic in the rice situation
and so cause disturbances with a view to embarrassing
the Settlement authorities. The proposed plan is that
when the situation has become so acute, the refugees
accommodated in Nantao will be sent into the
Settlement and French Concession with instructions
to loot rice shops in these two areas.

The above measure is formulated by the
Japanese, it is reported, for the blockading of the
foreign Settlements of Shanghai in an indirect manner,
so that they do not appear in the picture. It is
the opinion of those authorities that with a scarcity
of rice and those organized riots they will be able
to prevail upon the poorer classes through propaganda
to leave the foreign areas for the Japanese occupied
areas where foodstuffs will be obtainable at specially
reduced prices.

C. Crawford.
D. I.
D.C. (Special Branch).

报告
日期：1939年8月21日。
事由：日本方面干扰上海的大米供应
由/并经督察员Crawford撰写并转发

日本当局一直在干扰上海的大米供应，尤其是运往公共租界和法租界的供应。据相当可靠的消息来源称，其意图是制造大米恐慌，从而引发骚乱，旨在使租界当局陷入困境。拟定的计划是，当局势变得如此严峻时，将安置在南市的难民送入租界和法租界，并指示他们在这两个区域抢劫米店。

据报道，上述措施由日本人制定，旨在以间接方式封锁上海的外国租界，使其不直接露面。这些当局认为，通过大米短缺和有组织的暴乱，他们将能够通过宣传手段迫使贫困阶层离开外国辖区，前往日军占领区，在那里可以以特别降低的价格获得食品。

C. Crawford.

S.1, Special Branch,
July 3, 1939.

Proclamation issued under the name of Mayor Fu posted outside
the Western District Branch Police Bureau, 92 Jessfield Road.
------------------------------------------------------------------------

On June 30, 1939, a proclamation issued by the Shanghai City
Government was found posted outside the Western District Branch
Police Bureau, 92 Jessfield Road, and announces that the City Govern-
ment is arranging for the transportation of rice from Anhwei province
in order to relieve the rice shortage in Shanghai and that the C.M.F
and S.M.C. have been requested to prohibit the sale of rice above
$15.00 per "sar". A translation of the proclamation is as follows:-
"Proclamation of the Shanghai City Government

A nation depends upon her people for existence and the people
depend upon food in order to live. The price of rice has been in-
creased daily recently and is apparently due to manipulation by
unscrupulous dealers. The increase is harmful to the people.
With a view to relieving this state of affairs, the Shanghai City
Government has telegraphed to Anhwei Province in order to obtain
supplies of rice for Shanghai. Letters have also been despatched
to the S.M.C. and C.M.F. requesting them to prohibit the sale of
rice at prices above $15.00, so that the people may be relieved of
their burdens. This proclamation is issued for the information
of the public and there is no reason for fear over the rice
situation.

Mayor Fu Hsiao-an.
June 30, 28th year of the Chinese Republic."

Certified true copy

J. F. Lovell

JFL.

1939年6月30日，在杰斯菲尔德路92号西区分局警察局外发现张贴了一份由上海市政府发布的公告，宣布市政府正安排从安徽省运输大米，以缓解上海的米荒，并已要求法公董局（C.M.F）和工部局（S.M.C.）禁止以每“sar”（原文如此，疑为石或担之误）15.00元以上的价格出售大米。公告译文如下：-
“上海市政府公告

国家依靠人民而存在，人民依靠粮食而生存。近期米价日日上涨，显系奸商操纵所致。这种上涨有害于民众。
为了缓解这一状况，上海市政府已致电安徽省，以便为上海获取大米供应。此外，还致函工部局和法公董局，请求他们禁止以15.00元以上的价格出售大米，以减轻民众负担。特此发布公告，供公众知悉，民众无需对米况感到恐慌。

市长傅筱庵。
中华民国二十八年六月三十日。”

核证无误副本

J. F. Lovell

JFL.

Subject. Rice situation - enquiries re Cheng Kee Company, a
rice buying syndicate.

Made by. and Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

URGENT

Discreet enquiries have been carried out
as to the constitution of the Cheng Kee Company, a
rice buying syndicate operating under Japanese
protection and the only information available is
to the effect that this company is sponsored by the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha
who are assisted in their monopolising activities
by the Japanese Military. All rice boats arriving
from Sungkiang are detained by the military at Mi
Shih Tu and it is estimated that up to the present
time, more than one hundred boats have been so
detained, representing approximately 20,000 bags
of rice. This rice has been bought by the Cheng
Kee Company under pressure at prices ranging from
$11.80 to $12.50 per "zar" being about 50 cents
below the standard market price. After purchase,
as far as can be ascertained, the rice has been
transported to Woosung and vicinity by steam
launches and lighters and exported to North China
in Japanese vessels. Information tends to show that
very little of this rice is stored or kept for any
length of time in Shanghai, and as a bigger profit
can be obtained by exporting the rice, it is
considered unlikely that the company would consider
selling in the local market.

Exhaustive enquiries among the local
rice dealers circles have failed to gain particulars

由. 并经督察员Crawford撰写并转发

紧急

已就成记公司（一家在日本保护下运作的大米采购辛迪加）的组成情况进行了谨慎查询，目前掌握的唯一信息显示，该公司由三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）和三菱商事株式会社（Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha）赞助，并在其垄断活动中得到日本军方的协助。所有从松江抵达的大米船只在米市渡（Mi Shih Tu，音译）被军方扣留，据估计，截至目前，已有超过一百艘船只被扣，代表约20,000袋大米。这些大米是在压力下由成记公司以每“zar”（原文如此，疑为石或担之误）11.80至12.50元的价格购买的，比标准市场价格低约50分。据查，购买后，大米已通过汽艇和驳船运往吴淞及周边地区，并由日本船只出口到华北。消息显示，这些大米在上海储存或保留的时间很短，由于出口大米可获得更大利润，因此认为该公司不太可能考虑在当地市场销售。

With reference to the attached translation regarding the alleged blockade of Mi Shih Tu (米市渡) on the South Whangpoo and forcible purchase of rice by a Chang Kee Company, enquiries made among the local rice dealers revealed that recently a certain Japanese firm, with the assistance of Japanese military, has been holding up rice boats at Mi Shih Tu on the upper Whangpoo, through which rice boats from Sungkiang to Shanghai must pass. It is reported that up to the present, some 130 boats have thus been held up and their cargoes forcibly purchased by the Japanese firm at $11.00 per "zar". Enquiries however failed to confirm the name of the firm in question. In consequence of the above, the number of rice boats arriving from the Sungkiang area has been reduced from more than ten boats to an average of about three boats per day; these boats succeeded in reaching Shanghai by avoiding passing through Mi Shih Tu.

During the course of enquiries it is further learned that the local rice dealers have received information from the dealers in Soochow that the Japanese Military authorities there have been holding up rice boats at Van Nien Jao (萬年橋), an important place which rice boats from the suburbs of Soochow must pass before reaching Soochow. Some twenty boats are said to have been held up since May 2, and the manner in which the rice will be disposed of by the Japanese is yet unknown.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 5 MAY 1939）

Further information shows that the Japanese

lifted, and commencing from May 1, not more than

With reference to the attached newspaper translation
regarding the transportation of Chinese rice from the interior
to Shanghai, enquiries made show that recently certain
German and Italian businessmen, who have obtained passes
from the Japanese military authorities, have been engaged
in transporting rice to Shanghai from the interior, on
behalf of the Chinese rice dealers. It is learned that a
charge of $3, in addition to a transportation fee of $0.50,
is levied for each bag of rice brought to Shanghai. The
$3 is divided between the Japanese and foreign merchants
concerned, but how they share this money is unknown.

With regard to the collection of taxes by the
Japanese authorities, the following information has been
obtained. In November, 1938, the Japanese authorities
and the puppet administrative authorities in Wusieh
commenced to levy on rice a so-called "import and export
tax" at 40 cents per bag (the tax is at present collected
at a discount of 20%, i.e. $0.32 per bag).

On January 10, 1939, another levy in the form of
a "transit tax" came into effect in Changshu. This levy
is collected at a rate similar to that in Wusieh on rice
passing through Changshu. The majority of the rice
destined for Shanghai arrives from Wusieh and rice dealers
are required to pay taxes on two occasions, the one at
Wusieh and the another at Changshu, before it is allowed
to proceed to Shanghai, consequently, the dealers feel
rather displeased with this extra taxation but they dare
not raise objections; there are no signs that they intend
striking. The rice dealers claim that under the new

Rice dealers and transportation

called a strike to protest against the
allegedly exorbitant tax collected

to be responsible for fewer rice
boats coming to the city during the
past two days. The number of
incoming rice boats was suddenly

levied on merchants transporting

another.
According to the reports, the new
tax affects rice dealers most ser-
iously especially those engaged in
transporting rice for farmers.
Formerly, it is stated, a bag of rice
transported to Shanghai had to pay
only $1.35 for everything including
the tax but since the new tax
regulations have gone into effect

$1.75 or sometimes $1.80.

Extract from North China Daily News dated 16-1-39

LOCAL RICE DEALERS START STRIKE
Protest against Taxes in Japanese Territory.
------------
Rice dealers and transportation firm managers in the interior have called a strike to protest against the allegedly exorbitant tax collected by the Japanese on rice exported to Shanghai, which fact is reported to be responsible for fewer rice boats coming to the city during the past two days. The number of incoming rice boats was suddenly reduced on Saturday when the merchants struck in earnest.
Chinese reports state that ten kinds of taxes are being collected by the Japanese and "puppet" officials on goods imported to or exported from the occupied districts in the interior, and recently a new burden was added to the shoulders of merchants in the form of the "removal tax" which is levied on merchants transporting their goods from one place to another.
According to the reports, the new tax affects rice dealers most seriously especially those engaged in transporting rice for farmers. Formerly, it is stated, a bag of rice transported to Shanghai had to pay only $1.35 for everything including the tax but since the new tax regulations have gone into effect the figure has now been increased to $1.75 or sometimes $1.90.

Certified true copy:
H. C. Yardley
pages.zh:
摘自1939年1月16日《字林西报》

本地米商开始罢工
抗议日占区内的税收。
------------
内地米商及运输公司经理发起罢工，以抗议日本人对出口至上海的大米征收据称过高的税款，据报道，过去两天抵沪米船减少即由此造成。周六当商人认真实行罢工时，抵沪米船数量突然减少。
中方消息称，日本人和“伪”官员对进出内地占领区的货物征收十种税款，最近又以“迁移税”的形式给商人增加了新的负担，该税向将货物从一地运往另一地的商人征收。
据报道，新税对米商影响最为严重，尤其是那些为农民运输大米的人。据称，以前一袋大米运至上海，包括税款在内的所有费用仅需支付 1.35 美元，但自新税规生效后，该数额现已增至 1.75 美元，有时甚至达 1.90 美元。

核证无误副本：
H. C. Yardley

INDUSTRY
January 12, 39.
Increase in rice prices and purchases by the Japanese.

With reference to the Commissioner of Police's
memo. dated January 7, 1939, regarding increases in the
prices of rice and purchases by the Japanese, enquiries
among rice dealers show that the Japanese began buying
Chinese rice in Wusieh, Changchow and Sungkiang as early
as November, 1938. It is estimated that since that time,
they have purchased approximately 300,000 "sars" of rice
in Wusieh and Changchow which have either been transported
to North China by the Tientsin-Pukow Railway, or shipped
to Japan via Kiangyin; some 110,000 "sars" were bought in
Sungkiang which were transported by rail to Woosung and
thence to Japan in Japanese ships.

According to the rice dealers, the Japanese are
purchasing about 200,000 "sars" per month or 2,400,000 "sars"
per annum, but this will not affect the supply of rice to Shang-
hai although it may tend to increase the price. The price
of rice has recently been increased by about 50 cents per
"sar", believed to be due to the Japanese purchases, but
allowing for the increase, the present price can be regarded
as normal when compared with those prevailing in previous
years.

The approximate average yield in the rice producing
areas in the southern part of Kiangsu and a small part in
Chekiang, the principal source of local supplies, is in the
region of 30,000,000 "mows" per year and no shortage is
anticipated. Although the fields adjacent to the highways
and railways in the area mentioned above were not cultivated
in 1938 in consequence of the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
pages.zh:
原件在 F2
行业
1939年1月12日。
米价上涨及日本人收购情况。

关于警务处长1939年1月7日有关米价上涨及日本人收购情况的备忘录，经向米商查询显示，日本人早在1938年11月就开始在无锡、常州和松江收购中国大米。据估计，自那时起，他们在无锡和常州收购了约30万“石”大米，这些大米要么通过津浦铁路运往华北，要么经由江阴装船运往日本；在松江收购了约11万“石”，经铁路运至吴淞，再由日本船只运往日本。

据米商称，日本人每月收购约20万“石”，即每年240万“石”，但这不会影响对上海的供应，尽管可能会导致价格上涨。近期大米价格每“石”上涨了约50美分，据信是由于日本人收购所致，但考虑到这一涨幅，与往年 prevailing 的价格相比，目前的价格可视为正常。

江苏南部及浙江小部分主要本地供应来源的大米产区，年平均产量约为3,000万“亩”，预计不会出现短缺。尽管由于中日敌对行动，上述地区邻近公路和铁路的农田在1938年未耕种。

pages.en:
- 2 -
the harvest of 1938 is a good one and amounts to about
80% to 85% of the average yield, i.e. approximately
24,750,000 "sars". Since the local consumption is about
3,600,000 "sars" per year, according to the present
estimates, the rice dealers would have no difficulty in
obtaining sufficient supplies for local demands, because
the rice producing areas would still have about 19,000,000
"sars", even if the Japanese continue to purchase rice
at the present rate.
The present stock of rice in Shanghai amounts
to approximately 600,000 "sars" which is thought enough
for a period of about two months. This stock is expected
to be increased by about 200,000 to 300,000 "sars" by the
end of the Lunar Year (i.e. about the middle of February,
1939), when farmers and dealers will, no doubt, be eager
to sell their holdings as has been done in previous years.
The stock then accumulated will be sufficient to May, 1939.
As the local stock will continue to be supplemented,
possibly by arrivals of smaller quantities, after the
Chinese New Year (Lunar), there is no likelihood of a
shortage taking place locally before the next harvest, if
the exportation of rice from Shanghai is still kept under
restraint. The dealers do not expect that the price of
rice in 1939 will exceed $14.00 per "sar", although a
seasonable increase generally takes place in the months
of June, July and August.
During the course of enquiries, it has been
learned that prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
pages.zh:

1938年的收成良好，约为平均产量的80%至85%，即约2,475万“石”。由于本地年消费量约为360万“石”，根据目前的估算，米商在满足本地需求方面不会遇到困难，因为即使日本人继续以目前的速率收购大米，大米产区仍将有约1,900万“石”的余量。
上海目前的大米库存约为60万“石”，被认为足以维持约两个月。预计到农历年底（即1939年2月中旬左右），库存将增加约20万至30万“石”，届时农民和商人无疑会像往年一样急于出售其存货。届时积累的库存将足以维持到1939年5月。
由于农历新年后本地库存将继续得到补充，可能是以小批量到货的形式，如果从上海出口大米仍受到限制，那么在下次收获之前，本地不太可能出现短缺。米商预计1939年大米价格不会超过每“石”14.00美元，尽管通常在6月、7月和8月会出现季节性上涨。
在调查过程中获悉，在中日冲突爆发之前

pages.en:

hostilities, large quantities of inferior rice known as
"See Mee" (rice of the Saigon rice origin produced in
China) arrived in Shanghai from Hunan, Kiangsi and Anhwei,
at a yearly average of approximately 1,500,000 "sars".
The majority of this rice was exported from this port,
while the remainder was bought locally by the people of
the lower classes. After the withdrawal of the Chinese
troops to the interior, the supply from this source
diminished, but since August, 1938, small quantities have
been arriving in Shanghai from Wuhu, Anhwei, and it is
estimated that some 100,000 bags have been brought here
in this way. Owing to the difficulties experienced in
transportation, very few rice dealers are prepared to
transport rice to Shanghai from this area.

大量被称为“See Mee”（在中国生产的西贡米源大米）的劣质大米从湖南、江西和安徽运抵上海，年平均约为150万“石”。这批大米大部分从此港口出口，其余部分由下层民众在本地购买。随着中国军队撤往内地，来自此来源的供应减少，但自1938年8月以来，少量大米从安徽芜湖运抵上海，据估计以此方式运抵此处的大米约有10万袋。由于运输困难，很少有米商愿意从该地区将大米运至上海。

Eastern Times :-
JAPANESE BUYING HUGE QUANTITIES OF RICE
On November 1, 1938, the Japanese firms in Sung-
kiang notified the various rice hongs in the city to
purchase for them 200,000 piculs of rice before December 31.
This order has been fully delivered. Yesterday the
Japanese firms placed a second order for 200,000 piculs of
rice. In consequence, the price of rice has gone up; the
price for one picul of coarse rice has been increased to
over $8. All the rice hongs in Sungkiang are working to
execute the order. No rice boats are being allowed to leave.

《申报》：
日本人大量收购大米
1938年11月1日，松日的日本商行通知市内各米行，在12月31日前为其收购20万担大米。该订单已全额交付。昨日，日本商行下达了第二份20万担大米的订单。因此，米价上涨；糙米每担价格已涨至8美元以上。松江所有米行都在忙于执行该订单。不允许任何米船离开。

1937年12月2日下午12时05分，史密斯巡长和达菲巡警向巡捕房报告称，今天中午12时许，他们在外滩栈桥巡逻时，观察到7号浮码头上有一群人。走近现场后，他们看到日本登陆队的数名成员在一艘海军汽艇上扣押了一艘装载袋装大米的华式驳船。登陆队负责军官告诉他们，一些中国人在未获得日本当局许可的情况下，从万西封锁线内的禁区运走了大米，当海军汽艇靠近栈桥进行查问时，船夫和一辆已装载少量大米的机动卡车已经逃匿。

因此，该驳船被拖至中国政府渡轮前的12号浮码头，并系泊于此

根据高级警探的指示，具名者前往北四川路的日本俱乐部，采访了定居点区域日本驻军指挥官野口中尉 (音译)，后者表示扣留该船是为了进行调查。

截至下午5时，本巡捕房未收到有关扣留该驳船的任何投诉。

（印：特务科 - 1937年12月3日. 上海公共租界警务处）

REPORT
Date Dec. 3 2, 1937

Subject (in full) Seizure of rice by the Japanese military at No.7
Pontoon on The Bund near Hankow Road.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Laurier

At about 11.50 a.m. December 2, a boat carrying
160 bags of "See Mee" (Rice), while being unloaded at
the No.7 Pontoon, The Bund near Hankow Road, was seized
and towed away by a party of seven Japanese (five in
military uniform and two in plain clothes) who arrived
on a steam launch.

The rice belonged to the Zang Nyi ( 長義 )
Rice Hong, Nantao, and was transported from Nantao to
the Settlement for sale at rice shops. Only about 20
bags had been unloaded before the ship was seized by
the Japanese.

Laurier
D. S. I.

由副督察劳里尔 (Laurier) 制作并提交

12月2日上午11时50分左右，一艘载有160袋“See Mee”（大米）的船只在汉口路附近外滩7号浮码头卸货时，被乘坐蒸汽汽艇抵达的七名日本人（五人身着军装，两人身着便服）扣押并拖走。

该大米属于南市长义米行，是从南市运至租界供米店销售的。在日本人扣押该船之前，仅卸下了约20袋。

POLICE FORCE
6 MAY 1941

This is a copy of letter to Council from the
Indian Miscellaneous Cereals and Grain
Wholesale Dealers' Association.
Dated 20th April, 1941.

Rice samplers and identification cards.

In view of the difficulties and abuses connected with the
taking of samples during delivery of rice and other cereals, the
proprietors of various godowns in the neighbourhood of wharves,
desiring to improve matters and to stop abuse, some time ago
proposed issuing Samplers' Identification Cards. This idea is
excellent, and it was discussed by the port authorities concerned with
this association. For the sake of convenience it was agreed that
this association should undertake the issuing of the Identification
Cards, and it was decided that the various godown authorities
should do their utmost to co-operate so that the plan may be
carried out smoothly. It is hoped that when this joint effort
proves successful the proprietors of the various godowns will be
able to protect the goods of their customers who will be saved
unnecessary loss. As the plan is in the interest of all concerned
and the decision was unanimously approved, we commenced the work
of issuing samplers' Identification Cards to employés of members
of this Association last March; the work is now in full swing.
Altogether 160 member shops have applied to us for cards and
more than 900 cards have been issued to employés of shops. To
facilitate identification a photograph of the employé concerned
is affixed to each card. It has now been arranged that beginning
from 1st May samples may only be taken by persons holding cards.
The cards must be produced for the inspection of the godown
authorities when employés of member shops are sent to godowns to
sample grain before taking delivery. We have notified all our
pages.zh:
档案号. 730/12
警务处
1941年5月6日

这是印度杂粮谷物批发商同业公会致工部局信函的副本。
日期为1941年4月20日。

大米取样员及身份证件。

鉴于在大米及其他谷物交付过程中取样相关的困难和弊端，码头附近各仓库的所有者为改善状况并制止滥用行为，于前一段时间提议签发取样员身份证件。这一想法极佳，并与负责港口事务的有关当局及本公会进行了讨论。为方便起见，各方同意由本公会承担签发身份证件的工作，并决定各仓库当局应尽力配合，以便计划顺利实施。希望当这一共同努力证明成功时，各仓库所有者将能够保护其客户的货物，使客户免受不必要的损失。由于该计划符合所有相关方的利益，且决定获得一致批准，我们于今年三月开始向本公会会员店的雇员签发取样员身份证件；目前工作正在全面展开。共有160家会员店向我们申请了证件，已向店铺雇员签发了900多张证件。为便于识别，每张证件上都贴有相关雇员的照片。现已安排，自5月1日起，仅允许持证人员取样。当会员店雇员被派往仓库在提货前对谷物进行取样时，必须出示证件供仓库当局检查。我们已通知所有我们的

pages.en:
- 2 -

members and the proprietors of the various godowns near wharves
that beginning from 1st May only rice shop employees possessing
Identification Cards are to be allowed to enter godowns to work,
or to take samples, in connexion with delivery; any person not
duly authorized must be refused admittance. Apart from that,
we venture to report to the Council the particulars leading up
to the issue of these cards; we also enclose a specimen card
for the Council's inspection and beg that the matter be placed
on record.

It not infrequently happened that unscrupulous persons
fraudulently pretending to be sent from rice shops, abstracted
samples during the delivery of rice. Owners suffered serious loss
through these depredations, and the evil was getting worse while
the price of rice and other cereals soared to unprecedented
heights. If this malpractice be not stopped, owners will seek
to make good their losses by selling at still higher prices. It
is, therefore, imperative that steps should be taken to stop this
evil.

Last year we introduced a standard tube for taking samples,
and we asked the Council's assistance in this matter. So far we
have achieved very satisfactory results.

In view of the seriousness of the evil we decided to issue
identification cards to employees engaged in sample taking. The
Council is asked to instruct the Police to give us assistance by
detaining suspicious characters who carry rice samples in the
streets, and calling on them to produce their identification cards.
If they cannot produce cards, they are impostors and should be
properly dealt with to serve as warning and to help improve the
situation.

(Chopped) Shanghai Miscellaneous Cereals and Bean
Cake Dealers' Association.

(Note: Received for translation late p.m. 1st May, 1941.)
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL MAY 2 1941）

- 2 -

会员及码头附近各仓库的所有者，自5月1日起，仅允许持有身份证件的大米店雇员进入仓库工作或进行与交付相关的取样；任何未经正式授权的人员必须拒绝入内。除此之外，我们冒昧向工部局报告导致签发这些证件的具体情况；我们还附上证件样本供工部局查阅，并恳请将此事备案。

不法分子假冒受米店派遣，在大米交付过程中窃取样品的情况屡见不鲜。业主因这些掠夺行为遭受严重损失，而在大米及其他谷物价格飙升至前所未有的高位之际，这种恶行愈演愈烈。如果不制止这种弊病，业主将通过以更高的价格出售来弥补损失。因此，必须采取措施制止这种恶行。

去年，我们引入了标准取样管，并在此事上请求工部局协助。到目前为止，我们取得了非常令人满意的结果。

鉴于该弊病的严重性，我们决定向从事取样工作的雇员签发身份证件。现请工部局指令警方给予我们协助，拘留在街头携带大米样品的可疑人物，并要求他们出示身份证件。如果他们无法出示证件，即为冒充者，应予以适当处理，以起到警示作用并帮助改善局势。

（盖章）上海杂粮豆饼业同业公会.

（注：1941年5月1日下午晚些时候收到待译稿。）
（印：上海公共租界工部局 1941年5月2日）

Regulations Governing Agriculture,
Mining, Industry and Commerce During
the Period of Emergency.

(Revised and promulgated by the National
Government on October 6, 1938)

Article 1. During the period of emergency, the
Ministry of Economics may designate the following
agricultural, mining, industrial and commercial enter-
prises and articles to be under its control in accord-
ance with these Regulations upon approval of the
Executive Yuan.

1. Cotton, silk, hemp, wool and their products;
2. Gold, silver, steel, iron, copper, tin,
aluminum, nickel, lead, zinc, tungsten,
antimony, manganese, mercury and their
products;
3. Provisions, plant oil, tea, sugar, leather,
timber, salt, coal and charcoal, kerosene,
gasolene, crude oil, lubricating oil, paper,
lacquer, wine spirit, cement, lime, alkali,
matches, communication material, electrical
material, electrical engineering instruments,
educational equipments, medicines, artificial
fertilizer, pottery, bricks, tiles and glass.
4. Other articles designated by the Ministry
of Economics and approved by the Executive Yuan.

Article 2. Where any matter relating to control as
laid down in these Regulations concerns the functioning
of other ministries or commissions, the Ministry of
Economics shall deal with it jointly with the respective
ministry or commission by consulting with it.

The Ministry of Economics may order, either
directly or after consulting with the Ministry or Com-
mission referred to in the last Section, the local
public office to be in charge of the matter.

Article 3. The Ministry of Economics may specially
establish separate organs to execute the matters regarding
the control of the enterprises or articles designated by it.

非常时期农矿工商管理条例.

（由国民政府于1938年10月6日修订并颁布）

第一条. 在非常时期，经济部经行政院批准，可根据本条例指定下列农、矿、工、商企业及物品受其管制。

1. 棉、丝、麻、毛及其制品；
2. 金、银、钢、铁、铜、锡、铝、镍、铅、锌、钨、锑、锰、汞及其制品；
3. 粮食、植物油、茶、糖、皮革、木材、盐、煤及木炭、煤油、汽油、原油、润滑油、纸、漆、酒精、水泥、石灰、碱、火柴、通讯材料、电气材料、电气工程仪器、教育设备、药品、人造肥料、陶器、砖、瓦及玻璃。
4. 其他由经济部指定并经行政院批准的物品。

第二条. 凡本条例规定的管制事项涉及其他部会职能者，经济部应与 respective 部会协商共同处理。

经济部可直接或在与上一款所述部会协商后，命令地方公共机构负责该事项。

第三条. 经济部可特别设立独立机构，以执行对其指定的企业或物品的管制事宜。

Article 4. The Ministry of Economics, so far as the
enterprises or articles designated by it are concerned,
may clearly lay down a suitable standard in respect of
the following headings.
1. Method of production or management;
2. Kinds of materials and their quantities
in stock;
3. Working hours and labourers' treatment;
4. Qualities and output and quantities in
stock;
5. Cost of production;
6. Methods of transportation and sale;
7. Selling prices and profits.
Article 5. For the purpose of meeting the demands
during the period of emergency, upon permission of the
Executive Yuan, the Ministry of Economics may take
over the following enterprises and put them under the
management of the government or run them jointly by
the government on contributing a part of the capital.
1. Mining enterprises indispensable during war;
2. Industrial enterprises manufacturing articles
for military use;
3. Electrical enterprises.
Article 6. The Ministry of Economics, in order to
meet the demand of production during the period of
emergency may compulsorily use or requisition private
owned barren lands.
Article 7. Where a designated enterprise or article
is indispensable in daily life, the Ministry of Economics
may, for the purpose of meeting the demand of the various
localities, at any time undertake to manage it directly
according to its kind and the locality.
pages.zh:
-2-
第四条. 就其指定的企业或物品而言，经济部可在以下方面明确规定适当的标准。
1. 生产或管理方法；
2. 原料种类及其库存数量；
3. 工作时间及劳工待遇；
4. 质量、产量及库存数量；
5. 生产成本；
6. 运输及销售方法；
7. 销售价格及利润。
第五条. 为满足非常时期的需求，经行政院许可，经济部可接管下列企业，由政府管理或通过出资部分资本由政府合营。
1. 战时必需的矿业企业；
2. 制造军用物品的工业企业；
3. 电力企业。
第六条. 为满足非常时期的生产需求，经济部可强制使用或征用私人拥有的荒地。
第七条. 若指定的企业或物品为日常生活所必需，经济部为满足各地需求，可随时根据其种类及地点直接进行管理。

Article 8. Unless with the permission of the
Ministry of Economics, the producers or managers
of the different designated enterprises and articles
shall not close their plants or shops or suspend
their works. Those who have already closed or
suspended their works may be ordered by the Ministry
of Economics to resume their business or work within
a prescribed period.
Article 9. Where enterprises designated by the
Ministry of Economics are in the war zone or near it,
the said Ministry may on account of necessity order
their removal.
Article 10. Whoever, having received the orders
referred to in the last two preceding articles, actually
has no means of resuming his business or work or removing
his enterprise, aside from the application of Article 25,
the provision of Article 5 may also apply.
Article 11. Employees and workers of the designated
enterprises shall not declare strike or on go-slow
strikes.
Article 12. The producers or managers of the
designated enterprises and articles shall not speculate,
manipulate or commit other speculative acts.
Article 13. The Ministry of Economics may on account
of necessity restrict or prohibit the import or export
of designated articles.
Article 14. The Ministry of Economics may regulate
the consumption of the designated articles according
to the actual demand and supply of same.
Article 15. The Ministry of Economics may on account
of necessity prohibit the sale of or regulate the prices
of the designated articles.
pages.zh:
-3-
第八条。除非获得经济部许可，各类指定企业及物品的生产者或管理者不得关闭其工厂或商店，或停止作业。已经关闭或停工者，经济部可命令其在指定期限内恢复营业或作业。

第九条。凡经济部指定的企业位于战区或靠近战区者，该部可视必要情况命令其迁移。

第十条。凡接到前两条所述命令者，若确实无力恢复营业、作业或迁移企业，除适用第二十五条外，亦可适用第五条之规定。

第十一条。指定企业的雇员和工人不得宣布罢工或实行怠工。

第十二条。指定企业及物品的生产者或管理者不得进行投机、操纵或实施其他投机行为。

第十三条。经济部可视必要情况，限制或禁止指定物品的进出口。

第十四条。经济部可根据指定物品的实际供需情况，调节其消费。

第十五条。经济部可视必要情况，禁止出售指定物品或管制其价格。

Article 16. The Ministry of Economics may on account
of necessity order the producers or managers of the
designated articles to store them or to transfer to
another place for keeping.
Article 17. For the purpose of meeting the necessity
during the period of emergency, the Ministry of Economics
may purchase the entire stock or only a part of the

Article 18. The Ministry of Economics may on account

Article 20. The Ministry of Economics may restrict

Article 21. Where there is necessity to improve the
skill or management of a designated enterprise, and
it fails to make improvement when ordered to do so, the

第十六条。经济部可视必要情况，命令指定物品的生产者或管理者将其储存，或转移至他处保管。

第十七条。为应付紧急时期之需要，经济部可按管制价格，购买指定物品的全部库存或部分库存。

第十八条。经济部可视必要情况，命令指定企业增加资本、合并或缩减其业务范围。

第十九条。企业如有下列情形之一者，经济部可命令其停业：

第二十四条。凡对指定企业或物品拥有特别发明或垄断权者，经济部可视必要情况，命令其报告实验情况，或禁止其发表或披露。政府可接管以供利用，或出资与其合作。

第二十五条。经济部可根据下列规定，按照指定企业的需求程度给予协助。凡经济部根据第八条命令其复工或复业，或根据第九条命令其迁移，或根据第十八条命令其增加资本或合并业务者，亦适用同一规则。
1. 扩充资本；
2. 供应材料；
3. 规划建设；
4. 增添设备；
5. 提供技术知识；
6. 调节动力供应；
7. 调节产品运输与销售；
8. 调节劳动力供应。

Measures Relating to Regulation of
Commodity Prices and Repressing of
Speculation and Manipulation during
the Period of Emergency.

(Promulgated by the National Government
on February 20, 1938).

Article 1. During the period of emergency the
regulation of prices of daily necessaries of all places
and the repressing of speculation and manipulation shall,
except otherwise provided by law, be dealt with in
accordance with these measures.

Article 2. The competent public office of the
locality shall, in conjunction with the organizations
concerned, Chamber of Commerce, or the guilds dealing
in goods of daily necessaries, establish a Prices Regula-
tion Committee, and the committee shall deal with all
matters relating to the regulation of prices of daily
necessaries of the locality.

The aforesaid competent public office shall
be the Social Affairs Bureau in Municipalities which
are under the direct control of the Administrative Yuan,
the Hsien Government in Hsien districts, and the
Municipal Government in Municipalities.

Article 3. The members of the Prices Regulation
Committee shall be nominated and appointed by the
organizations referred to in the preceding Article,
and the officer appointed by the competent public office
shall be the Chairman.

The number of members nominated by the Chamber
of Commerce or the Guilds shall not exceed half of the
total number of members of the Committee.

第二条。地方主管官署应会同有关组织、商会或经营日常生活必需品的同业公会，成立物价管制委员会，该委员会负责处理当地日常生活必需品价格管制的一切事项。

上述主管官署，在行政院直辖各市为社会局，在县为县政府，在市为市政府。

第三条。物价管制委员会委员由前条所述各组织提名任命，并由主管官署派任的官员担任主席。

由商会或同业公会提名的委员人数，不得超过委员会总人数的一半。

Chinese-American Daily News :- 11/41.

THE RICE PROBLEM : COUNCIL COULD DO MORE

With the object of stabilizing the local
food problem, the senior Chinese employees of the Shanghai
Municipal Council some time ago suggested that the Council,
within its capability, make large purchases of foreign rice
for supply to the local market from time to time as a means
to check the price of rice. However, this proposal has up
to the present received no agreement from the foreign
employees of the Council. It is for this reason that
Chinese circles have expressed regret over the attitude of
the foreign authorities of the Council. The Chinese are of
the opinion that to the foreign employees of the S.M.C. who
depend upon bread as their daily necessary, the rise or drop
in the price of rice means nothing. However, as most of the
residents of the Settlement are Chinese whose staple food
is rice, and as the S.M.C. is able to make purchases of
foreign rice, a temporary defrayment of the cost will prove
no disadvantage to the Council. Consequently, it is
improper for the Council to withhold its agreement to this
proposal.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 3 JAN 1941）

P.T.O.

《中美日报》：1941年11月。

米荒问题：工部局可做得更多

为稳定本地粮食问题，上海公共租界工部局的高级华籍职员曾于不久前建议，工部局在其能力范围内，不时大量购入洋米供应本地市场，以此作为抑制米价的手段。然而，这一提议迄今未获工部局外籍职员的同意。正因如此，华人各界对工部局外籍当局的态度表示遗憾。华人认为，对于以面包为日常必需品的工部局外籍职员而言，米价的涨跌无关紧要。然而，由于租界居民多为以大米为主食的华人，且工部局有能力购买洋米，暂时的垫资对工部局并无不利。因此，工部局不同意此提议是不妥当的。

（印：上海公共租界工部局总办处 1941年1月3日）

Chinese-American Daily News :-

ADULTERATED RICE BEING SOLD IN MANY SHOPS

Although ostensibly the rice shops are
conducting retail sales at a fixed price and are deriving
a commission of $1.50 from every picul of rice sold, yet
actually they are making quite a good profit through such
sales because the rice thus sold is mixed with inferior
quality goods or other provisions. It is, therefore, hoped
that the authorities will keep a sharp look-out for such
practices and will, as a warning to others, impose severe
fines upon those who are found to be selling rice mixed
with inferior quality wares.

（批：S. [签名]）

December 13, 1940. Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yien Pao, National Herald,
Shun Pao and Sin'an Pao :-

THE RICE SITUATION

Yesterday the following two resolutions
passed by the rice trading bodies on December 11 were
promulgated by the rice mart :-
(1) That for every bag of rice transacted
a deposit of $5 be paid and that the whole quantity of rice
involved in the transaction be claimed within ten days.
(2) That in connection with the first grade
Saigon rice already ordered by local rice trade the export
of which has been banned by the French-Indo-China
authorities, the various rice trading bodies concerned
register their orders with the Provision Dealers' Guild and
the Bean and Rice Trade Guild before Saturday (December 14)
pending negotiations.
Despite the emergency measures adopted
by the rice trading bodies, signs of unstability were still
noticeable in the rice mart yesterday because the speculators
have resumed their activities, with the result that the
prices of various kinds of foreign rice registered an increase
of $2 per picul yesterday.
According to information secured from
quarters undertaking the erection of a public granary for the
storage of rice as a means to stabilize the price of rice, it
is learned that local rice trading circles have promised to
purchase 50,000 bags of foreign rice for storage, while the
balance of 150,000 bags will be procured by local public
bodies. A meeting of representatives of local banking circles
and cotton trade guild, etc. will soon be called to discuss
the erection of a public granary.
It is also learned that Mr. Yu Ya-ching,
the promoter of the scheme, has likewise agreed to purchase
50,000 bags of foreign rice for storage and that local banking
and other influential bodies will be responsible for the
purchase of the balance.

Chinese-American Daily News (comment) :-

We have more on than one occasion published
articles on the rice problem. We advocated at the very
outset that one urgent task that should be done at present
is to conduct an investigation into the total quantity of
rice in stock. It was for this reason that we expressed the
opinion that the decisions reached at the Council's meeting
on December 9 would have no effective result, especially
in view of the fact that the meeting did not bring up this
matter for discussion.
A slight drop was registered in the price
of rice on December 10 and 11. The general public, in their
joy, attributed the drop to the decisions of the Council
meeting and we had to point out that this was but a slight
decrease after a high increase. It was nothing but a clever
trick on the part of the hoarders. One aspect that deserves
attention is the high increase after a slight drop.

米市情况

昨日，米业公所公布了米业团体于12月11日通过的以下两项决议：
（1）每交易一袋大米需缴纳5美元定金，且涉及交易的全部大米须在十天内提货。
（2）关于本地米商已订购但被法属印度支那当局禁止出口的一等西贡米，各相关米业团体须在周六（12月14日）前向 Provision Dealers' Guild（暂译：配给商公会）和豆米业公会登记订单，以待谈判。
尽管米业团体采取了紧急措施，但昨日米市仍可见不稳定迹象，因为投机者已恢复活动，导致昨日各种洋米价格每担上涨2美元。
据从负责建造公共粮仓以储存大米从而稳定米价的部门获得的消息获悉，本地米业界已承诺购买50,000袋洋米用于储存，其余150,000袋将由本地公共机构采购。不久将召开本地银行界和棉业公会等代表的会议，讨论建造公共粮仓事宜。
另悉，该计划的发起人虞洽卿先生也已同意购买50,000袋洋米用于储存，其余部分将由本地银行界及其他有影响力的机构负责购买。

《中美日报》（评论）：

我们已多次刊登有关米荒问题的文章。我们在最初就主张，当前亟待完成的一项任务是调查大米库存总量。正因如此，我们认为12月9日工部局会议达成的决定不会产生有效结果，特别是鉴于会议并未将此事项提上讨论日程。
12月10日和11日，米价略有下跌。公众欣喜之余，将下跌归因于工部局会议的决定，而我们不得不指出，这不过是大涨之后的小跌。这不过是囤积居奇者的巧妙伎俩。值得关注的一个方面是小跌之后的大涨。

That our view was correct can be verified
by the increase in the price of rice yesterday,
which is now near the limit fixed. There is lack of
determination on the part of the authorities to conduct an
investigation into the quantity of hoarded rice. We can
only hope that the hoarders will show some consideration for
the "face" of the Council, otherwise we deem it necessary
that the Council should take drastic action without delay.

Bing Pao (comment) of December 12 :-

S.M.C. SHOULD START CURTAILING ITS EXPENDITURE FOR NEXT YEAR

The approval by the Shanghai Municipal
Council of the increase in the allowances granted to its
employees has resulted in an increase of more than $900,000
per mensem in its expenditure. The S.M.C. states that its
service is similar to that rendered by any public utility and
that as a result of the recent increase in the allowances for
its staff, the Council will have to get more money from the
public. Hence, it is possible that when the Finance Department
of the S.M.C. discusses next year's estimates, it will likely
suggest an increase in the rates.

According to information given to a reporter
by a certain ratepayer, the S.M.C. has already increased the
municipal rate several times. Formerly, the municipal rate
was 14%, then it was increased to 18% after the outbreak of the
hostilities, while since July this year, a surcharge of 50%
on all rates and taxes was put into force. The burden of
the public is really very heavy and a further increase in the
rates will become almost unbearable to the public. Therefore,
it is hoped that the Council will curtail its expenses and
seek other sources of revenue.

With regard to the improvement in the
livelihood of its middle and low grade employees, the rate-
payers, of course, have nothing to criticize, but it seems
that heavy expenses, such as those for the Municipal Orchestra,
should no longer be included in the estimates. A special
policy should be adopted and the burden of the public
should not be increased. An increase in the amusement taxes
and in the rates levied upon speculation will, however, meet
with no objection.

Cheng Yien Pao, National Herald, Shun Pao and Sin'an Pao :-

ANNIVERSARY OF SIAN INCIDENT

Yesterday was the anniversary of the Sian
incident. The various circles in Shanghai have become more
loyal to the Chief Executive and are firmly supporting the
national policy so as to complete the great work of national
reconstruction. Owing to the prevalence of extraordinary
conditions in Shanghai, no ceremony was held.

昨日米价上涨，目前已接近规定的限价，这证实了我们的看法是正确的。当局在调查囤积大米数量方面缺乏决心。我们只能希望囤积者能对工部局的“面子”稍加顾及，否则我们认为工部局有必要立即采取严厉措施。

12月12日《炳报》评论：

工部局应开始削减明年的开支

上海公共租界工部局批准增加其雇员津贴，导致其每月支出增加超过90万元。工部局称，其服务性质与任何公用事业类似，鉴于近期增加了员工津贴，工部局将不得不从公众那里获取更多资金。因此，当工部局财务处讨论明年预算时，很可能会建议提高捐率。

据一位纳税人向记者提供的信息，工部局已多次提高市政捐。此前，市政捐率为14%，战事爆发后增至18%，而自今年7月起，对所有捐税征收50%的附加税。公众负担确实非常沉重，若再增加捐率，公众将几乎无法承受。因此，希望工部局能削减开支并寻求其他收入来源。

关于改善其中低级职员的生活待遇，纳税人当然无可非议，但似乎像市管弦乐队之类的巨额开支不应再列入预算。应采取特别政策，不应增加公众负担。然而，增加娱乐税和对投机行为征收的捐税，则不会遭到反对。

Reading The News
By JOHN AHLERS

Behind the Shanghai labor trouble certainly is a great amount of political agitation and instigation. It is perfectly obvious that quarters not in sympathy with the present administration and order in Settlement and Concession attempt to make trouble for the purpose of trouble. It is obvious that these quarters avail themselves of local labor as a convenient means of creating such trouble.

Shanghai labor would do well, in its own interest, to gather some information on the situation and position of labor in the Nippon controlled hinterland of Central China. The information we have tends to show that in that region labor is being paid still more poorly than at Shanghai, that it is conceded there still fewer rights, and that it is refused altogether the right to go on strike. Undoubtedly, if the political instigators of the local troubles managed to overthrow the existing order, and to establish instead their own new order, local labor would be much worse off than it is now.

On the other hand, there should be no illusion that political instigation is entirely the cause of the local labor situation. It merely is an element of encouragement. At the bottom of Shanghai labor unrest and strikes are the extremely high living costs, and the enormous reduction in local industrial workers' real income during the past three years of war. Hundreds of thousands of Shanghai workers for many months have been leading a life of continuous starvation. Their poverty and misery contribute to the business depression, and form a threat to the local community as a whole. Industrial workers certainly are entitled to a new deal.

Rice constitutes the major problem in the domestic budgets of local industrial laborers. The importance of rice, in this respect, hardly can be over-estimated. The average Chinese wage or salary earner at Shanghai has two-and-a-half mouths to feed. In the case of cash incomes up to sixty local dollars, the major portion of such incomes, or all of it, has to be devoted to the purchase of rice alone. Cash incomes below thirty local dollars cannot even buy sufficient rice to feed two mouths and a half.

At this time last year, native rice sold locally below $20 per sah, with Saigon rice somewhat cheaper as usual. Now native rice is at $86 per sah, and Saigon rice above $70. There hardly will be a single worker in town who despite this
