上海劳工纠纷的背后，肯定存在大量的政治煽动和挑唆。显而易见，那些不同情租界和法租界现行行政管理和秩序的人士，正试图为了制造麻烦而制造麻烦。显然，这些人士利用当地劳工作为制造此类麻烦的便利手段。

上海劳工为了自身利益，最好收集一些关于华中日本控制腹地劳工状况和地位的信息。我们所掌握的信息倾向于表明，在该地区，劳工获得的报酬甚至比上海更低，享有的权利更少，并且完全被剥夺了罢工权。毫无疑问，如果当地骚乱的政治煽动者成功推翻现有秩序并建立他们自己的新秩序，当地劳工的处境将比现在糟糕得多。

另一方面，也不应产生错觉，认为政治煽动是当地劳工局势的唯一原因。它仅仅是一个助推因素。上海劳工动荡和罢工的根源在于极高的生活成本，以及过去三年战争期间当地产业工人实际收入的巨大减少。数十万上海工人在许多个月里一直过着持续饥饿的生活。他们的贫困和苦难加剧了商业萧条，并对整个当地社区构成威胁。产业工人当然有权要求新的待遇。

大米构成了当地产业劳工家庭预算中的主要问题。在这方面，大米的重要性怎么强调都不为过。上海普通的薪金或工资收入者需要养活两口半人。对于现金收入在六十元本地货币以下的情况，大部分甚至全部收入都必须专门用于购买大米。现金收入低于三十元本地货币的，甚至买不到足够养活两口半人的大米。

去年这个时候，本地大米在当地售价每石低于20元，西贡大米通常更便宜一些。现在本地大米价格为每石86元，西贡大米超过70元。尽管自去年秋季以来大米价格上涨了400%，但镇上几乎没有任何一名工人

rice price increase of 400 percent since last fall secured a wage
increase of 100 percent. Most workers got much smaller wage
increases. It is obvious that their situation has greatly de-
teriorated, and that they have been robbed of a large portion
of their former real income, as expressed in terms of commodi-
ties, they can buy.
The Settlement's and Concession's efforts to control, and
to keep low, prices of rice have come to nothing. Neither big
nor small merchants obey the rice price regulations decreed
by the two areas' authorities. Settlement and Concession lack
the funds to buy big rice supplies of their own and compel,
by means of competing with the regular rice trade at a low
rate of profit, that trade to be satisfied with moderate returns,
and to refrain from rice speculation and profiteering.
In this situation, it would seem that local industries would
do well to consider the organization of their workers' supply
with cheap rice by industry itself. If the major industries in
town, or only some of them, decided to get together and to
start importing rice on their own, they should be able to re-
lieve the rice situation. They might sell to their workers rice
imported by themselves at a low profit accounting for interest
on the capital engaged, or at cost, or below cost, in the latter
instances booking the loss as another form of wage increase.
A capital outlay of some $50,000,000 would be sufficient
to finance the whole of Shanghai's rice supply, and $15,000,000
would be enough to finance the rice consumption of the work-
ers of Shanghai's major industries. The raising of such sums
undoubtedly is within the capacity of the local industry's
financial strength, and of the Shanghai capital market. In-
vested in rice, this capital would appreciate and depreciate
with prices of this important commodity, and would be im-
mune from danger of annihilation by currency devaluation.
The ideal solution would seem to be that all big Shanghai
industries join hands in the establishment of a gigantic rice
import company. They might raise part of the capital out of
their own funds, and part of it by appealing to the capital
market. They would buy in large quantities at correspond-
ingly favorable prices; they would be able to mobilize shipping
space at reasonable rates; they would be assured of their
customers. Local industrial wages might be partitioned into
a rice section, to be paid out in form of a certain volume of
rice per worker's head, and a cash section. The fixation of
a minimum rice supply per worker would stabilize an important
part of the workers' wages, save the latter from the danger
of further deterioration in commodity terms, and give laborers
a new and greater interest in the industries which employ them.
Should such an enterprise be seriously attempted, with
an honest intention of doing something for the workers and
granting them at least partial compensation for the recent
loss in real income they incurred, the local labor situation may
be greatly improved.
pages.zh:
获得了100%的工资增长。大多数工人的工资增幅要小得多。显然，他们的处境已大大恶化，他们失去了很大一部分以前的实际收入，这体现在他们能购买的商品数量上。

租界和法租界控制和保持低米价的努力已归于失败。大小商人均不遵守两区当局颁布的大米价格规定。租界和法租界缺乏资金自行购买大量大米储备，并通过以低利润率与正常大米贸易竞争的方式，迫使该行业满足于适度回报，并避免大米投机和牟取暴利。

在这种情况下，当地工业界似乎最好考虑由行业自身组织向其工人供应廉价大米。如果镇上的主要工业企业，或者其中部分企业，决定联合起来自行进口大米，它们应该能够缓解大米供应紧张的局面。它们可以向工人出售自行进口的大米，仅收取涵盖所用资本利息的微薄利润，或者按成本价，甚至低于成本价出售，在后一种情况下，将亏损记为另一种形式的工资增加。

约5000万元的资本支出足以资助整个上海的大米供应，而1500万元足以资助上海主要工业企业工人的大米消费。筹集如此数额的资金无疑在当地工业界的财力范围和上海资本市场的能力之内。这笔资金投入大米后，其价值将随这一重要商品的价格波动而增减，并且不会受到货币贬值导致资产灭失的危险。

理想的解决方案似乎是所有上海大型工业企业联手成立一家巨型大米进口公司。它们可以从自有资金中筹集部分资本，并通过向资本市场募集来筹集其余部分。它们可以以相应优惠的价格大批量采购；能够以合理的费率调动航运空间；并且拥有确定的客户群。当地工业工资可以分为大米部分和现金部分，大米部分以每位工人一定数量的大米形式支付。确定每位工人的最低大米供应量，将稳定工人工资的重要组成部分，使后者免受商品计价进一步恶化的危险，并使劳动者对其受雇的行业产生新的、更大的兴趣。

如果真诚地尝试开展此类企业，旨在为工人做些实事，并对他们最近遭受的实际收入损失给予至少部分补偿，那么当地的劳工局势可能会得到极大改善。

REPORT
Date April 26. 1940.

Subject Press report - Increase in godown charges for rice.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

With reference to the attached extract from
the China Press of April 23, 1940, regarding the
management of large godowns increasing their
charges and stipulating that unless the huge
quantities of rice are removed from storage an
additional increased charge for space would be made,
enquiries show that the report is highly exaggerated.
The majority of the owners of godowns in the
Settlement and French Concession have increased their
space rentals during the past few months, but in
most cases the increase was made as a result of the
general increase in the cost of living.
The following list is that of the larger
godowns.
The Roosevelt Terminal godowns on the French
Bund were charging a godown space rental of $0.11
per bag of rice for any period exceeding ten days,
Because of this cheap rate, many owners of rice,
stored therein, delayed taking delivery of their
goods with the result the godowns have become
congested with rice to the exclusion of other
commodities. In order to remedy this situation,
the management on March 10 published a notification
in the local Chinese press stating that with effect
from March 15, the godown charges on rice would be
as follows :-
Up to 10 days - Free

主题 新闻报道 - 大米仓库费用增加。

撰写及呈送人 D. I. Crawford

关于附带的1940年4月23日《字林西报》摘录，其中提到大型仓库管理者增加费用并规定，除非移除储存的大量大米，否则将收取额外的空间占用费，经查询显示，该报道严重夸大。

CHINA PRESS.

Godowns Here To Hike Space
Rent On 400,000 Bags Rice

Managements of large godowns
here have served notice on their
customers that unless the huge
quantities of rice be removed
from the storage establishments
they would be subject to enor-
mously increased space rentals
in the immediate future, THE
CHINA PRESS learned yester-
day.
Among godown owners who have
issued this notice were the Butter-
field and Swire, the large banks here
and a few Chinese business houses.
The measure was adopted, it was
learned, in view of the fact that
the large stocks of rice in the go-
downs had crowded out merchandise
which under ordinary circumstances
would be given precedence in the
godowns.
Authoritative quarters yester-
day voiced their approval of the
measure since, if the rice be
forced out of the godowns, it
might help to improve prices
here.

400,000 Bags Stored

Although the exact amount of
rice in the godowns could not be
ascertained, dealers here estimated
that it totaled from 300,000 to 400,000
bags in the larger godowns alone.
Some of the stocks were said to
have been stored in the godowns
for many months, the owners, it was
said, finding it more profitable to
pay the space rental than disposing
of them at present.
The ruling of the godowns found
an especially warm reception among
officials of the Committee in charge
of Cheap Rice Sale here who be-
lieved that the unloading of this
huge amount of rice into the mar-
ket would have the inevitable effect
of lowering the price of rice.
Interviewed by THE CHINA PRESS,
an official of the Committee, stated
that another meeting would be held
this Friday to draft final plans for
resumption of the cheap sale here.
He revealed that a large group of
representative businessmen here
would attend the meeting at which
further financial pledges would be
made for support of the sale.

Funds Still Needed

The Committee's plan to raise
funds for continuation of the sale
was reported yesterday to be still
far short of its $1,000,000 objective.
Thus far, only a little more than
$250,000 has been received, repre-
senting contributions by committee
members themselves.
Public donations to the fund may
be made at any branch of the
Chartered Bank or the Hongkong
and Shanghai Banking Corporation.
Prices of both domestic and im-
ported rice improved slightly in the
local market. Saigon rice was
quoted at about $9 per picul, and
rice of other varieties ranged from
about $8.

《字林西报》。

此处仓库拟提高40万袋大米的仓储租金

据《字林西报》昨日获悉，本地大型仓库的管理方已向其客户发出通知，除非将大量大米从仓储设施中搬离，否则在不久的将来将面临大幅上涨的仓储租金。

发出此通知的仓库业主包括太古洋行（Butterfield and Swire）、本地各大银行以及少数华商企业。据悉，采取这一措施是因为仓库内的大量大米库存挤占了通常在仓库中享有优先权的商品空间。

权威人士昨日对该措施表示赞同，认为如果迫使大米流出仓库，可能有助于改善本地米价。

储存量达40万袋

虽然无法确定仓库中大米的确切数量，但本地商人估计，仅大型仓库中的总量就达到30万至40万袋。据说部分库存已在仓库中存放数月，业主们发现，支付仓储租金比目前将其处置更为有利可图。

仓库的这一决定在负责本地平价大米销售委员会的官员中受到了特别热烈的欢迎，他们认为将如此大量的大米投放市场必然会产生降低米价的效果。

该委员会的一位官员在接受《字林西报》采访时表示，本周五将举行另一次会议，起草恢复本地平价销售的最终计划。他透露，本地一批具有代表性的商界人士将出席此次会议，并在会上为进一步支持销售作出更多的资金承诺。

资金仍有缺口

据报道，委员会为延续销售而筹集资金的计划目前仍远未达到100万美元的目标。迄今为止，仅收到略高于25万美元的款项，这些款项代表委员会成员自身的捐款。

公众向该基金的捐款可在麦加利银行（Chartered Bank）或汇丰银行（Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation）的任何分行进行。

本地市场上国产和进口大米的价格均略有回升。西贡米报价约为每担9元，其他品种的大米价格约为8元。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. ...
No. 503957 D. Blanchet
Date: April 26 1940

Subject. Sales of rice to Chinese and Annamite Constables in
the French Police.

Made by. D.S.I. Hide. Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

On April 25, 1940, Lt. F. Blanchet,
Deputy Commissioner of the French Police, was
interviewed regarding the recent reports in the
Chinese press relating to the official cheap sale
of rice to Chinese and Annamite constables of the
French Police.

He explained that the permission granted
the French Municipal Council by the Japanese
Authorities for the purchase of rice from Quinsan
was in the nature of a quid pro quo to accelerate
negotiations for the opening of the gates giving
access to Nantao and for the passage of military
supplies through the Concession.

Present arrangements cover the purchase
of some three thousand piculs at $36.00 which is
being transported from Quinsan to Shanghai by
trucks supplied by the French Authorities. This
quantity is sufficient for each Chinese and Annamite
constable to purchase three quarters of a picul.

Efforts are being made to arrange for the
purchase of further supplies under similar conditions
but it is doubtful if they will prove successful.

Lt. Blanchet stated it was extremely
regrettable that these arrangements have been reported
in the press and he would appreciate it if this
information is treated as confidential and not put
into writing.

Commr. of Police

事由。向法租界警务处的华籍及安南籍巡捕出售大米。

制作人。特别处督察长 Hide。转呈人。副督察长 Crawford

1940年4月25日，就中文报纸近期关于法租界警务处官方廉价向华籍及安南籍巡捕出售大米的报道，约谈了法租界警务处副总监 F. Blanchet 中尉。

他解释说，日本当局允许法公董局从昆山购买大米，这在性质上是一种交换条件，旨在加速关于开放通往南市的大门以及允许军用物资通过租界的谈判。

目前的安排包括以36.00元的价格购买约三千担大米，这些大米正由法国当局提供的卡车从昆山运往上海。这一数量足以让每名华籍和安南籍巡捕购买四分之三担。

目前正在努力安排在类似条件下购买更多供应品，但能否成功尚存疑问。

Blanchet 中尉表示，这些安排见诸报端令人极为遗憾，他希望将此信息作为机密处理，且不形成书面记录。

National Herald, Ta Mei Pao, Chinese-American Daily News,
Hwa Pao and Sin Wan Pao :- 7.12.39 (AM)

THE RICE SITUATION

Of late, the price of rice has been increasing
rapidly every day and is now over $40 per picul. This is
not due to lack of supply but to the hoarding and
manipulation on the part of unscrupulous merchants. If
such acts are allowed to carry on without restrictions, the
livelihood of the people of the middle and the lower classes

will be greatly affected. As the situation constitutes
a direct menace to peace and order in the Foreign Settlements,
the S.M.C. has tried to put a stop to the hoarding of rice
but has failed. In view of the fact that without effective
measures against such acts the situation cannot be improved,
the S.M.C. has instructed its Legal Department to devise
effective measures against the unscrupulous merchants. It
is learned that the authorities of the Shanghai First Special
District Court are also paying close attention to the rice
situation and are planning co-operation with the Legal
Department of the S.M.C.
It is also learned that the Control Committee
of the Rice Market has attained good results by adopting
supervisory measures in the market. According to a member
of the Control Committee, speculation has been less recently,
so that the market is not so chaotic as before. Since the
rice owners must first register with the Control Committee
before they can carry out their business transactions,
there were over 4,000 bags of rice registered with the
Committee yesterday, showing an increase of over 2,000 bags.
Therefore, it is anticipated that the price will be reduced
when the transactions are flowing normally.
According to a certain banker, banking
circles have agreed to extend loans for the purchase of
foreign rice for cheap sales. However, they will not start
these loans until a sound method has been devised by various
public bodies and people of various circles. Moreover, the
increase in the exchange rate has also been the cause of the
postponement in purchases of foreign rice.
Yesterday about 4,000 bags of rice were
transported to Shanghai from the interior and over 20,000
bags of foreign rice were shipped to Shanghai by Butterfield
and Swire. The price of Chinese rice was steady in the
market yesterday, while a decrease of $0.50 per picul in the
price of foreign rice was registered.

《国民日报》、《大美晚报》、《中美日报》、
《华报》和《新闻报》:- 1939年12月7日（上午）

米价形势

近来，米价每日迅速上涨，目前已超过每担40美元。这并非由于供应短缺，而是由于不法商人的囤积和操纵。如果允许此类行为不受限制地继续下去，中下层民众的生计

将受到严重影响。鉴于这种情况对外国租界的和平与秩序构成直接威胁，工部局（S.M.C.）曾试图制止大米囤积，但未能成功。鉴于如果没有针对此类行为的有效措施，局势无法改善，工部局已指示其法律科制定针对不法商人的有效措施。据悉，上海第一特区地方法院当局也密切关注米价形势，并计划与工部局法律科合作。
另悉，米市场管理委员会通过在市场采取监管措施，已取得良好成效。据管理委员会成员称，近期投机活动减少，因此市场不像以前那样混乱。由于米商必须先向管理委员会注册才能进行交易，昨日在该委员会注册的大米超过4000包，增加了2000多包。因此，预计当交易恢复正常流动时，价格将会下降。
据某银行家称，银行界已同意提供贷款用于购买外国大米以进行廉价销售。然而，在各公共机构和各界人士制定出健全的方法之前，他们不会启动这些贷款。此外，汇率上涨也是推迟购买外国大米的原因。
昨日约有4000包大米从内地运抵上海，另有20000多包外国大米由太古洋行（Butterfield and Swire）运抵上海。昨日市场上中国大米价格稳定，而外国大米价格每担下跌了0.50美元。

AMPLE STOCKS OF RICE IN SHANGHAI : NO INTERFERENCE
WITH SOURCES OF ARRIVALS : UNSCRUPULOUS MERCHANTS
FABRICATE RUMOURS IN ORDER TO GET PROFITS.

The rice situation is closely connected
with the residents of Shanghai. The price of rice
has been increased greatly during the past few days,
this being due to a rumour among the public that
rice stocks are reduced and the transportation of
rice interrupted. This rumour has been spread by
unscrupulous people. As a matter of fact, the
stocks of rice in this locality are sufficient to
maintain the people for some time. Meanwhile,
rice is being transported to Shanghai continuously
from rice producing areas and this is more than
sufficient to make good the stocks consumed.
Unexpectedly, certain unscrupulous merchants are
holding large quantities of rice and in the meantime
spread rumours that the arrival of rice is
interrupted, with the object of raising the market

pages.en:
RICE SITUATION.

The rice situation as it affects the Shanghai
public is one of paramount importance, but not as some
unscrupulous people would like the Chinese populace to
believe, one of immediate shortage and lack of supplies.
The stocks held at present in Shanghai are ample for
some time to come and arrivals from the rice producing
areas are well above the average, in fact the stocks are
greatly supplemented by these excess arrivals being more
than sufficient to offset the demand or sales - yes sales -
provided those unscrupulous people who call themselves
dealers and who are known to the authorities do not abuse
their calling by buying supplies over and above their
nominal business. They are the people who with large
orders bought start rumours of interference with supplies
which are non-existent and who re-sell their stocks when the
price has been inflated by their low-down trickery. Anyone
who cares to follow the sales of rice will see at a glance
that there is overbuying in the market with the consequent
increase in price which is just what those unscrupulous
people have been angling for. This unethical way of doing
business is to be deplored and the authorities are, it is
reported, alive to this state of affairs and we may look
forward to the plans of those unscrupulous people being
made to toe the line.

（批：Copy given to Press & S.I.）
pages.zh:
米价形势。

米价形势对上海公众的影响至关重要，但并不像一些
不法分子希望中国民众相信的那样，是立即出现的短缺和供应不足。
目前上海持有的库存足以维持未来一段时间，来自产米区的到货量远高于平均水平，事实上，这些超额到货极大地补充了库存，足以抵消需求或销售——是的，销售——前提是那些自称为经销商且被当局所知的不法分子不要滥用其职业，购买超出其名义业务所需的供应品。正是这些人带着大额订单开始购买，散布供应受到干扰的谣言（实际上并不存在），并在价格因其卑鄙伎俩而被抬高后转售其库存。任何关注大米销售的人都会一眼看出市场上存在过度购买，从而导致价格上涨，这正是那些不法分子所企图的。这种不道德的经营方式令人遗憾，据报道，当局已意识到这一事态，我们可以期待那些不法分子的计划将被迫就范。

September 21, 1939. Morning Translation.

Central China Daily News, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Hwa Pao:

THE CHEAP SALE OF SAIGON RICE

Yesterday was the third day of the cheap sale
of Saigon rice at the five depots established by the Rice
Shop Owners' Guild. Large numbers of people made purchases.
The sales were carried out in good order.
The first depot is located on a piece of
vacant ground at the corner of North Honan Road and Range
Road. Thanks to the protection accorded by Chinese
and foreign detectives and uniformed men of the two Foreign
Settlements, the sales have been carried out safely. The
first depot sold 200 bags of Saigon rice between 7.45 and
11.15 a.m. yesterday.
To avoid unexpected incidents at the first
depot at the corner of North Honan Road and Range Road
because of its proximity to Chapel, the Rice Shop Owners'
Guild has decided to amalgamate, as from to-day, the first
with the second depot at the corner of Avenue Road and
Carter Road. A notice to this effect has been issued
by the Guild. As from to-day the number of bags of
Saigon rice to be sold at the second depot will be increased
to 400.
According to Chen Shao-li (陳少盧), a leading
member in rice trade circles, the 8,000 bags of Saigon
rice have been found to be insufficient to meet the demand;
therefore the Rice Shop Owners' Guild is planning a second
cheap sale. However, no decision in this respect has
been reached because supplies of Chinese rice are arriving
in Shanghai and the price has dropped. The holding
of a second cheap sale of Saigon rice will depend upon
the price of Chinese rice.
The control of rice by the Nan Shing Company
(南興公司) is affecting the supplies of rice to the common
people in Nantao. Recently they requested the Supervisory
Committee of the Nantao Refugee Zone to undertake a
cheap sale of rice.
It is learned that certain plans have been
drawn up by the Committee and preparations to undertake
the cheap sale of rice will be started in a few days. All
people who are extremely poor will be given accommodation
and food at the camp of the Committee.

Hwa Pao of Sept.20:

The Rice Shop Owners' Guild suspended the
cheap sale of rice on the anniversary of the September 18
Incident, but resumed the sales on the following day.
The third depot at Yu Fu Shih Temple (玉佛寺), Gordon
Road, was opened at 8 a.m. September 19. Over 5,000
poor people assembled at the place to make purchases.
The crowd was so large that the detectives and policemen
were unable to control it and some disorder occurred,
resulting in an old coolie of about 60 years old being
injured. The detectives then instructed the depot
to suspend the sale and removed the injured man by
ambulance to the Lao Kung Hospital (勞工醫院).

1939年9月21日。晨间翻译。

《华中日报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《华报》：

西贡大米廉价出售

昨日是米业公会设立的五个经销点进行西贡大米廉价出售的第三天。大量民众前来购买。销售秩序井然。
第一个经销点位于北河南路与靶子路（Range Road，今武进路附近）拐角处的一块空地上。得益于中外租界便衣侦探和制服警员的保护，销售安全进行。昨日上午7:45至11:15，第一经销点售出200包西贡大米。
为避免因靠近教堂（Chapel，原文如此，可能指某特定地点或为OCR错误，暂按原文语境理解，或指虹口某地标）而在北河南路与靶子路拐角处的第一经销点发生意外事件，米业公会决定从今天起将第一经销点与位于爱文义路（Avenue Road，今北京西路）与卡特路（Carter Road，今大田路或附近）拐角处的第二经销点合并。公会已发布相关通知。从今天起，第二经销点销售的西贡大米数量将增加到400包。
据米业界知名人士陈少卢（Chen Shao-li）称，发现8000包西贡大米不足以满足需求；因此米业公会正计划进行第二次廉价销售。然而，对此尚未做出决定，因为中国大米正运抵上海，且价格已下跌。是否举行第二次西贡大米廉价销售将取决于中国大米的价格。
南兴公司（Nan Shing Company）对大米的控制影响了南市普通民众的大米供应。最近，他们请求南市难民区监护委员会承担大米廉价销售工作。
据悉，委员会已制定某些计划，并将在几天内开始准备进行大米廉价销售。所有极度贫困者将在委员会的营地获得食宿安置。

9月20日《华报》：

米业公会在九一八事变纪念日暂停了大米廉价销售，但于次日恢复销售。位于戈登路（Gordon Road，今江宁路）玉佛寺的第三经销点于9月19日上午8点开放。超过5000名穷人聚集在此购买。人群过于庞大，侦探和警察无法控制，发生了一些混乱，导致一名约60岁的老苦力受伤。随后侦探指示经销点暂停销售，并用救护车将伤者送往劳工医院（Lao Kung Hospital）。

pages.en:
At 9 a.m. the depot re-opened, but owing to
the presence of another huge crowd, it ceased selling rice
again. Under the direction of the detectives and
policemen, a space was railed off with a rope. The depot
re-opened its doors at 11.15 a.m. and the rice was sold
under more orderly conditions. By 12.40 p.m., 200 bags
of rice had been sold whereupon the depot closed for the
day as its stock was sold out.
The first depot sold 300 bags by 1 p.m. at
which hour it closed for the day. The second depot and
the fourth depot sold 200 bags each and the fifth depot had
sold 300 bags by 6 p.m. Good order was maintained and
no accidents occurred.
It is learned that the cheap sale will be
continued to-day until all the 8,000 bags have been sold.
According to Su Fah-hsiun (苏法勋), a member
of the Rice Shop Owners' Guild, each of the five depots
will limit its sales to 200 bags only.
In view of the overcrowding and
disorder at some of the depots, the Rice Shop Owners'
Guild convened a meeting on September 19 at which it was
proposed to request the various benevolent bodies and
reliable rice shops to issue tickets in order to prevent
disorder at the sales.
A supervisor is sent to each of the five
depots to check the takings. After deducting expenses,
the balance is sent to the Guild. All the workers of the
five depots are employees of rice shops; they are giving
their services gratis.
The proceeds of the first two days amounted
to $32,000. The money has already been handed over to
the Rice Shop Owners' Guild.
On September 19 rice owners attended the
Control Committee of the Rice Market to register their
willingness to undertake the sale of 4,980 bags of rice.
A consignment of 540 "zar" of rice has arrived
on three junks in the Soochow Creek.
Owing to the over-stocked position and the
cheap sale of rice by the five depots, the price has
dropped by $1, best quality "See Mee" being sold at
$25 per "zar".
pages.zh:
上午9点，经销点重新开放，但由于另一大批人群的出现，再次停止售米。在侦探和警察的指挥下，用绳子隔出了一块空间。经销点于上午11:15重新开门，大米在更有序的情况下出售。截至下午12:40，已售出200包大米，随后因库存售罄，该经销点当日关闭。
第一经销点在下午1点前售出300包，随即当日关闭。第二经销点和第四经销点各售出200包，第五经销点在下午6点前已售出300包。秩序良好，未发生事故。
据悉，廉价销售将持续到今天，直到8000包全部售罄。
据米业公会成员苏法勋（Su Fah-hsiun）称，五个经销点每个仅限制销售200包。
鉴于部分经销点拥挤和混乱，米业公会于9月19日召开会议，提议请求各慈善团体和可靠的米店发放票证，以防止销售时的混乱。
每个经销点都派有一名监督员检查收款情况。扣除费用后，余额上交公会。五个经销点的所有工作人员均为米店雇员；他们是无偿提供服务。
前两天的收入共计32,000美元。这笔钱已移交给米业公会。
9月19日，米商参加了米市场管理委员会，登记愿意承担4,980包大米的销售。
一批540“石”（zar，音译，可能指担或石）的大米已由三艘舢板运抵苏州河。
由于库存过剩以及五个经销点的廉价销售，价格下跌了1美元，最好的“西米”（See Mee，音译，可能指某种米）售价为每“石”25美元。

September 18, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Hwa Pao:

THE RICE SITUATION : CHEAP RICE SALES DEPOTS SUSPEND
SALES TO-DAY

The Rice Shop Owners' Guild has been undertaking the cheap sale of the 8,000 bags of Saigon rice at its five depots in the Foreign Settlements. Yesterday was the second day of the cheap sale of such rice. Despite the rainy weather, poor people collected in large numbers to make purchases. In view of the disorder prevailing on the first day of the cheap sale, resulting in a fatal tragedy at the fourth depot, the Guild in question yesterday adopted every precaution to prevent unfortunate incidents. As the sales were carried out more smoothly than on September 16, there was no trouble.

Yesterday 199 bags of Saigon rice were sold by the first depot, 300 bags by the second and 200 bags by the third. The purchasers at these three depots totalled about 3,000 (?). The sale derived about $4,900 (?). The fourth depot sold about 183 bags to some 5,000 persons and took in $6,974.40, while the fifth depot sold about 230 bags to some 3,000 persons and took in $4,580.

To-day being the anniversary of the September 18 Incident, the Police authorities of the Foreign Settlements, fearing that untoward incident might take place, notified the Rice Shop Owners' Guild yesterday to suspend the sale on September 18.

Upon receipt of the notice, the Guild immediately directed the depots to suspend the sales on September 18 and to resume it on September 19.

According to information received, various public bodies are planning a second sale of cheap rice after the first consignment of Saigon rice of 8,000 bags has been sold out.

As the price of rice in Nantao is higher than that in the Foreign Settlements, owing to the control of rice supplies by the Nan Shing Company (南兴公司), a number of poor people in Nantao recently called at the International Relief Committee in the Refugee Zone and requested that cheap sales of rice be held. It is learned that owing to financial and other difficulties, the Committee has to give careful consideration to the request.

It is also learned that the old woman named Chang Yu Sz (张余氏), native of Ningpo, age 73, who was seriously injured on September 16 as a result of overcrowding of purchasers at the fourth cheap rice sales depot at the Shantung Guild (山东会馆) on Rue Porte de l'Ouest, corner of Avenue Dubail, died at the St. Marie Hospital at about 7 a.m. yesterday. Her son Chang Li-fah (张立法), age 40, is a worker of the Raw Cotton Department of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.

1939年9月18日。
下午译件。

《新闻报》、《申报》、《华报》：

米价情况：平价米售处今日停售

米业同业公会一直在其位于公共租界的五个分销处进行8,000袋西贡米的平价销售。昨日是此类大米平价销售的第二天。尽管天气下雨，贫民仍大量聚集购买。鉴于平价销售首日秩序混乱，导致第四分销处发生致命惨剧，该公会昨日采取了各种预防措施，以防不幸事件发生。由于销售工作比9月16日更为顺利，未发生骚乱。

昨日，第一分销处售出西贡米199袋，第二分销处售出300袋，第三分销处售出200袋。这三处分销处的购买者总数约为3,000人（？）。销售额约为4,900美元（？）。第四分销处向约5,000人售出约183袋，收入6,974.40美元；第五分销处向约3,000人售出约230袋，收入4,580美元。

今日正值“九一八”事变纪念日，公共租界警方担心可能发生不测事件，于昨日通知米业同业公会在9月18日暂停销售。

接到通知后，公会立即指示各分销处于9月18日暂停销售，并于9月19日恢复销售。

据收到的消息，在首批8,000袋西贡米售罄后，各公共团体正计划进行第二次平价米销售。

由于南兴公司控制大米供应，南市的大米价格高于公共租界，近期南市的一些贫民前往难民区的国际救济委员会，请求举行大米平价销售。据悉，由于财政和其他困难，委员会必须慎重考虑这一请求。

另悉，宁波籍老妇张余氏，73岁，因9月16日在法租界贝当路（Avenue Dubail）与西门路（Rue Porte de l'Ouest）拐角处的山东会馆第四平价米售处购买者拥挤而受重伤，于昨晨7时许在圣玛丽医院去世。其子张立法，40岁，系三井物产株式会社原棉部工人。

August 30, 1939.
Morning Translation.

Hwa Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Chinese-American Daily News
(Chungking telegram) :-

CHUNGKING GOVERNMENT ALLOTS EXCHANGE FOR PURCHASE OF
SAIGON RICE

Owing to the interruption to communications
caused by the Japanese and the puppet authorities, a
shortage of rice prevailed and cases of rice stealing
have been reported in Shanghai. On August 24, Messrs Yu
Ya-ching, Li Min and Hsu Chi-ohing sent the following
joint telegram to Dr. H.H. Kung, President of the Executive
Yuan of the National Government requesting permission
for local public bodies to purchase £10,000 worth of
Saigon rice (about 20,000 piculs) :-

"Owing to the interruption of the transportation
of Chinese rice, coupled with the difficulty of making
purchases of foreign rice, a serious shortage of rice
supply has been experienced in Shanghai. There are
now only 80,000 bags of rice in stock in the Foreign
Settlements while the price of rice has gone up to as
high as $36 a picul. Moreover, there are more than
80,000 refugees in Shanghai, the maintenance of whose
livelihood will become very difficult. Local public
bodies have decided to make a joint purchase of 20,000
piculs of Saigon rice to relieve the situation. We
therefore request permission to make application for an
allotment of £10,000 at the rate of the Central Bank of
China and the Bank of Communications to pay for this
purchase of Saigon rice".

In reply, the following telegram has been
received from Dr. Kung :-

"Your request is noted, and in reply permission
is granted to make application for a sum of £10,000 at
the rate quoted by the two banks to pay for the purchase.
The rice should be transported to Shanghai as quickly
as possible to relieve the shortage. For the sake of
poor people, the rice should be allowed to enter Shanghai
free so as to reduce its selling price. Instructions
have been issued to this effect to the Foreign Exchange
Examination Committee and the Inspector-General of Customs."

It is learned that the first consignment of
Saigon rice amounting to 18,000 bags, ordered through
the good offices of Mr. Yu Ya-ching, is expected in Shanghai
before September 10.

（批：crwms 396）

《华报》、《新闻报》、《申报》、《中美日报》
（重庆电报）:-

重庆政府拨付外汇购买西贡大米

由于日本人和傀儡当局造成通讯中断，上海出现大米短缺，并有盗米案件报道。8月24日，虞洽卿、李敏和徐寄庼先生联名致电国民政府行政院院长孔祥熙博士，请求允许地方公共团体购买价值10,000英镑的西贡大米（约20,000担）:-

“由于中国大米运输中断，加之购买外国大米困难，上海大米供应严重短缺。目前公共租界库存大米仅80,000袋，而米价已涨至每担36美元之高。此外，上海有难民8万余人，维持其生计将变得非常困难。地方公共团体决定联合购买20,000担西贡大米以缓解局势。因此，我们请求允许按中国银行和交通银行的汇率申请拨款10,000英镑，以支付此次西贡大米采购费用”。

孔博士复电如下：-

“所请已悉，兹答复准许按两家银行报价申请款项10,000英镑以支付采购费用。大米应尽快运往上海以缓解短缺。为了贫民利益，应允许大米免税进入上海，以降低其售价。已就此向外汇审核委员会和海关总税务司发出指令。”

据悉，经虞洽卿先生斡旋订购的首批18,000袋西贡米，预计将于9月10日前抵达上海。

（批：crwms 396）

Translation

Dear Editor,
Of late the price of rice has been
increasing rapidly. The people will be facing starvation.
Who is responsible for this state of affairs?
Now let us tell you openly the cause of
all this. Since June 25, the Shanghai Municipal Council
has hoarded more than 500,000 piculs of rice and it is
still purchasing rice. The hoarded rice is being stored
in the godowns of large banks. This is perfectly true
and reliable information.
In addition, heartless traitorous merchants,
in conspiracy with the shameless Sin Shun News Agency
(新聲社), are engaged in fabricating poisonous and false
propaganda with a view to misleading the public.
Unless we want to die of starvation, we
should unite and ask the S.M.C. to bring out from the
godowns all its hoarded rice and sell it at a reducedprice
to poor people. It is better to commit suicide than to
die of starvation. There remains only one course open to
us: We should unanimously fight the S.M.C.; it is better
to die fighting.
We would like to reiterate here that this
Corps has been established purely under the principle of
seeking death rather than to die of starvation and that
we are in no way being utilized by any other party.
All the foregoing is true and reliable.
We request your esteemed paper to publish it.

(Signed) Kuh Tien-min (葛天明)
Chief of the Settlement Righteousness
and Life-Saving Corps.
pages.zh:
译文

编辑先生：

近来米价飞涨。百姓将面临饥荒。

谁应对此局面负责？

现在让我们向贵报公开披露造成这一切的原因。自6月25日以来，上海公共租界工部局已囤积大米五十余万担，且仍在继续购米。所囤积之大米正储存在各大银行的仓库中。此信息完全真实可靠。

此外，一些黑心的奸商与无耻的“新声社”（Sin Shun News Agency）勾结，编造有毒的虚假宣传，旨在误导公众。

除非我们想饿死，否则我们应当团结起来，要求上海公共租界工部局将其囤积在仓库中的所有大米拿出，并以低价出售给贫民。与其饿死，不如自杀。我们只剩下一条路可走：我们应一致对抗上海公共租界工部局；战死胜于饿死。

我们在此重申，本团体的成立纯粹本着宁死也不愿饿死的原则，我们绝未被任何其他党派所利用。

以上所述均真实可靠。

恳请贵报予以刊登。

（签名）葛天明（Kuh Tien-min）
租界正义救生团团长

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Gassi
With reference to the attached anonymous letter
against the Dong Yui Rice Shop, 620 Peking Road, alleg-
ing that the owner of this shop had concealed stocks of
rice awaiting higher prices, enquiries show that the
allegation is entirely unfounded.
The shop consists of a single house with two
floors, the downstairs room being used as a shop, while
the room upstairs is used by the family of the proprietor
named Fee Sieu-kan (費秀干), his mother and wife.
The proprietor is assisted by his wife, a coolie
and an apprentice, and the shop has a stock of 40 "zar"
of Chinese rice. There is a notice in the shop which
states that each customer will only be allowed half a
"zar" of rice.
The owner of this shop named Fee Sieu-kan (費秀干),
is a native of Soochow and was formerly an employee of
the Hung Dah Rice Hong, North Szechuen Road. About
six years ago, Fee established the Dong Yui Rice Shop
at its present address with a capital of $5,000. The
business has been on the small side; and because of his
he
lack of social standing and ambition,/has failed to
obtain the usual financial backing from his fellow
traders and consequently at the end of 1938 had lost
some $3,000 of his capital.
Enquiries among the rice shop owners have failed
to elicit any information that he has a godown in addi-
tion to the shop.
Sih Tse Liang

店主由其妻子、一名苦力和一名学徒协助经营，店内库存有40“扎”中国大米。店内张贴有一则告示，声明每位顾客仅允许购买半“扎”大米。

该店店主名为费秀干（Fee Sieu-kan），系苏州人，曾任北四川路洪大米号的雇员。约六年前，费氏以5,000元资本在现址创办东裕米店。生意规模较小；且因其缺乏社会地位和野心，未能从同行商人处获得通常的金融支持，因此至1938年底已亏损资本约3,000元。

向其他米店业主查询后，未获知他除店铺外还拥有仓库的任何信息。

Date August 12, 1939.

Subject Rice situation - Broadcast message by Tsu Jiu Kee Rice
Hong - Price of rice in producing districts rises.
Made by J.S.I. Lacadie Forwarded by C Gaylor

* See O. 6813/10/II (1)

At 2 p.m. August 10, 1939, the Tsu Jiu
Kee (朱球記) Rice Hong, 145 Chekiang Road, broadcast
the following message over the Ling Yuen Broadcasting
Station, 132 Hoopeh Road (XHHF - K.C.960):-
"As rice shops are observing the price limit,
they have been purchasing less stocks, with the
result that their stocks on hand have become depleted.
There were few transactions in the Rice Market and
the prices were same as those of yesterday. It is
reported that owing to the high price in the
producing areas, the price limit here may probably
be modified. Rice hongs at different places are
therefore requested to transport rice to Shanghai
as freely as possible in order to maintain the
situation here. The price for Changchow and Wusieh
rice is approximately $24 and $25 (per "zar") and
Soochow rice approximately $23 and $23.50. Stocks
of Tuh Foong (德丰) Hong, Soochow, and of the
Chang Yung Kee (張永記) Hong, Chenmoo, have now
been delivered and the money paid to the Kingcheng
Banking Corporation. Tsu Jiu Kee, August 10."
It is reported that in consequence of this
message, the price of rice in the Sungkiang area rose
from $17 to $20 per "zar" and that a number of rice
merchants, who proceeded there in the morning of
August 10 for the purpose of purchasing rice, returned
without making any purchases because of the increase
in the price.

1939年8月10日下午2时，位于浙江路145号的朱球記（Tsu Jiu Kee）米行，通过位于虎丘路132号的灵元广播电台（XHHF - K.C.960）广播了如下消息：
“鉴于各米店遵守限价规定，进货量减少，导致现有库存耗尽。米市场交易寥寥，价格与昨日持平。据悉，由于产区价格高企，此地的限价规定可能会予以调整。因此，请各地米行尽可能自由地将大米运往上海，以维持本地局势。常州和无锡大米的價格约为每‘石’24元和25元，苏州大米约为23元和23.50元。苏州德丰（Tuh Foong）米行及陈墓张永記（Chang Yung Kee）米行的存货现已交付，款项已支付给金城银行（Kingcheng Banking Corporation）。朱球記，8月10日。”

由 J.L. Crawford 撰写并转呈

5月29日收到一封致上海公共租界工部局的信函，发信人名为赵庆（Zao Ching Lai，即趙慶），住址为克勒兹路（Rue Kraetzer）曾平里17号。信中建议工部局趁目前时局尚属平稳之际，采纳一项提高米价的计划，将由此产生的资金用于在紧急时期抵消米价上涨带来的影响。经对写信人的背景进行调查，查明赵庆澜，40岁，此前曾在上海的三家交易所担任经纪人并开展业务，其父为同顺（Doong Zung）米行的所有者，该米行现已停业，原址位于南市豆市街（Deu Dz Ka）。他使用过以下名称：

交易所名称 所用名称
杂粮交易所 顺记（Sung Kee）
金条交易所 协大森记（Yah Dah Sung Kee）

战事爆发后，他结束了业务，据称是因为遭受了重大损失。此后直到1938年6月才再次听到他的消息，当时他正从事从吴淞（Wusieh）和常熟向上海运输大米批发的业务。据称，1938年8月至11月期间，他代表日本方面在福州路515号的米市场购买了大量大米

pages.en:
Translation of letter to Council from Zao Ching Lai (趙慶)
dated 28th May, 1939

Rice Situation

During the last few days the newspapers were full of
reports concerning the rice situation. The highest price
recorded exceeded $18, which amounts to more than $20 per
picul calculated according to the old system of weights.
This is surprising. The time of the new crops it still
distant. Conferences with a view to maintaining reasonable
price levels have not had any satisfactory result. As the
question bears immensely on peace and good order, the Council
officers, who are all men of profound knowledge and experience,
must be working out a suitable solution. I have a certain
humble suggestion and I am deeply concerned over the matter.
The problem is so important, and judged by the present
circumstances, the causes for the rise of prices are so
numerous, that I venture to think that co-operation from
all quarters must be welcome. I therefore beg to submit
my humble views as follows :-

Meetings of rice dealers have not succeeded in
arriving at an effective and fundamental solution principally
for the following reasons : (1) Persons engaged in the rice
business found themselves in a difficult situation and
feared to advocate unusual measures. (2) Certain dealers
were unwilling to suffer losses. (3) Officers of rice
organizations were incompetent and could not satisfy the
wishes of the various parties. (4) Suggestions from certain
members, who were considered unimportant, were ignored.

After the outbreak of hostilities Shanghai became
a haven of safety for refugees from various places, resulting
in a great increase in population. As the distribution of
wealth among these people is extremely unequal, existence
becomes a difficult problem for most of the residents.
Clothing, food and shelter are the three most important
necessities. We can manage to live with very little clothing
pages.zh:
赵庆（Zao Ching Lai）致工部局信函译文
日期：1939年5月28日

米粮状况

近几日，报纸上充斥着有关米粮状况的报道。 recorded 最高价格超过18元，若按旧制重量计算，每担折合超过20元。这令人惊讶。新粮上市尚需时日。旨在维持合理价格水平的会议并未取得任何令人满意的结果。鉴于此事极大关系到和平与秩序，各位学识渊博、经验丰富的公董局董事们必定正在制定合适的解决方案。我有一项卑微的建议，并对此事深感关切。问题如此重要，且据目前形势判断，导致价格上涨的原因如此之多，以至于我认为各方的合作将是受欢迎的。因此，谨呈鄙见如下：

米商会议未能达成有效且根本的解决方案，主要原因如下：(1) 从事米业的人士发现自己处境困难，不敢提倡非常措施。(2) 某些商人不愿承受损失。(3) 米业组织的职员能力不足，无法满足各方意愿。(4) 某些被认为无足轻重的成员提出的建议被忽视。

战事爆发后，上海成为来自各地难民的避难所，导致人口大幅增加。由于这些人的财富分配极不均衡，生存对大多数居民来说成为一个难题。衣、食、住是三大最重要的必需品。我们可以靠着极少的衣物

pages.en:
- 2 -
and shelter; but we cannot exist for a day without food.
We may save money if we do not eat, or eat sparingly,
but this is very difficult to be put into practice. Therefore
the Council should not overlook this vital question of food
supply, but should appoint public-spirited, unselfish and
conscientious persons to take charge of the matter. As this
isolated oasis is not a producing centre, rice in ordinary
times must be imported by profit-making dealers. Owing to
difficulties in transportation and unsettled conditions in
various places along the routes traversed, it is but natural
that the price of rice should exceed the limit. At this time
of emergency why does not the Council take special measures
to cope with the difficult situation. Although the time may be
a little too late, there are still remedies.
The Council should in prosperous times slightly
increase the price of rice. The funds thus accrued could
be used to offset any increase in price in time of emergency.
What is taken from the people is used for the people; it
will not be necessary to appropriate funds from the Council's
revenue. This method is quite different from the present
measures which make the situation so difficult for dealers
to import rice to Shanghai and which have no practical value.
For instance the question of refugee relief should also be
carefully dealt with. Only by precautionary and fundamental
measures can the present difficult time be tided over. Empty
talk will not bring immediate relief. The time will come
when even the well-to-do and wealthy families will find it
difficult to live.
I have been a rice merchant for many years and in the
past I established branches in various cities; therefore, I
am quite familiar with the rice business. If the Council should
desire it, I am very willing to submit my inside opinions and
proposals. If the Council has already devised suitable
measures to cope with the situation, I have no objection to
pages.zh:
- 2 -
和住所勉强生活；但没有食物我们一天也无法生存。如果不吃或少吃，我们可以省钱，但这很难付诸实践。因此，公董局不应忽视这一至关重要的粮食供应问题，而应任命具有公益心、无私且 conscientious 的人员来负责此事。由于这个孤立的绿洲并非生产中心，平常时期的米粮必须由以营利为目的的商人进口。由于运输困难以及沿途各地局势动荡，米价超出限度也是自然之事。在此紧急时刻，公董局为何不采取特别措施来应对这一困难局面。虽然时间可能稍晚，但仍有补救之法。
公董局应在繁荣时期略微提高米价。由此积累的资金可用于抵消紧急时期价格的任何上涨。取之于民，用之于民；无需从公董局的财政收入中拨款。这种方法与目前的措施截然不同，目前的措施使得商人难以将米粮进口到上海，且没有实际价值。例如，难民救济问题也应得到仔细处理。只有采取预防性和根本性的措施，才能渡过目前的困难时期。空谈不会带来 immediate relief。总有一天，即使是富裕家庭也会发现生活艰难。
我从事米商多年，过去曾在各个城市设立分店；因此，我对米业相当熟悉。如果公董局愿意，我非常乐意提交我的内部意见和提议。如果公董局已经制定了合适的措施来应对局势，我不反对

pages.en:
withdraw my suggestions.
(signed) Zao Ching Lai
Address: No.17 Tseng Ping Li, Rue Kraetzer.
(Note: Received for translation noon 31st May, 1939)

February 21, 1938. Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated February 20 :-

RICE TO PAY CUSTOMS DUTY

Last year, when there was a shortage
of rice in Shanghai, the authorities of the Foreign
Settlements obtained a number of permits for the
importation of duty-free rice. These permits have now
been used up. In future, therefore, rice dealers
importing rice from abroad will have to pay Customs duty.
Recently, hawkers who had procured rice
from the surrounding districts have been selling rice on the
streets. As much as several hundred piculs are sold
daily. As this affects the business of rice shops, the
Rice Shop Owners' Association and the Chia Koh Daung
(嘉穀堂 Rice Dealers' Guild) the other day sent a letter
to the authorities of the two Foreign Settlements requesting
them to suppress these rice hawkers. With a view to
preventing bad elements from entering the Settlement
under pretext of selling rice as well as to preserve
order on the streets, the S.M.C. has decided to suppress
the rice hawkers. It has also decided to begin the collection
soon of a Refugee Relief Tax of $2 on every picul of
Chinese rice transported from interior districts by rice
dealers.

In order to relieve the serious shortage
of rice in Tientsin, Dairen, Tsingtao and other places
in the North, the Japanese firm Arai Yoko and a number
of influential rice dealers in North China have formed
a large transportation and sales company. Representatives
have been sent to Quinsan, Sungkiang, Tsingpu and
Chukiakoo to purchase 100,000 piculs of rice.

2月20日《华美晚报》：-

米粮须缴纳关税

去年上海米粮短缺时，外国租界当局获得了一批免税进口米粮的许可证。这些许可证现已用完。因此，今后从国外进口米粮的米商必须缴纳海关关税。最近，从周边地区获取米粮的小贩一直在街头售卖米粮。每日销量多达数百担。由于这影响了米店的生意，米店业主协会和嘉穀堂（米业公会）日前致函两个外国租界当局，请求取缔这些米贩。为了防止不良分子借卖米之名进入租界，并维护街道秩序，工部局决定取缔米贩。还决定不久开始对米商从内地地区运输的中国米每担征收2元难民救济税。

为了缓解天津、大连、青岛及华北其他地方的严重米荒，日本商行 Arai Yoko 和华北一些有影响力的米商组建了一家大型运输和销售公司。代表已被派往昆山、松江、青浦和朱家角购买10万担米粮。

每人出售的最大数量为24磅，任何剩余盈余将由各区负责人保留，等待总部的指示。

已向各分局发放了足够的供应品，各区负责人将做出必要的分发安排，并将在本月月底从购买米粮者的薪水中扣除款项。

必须明确，这是因暂时短缺而做出的特殊安排，不太可能再次发生，因此应告知华籍雇员，他们必须尽一切努力以通常方式满足自身需求。

这种米仅发给工部局的实际华籍雇员。

每个分局将发放两个量具，装满平口时分别容纳2磅和10磅。

13
Police permits for removal of rice.
8027/5(a)-1
From August 4, 1941 a charge of 10 cents per bag will be
made in respect of permits issued by the Police for removal of rice.
Applications for these permits are first submitted, in
duplicate on special forms, to the Secretariat (Mr. O'Connell).
When approved the fee payable is typed at the foot of each form,
the form is endorsed 'approved' by the Secretariat and one copy
of each application is forwarded to the Police (S. Sherman).
Permits are written out by a Police clerk at the time
the applicants present themselves at the issuing office.
Permits are not prepared beforehand.
Revenue Office shroff will be on duty in the Rice
Department Office No.695 during office hours to collect the fees.
The Police clerk will mark the fee payable on each permit
i.e. $...... and will pass both permit and application form to the
shroff who will collect the fee, enter permit number and fee in
his cash book, receipt the permit and pass it to the applicant.
The shroff will initial the application form, against the
fee payable, and pass it back to the Police clerk.
At the end of the day the money collected by the shroff
must agree with the total number of bags of rice, at 10 cents
per bag, covered by the permits prepared by the Police clerk.
When the cash has been balanced the Police clerk will prepare
a comprador's paying in slip and give it to the shroff who
will pay the money into the compradore and obtain his quittance.
The shroff will prepare a credit form as per specimen, and hand
it together with the compradore's receipt to the cashier.
The cashier will enter particulars in the Police Rice
Removal Permits register and will pass the credit slip through
in the ordinary way.
At the end of each month the cashier will receive a summary
of "applications approved and passed to Police" from the Secretariat
and a summary of "permits issued and permits not applied for" from
the Police Department. These two statements should agree and the
total in the Police Rice Removal Permits Register should agree with
the Police Summary of Permits issued. Any discrepancy must be
accounted for by the cashier.
The monthly statements will be kept on the cashier's file.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE AUG 4 1941）
pages.zh:
13
大米搬运警察许可证。
8027/5(a)-1
自1941年8月4日起，针对警方签发的用于搬运大米的许可证，将按每袋10美分收取费用。
此类许可证的申请须首先以专用表格一式两份提交至秘书处（奥康奈尔先生 O'Connell）。
申请获批后，应在每份表格底部打印应付费用，由秘书处在表格上背书签注“批准”，并将每份申请的一份副本转交警务处（S. 谢尔曼 S. Sherman）。
许可证由警务处文员在申请人前往发证办公室时当场填写。
许可证不预先制备。
收入处收款员将在办公时间内于大米部695号办公室值班，负责收取费用。
警务处文员将在每张许可证上注明应付费用，即“$......”，并将许可证和申请表一并交给收款员；收款员收取费用，在其现金账簿中登记许可证号码和费用，在许可证上出具收据，并将其交给申请人。
收款员将在申请表上对应付费用处签署简写姓名，并将表格退回给警务处文员。
每日终了时，收款员收取的款项必须与警务处文员所制备许可证涵盖的大米总袋数相符，按每袋10美分计算。
现金核对平衡后，警务处文员将编制买办缴款单并交给收款员，由收款员将款项存入买办处并取得其收据。
收款员将按样本格式编制贷记单，并将其连同买办收据一并交给出纳员。
出纳员将在《警方大米搬运许可证登记簿》中录入详情，并按常规程序处理贷记单。

Special Branch,
July 21, 1941.

Rice Removal Permite:-
Increase in work and suggested charge
for issue

Since its inception in July 1938, the work
of issuing Permits for the transportation of rice outside
the limits of the International Settlement has been under-
taken by the Special Branch. However, as the following
figures will show, the number of permits issued each
month has increased to such an extent that it can no
longer be undertaken by the Branch without great detriment
to other work, unless additional clerical assistance is
made available.

The table below gives the number of Permits
issued since the beginning of this year:-

| Month | No. of Permits | No. of bags |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| January | 383 | 29,231 |
| February | 468 | 40,702 |
| March | 410 | 33,657 |
| April | 363 | 30,775 |
| May | 500 | 38,907 |
| June | 1,140 | 99,544 |

From the above it will be seen that the work
has increased from a minor task which could be carried
out by a clerk in addition to his ordinary duties to a
nearly full time job. During the first 18 days of
July, an average of 64 permits per day have been issued
each working day, and this, allowing 5 minutes for the
issue of each permit (typing in English, writing in
Chinese and recording), means over five hours work a
day, allowing no time for investigating and checking up
of cases in doubt.
pages.zh:
特务科，
1941年7月21日。

大米搬运许可证：-
工作量增加及建议的发证收费

自1938年7月开始以来，签发运出国际租界范围的大米运输许可证的工作一直由特务科承担。然而，如下列数据所示，每月签发的许可证数量已大幅增加，除非提供额外的文书协助，否则该科将无法在不严重损害其他工作的情况下继续承担此项任务。

下表列出了今年年初以来签发的许可证数量：-

| 月份 | 许可证数量 | 大米袋数 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 一月 | 383 | 29,231 |
| 二月 | 468 | 40,702 |
| 三月 | 410 | 33,657 |
| 四月 | 363 | 30,775 |
| 五月 | 500 | 38,907 |
| 六月 | 1,140 | 99,544 |

由此可见，这项工作已从一名文员在完成日常职责之余即可处理的次要任务，增加到几乎成为全职工作。在7月的前18天里，每个工作日平均签发64张许可证，若每张许可证的签发（英文打字、中文书写及记录）耗时5分钟，则意味着每天工作超过五小时，从而没有时间去调查和核实可疑案件。

- 2 -

To meet the present situation it is suggested
that an extra clerk be engaged and assigned to this
office, the added expenses to be covered by a charge
of ten cents per bag of rice for which permits are
issued.

At a meeting of S.M.C. and F.M.C. officials
held on November 19, 1940 it was resolved that
Exportation Permits would involve a tax of ten cents
per bag of rice exported from the French Concession
but Mr. Beesley stated that the Settlement Authorities
were not empowered to charge a tax.

However, the payment would not be considered
a tax but a fee covering clerical expenses.

Should this suggestion be adopted it will be
necessary to amend Municipal Notification No. 4976
dated July 7, 1938.

Certified true copy.

为应对当前情况，建议增聘一名文员并分配至该办公室，增加的费用将通过按每张许可证涉及的大米每袋收取10美分来弥补。

在1940年11月19日举行的上海公共租界工部局和法公董局官员会议上，曾决议出口许可证将涉及对从法租界出口的每袋大米征收10美分的税，但比斯利先生 (Mr. Beesley) 表示，租界当局无权征税。

然而，这笔付款不被视为税收，而是涵盖文书费用的规费。

若采纳此建议，则有必要修订1938年7月7日发布的第4976号工部局通告。

"Staple Food Regulation Committee" - formation

The Staple Food Regulation Committee of
Shanghai (上海市民食調節協會), sponsored by prominent
members of the local Chinese community for the purpose
of regulating the price and supply of rice, was
formally inaugurated at a meeting held in the Bankers'
Club, 59 Hongkong Road, on the afternoon of December
18, 1939. Mr. Yu Ya Ching presided.

Following reports by Messrs. Kwei Yien Fang
(貴延芳), Wong Yui Ching (王禹卿) and William
Gockson (郭順) on the result of their negotiations
with foreign firms in connection with the importation
of rice, the meeting discussed and passed the
following resolutions :-

1. That a committee of 17 persons be elected.
2. That the drafted regulations of the committee be
discussed and published in due course.
3. That Messrs. Woo Yuin Tsai (吳齋), Kwei Yien
Fang and Hsu Chi-ching (徐寄) be appointed to
request the bankers to render financial aid in the
importation of rice.

“主食调节委员会” - 成立

上海市民食调节协会（Shanghai Staple Food Regulation Committee），由当地华人社区知名人士发起，旨在调节大米价格和供应，于1939年12月18日下午在香港路59号银行公会举行的会议上正式成立。虞洽卿先生主持会议。

在桂延芳、王禹卿和郭顺（William Gockson）三位先生报告了他们就大米进口事宜与外商谈判的结果后，会议讨论并通过了以下决议：-

1. 选举产生一个由17人组成的委员会。
2. 适时讨论并公布委员会起草的规章。
3. 委派吴齋（Woo Yuin Tsai）、桂延芳和徐寄庼（Hsu Chi-ching）三位先生请求银行家在进口大米方面提供财政援助。

Despite the large number of arrests on
on shops
December 15, attacks continued the following day,
34 shops being affected and 63 persons arrested.
On December 17, however, there was a falling off in
the number of raids, 3 being recorded in addition to
one on a flour shop. Investigation among members
of the Rice Guild strengthen the view that the trouble
was organized. In the majority of cases, the initial
move was made by one or more individuals of the better
dressed loafer type who decamped immediately their
lead had been taken up by the crowds that gathered
comprising mostly mill workers and those of the poorer
class.

- 3 -

Meeting of Shanghai Bean and Rice Dealers' Guild
and Rice Shop Owners' Guild

Twenty one committee members of the Shanghai
Bean and Rice Dealers' Guild held a meeting in their
office, 15 Avenue Edward VII, between 3.45 p.m. and
6.30 p.m. December 16, when Ying Ta Kiang (邢志剛)
presided. He reported that Messrs. Chen Ts Yi
(陳子彝), Tsu Ts Shiang (朱子香), Chow Ts Tseng
(周子楨) and Koo Yin Sung (顧益生) had called
on Mr. T.K. Ho of the S.M.C. in the forenoon
requesting adequate protection for legitimate rice
dealers and also discussed the new price limit of
$40 and $33 per "zar". The following resolutions
were then discussed and passed :-

1. That the price limit be revised and fixed at
$40.00 per "zar" for "Kan Mee" and $33.00 for
"See Mee" with effect from December 17, and that
no restriction be placed on Saigon rice because
of the fluctuation in the exchange rate.

2. That a letter of complaint be addressed to the
authorities of the two foreign areas regarding the
looting of shops since the proclamation was issued -
further that a request be made to define clearly
the real sense of rice hoarding and speculation
so that legitimate dealers can be protected.

Twenty three committee members of the Shanghai
Rice Shop Owners' Guild held a meeting in their office,
Lane 153, 58 Shanhaikwan Road, at 4 p.m. December 16

上海豆米业同业公会及米业同业公会会议

12月16日下午3时45分至6时30分，上海豆米业同业公会的21名委员在其办公室（爱多亚路15号）举行会议，由邢志剛（Ying Ta Kiang）主持。他报告说，陈子彝、朱子香、周子楨和顾益生四位先生于当天上午拜访了工部局的何德奎（T.K. Ho）先生，要求为合法米商提供充分保护，并讨论了每“担”40元和33元的新限价。随后讨论并通过了以下决议：-

December 12, 1939. Morning Translation

Shun Pao :-

Japanese Preventing Transportation Of Rice To Shanghai

Since the enforcement of a control by the Japanese authorities over the supply of food provisions for Shanghai, the city has felt a shortage of arrivals of foodstuffs, with the result that the price of rice has gone up rapidly. Recently, the Japanese authorities withdrew all the passes issued to the transportation companies for the transportation of rice, thereby preventing transport of rice to the Foreign Settlements. This action on the part of the Japanese authorities has given a good opportunity to the rice hoarders to raise the price of rice, but on the other hand it has brought about a state of stagnation in the rice market in the interior owing to lack of purchasers. Consequently, the peasants, considering it a good opportunity to make profits, have resorted to the use of bicycles for the transportation of rice into the Foreign Settlements by way of Chungshan Road via Chapel and Hongkew. They have been able to make a profit of more than $10 a day each with the result that transportation of rice by this means has been carried out extensively. The transportation has now been forbidden by the Western District Branch of the Japanese Military Headquarters on Lincoln Road which has detained many bicycles and the rice under transportation. It is learned that more than 400 bicycles were held up by the Japanese in the past two days.
（批：S/p Br- ?）
（印：RECEIVED 13 DEC. 1939 COMMISSION...）
（批：+12）

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-

Japanese Army To Co-operate In Prevention Of Hoarding

The continued increase in the price of rice has greatly affected the people in Shanghai and has now become a serious social problem. Many people have been spreading counter-propaganda saying that the increase in price of rice is due to the restrictions placed by the Japanese Army upon the new harvest. However, this is entirely contrary to fact and the Japanese Army has tried by all means to facilitate the work of the new harvest. In fact, the situation has been caused by the hoarding of unscrupulous rice merchants. A joint proclamation was issued by the authorities of the Shanghai Municipal Council and the French Municipal Council with the object of eradicating the unscrupulous merchants. The Japanese Army will also render its assistance to this strong attitude taken by the authorities of the Foreign Settlements and at the same time is hoping that the order will be thoroughly carried out.

1939年12月12日。晨间译文

《申报》：-

日本阻止大米运往上海

自从日本当局对上海食品供应实施管制以来，该市感到食品到货短缺，导致米价迅速上涨。最近，日本当局收回了发给运输公司用于运输大米的所有通行证，从而阻止大米运往外国租界。日本当局的这一举动给囤积居奇者提供了抬高米价的良机，但另一方面，由于缺乏买家，也导致内地大米市场陷入停滞状态。因此，农民们认为这是获利的好机会，便利用自行车经闸北和虹口，沿中山路将大米运入外国租界。他们每人每天能获利10元以上，导致这种运输方式被广泛采用。目前，位于林肯路（Lincoln Road）的日本军事总部西区支部已禁止此种运输，并扣押了许多自行车及运输中的大米。据悉，过去两天日本人扣留了400多辆自行车。
（批注：S/p Br- ?）
（印章：1939年12月13日收讫 警务总...）
（批注：+12）

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：-

日军合作防止囤积

米价的持续上涨极大地影响了上海市民，现已成为一个严重的社会问题。许多人散布反面宣传，称米价上涨是由于日军对新粮收获施加限制所致。然而，这完全与事实不符，日军已竭尽全力促进新粮收获工作。事实上，这种情况是由不法米商囤积居奇造成的。上海公共租界工部局和法公董局当局联合发布公告，旨在铲除不法商人。日军也将协助外国租界当局采取的这一强硬态度，同时希望命令得到彻底执行。

has recently shown a decided falling off, and no
rice has arrived from Kompo since November 1. The
rice from this area is being reserved for local use,
it is reported, and therefore no supplies will be

rice producing district, has been closed to Chinese
dealers and only Japanese dealers are now being
permitted to transport their rice from that place.

remains the same, the stocks are being gradually
decreased through the smallness of arrivals which
do not offset the demand and of course increases in
the price are the natural consequences.

Date August 9, 19
Subject. Rice Situation.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

On the forenoon of August 8, transactions
in rice at prices above the limit were carried out
on a large scale in a secret manner. The prices
quoted are reported to be from $3.50 to $5.00 above
the price limit and it is estimated that some 6,000
bags were sold. Although rice shop owners on
August 5 decided not to purchase rice above the
price limit, they resumed buying because their
stocks have run short in consequence of their refusal
to augment the stocks during the past three days.
As previously reported, the dealers have
no proper records of the transactions done and
remain reticent on the approach of any strangers,
and it is an impossibility for the police to obtain
evidence. The buyers, being mostly rice shop
owners, though complaining of the high prices, show
an unwillingness to disclose any particulars of
those sellers because of a fear of reprisals by the
dealers who will refuse to sell them rice in the
future. There are 104 rice hongs doing business
in the Rice Market, the majority of whom are concerned
in those underhand transactions.
It is necessary to emphasize here that this
state of affairs is well known to the management of
the Rice Market which is composed of the managers of
six rice hongs, who, however, apart from maintaining
a fixed policy by suspending their own buying for
the time being, are unwilling to take upon themselves

主题. 大米情况。
由督察长克劳福德撰写并转发

8月8日上午，以高于限价的价格进行的大米交易秘密大规模进行。据报，报价比限价高出3.50至5.00元，估计售出了约6,000袋。尽管米店老板在8月5日决定不购买高于限价的大米，但由于过去三天拒绝增加库存导致存货短缺，他们恢复了购买。如前所述，经销商没有适当的交易记录，并对陌生人的接近保持沉默，警方无法获取证据。买家大多是米店老板，虽然抱怨价格高昂，但因害怕遭到经销商报复（即未来拒绝向他们出售大米），不愿透露卖家的任何细节。大米市场内有104家米行从事业务，其中大多数参与了这些幕后交易。
在此必须强调，大米市场管理层对此状况非常清楚，该管理层由六家米行的经理组成，然而，除了暂时停止自身采购以维持既定政策外，他们不愿承担

their co-operation it is almost impossible for the
police to discover the offenders.
Should a stricter control be enforced in
the market, there is the possibility that the
dealers will do business outside the market, what
control which is small would disappear altogether.
It has been found that the merchants purchasing
in the Sungkiang area gather stocks in small
quantities at different places in order to hoodwink
the Japanese authorities and therefore it would be
very difficult to endeavour to corner this area.
The only other alternative is to strike at the
source of the commodity and if it was at all possible
to release the stocks which are abundant, from the
Wuhu area, the situation would be greatly relieved,
but this entails negotiations with the Reformed
Government authorities and the Japanese military.
It is known that stocks are being hoarded but it
would be a very difficult job to check on all shops
and godowns ourselves and it is doubtful if we could
do so legally.

Between July 20 and 25, 40,000 bags of "See Mee"
were brought into Shanghai by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and
Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha. Some 20,000 bags of this
consignment have already been sold and are now on sale
in the local market. The remaining part of this rice is
stored in the godowns of the Central and Lower Wharves
of the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company in the
Hongkew district.
In the early part of July, some 42,000 "zars"
of Chinese rice were exported from Shanghai to Tientsin,
Chefoo, Tsingtao, Swatow and Hongkong. The exportation
of this rice was not affected by the order prohibiting
exportation of rice from Shanghai from July 1, as arrangements
for the exportation were completed with the Customs
Authorities prior to July 1. No rice was exported after
July 10, with the exception of some 500 "zars" which were
transported to the area north of the Soochow Creek daily,
believed for use in rice shops in that area.
The present rate of consumption is in the region
of 9,000 "zars" per day, and is composed mostly of Chinese
rice. The amount of Saigon Rice consumed is negligible,
and the market is now almost devoid of that rice, there being
only 3,000 bags distributed among the 700 rice shops in the
Settlement and French Concession. The present stock of
rice on hand in Shanghai is considered sufficient to last
for a period of one month, at the present rate of consumption.

Exportation
and con-
sumption
Chinese rice has recently been exported from
Shanghai to ports in south and north China. Rice exported
is purchased by outport dealers at the Rice Market in the
Tsing Lien Koh Teashop, 515 Foochow Road, in quantities of
several thousands "zars". The rice so purchased is
stored in godowns, and after a few days, when several
purchases have been made, the rice is then exported. Of
the rice exported to the North, certain portions are not
purchased at the Rice Market, but bought directly from
local dealers.

Rice for ports in North China, such as Tientsin,
Chefoo, Dairen, etc. is removed from the godowns where it
is stored, to wharves north of the Soochow Creek. As the
exportation is not subject to Customs supervision, the
exact amount exported cannot be ascertained. It is however
known that approximately 1,000 "zars" are purchased through
the Rice Market almost daily by dealers engaged in
exporting rice to the North.

Rice for ports in the south is mostly shipped
from wharves on the French Bund, with Customs formalities,
supported by certificates from the Chinese Chambers of
Commerce at outports and also by certificates from the
local Chinese Chamber of Commerce. It is estimated
that approximately 70,000 "zars" have been sent to Swatow
and Amoy, and 8,000 "zars" to Ningpo. No exportation

THE EXPORTATION OF RICE FROM SHANGHAI

With a view to preventing a shortage of rice
in Shanghai, the authorities of the French Concession
have adopted certain measures prohibiting the exportation
of rice from Shanghai. A petition has now been submitted
to the local French Consul-General by the Bean and Rice
Dealers' Association requesting the abolition of these
measures.

A meeting was held yesterday by the S.M.C.
at which the question of prohibiting the exportation of
rice from Shanghai was brought up for discussion.

Consequent upon the adoption of these measures
by the French Concession authorities, the merchants of
Swatow are unable to secure the approval of the Customs for
the exportation of the rice which they had purchased in
Shanghai.

Enquiries made by our reporter among local rice
dealers show that the Shanghai Bean and Rice Dealers'
Association has asked for the abolition of the order
prohibiting the exportation of rice from Shanghai because
there are now sufficient quantities of rice in stock in
Shanghai.

It is learned that rice which is transported to
North China is exported from Shanghai from wharves in Hongkew.

上海大米出口

为了防止上海出现大米短缺，法租界当局采取了某些措施，禁止从上海出口大米。豆米同业公会现已向当地法国总领事提交请愿书，请求废除这些措施。

工部局昨日举行会议，会上提出了禁止从上海出口大米的问题进行讨论。

由于法租界当局采取了这些措施，汕头商人无法获得海关对其在上海购买的大米出口的批准。

本报记者向本地米商查询得知，上海豆米同业公会要求废除禁止从上海出口大米的命令，因为上海目前有足够的大米库存。

Morning Leader and other local newspapers :-24/5/38(A.M)

HUGE RICE STOCK IN SHANGHAI

There are more than 500,000 piculs of rice
in Shanghai. During the past few days, more than 50
rice boats have been arriving in Shanghai daily from
Changshu, Wusih, Tsingpu and Pinghu. Foreign steamers
have also been carrying rice to Shanghai from Changyinsha.
Dealers from Tientsin, Dairen, Chefoo, Tsingtao,
Weihaiwei, Swatow and Ningpo have ordered large quantities
of rice from Shanghai. In order to prevent a shortage
of rice, the French Concession authorities have issued an
order prohibiting the exportation of rice without the
approval of the authorities.
Rice dealers are requesting the French
authorities to permit exportation on the ground that there
is a large stock of rice in Shanghai, that the rice, if
kept in the godown, will decay in damp weather, and that
the Customs does not prohibit the exportation of rice.
The French authorities have approved the exportation of
rice to Ningpo because this rice will be sold at a low
price to poor people. A first consignment of 6,000
bags has already left for Ningpo.
Owing to the control enforced on foreign
exchange by the Chinese Government, private dealers have
ceased to purchase rice from abroad. The authorities of
the International Settlement and the French Concession will,
if necessary, continue to buy rice from Saigon. It is
believed that the measures adopted by the authorities and
the rice dealers have removed all dangers of a rice
shortage.

上海大米库存巨大

上海有大米50多万担。在过去几天里，每天有50多艘运米船从常熟、无锡、青浦和平湖抵达上海。外国轮船也从崇明岛运送大米到上海。来自天津、大连、烟台、青岛、威海卫、汕头和宁波的客商已向上海订购了大量大米。为了防止大米短缺，法租界当局发布命令，禁止未经当局批准出口大米。
米商请求法国当局允许出口，理由是上海有大量大米库存，如果将大米留在仓库中，会在潮湿天气中变质，且海关并不禁止大米出口。法国当局已批准向宁波出口大米，因为这些大米将以低价出售给穷人。第一批6,000袋大米已启运前往宁波。
由于中国政府实施外汇管制，私人商贩已停止从国外购买大米。如有必要，公共租界和法租界当局将继续从西贡购买大米。相信当局和米商采取的措施已消除了大米短缺的所有危险。

importers who have stocks bought before are holding

the higher prices. Dealers have again resorted to
the practice of buying and holding and then reselling
on the Rice Market when the price increases.

the foreign import firms are now offering 1st and 2nd
quality Saigon rice at $54.00 and $49.00 per bag

Shanghai Rice Shop Owners' Guild held a meeting in

the request from the Shanghai Staple Food Regulation
Committee for the conducting of cheap sales of rice.

Situation in Pootung

Following the attacks on rice shops in
Pootung on February 18 and 20, 1940, the rice shops
there refuse to augment their stocks, because of a
fear of further attacks, with the result that the
majority of them have no stock. In order to show his
benevolence, Mr. Hashimoto, Chief of the Pootung
Section of the Japanese Military Special Service
Department on February 22 arranged for the transporta-
tion of 300 bags of rice from Minghong, and this rice
was distributed among rice shops, numbering 40 at
$36.00 per "zar". Tsu Ngoh Tseng (朱玉軫), Chief
of the Pootung Administrative Office of the Shanghai
City Government was responsible for the distribution
and those rice shops were instructed to sell this rice
at $37.00 per "zar", each purchase being limited to
$1.00 worth of rice.

Despite these instructions the rice shops
were retailing at $1.00 for 0.025 "zar" which is
equivalent to $40.00 per "zar".

浦东情况

继1940年2月18日和20日浦东米店遭受袭击后，那里的米店因担心再次遭到袭击而拒绝增加库存，导致大多数米店没有库存。为了显示其仁慈，日本军方特务部浦东section主任桥本先生（Mr. Hashimoto）于2月22日安排从闵行运输300包大米，并将这些大米分发给40家米店，价格为每“石”36.00美元。上海市政府浦东行政办事处主任朱玉軫（Tsu Ngoh Tseng）负责分发工作，并指示这些米店以每“石”37.00美元的价格出售此米，每次购买限值为1.00美元的米。

- 3 -

Situation in Pootung

The price of rice in Pootung has been
rising recently. On February 18, the price reached
$40.00 per "zar"; only inferior quality and broken
rice is being sold by the various rice shops.

At 10 a.m. February 18, a consignment of
48 "zars" of Kan Mee rice which was being
transported from Chowpu to the Yuan Chong Rice Shop
(源昌米号), Tung Chong Road, Pootung, was looted
in the course of transportation near Lung Wong
Miao, Pootung, by a party of poor people.

At 2 p.m. the same day, an attempt was
made to attack the Hwang Tseng Kee (黄增记) Rice
Shop, Tung Chong Road, Pootung, when some four
hundred persons of the poor class gathered at
the shop but were dispersed by members of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party, who were summoned
to the scene by the shop master.

Following this incident, other rice shops
in the Tung Chong Road area, Pootung, closed their
doors and were placed under the protection by the
Pootung Branch of the Bureau of Police. The rice
shops resumed business on February 19.

C. Crawford
D. I.

February 1,1940.
Afternoon Translation.

Circulation Daily News :-

PRICE OF RICE EXCEEDS LIMIT

Yesterday only about 600 bags of rice arrived
in Shanghai. Due to scanty arrivals coupled with the
unwillingness of the owners to sell, the rice situation
has become more serious and some difficulty is being
experienced to keep prices within the fixed limit. Private
transactions have again become more common. It is said
that the price of the best quality Kan-Mee rice from
Quinsan has reached as high as $46 per "zar," while that
of second grade has likewise exceeded the limit by one to
two dollars.
The rice that is being sold at the price
limit is of very inferior quality.

CHINA PRESS

FEB 2 1940

Record Smashed
Domestic Rice
Is Sold At
$46 Per Picul

Prices of domestic rice yesterday rose to an unprecedented high as Changshu products were quoted in local markets at as high as $46 per picul.

Rice dealers informed THE CHINA PRESS last night that due partly to increasing hoarding activities here and partly to curtailment of arrivals, domestic rice was virtually totally absent from the local markets.

Slightly lower were the prices of Saigon rice which were sold at rice shops yesterday at about $42 per picul. Arrivals of rice from the French Colony continued to register large quantities.

Rice In Hongkew

Japanese quarters were still non-committal yesterday regarding the long-promised shipments of rice to relieve the scarcity here. It was reliably learned that the Japanese had brought huge quantities to Hongkew but would allow not one grain of it to be transported to the Settlement and Concession.

Relief workers here were reported to have communicated with the Japanese for shipment of domestic rice here for the exclusive use of the destitute. Thus far, according to one report, the Japanese have definitely turned down any consideration of the suggestion.

Shops Jammed By Poor

The daylong drizzling rain notwithstanding, more than 30,000 of the city's poor jammed local rice shops engaging in "cheap sales." As on previous days, the allotment at each shop was completely sold.

Yesterday the Benevolent Bodies Joint Association resumed distributing bread to the poor on Majestic Road, under the sponsorship of Mr. Loh Tah-shun and other civic leaders. Foreign and Chinese police officers were detailed to the distribution center to maintain order.

It was learned that in view of

《字林西报》

1940年2月2日

纪录被打破
国产米
售价达
每担46美元

昨日国产米价格涨至前所未有的高位，常熟产大米在本地市场的报价高达每担46美元。

米商昨晚告诉《字林西报》，部分由于本地囤积活动加剧，部分由于到货减少，国产米在本地市场上几乎绝迹。

西贡米的价格略低，昨日米店的售价约为每担42美元。来自法属殖民地的大米到货量继续保持在较大水平。

虹口的大米

关于长期承诺的旨在缓解本地短缺的大米运输，日方辖区昨日仍持保留态度。据可靠消息获悉，日本人已将大量大米运至虹口，但不允许其中一粒米运往租界和公董局辖区。

据报道，本地的救济工作人员已与日方联系，要求运送国产米至此，专供贫民使用。据一份报告称，截至目前，日方已明确拒绝考虑该建议。

穷人挤满店铺

尽管整天下着毛毛雨，本市仍有超过30,000名穷人涌入本地米店参与“平价销售”。与前几天一样，每家店铺的配给额全部售罄。

昨日，在罗达顺（Loh Tah-shun，音译）先生和其他社会领袖的赞助下，慈善团体联合协会在马杰斯提克路（Majestic Road，即今延安中路近西藏南路段，或指爱多亚路附近，此处依原文音译）恢复向穷人分发面包。中外警官被派往分发中心维持秩序。

A continuous decrease has taken place in
the price of Saigon rice during the past ten days,
and is believed to be due to the following reasons:-
    a) The price in the producing areas has
shown a decrease. (The price quoted by foreign
import firms a fortnight ago was approximately
$60.00 per bag for 1st quality Saigon rice but the
price on March 18 was approximately $51.00.)
    b) In January, 1940, local rice dealers
placed orders with foreign import firms for
consignments of foreign rice due to arrive in April,
but the majority of these consignments unexpectedly
arrived in Shanghai in March because ships were
available earlier than expected. With this early
arrival of stocks, the import firms are demanding
that the dealers take delivery and clear their
accounts at once, consequently dealers must sell
to realise their money.

                                C. Crawford
                                    D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

A notice jointly issued by the Bean and Rice
Hong Owners' Guild and the Cereal Dealers' Guild
regarding rules governing delivery and payment of
prices, was exhibited at the Rice Market this morning,
December 13. A brief translation of the notice reads
as follows :-

"In compliance with instructions from the
Municipal Authorities, the rule that payment of price
be made on the 5th day and delivery taken within 10
days will be cancelled and the following rules will
be enforced from date :

"For any transactions done at the Rice Market,
bargain money of $5 per bag will be paid on the same
day when the transaction is settled,and the rice
purchased must be taken delivery of within five days
as well as the payment of the price. Failing to do
so, the bargain money paid will be confiscated and
the "buyer" will be held responsible for any loss to
be sustained therefrom by the "seller." In case,
the "buyer" refuses to observe this rule, the "seller"
should make a report to the Guild for submission to
the Municipal Authorities. Failure to report will
lead to both parties being punished."

C. Crawford
D. I.

A.C. (Special Branch)

1. In connection with the resolution passed at a
meeting held on December 3 in the S.M.C. Administra-
tion Building regarding the payment of bargain
money and the period of taking delivery, it was
decided that bargain money of $5 per bag be paid
on the day when transactions are settled and
that the delivery be made in accordance with the
rules passed on May 3, 1940, i.e. 50% of the price
for rice sold without a delivery order and 80%
for rice sold with a delivery order to be paid
on the 5th day and that the delivery of the rice
must be taken within 10 days when the full price
must be paid. Should the buyer fail to take
delivery within 10 days, the seller will be
permitted to sell the rice involved on the 11th
day at the prevailing market price, and any profit
thus obtained will be handed over to the buyer,
and any loss sustained made good from the money
already paid by the buyer. The Board of Management
of the Rice Market will be instructed to strictly
enforce this rule on December 12 and the offending
dealers will be referred to the authorities to be
dealt with.
2. That the dealers be notified to register with
the Guilds not later than December 14, 1940,
the quantities of No.1 Saigon rice on order through
import firms as well as the quantities on forward
sales.

SUBJECT: - 2 -

On April 26, the majority of the local
retail rice shops continued to refrain from purchasing
supplies of rice from the Rice Market as a protest
against the holders demanding secret "allowances"
in addition to the fixed price. A few of them,
however, appeared in the Market and conducted
business private in defiance of the decision of the
Rice Shop Owners' Association, and consequently
sales involving some 2,500 "zars" were transacted.
The so-called "allowance", it is believed, was still
charged in addition to the fixed price, the "allowance"
being the same as previously reported, i.e. $10.00
per "zar" for Kan Mee and $11.20 to $12.80 per "zar"
for Saigon and Rangoon rice. The market was
closed on April 27 (Sunday).

The fixed prices, announced by the Rice
Market Control Committee on April 17 in compliance
with the instructions of the Municipal Authorities,
are reported to have been removed from to-day,
April 28. The business transactions at the Rice
Market had not started by the time this report was
compiled, and the prices given below are those of
April 27 :-

Business in the Rice Market, 515 Foochow Road, was almost at a standstill on the morning of April 23.
